items.sum: Editorial celebrating the club's best season in 20 years: British League entry, record-breaking, juniors topping UK rankings, Commonwealth Games athletes, the Surrey AC merger and a new Battersea Park track.
items.s: HAPPY TIMES Editorial celebrating the club's best season in 20 years: British League entry, record-breaking, juniors topping UK rankings, Commonwealth Games athletes, the Surrey AC merger and a new Battersea Park track. It is possible to say, without fear of contradiction, that the last 6 months have seen the most rapid and significant upswing in the affairs of Belgrave for the last 20 years. Indeed there are some who would rate our progress higher and say that our advances on all fronts have no previous comparison. So to the facts. Our mens track and field team has gained entry into the British League. Our ladies team has been transformed from a depleted side at the start of the season into a match winning combination at the end. More Club records have been broken than in any previous season by both men and ladies. Our strength is in our youngsters and we have the unique situation of 2 juniors heading the U.K. Mens Junior T and F rankings at the blue ribbon events of the 800 and 1500 m plus a new U.K. 4 x 1 mile Junior record. And to ice the cake Ernie Obeng and Paul Blagg competed at Brisbane in the Commonwealth Games. Our walkers as usual performed at the highest levels. Towards the end of the season Surrey AC mens section decided to go into liquidation and the majority of the athletes and officials have joined with us to forge a stronger management and athletics teams for the years ahead. They are doubly welcome. And to cap it all Battersea Park Track is to be dug up in December 1982 and will be resplendant with one of the Country's finest all-weather surfaces in time for the next track season. The Gods are smiling on us. We deserve it. Ernie Obeng Ernie Obeng competed at the Commonwealth Games, Brisbane Paul Blagg Paul Blagg competed at the Commonwealth Games, Brisbane British Athletics League Commonwealth Games Brisbane Battersea Park Surrey AC

items.label: October 1982
items.h: Welcome — THE "AMALGAMATION" - SURREY AC MEN JOIN BELGRAVE.
items.sum: Account of how the Surrey AC men's section merged into Belgrave, and how Belgrave's place in British League Division 5 survived a challenge at the league AGM.
items.s: Welcome — THE "AMALGAMATION" - SURREY AC MEN JOIN BELGRAVE. Account of how the Surrey AC men's section merged into Belgrave, and how Belgrave's place in British League Division 5 survived a challenge at the league AGM. Welcome THE "AMALGAMATION" - SURREY AC MEN JOIN BELGRAVE. Many of you will have seen the controversial correspondence in "Athletics Weekly" about the amalgamation of ex Surrey AC members into Belgrave, their participation in our British League Promotion match and the resulting adverse reaction from a few individuals and teams. Confused? Well these are the facts. Belgrave was approached at the beginning of the T and F season by officials of London AC and Surrey AC who explained that both clubs were experiencing difficulty in finding officials and putting out league teams. Their proposal was to form a new Club with Belgrave. The matter was to be put to E.G.M's of the 3 Clubs but the plan fell at the first hurdle when LAC rejected the idea. At the Surrey AC meeting the ladies voted against joining Belgrave but the men could not raise enough officials and decided to close down and amalgamate with Belgrave subject to a full integration of officials and athletes into Belgrave's affairs. The Surrey men were welcomed into our ranks and already have made a positive impact by strengthening our administrative and athletic activities. The British and Southern Leagues were informed that as from August 31st 1982, Surrey men would join with Belgrave. At about the same time Belgrave learnt that it had qualified in 8th place for the British League qualifying match which was held at Luton on September 4th. Eight of the Surrey men wished to compete and after clearance in writing from the Southern Counties AAA's we ran them and won. Immediately the British League invited us into Div.5, we accepted and then the problems started. Many people could not accept that our actions were legal. The Secretary of the Southern League met with Senior Belgrave Officials and asked us to withdraw in favour of Windsor, S. and Eton. We felt we were in the right and so Windsor - backed by the Southern League - put a motion to the AGM of the British League demanding our withdrawal. Derek Crookes and Bill Laws went along to the AGM on October 30th and argued the Belgrave case. The debate was fair and wide ranging and only 1 club (a south London one) argued strongly in favour of the motion. After a 1½ hour debate a vote was taken. 28 were in favour of Belgrave and 5 against (Haringay, Hillingdon, Herne Hill, Leeds and Met. Police). A compromise solution was then put by the BAL executive and that was to include a 7th team (Windsor) in Div.5 for the next season only. After a card ballot it was agreed to include Windsor by 18-15 and everyone breathed a sigh of relief. To quote Wellington. "It was a damned close run thing". And so in 1983 the eyes of the BAL will be on Belgrave. Its up to you the athletes to show them how good you are. Your Club will give you every possible encouragement and support. items.sum: Summary of the treasurer's 1981/82 accounts presented by Jim Heathfield at the AGM, with income, expenditure and Belgrave Hall figures, and an appeal for more helpers.
items.s: MONEY MATTERS — 1981/82 Accounts. Summary of the treasurer's 1981/82 accounts presented by Jim Heathfield at the AGM, with income, expenditure and Belgrave Hall figures, and an appeal for more helpers. MONEY MATTERS 1981/82 Accounts. With so much demand for financial support for our teams, for coaching, as well as for developments at Belgrave Hall and Battersea Park Track it was with great anticipation that the treasurer's report at our AGM on Sept. 16th was so eagerly awaited. In masterful style which would have done justice to the AGM of a large Corporation Jim Heathfield took us step by step through the not insignificant sums which spelt out our financial achievements for the year. Subscriptions were up to a new record of £2,779 which when backed by other fund raising monies increased income to £4,356. Expenditure, however, increased to £4,179 so that the current account surplus for the year dropped to £177 from the previous year's £916. The two main items of expenditure were:- Printing, stationery and postage at £1,463 and Team fees and expenses at £1,123. So once again let it be noted that subscriptions in no way meet the running costs of the Club. The separate Belgrave Hall accounts presented a much rosier picture with total income reaching £12,732 offset by purchases and expenditure totalling £9,111 to give a nett profit of £3,621. Thus the overall Club profit for the year increased to £3,798 which helped to swell our cash in hand for our development programme to a robust £10,439. This healthy state of affairs is the result of efforts by those seemingly few hard working members who put your Club at the top of their priorities. There is so much to be done in the year ahead that everyone's help will be required. So please - examine what you did for your colleagues last year. If it wasn't a lot resolve to help and support other people's efforts in the year ahead. Remember we have plenty of members only too willing to give advice. The ones we cherish are those who believe in deeds - not words. Jim Heathfield Jim Heathfield treasurer; presented the 1981/82 accounts at the AGM Belgrave Harriers AGM Belgrave Hall Battersea Park

items.sum: Profile of Geoff Davis, former Surrey A.C. president elected Belgrave joint president, covering his sprinting career from 1948 and his work as an official and team manager.
items.s: GEOFF DAVIS - JOINT PRESIDENT Profile of Geoff Davis, former Surrey A.C. president elected Belgrave joint president, covering his sprinting career from 1948 and his work as an official and team manager. GEOFF DAVIS - JOINT PRESIDENT GEOFF DAVIS was elected Joint President with Derek Crookes at the A.G.M. in September having joined Belgrave following the Marriage with the men from Surrey A.C. where he was President.(For an appreciation of Derek Crookes refer to the Oct. 1981 issue of the BELGRAVIAN ). Like so many members, Geoff began his athletic career while at school and first hit the headlines in 1948 when he won the English Schools Boy's 220 yard Championship in 22.9 which was then an English Schools' record. Also while he was at school he was the British ATC National champion over both the short sprints in 1948 and 1949. Although living in the heart of Berkshire he joined Polytechnic Harriers and ran for Poly for a number of years. He won no less than 7 Berkshire A.A.A. titles at 100, 220 and 440 yards in the early 1950's and was a member of the Polytechnic 4 x 110 and 4 x 440 relay teams which includeded Macdonald Bailey, Arthur Wint and Brian Shenton, and which won A.A.A. titles. Running on the Poly track at Chiswick he won the SCAAA Junior 220 yards title in 1950 and 4 years later he was third in the Senior event at the same distance. At National level he took 3rd and 4th places in the junior A.A.A. 100 and 220 yards Championship at Birmingham in 1949 and followed this up in 1950 with 3rd in the 220 yards. He moved up to the 440 yard event in 1954, figured well in the National rankings in this event the following year and narrowly missed selection for the 1956 Melbourne Olympics. He represented the A.A.A's the Royal Air Force and Combined Services in representative matches and also competed in France, Holland, Belgium and Germany. When his competitive days were over he turned his attention to the administrative side of athletics and was Secretary of the Insurance A.A. for some years before joining Surrey A.C. in 1970 initially to support his daughter Nicola who won Surrey County honours in both Long Jump and 200m. He was for almost 10 years Secretary of Surrey A.C. and has been Team Manager for both their young athletes and senior sides. He is currently a Vice-President of Surrey A.A.A. and team manager for the Surrey County juniors and youths and a number of Belgravians will already know him through his association with the County. Under his leadership the Surrey Youths have won the annual Inter-Counties event for the last 3 years while the Juniors narrowly failed to complete a double hat-trick this year by a handful of points. He is particularly interested in developing the talents of young athletes and has encouraged many youngsters to develop into good senior athletes. Geoff is a married man with 2 daughters and a son and despite his youthful appearance has 4 grandchildren! In 1981 he qualified as a Track Referee and this year he refereed the Thorn E.M.I. items.sum: Obituaries of three long-serving members: veteran sprinter and walker Charlie Speechley, international cross-country runner and club captain Bert Footer, and cross-country runner Alf Taylor.
items.s: In Memorium Obituaries of three long-serving members: veteran sprinter and walker Charlie Speechley, international cross-country runner and club captain Bert Footer, and cross-country runner Alf Taylor. In Memorium We have recently mourned the deaths of three of our oldest members, their combined membership exceeded 170 years! Each played a part in the affairs and fortunes of the Club, and, in regretting their passing we pay tribute to their memories. CHARLIE SPEECHLEY. Probably the oldest active athlete in the country he was taking part in Vets sprint handicaps until fairly recently. About two or three years ago he fell from a ladder severely lacerating his legs, but he carried on with his legs in bandages. During his later years his eyesight was beginning to fail but this did not prevent him carrying out his activities. He was 94 years of age and joined us in 1919. He was also a keen swimmer and in 1908 he took part in the diving trials for the Olympic Games. His athletic hey-day, as a walker, was between the two World Wars and he took part regularly in Club and Open Handicaps and in Team Events. In 1933 he was a member of the team which won the Nijmegen Shield - awarded to the first Club to finish its complete team of 8 in the R.W.A. 20 miles Championship (now 35 kilos). BERT FOOTER. Without doubt the finest C.C. Captain we ever had is the unanimous opinion of those who knew Bert - indeed some would say that no Club ever had a better one. He was born in 1904 and joined us in 1922 and trained hard and became Club Champion. His prowess continued and he became County Champion and on one occasion he won the Southern Championship. It became his ambition to lead the Bels to a win in the "National" (E.C.C.U) title. For many years Birchfield H. had monopolized this race, gradually the Bels crept up the placings, third, second and, then on that glorious day in 1935 at Beaconsfield, he led the team to collect the winners medals, this was repeated in 1939 at Manchester. He gained two International Vests. In 1933 he was fourth home in the England (the winners) colours at Caerleon, and the following year he did the same again at Ayr - fourth man home with England winning again. In 1939 he set the marathon as his target, he had already made a name for himself at road races up to ten miles. He ran in the Poly Windsor to Chiswick, and, in one of the toughest races of his career he finished third. With the outbreak of World War II he joined the Marines and got involved in many tight situations. After the war he resumed his running, but others were coming along and he retired. He moved to Ramsgate and ran a small business. He developed arthritis which gradually worsened and eventually his general health deteriorated. A number of his old C.C. team mates attended his funeral to say "farewell" to a tough little man - a true C.C. type for whom gates, ditches, obstacles and "plough" held no terrors. ALF TAYLOR. A regular member of our cross country teams of the thirties which figured so prominently in the Southern and National Championships. He was a member of our winning teams in the Southern (1934) and the National (1935) as well as the London to Brighton Relay where he ran the six miles stage from Handcross to Hickstead. He was also a staunch Counties man and represented Middlesex on a number of occasions. In paying tribute to these three, typical good sportsmen of their era, we record our pleasure at having known them, not only for their athletic achievements but as friendly people whose company and memories we will treasure. Gordon Doubleday. items.s: BERT FOOTER Personal tribute to Bert Footer, who died on 23 April, from Arthur Penny, who joined Belgrave in 1928. BERT FOOTER who died on the 23rd. April was a dedicated Belgravian,achieved International Status and was a personality in his own right. A superb Club Captain and a leader of great spirit. That is how I shall remember him. I shall remember that when I joined Belgrave in 1928 Bert was already there,small in stature but a giant in dedication. He was the driving force behind all we achieved in the 30's, a man who was never beaten until the tape was broken. His successes were too numerous to list here but suffice to say his name was a household name. He leaves a widow and a daughter who had looked after him for years,for he was crippled with arthritis and had great difficulty in walking. Bert has now passed on. May he rest in peace. Arthur Penny (Nutty) Bert Footer BERT FOOTER died 23 April; club captain and international BERT FOOTER Bert Arthur Penny Arthur Penny (Nutty) nicknamed Nutty; joined Belgrave in 1928

MEMBERSHIP SECTION With the increased membership from Surrey A.C. there is obviously a heavier workload and, therefore, I should like to request a more prompt reply to subscription reminder notices. Regrettably, a few of our members many of whom are frequent users of club facilities, seem to be under the misapprehension that the reminders do not apply to them. To enable the system to work efficiently and weed out the dead wood, i.e. those that only join for a year - we are now carrying out the 6 month rule so be warned! Finally, a request to all those who move - please let me know as we are always getting "Gone Away" letters back and our postage costs are high. items.s: WALKING Walking section: Carl Lawton's review of the 1982 season and race reports April-September with Belgrave results, including Paul Blagg's international vest and Commonwealth Games selection and John Dunsford becoming Centurion No.734; the photo caption gives Carl Lawton 2nd and John Hall 3rd in the club 3000m championship, while the printed result has J.Hall 2nd and C.Lawton 3rd. WALKING Autumn leaves - that sums up the situation of the past few months. We won the National 10 mile, were 4th in the 20 kms. 2nd in the 35 kms. and 3rd in the 50 kms, but when the longer events came, except for the Dawlish, things were not so good. We were beaten in the Hastings,and did not start a team in the Brighton or National 100 kms. We would have won all Nationals if ..... But with so many fixtures these days, we cannot expect much else. Congratulations must go to Paul Blagg for his selection for the Commonwealth Games. By the time of reading this it will all be over and whether he succeeded or failed at least he got there which for many of us is a "pipe dream". Also congratulations to John Dunsford for completing the 100 miles at Leicester and thus joining the ranks of Centurions. John began having problems before 50 miles but managed to struggle on. The fact that we did not start a 100 kms.team means that we drop down in the senior rankings from our 2nd place. Next year I believe we can win the Mc Sweeney again, but unfortunately relies on one thing,co-operation from all club members. We now have a small girls section and the possibility of getting a senior girls side back on the road again. Obviously our failing is the U/20 mens side. Here we fall down on two fronts, lack of numbers and lack of help. Have I said enough! I have already, via a separate letter, requested that all semi and fully active walkers make an effort to compete regularly during the winter and I should now like to request that the non-active ones step forward and offer their services for the Belgrave 7 as pointsmen, recorders etc. and not have to rely on members from other sections who are already overloaded. e: Inter Banks Track and Field Championships
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's section's 1982 season, with its growth in juniors, Southern League placing and individual performances. WITH THE LADIES It has been a really exciting and extremely rewarding season. At the beginning of the year the whole future of the section looked very bleak indeed. Although we had a good nucleus of Seniors we had only a handful of Juniors. However, the crisis resolved itself with an influx of juniors, all from one school to begin with, (Walsingham) and later in the season from other schools in the Wandsworth and Battersea area - notably from Elliots, Mayfield, Battersea County and Notre Dame. Useful contacts have been forged and there is some very good athletic talent around the area that is, as yet, untapped. Highlight of the year must be the 3rd placing in the Inter Ladies 200m Final in the Womens A.A.A. Championships by Jackie Harman. Jackie also placed 4th in the 100m Final and set club records in the Heats. Unfortunately, Jackie was unable to compete in any of our Southern League matches this year. The Senior Relay Squad are now Southern Counties Relay Champions,unfortunately because only Belgrave showed up on the day, but the squad equalled the club record. In the Southern League Div.3 N.E. we finished in 8th place. This was a very good position to attain and makes us hopeful for the future. We hope to be able to get to the 2nd Division in 1983. Our 8th position was achieved without the benefit of a home match. The fact that some of our new youngsters had only the benefit of a months training before being thrown in at the deep end says a lot for their character and it was good to see them all doing their best for Belgrave. Just to emphasise how well everyone has done, Club Records have been equalled or improved on over 20 occasions and personal best performances have been set on numerous occasions (at least 30 in our last 3 Southern League matches.) Good performances were put up by Wendy Dunsford, who had a steady season with the Shot and Discus. Wendy was 3rd in the Senior Ladies Shot in the Middlesex Championships and 3rd in the Inter Banks Track and Field Championships. In the Javelin, Veronica St. Ange came 3rd in the Senior Ladies Javelin event in the Surrey Championships, and 3rd in the London Boroughs Championships throwing for Croydon. Good performances throughout the season too, from Jackie Barclay, Earlene Murrell, Dawn McNeil, Glenda Mahoney, and Tina Jordan. When they were available, newcomer Brenda Davis and veteran Pamela Davis gave very good accounts of themselves. Of the other Newcomers who have distinguished themselves Nikki King, Shirley Daure, Maude Okuley, Nana Nyarko have all given good performances and it is a pity that Pam Skeete was not always able to come to meetings. Turning to the Juniors, I would just like to praise Inoyo Etete, who joined us as a Shot Putter and Discus thrower but who was converted into a very good sprinter. Inoyo won the 200m and Shot in the Wandsworth Schools and won the shot in the London Schools Championships in her age group (by well over a metre) as well as anchoring her school relay team and Wandsworth Relay team. Notable performances from other Juniors have come from Jessica Palmer, Janice Porter, Lydia Montoute (who in her 3rd run for the club broke the Junior 200m record and also equalled the Junior 100m record and beat the Senior high jump record) Tracey Johnson, Audrey Clovey, Suzanne Jordan, Gail Porter, Sharon Martins, Janet Johnson , Diane Williams Lucia Spinelli and Alex MacLean. All this could not have been possible without help, and I have had some excellent assistance from Frank Simmons, Harry Porter, Joann Warnett and Jackie Barclay. A few more people like those mentioned are needed down at Battersea Park. Come on Belgravians and parents - where are you? Come along and get stuck in and help. Every section needs help. Not just us. To the Girls I would say this. It is Commonwealth Games Year. In four years time these Games will be in Britain. Work hard and do as you are told and it could be you who will be there. Well done all of you. Ladies Secretary Derek Jones Derek Jones Derek Jones Ladies Secretary Jackie Harman Jackie Harman 3rd Inter Ladies 200m and 4th 100m final, Womens A.A.A. What more could you ask for to the start of a season. A few sleepless nights had been spent in worrying about how we would get on and whether everyone would turn up. Any doubts were soon cast aside as everybody did extremely well. Without mentioning too many names, there were good runs from both Junior sprinters Janice Porter and Jessica Palmer, the ever improving Tracey Johnson and Suzanne Jordan and Gail Porter finishing, despite having a badly twisted ankle. items.h: JUNE 19th 1982 - ELTHAM - SOUTHERN WOMENS LEAGUE DIV.3 (NE)
items.sum: Report and Belgrave results from the Southern Women's League Division 3 (NE) match at Eltham on 19 June 1982, where Belgrave were second.
items.s: JUNE 19th 1982 - ELTHAM - SOUTHERN WOMENS LEAGUE DIV.3 (NE) Report and Belgrave results from the Southern Women's League Division 3 (NE) match at Eltham on 19 June 1982, where Belgrave were second. JUNE 19th 1982 - ELTHAM - SOUTHERN WOMENS LEAGUE DIV.3 (NE) Teams: 1. Cambridge 193½; 2.BELGRAVE 158½; 3.Peterborough 156½; 4.East Grinstead 122½; 5. Colchester 82. We did extremely well to come 2nd. The Juniors seem to improve with every meeting and good runs too from the 2 1500m runners. Suzanne Jordan has knocked over 20 seconds from her time since the beginning of the season. Gail Porter has improved her best time by over 30 seconds on last year. Good runs too from our hurdlers Janet Johnson and Lucia Spinelli and steady improvement too from Sharon Martins in the Javelin with good support, as usual, from Suzanne Jordan. Once again good performances from Inoyo Etete, Tracey Johnson, Lucia Spinelli, Jessica Palmer and Janice Porter. Janice has knocked nearly 3 seconds off her 200m time since April. In the senior squad injuries to key members did not help matters, but several of our new members were able to show their potential. Mention should also be made of Pam Davies, running in Belgrave colours for the first time and knocking nearly 27 seconds off the previous best 3000m time. items.s: SPONSORED RUN Report of the women's section's two-hour sponsored run at Battersea Park to raise money for a secondhand minibus. SPONSORED RUN Nineteen of our young ladies turned up at Battersea Park track on Sunday 3rd October for a 2 hour sponsored run aimed at raising funds towards the cost of a secondhand minibus. The furthest distance was achieved by 14 year old Gail Porter who ran 13½ miles with other splendid performances from 13 year old Suzanne Jordan (11¾ miles), sprinter Jackie Barclay (11¼ miles) and shot putter Wendy Dunsford (11 miles). Everyone enjoyed themselves and if all the promised sponsorships are realised the 'Bus Fund' stands to gain well over £500. items.s: CHAMPIONSHIP ROUNDUP Round-up of Belgrave women's and girls' performances in the 1982 school, county and national championships. CHAMPIONSHIP ROUNDUP Several excellent performances were recorded by Belgrave Ladies in the various School and County Championships this year. Surrey Champs. (April 24th, May 13th) In the Senior Javelin, Veronica St Ange took the bronze medal with 33.60 and Suzanne Jordan ran 5 21.3 for 1500m in the Junior Ladies event. Middlesex Champs. (May 15th) Wendy Dunsford won the bronze in the Senior Ladies shot with a fine 11.03. (Soon after in the Barclay Bank Championships Wendy set a new Club Record for the discus of 26.54). English Schools Champs. (July 10th) Glenda Mahoney was a member of the London 4 x100m team which recorded 48.1 to finish in second place. London Schools Champs. (July 14th) Wandsworth was first in 12 year old and second in the 13 year old groups aided by some good Belgrave performances. In the younger group Jessica Palmer was second in the 100m with 13.8, Inoyo Etete won the shot by a large margin in 9.45 and the 4 x 100m relay squad with Jessica and Inoyo won in 55.6. Of the 13 year olds Janice Porter was 3rd in the 200m with 28.1 (28.0 Heat), Gail Porter was 3rd in the 1500m with 5 30.0 and Janice helped the 4 x100 m in squad to first place in 53.1. Womens AAA's Champs. (July 30th and 31st) Two fine runs by Jackie Harman, who has recently joined us from Herne Hill, and these set new Club Records. Jackie finished 4th in the Inter Ladies 100m in 12.15 and won the bronze in the 200m in 24.31. SCWAAA's Multi Events Champs. (August 14th and 15th) We won the 4 x100m Senior relay by default due to the non-appearance of other teams but the Club Record of 50.0 was equalled by Glenda Mahoney, Nikki King, Nana Nyarko and Jackie Barclay. Our 3 x 800 in 'Senior' squad of Brnda Davis, Suzanne Jordan and Shirley Daure was 2nd in 7 59.4. London Borough Champs. (September 5th) Veronica St Ange came 3rd in the javelin with 35.42. items.sum: Note on the women's and youth coaching arrangements, crediting Frank Simmons, Ted Warren and Mike Winch, and on the Battersea Park track resurfacing.
items.s: Coaching Scheme Note on the women's and youth coaching arrangements, crediting Frank Simmons, Ted Warren and Mike Winch, and on the Battersea Park track resurfacing. Coaching Scheme It may be that many people will consider that the re-appearance of Frank Simmons as Ladies Coach and the rapid increase in the fortune of our young ladies are two entirely unconnected events. Nothing could be further from the truth. Franks encouragement, determination to see that no one wastes their talents, and whole hearted devotion to our younger members is greatly appreciated by all concerned. Ted Warren has agreed to be added to our Coaching strength and although he has his own squad of promising youths he has agreed to take a special interest next year in the welfare of members at Norbiton track. This is one area where we will need to pay special attention and we hope that the former Surrey AC members will make a special effort to ensure that all our hopes and plans are turned into reality As far as Battersea Park track is concerned the new works will inhibit training until May of next year. As a result it is not planned to make a big splash with the local schools until we can take youngsters down to the re-surfaced track. It may be possible to continue with specialist field event training and we hope to retain the services of Junior International discus thrower Kevin Horne. As far as our top field events men are concerned we have been most grateful for the training which Mike Winch has provided at his Wimbledon Gymnasium.. items.label: October 1982
items.sum: Account, based on an interview with Bill Laws, of how the club secured G.L.C. agreement to an all-weather track and improved field facilities at Battersea Park.
items.s: ALL WEATHER TRACK AT BATTERSEA Account, based on an interview with Bill Laws, of how the club secured G.L.C. agreement to an all-weather track and improved field facilities at Battersea Park. ALL WEATHER TRACK AT BATTERSEA At last, it really is going to happen. Battersea Park is to have an all-weather track with improved jumping and throwing facilities. And the deadline is not years hence but right now. Indeed, if you pull out your copy of this issue of THE BELGRAVIAN over the Christmas holiday work will have already begun on digging up the running surface. . And so how has this happened so quickly? Well to find out and to put the course of events on record we interviewed our 'Special Projects Man' - Bill Laws - who single-handed has negotiated the deal with the G.L.C. Talk of developing Battersea Park track has been going on for at least the last 10 years. Hopes were high in 1974 when the London and South East Region of the Sports Council published its forward strategy for developing athletics in London. In that document 14 tracks were highlighted as being in need of special development and some of them would have greater importance as Regional Stadia with good spectator facilities. Battersea Park figured high in the list and we sat back and waited. Year by year developments occured, not at Battersea, but at Copthall, New River, West London, Southwark Park and so on. Year by year Belgrave officials visited the G.L.C. Parks Department to encourage progress and on occasions Parks Officials were guests at our Annual Dinner and Dance. And still nothing happened. It became clear that our big drawback was the G.L.C. itself. All the other tracks were owned by Local Authorities and many of them were prepared to put up substantial sums of money to develop athletics and enrich local community life. Not so with Wandsworth Council - they did not own the track and that was the end of it. It was up to the G.L.C. Desperate to see some progress Bill Laws was asked by the Belgrave Committee to see whether some way through could be found. Bill was keen to have a go because his pet scheme - The Masters Coaching Scheme - was not firing on all cylinders partly ,due to many of our better ahtletes not wishing to train on the famous 'pudding basin'. The boost of an all-weather surface was obvious. So Bill approached the permanent officers of the G.L.C. once again. After some delving it became clear that a master development plan involving the track did exist. This plan, if implemented, would have cost around £9 million and involved the construction of new football pitches, a multi-sport indoor centre, direct access to Chelsea Bridge Road and the re-siting of the track on an axis 60 degrees from the present one. When pressed for starting dates it was pointed out that total G.L.C. funding was impossible, external private money would be needed and that at the earliest 1987 would be the start date. Not content with this Bill prepared counter proposals based on upgrading the existing facility for a comparatively modest £350,000. The response from the Bureaucrates? Nothing. OK try again. This time the document was sent to the London and South East Region of the Sports Council. A good welcome from Anthony Walters. How could he help - with money? Great. Next to the Wandsworth Sports Council. Yes they would back it in principle but no money. The crucial breakthrough was to contact one of the influential and financially powerful elected Members Committees of the G.L.C. - The Arts and Recreation Committee - chaired by Tony Banks with Peter Pitt as Vice Chairman. Tony seemed to lead the Arts side with an annual ad-hoc budget of £4 million while Peter was busily trying to attract that sort of money in support of the Sports side. The time was the Brixton riots and suddenly the quality of inner city life was a political hot potato. Peter Pitt was looking for projects. Belgrave had a good one and what's more we had a good record of helping youngsters as a result of the Masters Coaching Scheme. It was agreed Bill would make a presentation and to further smooth the way he lobbied the two Wandsworth Councillors on the G.L.C. Arts and Recreation Committee. The plan was quickly approved in principle - it was now up to the full time officers to cost it out. Specifications and budget estimates were prepared. The Sports Council would give some financial help. It was all systems go. From this point on liaison with the G.L.C. became first class. Plans were received and circulated within Belgrave and many useful comments and requests made, many of which have been incorporated in the final scheme. By August 1982 the G.L.C. had written formally announcing its intention to proceed and in the same month we informed both the Southern and British Leagues in the hope we would get home fixtures in 1982. The only possible drawback would be if the quotes to the final specification which was issued in September 1982 exceeded the budget figure. It was with some relief we learned that by the closing date of mid-October at least 5 tenders had been received at prices below the final estimates. A big sigh of relief all round. Work is to start in mid-December 1982 and is to be completed by May 1983. And Bill's reactions? "I'm glad that's over. It does show what can be done in 1 year when everyone's focussed up. The G.L.C. and the sports Council can be proud of this one." So are we. Bill Laws Bill Laws 'Special Projects Man'; negotiated the Battersea track deal with the G.L.C. items.s: BOXING DAY MEETING - VENUE CHANGED Notice that the Boxing Day handicap events at Battersea Park are cancelled because of rebuilding and replaced by a fancy-dress handicap race on the Yacht '3' course on Monday 27th December. BOXING DAY MEETING - VENUE CHANGED FOOTNOTE : DUE TO PLANNED REBUILDING THE BOXING DAY HANDICAP EVENTS AT BATTERSEA PARK ARE CANCELLED. It is now intended to hold a handicap race around our famous Yacht '3' course on 'Boxing Day' the 27th December. Note the date - not Sunday 26th December but the Monday. It will give a chance for your Xmas Pud. to go down. Changing at Belgrave Hall from 10 a.m. Race to start 11 a.m. The Boxing Day '3' will however be somewhat unusual. Although it will be quite in order for anyone seeking a serious run to belt round as fast as he or she likes the main idea will be to compete in fancy dress or attire unusual for the Gentlemanly sport of foot racing. Prizes will be awarded to the most outrageous and innovative entries. If you happen to enter as an ostrich and run the fastest time of the day then you can expect something really special. Boxing Day Handicap Battersea Park Belgrave Hall

items.label: October 1982
items.sum: Short historical piece on the 1908 London Olympic Marathon: Dorando Pietri's disqualification, the origin of the 26 miles 385 yards distance and the refreshments offered.
items.s: THE 1908 MARATHON. Short historical piece on the 1908 London Olympic Marathon: Dorando Pietri's disqualification, the origin of the 26 miles 385 yards distance and the refreshments offered. THE 1908 MARATHON. The 1908 London Olympic Marathon is famous for the collapse of Italian Dorando Pietri. He did actually cross the line first but having been "helped" by the officials, who guided him as he staggered over the last metres, he was inevitably disqualified. However, that marathon also has other claims to fame. The race had been scheduled to be run over 40km (24 miles 1,504 yards) but the distance from the East Terrace of Windsor Castle to the White City Stadium proved to be 26 miles and a further 385 yards were required to reach the Royal Box. This was the distance finally adopted the world over - 42.195kms. The competitors themselves must have been the best fed and sweetest smelling marathoners of all time. At four points along the route runners were offered rice puddings, raisins, bananas, milk, soda, Oxo - and eau-de-Cologne. Dorando Pietri Dorando Pietri Italian; first across the line in the 1908 Olympic Marathon but disqualified Olympic Games London Windsor Castle White City Stadium

items.label: October 1982
items.sum: Track and Field Secretary Leo Coy's review of the club's best track season for years, which brought qualification for the British League, thanking captains, regulars, newcomers, stars and juniors.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track and Field Secretary Leo Coy's review of the club's best track season for years, which brought qualification for the British League, thanking captains, regulars, newcomers, stars and juniors. TRACK AND FIELD In trying to summarise the 1982 Track and Field season one would need this entire issue of The Belgravian. It proved to be our best season after a number of years in the doldrums. Why did this happen? It was not entirely unexpected as we had aimed to consolidate our southern league position this year and hoped to qualify for the British League in 1983, but we obviously got our predictions wrong! There were many reasons why the track and field side made such impressive progress and I shall deal with each in turn. Derek Williams and John Aska were elected Track and Field Captains respectively and they fulfilled these roles admirably. Derek gave top class performances every time he competed and John played a vital role in our success all season and especially at Luton, even though he did not always compete himself. A large number of athletes turned out time after time and gave a very solid base to all our teams. Among them were Mark Shippen - how good to see him increase his club PU record at the end of the season; Steve Samson; Mark L. Bayley - who commuted from Scotland to be at every League match, Pat Lyttle; Snowy - now back in the BL after 10 years; Terry Welsh - our remaining resident Irish Guard;Paul Whitby - who intends to commute from Scotland next season. Then there were the newcomers to Belgrave colours including Mike Alleyne - who could be our top sprinter in 1983; Roy Vassall a popular and talented triple sprinter; Ken Onuaguluchi - who must be a great prospect for International honours; Vincent Cornibert proved that he can beat the best at javelin throwing; Keith Smith who joined us from the Grenadiers and will add strength to our field team next year; plus of course all our new members from Surrey A.C. who contributed to our win at Luton. There were also other contributions from our super stars. John Gladwin, Ernest Obeng and Stu Paton who all recorded World Class performances and helped to keep the name of Belgrave in the oppositions minds. Our Junior members also played a major part. Paul Richley, Kevin Clarke, Dave North, Richard Addison, John Warren all gained vital points throughout the season. Thank you all very much . Your joint team manager Bill Laws and myself look forward to seeing you early next year. Your support made it all worthwhile. Finally, thanks to the officials who assisted throughout the year. Looking forward to next year - we will be fielding two teams, so we will need your continued support. We must be ready for the early track season and there is no reason why with the right preparation we can't progress further. We intend to make a huge impact in next year's Surrey Championships in April/May. items.s: MAY 1st 1982 - PORTSMOUTH. - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I Report and results of the Southern League Division I opener at Portsmouth on 1 May 1982, where Belgrave were third with ten individual winners. MAY 1st 1982 - PORTSMOUTH. - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I Our 1982 league campaign got off to a much better start than last year, but we were still not quite good enough to win. Fielding our strongest throws team for many years we demolished the opposition in the field and we were well backed up by the jumps squad. But oh dear! we came unstuck on the track - apart from excellent runs by Stu Paton, Paul Richley, Dave North,MLB and Kev.Clarke we were swamped in this traditionally strong section. A look at the following results will show we had ten individual winners. We also welcomed newcomers Keith Smith, Dave Armstrong, Roy Vassall, and Youth John Warren. John was thrown in at the deep end in the 1500 and gave a gutsy performance on a very windy day. Snowy made a welcome return and boosted our field team. We now have four big men capable of beating the best and it was good to see Field Captain John Aska keeping everybody on their toes. 100: 4.D.Armstrong 11.4; 5.P.Lyttle 12.0; 200: 4.D.Armstrong 23.1; 5.A.Nwosu 24.7; 400: 4.D.Williams 53.0; 4.R.Vassall 55.7; 800: 1.S.Paton 1.58.4; 5.M.Waller 2.09.9; 1500: 5.J.Warren 4.22.5; 5.M.Waller 4.33.4; 5000: 3.P.Richley 15.19.7; 2.D.North 15.47.8; 3000 S/C: 5.L.Lyons 10.15.0; 5.M.Manning 10.50.0: 110 H: 1.M.L.Bayley 15.8; 4.K.Clarke 17.3; 400 H: 2.M.L.Bayley 58.7; 3.K.Clarke 64.3; PV: 1.M.Shippen 3.00; 1.S.Samson 2.40; HJ: 1.S.Samson 1.85; 1.M.L.Bayley 1.76; LJ: 1.D.Williams 7.19; 4.M.L.Bayley 5.95; TJ: 5.R.Vassall 12.31; 3.D.Williams 12.08; HT: 2.K.Smith 39.86; 1.T.Welsh 36.50; DT: 3.C.Brooks 35.70; 1.K.Smith 33.98; SP: 3.C.Brooks 12.22; 2.J.Aska 11.67; JT: 2.J.Aska 49.58; 1.C.Brooks 48.00; 4x100: 3.(R.Vassall, K.Clarke; D.Armstrong, D.Williams) 46.4. 4x400: 3.(K.Clarke, D.Williams, R. items.s: MAY 5th 1982 - BATTERSEA PARK - CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and results of the club 10,000m and 400m championships at Battersea Park on 5 May 1982, won at 10,000m by Leo Lyons. MAY 5th 1982 - BATTERSEA PARK - CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Leo Lyons won his first track championship beating Laurie and Tony Binda in an intriguing race. Leo took the lead from the start and proceeded to run the opposition into the ground. Laurie and Tony battled for second place with our most famous veteran running away over the final lap. Surprise run of the night came from Mike Nouch who stayed with the first three for the first half, but then blew out. The low turn-out can be attributed in some way to the London Marathon on the following Sunday. 10,000m: 1.L.Lyons 33.10; 2.L.O'Hara 33.23; 3.A.Binda 33.35; 4. items.h: BELGRAVE WINS — MAY 22nd 1982 - NORBITON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I
items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's Southern League Division I win at Norbiton on 22 May 1982.
items.s: BELGRAVE WINS — MAY 22nd 1982 - NORBITON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I Report and results of Belgrave's Southern League Division I win at Norbiton on 22 May 1982. BELGRAVE WINS MAY 22nd 1982 - NORBITON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I To remain in contention at the top of the league table, this was a match that we had to win - and win we did. Recording less wins than in our first match, we were this time backed up a much stronger track team. Our two hurdlers were a class apart and got us away to a great start. Other winners included Stu Paton (800), Steve Samson (PV) Terry Welsh (HT), Snowy (JT). John Aska did his usual great work organising the field side and surprised himself and everybody else, with his largest javelin throw for some time of 53.84. JUNE 5th 1982 - WINDSOR - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I. In this match we met Windsor who were unbeaten in the league for eight matches. At the end of a long and very hot day they were still unbeaten - proving too strong for us on the day. Thanks to a second dress rehearsal for Trooping the Colour, we could not call on any of our guards and with Snowy also unavailable we were very weak in the throws. The one exception was Vincent Cornibert making his first appearance for the club and launching the Javelin 58.24 metres. What a tremendous prospect for the future as he has just turned Senior. Other good performances were recorded by J.Gladwin 400, 49.3 (PB), S.Paton and M.Sinclair 800; MLB and Kevin both recorded p.b's in the 400 H. MLB set a new club record in the 110 H of 15.3; S.Samson PV; D.Williams and Roy Vassall TJ. and both relay teams One final word about the other team - the Belgrave Supporters who cheered everything in claret and gold whilst consuming vast quantities of roast chicken, washed down by numerous bottles of wine. items.s: JULY 3rd 1982 - NORWICH - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I. Report and results of the Southern League Division I match at Norwich on 3 July 1982, where Belgrave were second to Norwich and moved up to fifth in the league. JULY 3rd 1982 - NORWICH - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I. At the half-way stage in the league we were lying in 6th place with 12 points. In this match one of our opponents, Hounslow, were in 4th place, so it was essential that we beat them. Well we did manage to beat a very weak Hounslow, but found ourselves pipped by the Home Team. Our Hurdlers again proved invincible winning A & B races. Roy Vassall headed Derek in the Triple at one stage, but was eventually shaded by 4 cm. in taking the B String. How good to see these two picking up almost maximum points in what has been our weak event for many years. The other stars on the day were Mark in the P.V. Derek 400, LJ; Snowy SP and the announcer's nightmare! Making his first appearance for Bels. Ken Onuaguluchi. Another outstanding talent for the future and still not twenty, Ken won the Discus and was second in the Shot. He can also throw the Javelin but is not too keen on the Hammer! Welcome Ken. After this match we moved up to 5th in the league our best position for a number of years, and well done to all 17 who travelled and were stretched to give us the points. JULY 11th 1982 - SOUTHWARK PARK - GRE CUP - SECOND ROUND Because of the efforts of the nine competitors at Deansgate, we were awarded with a match on Tartan against British League clubs Brighton and HHH. In the event we fielded a team that was brilliant in parts and not so good in others. Thus was our first year back in this competition after opting out for a number of years. We proved that we can match the very best by finishing close behind HHH and Brighton with a slightly stronger team we could have qualified for the semi-finals. Good performances were recorded by K.Onuaguluchi in the Discus, Javelin and Shot; Derek, Long and Triple; John Bicourt S/C and John Gladwin. items.s: BELGRAVE WINS AGAIN — JULY 17th 1982 - NEW RIVER - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I Report and results of the Southern League Division I match at New River on 17 July 1982, which Belgrave won with what is called the best ever performance by a Belgrave track and field team, helped by members from the Irish Guards. BELGRAVE WINS AGAIN JULY 17th 1982 - NEW RIVER - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I This was the crunch match of the season. In the league old Gayts. were 2nd, North London were 3rd and we were 5th. In the week prior to the match our members from the Irish Guards returned from Germany and added strength to our team. They turned up from Windsor, on the day, in an army lorry and it was great to see them all again. We held the opposition well on the track, but in the field events hurdles and relays we out-classed them. Of the 22 separate competitions in these three categories we recorded 14 wins, 6 seconds and 2 thirds. Remarkable scoring. It would be unfair to single out individual performances, every one was a hero and contributed to the best ever performance by a Belgrave track and field team. Congratulations to everybody with special thanks to Pat Roberts and the Irish Guards. There is no truth in the rumour that the Irish Guards now have more Belgrave vests than Douglas Sports. 100: A - 3.D.Hemphill 11.2*; B - 3.P.Lyttle 11.5; 200: A - 5. items.h: AUGUST 7th 1982 - WEST LONDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I
items.sum: Report and results of the final Southern League Division I match at West London on 7 August 1982, where Belgrave were second to Hillingdon and finished fourth in the league.
items.s: AUGUST 7th 1982 - WEST LONDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I Report and results of the final Southern League Division I match at West London on 7 August 1982, where Belgrave were second to Hillingdon and finished fourth in the league. AUGUST 7th 1982 - WEST LONDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION I Following our great result at New River, we were lying fourth in the league table behind our opponents in this match Hillingdon. To reach third place we would have to beat them. The winners being assured of a place in the British league qualifying match. In the event we were beaten into second place by Hillingdon. There were only two clubs in the match and by winning 23 of the 36 events Hillingdon proved uncatchable. Our performances were very good in general. Our 5000 team of North and newcomer Karmy-Jones produced our best league times of the year with two outstanding runs. Derek Williams was at his brilliant best as were Ken, Snowy, Vincent, Mark and sprinters Pat Lyttle and Mike Alleyne. Benny did his usual trick in the B 800 of being last with 200 to go. This time he just failed to win. TVH kindly opened their Club House and a large number of Bels adjourned to ponder on what might have been. Our final league position was fourth and it appeared as though we'd blown it. 100: A - 3.M.Alleyne 11.4; B - 3.P.Lyttle 11.6; 200: A - 1.M.Alleyne 22.7; B - 2.P.Lyttle 400: A - 1.D.Williams 50.2*; B - 2.R.Addison 52.3; 800: A - 5.P.Richley 1.59.4; B - 2.A.Benn 2.00.3; 1500: A - 2.M.Sinclair 3.58.7; B - 1.A.Hughes 4.04.0; 5000: A 2.D.North 15.08.3*; B - 2.R.Karmy-Jones 15.11.0*; 3000 S/C: A - 3.L.Coy 10.05.3; B -; 400 H: A - 3.M.L.Bayley 57.3; B - 3.K.Clarke 59.3; 110 H: A 1.M.L.Bayley 15.8; B - 3.C.Brooks 17.1; LJ: A - 1.D.Williams 6.84; B - 4.R.Hopkins 5.98; TJ: A - 1. items.sum: Report and results of the British League qualifying match at Luton on 4 September 1982, which Belgrave won, with Stu Paton the star and the 4x100 relay equalling the British League record.
items.s: Belgrave First — SEPTEMBER 4th 1982 - LUTON - BRITISH LEAGUE QUALIFYING MATCH Report and results of the British League qualifying match at Luton on 4 September 1982, which Belgrave won, with Stu Paton the star and the 4x100 relay equalling the British League record. Belgrave First SEPTEMBER 4th 1982 - LUTON - BRITISH LEAGUE QUALIFYING MATCH Following our last Southern League match at West London, Leo Coy submitted the best A & B string performances to the British League in the faint hope that we might be invited to the qualifying match for British League Division Five. The invitation finally came 10 days before the match and resulted in many 'phone calls far and wide to re-assemble our team. In the meantime the absorbtion of Surrey A.C. Mens members took place which made their athletes eligible to compete. The venue was Luton, the weather was ideal, our team was the best ever fielded by Belgrave and the result was sensational. We demolished the opposition with some out-standing performances from Ernest Obeng, Colin Gaynor and Derek Williams but the star of the meeting was Stu Paton with wins over International competition in the 800, 1500 and a superb run of 48.0 in the 400 Relay. The 100 Relay team equalled the qualifying match record. Our supporters were in fine voice and at one stage even cheered when the lane draw was announced. This was a great day for the club and puts us back where we should be - that is where we were when the British League first began. 100: A - 1.E.Obeng 10.8; B - 1.C.Ga[illegible]nor 10.7; 200: A - 1.E.Obeng 21.7; B - 1.C.Gaynor 21.5; 400: A - 3.D.Mote 49.0; B - 5.D.Williams 51.3; 800: A - 1.S.Paton 1.53.4; B - 4.S. items.sum: Report of John Gladwin's fifth place in 1 46.46 at an Oslo invitation meeting on 7 July 1982, beating his own club 800m record by over two seconds.
items.s: NEW CLUB 800M RECORD — JULY 7th 1982 - OSLO - INVITATION MEETING. Report of John Gladwin's fifth place in 1 46.46 at an Oslo invitation meeting on 7 July 1982, beating his own club 800m record by over two seconds. NEW CLUB 800M RECORD JULY 7th 1982 - OSLO - INVITATION MEETING. A strawberry party and a bad nights sleep on a sofa were John Gladwin's preparation for his first International race in senior company. And what a night to remember on the superfast track at Oslo.- An 800 metres with some of the world's current top performers - John had hoped to be towed round to a personal best and so he was, passing through the 400 m in an incredible 51.0 and finishing 5th in 1 46.46 to knock over 2 seconds off the club record which he had set in 1980. And behind were some well established Internationals. In the National Press the headlines were for Dave Moorcroft's 5000m world record but for Belgravians the highlight was John's fine run. John Gladwin John Gladwin 5th in Oslo 800m in 1 46.46, new club record (previous record his own, set 1980) John Gladwin John Dave Moorcroft Dave Moorcroft 5000m world record at the same meeting Oslo invitation meeting Oslo

items.s: NEW CLUB 1500M RECORD — AUGUST 1st 1982 - CWMBRAN - AAA's UNDER 20 CHAMPIONSHIPS. Report of Stuart Paton winning the AAA under-20 1500m at Cwmbran in 3 43.06, a new club record beating John Thresher's 1968 time. NEW CLUB 1500M RECORD AUGUST 1st 1982 - CWMBRAN - AAA's UNDER 20 CHAMPIONSHIPS. Stuart Paton with two fast 800m's behind him travelled hopefully to Cwmbran while John Gladwin's series of races took their toll and he decided to give the under 20's Champ.s a miss.Stuart must have been delighted to set yet another p.b. in Saturday's heats recording 3 48.81,but who would have expected a further massive reduction in the final. Sitting in on a fast pace and never far off the lead our 19 year old Anglo-Scot used his now famous finishing burst to win in 3 43.06. This time not only set a new club record erasing John Thresher's time of 3 44.6 which was set in 1968 but headed the U.K.'s junior rankings. items.s: NEW CLUB 1500M RECORD — AUGUST 29th 1982 - AMSTERDAM - UNDER 25 INTERNATIONAL. Report of Stuart Paton winning the 1500m for Great Britain in an under-25 international in Amsterdam in 3 42.86, again improving his club record. NEW CLUB 1500M RECORD AUGUST 29th 1982 - AMSTERDAM - UNDER 25 INTERNATIONAL. Stuart Paton's fine win in the AAA's Under 20 Champ's was rewarded with a G.B. vest against under 25 teams from Belgium,Greece,and Holland as well as a full strengh team from Isreal. Stuart,now confident with his finishing kick,sat behind the leaders and jumped the field with 120m to go to win by a clear 1.6 sec.s from G.B. team mate Potter. Stu's time of 3 42.86 further reduced his Belgrave 1500m record to firmly place him in the selector's eyes. It is interesting to note that this year Stuart has raced a carefully planned schedule set by his coach, Mick Dunphy, as long as last winter. SEPTEMBER 17th 1982 - CRYSTAL PALACE - COCA COLA MEETING Ernie Obeng,Colin Gaynor and Stu. Paton were our representatives at the Coca Cola meeting. Ernie had to be content with 3rd. place behind Lattany and McFarlane, clocking 10.51 in the process. Ex-Surrey man Colin Gaynor was 5th in 10.65. What a great sight if they had both been wearing Club vests! Stu Paton had been hoping to break the Club 1 mile record in this last major meeting of the home season but the organisors thought better and swapped him to the 1000m where he ran a very fast 2 21.41 to finish 6th. Gary Staines -another talented Junior who trains from Belgrave Hall on a Sunday finished in 2 22.69. items.sum: Report on Ernie Obeng at the Commonwealth Games 100m and in later races against Wells in Australia, and Paul Blagg's 13th place in the Games 30km road walk.
items.s: OBENG AND BLAGG DOWN UNDER Report on Ernie Obeng at the Commonwealth Games 100m and in later races against Wells in Australia, and Paul Blagg's 13th place in the Games 30km road walk. OBENG AND BLAGG DOWN UNDER Ernie Obeng found his shortage of races this summer (due to injury) had affected his performances and he just failed to make the final of the Commonwealth Games 100m having recorded 10.27 in the quarter finals. Wells' win is now history but after the Games Ernie stayed on in Australia and on 13th October in Melbourne beat Wells recording 10.54 to 10.63. Four days later Wells reversed the result beating Ernie into second place. Our other representative in Brisbane Paul Blagg finished 13th in the 30 kilometres road walk in an excellent time of 2 30.42. items.s: Blackheath 25 x 1 mile relay — JUNE 13th 1982 - CRYSTAL PALACE - 25 x 1 MILE RELAY Report and leg times of Belgrave's four teams in the Blackheath 25 x 1 mile relay on 13 June 1982, where the A team was third of 50 and the first four juniors set a UK junior 4 x 1 mile record. Blackheath H[illegible] 25 x 1mile JUNE 13th 1982 - CRYSTAL PALACE - 25 x 1 MILE RELAY After the traumas of recent years resulting from the difficulty in getting out 100 of our better distance athletes yours truly had announced that he would step down from team managership this year. However, Blackheath decided to reduce the relay to 25 stages and so management was shared - with Bill Laws sorting out the A team, Ian Horton an under 16 team John Wasbrough a vets team and Bill Couzens with Brian Pritchard looking after a B team. As usual certain people didn't turn up and so some ran in several of the teams. NIKE who had taken over sponsership were offering some super prizes for all members of the first 3 teams and so there was some interest in the performance of our 'A' team and didn't they do well. Our 1st 4 juniors set a new U.K 4x1 mile record of 17 23.2 compared to the previous best of 17 48.5. In the process Stu Paton ran the fasteat leg of the day and so won an extra pair of Nike spikes. Of the 50 teams that finished at several venues around the Country our 'A' team finished an excellent 3rd. As every run deserved comment it is best to let the results speak for thelmselves - but perhaps just one mention. What a great run from 10 year old Adrian Ross who had been training with the Batttersea squad and recorded 5 56 !! Unfortunately the times for the first 10 legs were mislaid FINAL POSITIONS. 1. items.label: October 1982
items.sum: Review of the 1982 season for Belgrave's colts, boys and youths, noting new club records by Sean Richards, Simon Beaumont and Paul Richley and the progress of John Warren.
items.s: YOUTHS AND BOYS Review of the 1982 season for Belgrave's colts, boys and youths, noting new club records by Sean Richards, Simon Beaumont and Paul Richley and the progress of John Warren. YOUTHS AND BOYS As the results for our maturing Juniors have been reported in the main Track and Field Section the following relates to the achievements of the colts boys and youths. Ian Horton was unable to devote a great amount of time to the youngsters in the summer and this combined with the fact that we have been unsuccessful in attempts to get into any of the Young Athletes Leagues has meant that all of our colts, boys and youths have had to find competition elsewhere. Fortunately School and Area Championships have provided some chance for good competition and some first class performances have been achieved and several Club records broken. Two 14 year old's set new rec.s Sean Richards lowered the 400m time to 52.6 while Simon Beaumont claimed the 1500m record with 4.34 Our outstanding youth was John Warren who competed at every opportunity and turned out in Southern League senior races whenever asked. Father Ted. has been a tower of strength and runs a sizeable training squad of promising youngsters. The Warren family has shown great support for all things Belgrave and are an asset. Close behind John are Andy North and Mike Blackmore who have not competed as much as they would like due to 'O' level exams but still ran good times. But over the country they come into their own and already there's signs that John's superiority will be tested during the winter. And finally mention of Paul Richley's new Junior record of 8.33.7. The quality of this may be judged by reference to previous holders which have included ;Peter Carton,John Stow.Dave North, and Stu Paton!!! items.sum: Note on Sean Richards and Richard Allison winning schools 400m titles and being selected, with Paul Richley, for the English Schools.
items.s: OUTSTANDING PERFORMANCES Note on Sean Richards and Richard Allison winning schools 400m titles and being selected, with Paul Richley, for the English Schools. Saturday 12th June was the day of the Schools T and F County Championships and 2 of our younger members produced some outstanding performances to win gold. In the GLC's 14 year old Sean Richards won the junior boys 400m in an outstanding 52.6 secs while at Motspur Park 15 year old Richard Allison won the Surrey Schools 400m again with a personal best - a brilliant 51.6. As a result both youngsters were selected for the English Schools and were joined by Paul Richley who was selected as a Surrey 5000m representative following his fine run in our Southern league match at Portsmouth. items.s: JOHN WARRENS PROGRESS Note on John Warren's 1982 season: London Youth Games 1500m bronze, personal bests at 1500m and 800m and a new club youth 3000m record. The highlight of John Warren's season was winning the bronze in the London Youth Games 1500m held on Aug.1st. His time of 4 12.0 was however not his fastest for during the season he reduced his 1500m p.b. to 4 10.6. He also reduced his 800m time to 2 01.1. Add to this a new Club Youth 3000m record of 8 58.2 and we imagine John will feel well pleased with his progress. items.s: TORRID RUN Note on John Bicourt's fifth place in the Manitoba Marathon in Canada and 31st place in the Berlin Marathon in 1982. John Bicourt visited John Thresher in Canada and ran the Manitoba Marathon on 23rd June in 100% humidity. He recorded an excellent 2 24.48 in 5th place. John Bicourt again ran the Berlin Marathon this year which was held in excellent conditions on September 26th. Unfortunately, John could not match last year's form and finished in 31st position in 2 35.42. items.s: VETS. CORNER Veterans' notes: Laurie O'Hara's UK over-50 5000m record, Charlie Walker's 1500m win at the Southern Vets Championships, and Pamela Davis joining first claim. VETS. CORNER Laurie O'Hara who turned 50 on June 18th set a U.K. O/50 5000m record in the Southern Vets Championships held at Parliament Hill on June 27th when he ran 15 58.2. Laurie still holds the 45/49 Age best of 15 05.8 for 5000m which has not been beaten since he set it in 1978. Laurie didn't contest the 1500m and Belgrave was well represented by Charlie Walker who surprised everyone by jumping the field with one lap to go and although the pack swooped down the home straight Charlie just managed to hold on to win in 4 42.6. Pamela Davis has joined us first claim following the demise of Selsonia. Despite being a veteran now Pam continues to astound us with her long distance running. In the Belgrave 20 on July 17th Pam was the 3rd lady home in 2 hr.31.30. In the WAAA's Marathon held at Windsor on the 12th June Pam finished 19th in 3 hr.17.21. items.s: LETTERS Letter from Trevor Hart to the editor on the All Time Top Ten, lamenting today's apathy compared with the old team spirit and asking for a marathon top ten. LETTERS Dear Bill, Well done with edition 204 of the Belgravian, I was particularly interested in the Belgrave All Time Top Ten and noted that a high percentage was put up in the "old days". I find it a bit disturbing with regards the number of times that the words apathy and miserable approach appears and that the 36 year old John Bicourt is rated the best over the country. One of the reasons the old ones put up good times was due to team spirit, we would turn out in force, team competition was high and this improved the performance of both the stars and the scrubbers in their chosen events also the reason why the Belgrave team was feared. However, I do notice some bright hope with the juniors so that with the wish that the Belgrave teams will be feared again. All the best, Trevor Hart. P.S. How about a marathon top ten ?. Trevor Hart Trevor Hart Bill Bill the editor (Bill Laws) John Bicourt John Bicourt aged 36

items.label: October 1982
items.sum: Letter from Clive Shippen reporting on a visit to former walker and Belgravian editor Ben Knifton in Portugal, and on the American walking career of John Knifton.
items.s: Letter from Clive Shippen reporting on a visit to former walker and Belgravian editor Ben Knifton in Portugal, and on the American walking career of John Knifton. Dear Bill, For Belgravian purposes I thought you might like to know that I called on Ben Knifton while I was holidaying at Albufeira, Portugal. Ben retired to the Algarve with his second wife, Peggy, about 12 years ago and they have an apartment at the highest point overlooking the sea. Now 74 years old he is as fit and active as ever - swimming three or four times a week for all but two months of the year. He also travels quite a bit and a few days after my visit was due to bus it down to Algecires and hop across the Med for a 9 days spell in Morocco! Ben, of course, was very active in the Bels walking section and frequently second in our championship winning teams. He was also the second editor of The Belgravian, serving his stint between 1927 and 1929. Seeing Ben also brought me up to date on the other Knifton, John. "Young" John is now 42 years old and still living in Texas where he emigrated back in the mid-sixties after gaining a degree in Chemistry. He since obtained a Ph.D and is now Deputy Director of Research for Texaco and travels worldwide speaking at international symposia. Following several such visits to Europe he was recently elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry. He has a teenage son - a big strapping fellow who is a fine swimmer and footballer (American rules) - and a daughter. John will be remembered in Belgrave for his outstanding performances as a Junior and as a National title-holder. We did not see him at his best as a Senior, but the Americans did. Between 1970 and 1980 he won no less than 13 National walking titles between 3 km (track) and 50 km. He was also desparately unlucky to miss the U.S. Olympic team in 1976 when he suffered badly from the heat in the trial - a rare bad performance. Now a veteran, John is as active as ever and, apart from competing in open walking events, still with some success, he has also turned to running daily. He recently ran 4 marathons in 4 weeks clocking 3.03, 2.57, 2.55 and 2.53, having already tried his hand at the fast stuff with 34.00 for a track 10 km! Ben and John send their best wishes to all Belgravians and follow their progress with great interest. Sincerely, Clive Shippen. Clive Shippen Clive Shippen Ben Knifton Ben Knifton walker; second editor of The Belgravian 1927-1929; aged 74, retired to the Algarve Peggy Peggy Ben Knifton's second wife John Knifton John walker; emigrated to Texas mid-1960s; 13 US national walking titles 1970-80; Deputy Director of Research, Texaco John "Young" John Bill Bill the editor (Bill Laws) US Olympic Trials Albufeira Portugal Algarve Algecires Morocco Texas

items.sum: Social-section note that Sunday training numbers at Belgrave Hall are emptying the roof water tank, which a new tank will fix once the Hall development goes ahead.
items.s: SOCIAL — BELGRAVE HALL RUNS DRY ! Social-section note that Sunday training numbers at Belgrave Hall are emptying the roof water tank, which a new tank will fix once the Hall development goes ahead. SOCIAL BELGRAVE HALL RUNS DRY ! No, not a case of the bar running dry but almost as bad. Over the last few weeks there has been a substantial increase in the number of people training from the Hall on a Sunday morning. Packs of up to 40 seniors is not an unusual sight. Add to this the fast Junior pack and over 20 of our very young members and it will be appreciated that in the space of over 1 hour around 100 people can descend into the showers. Of course the most enjoyable part of a winter's run is the time in the showers which is generally spent on catching up with the latest gossip! Well that's all very well but of late there has been a great deal of important matters to discuss and the net result is that our fuel bills have gone up and even more importantly the roof water tank which supplies the whole boiler system sometimes runs dry. When this happens beware!! Bill Couzens-our Hall impresario- may be seen running around in ever decreasing circles uttering strange sounds known only to those who have experienced the traumas of trying to organise anything at Belgrave. What are the possible solutions? Well we could gag Brian Gorman. We could issue smaller bits of soap but the only suitable solution will be to install a new 3000 gallon tank in the roof. This is a major undertaking bearing in mind the weight involved and it will only be possible when we start work on the development of the Hall. And when is that likely to be? Well, hopefully next year. We understand that as a result of the improvement in our finances the BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT FUND now stands at over £10,000. Bill Couzens Bill Couzens Belgrave Hall impresario Brian Gorman Brian Gorman Belgrave Hall

items.label: October 1982
items.sum: Notice of the Jaguars' members-only farewell performance at Belgrave Hall on 22 January, with tickets limited to 150.
items.s: FAREWELL SOCIAL Notice of the Jaguars' members-only farewell performance at Belgrave Hall on 22 January, with tickets limited to 150. There have been many requests and enquiries for another Social at Belgrave Hall. It is now more than 6 months since the last Disco and as many of you will be aware that ended in a most unpleasant fashion due to a group of unruly youngsters who gatecrashed and then started trouble which required the Police to be called. Since then all our functions have been restricted to Club members and have mainly taken the form of small,intimate and enjoyable Soirees with food and wine which have proved particularly effective in attracting family groups. Of course many years ago we had Open Socials without problems. Top of our charts was one particular Group - The JAGUARS - who have played to packed houses at the Hall on 14 seperate occasions. Sadly, The Jaguars are now to break up and the various members will depart to the four corners of the world. Their FAREWELL PERFORMANCE will be at BELGRAVE HALL on JANUARY 22nd and entry will be by ticket only. The sale of tickets will be to members only and there will be a minimum age limit. To ensure that there will not be overcrowding the number of tickets will be limited to.150. Already over half the tickets have been sold so if you want a really great Club night out BOOK NOW ! Belgrave Hall

items.s: THE ONE LAP MONEY TARGET / BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT FUND. Belgrave Hall Development Fund appeal with a running-track diagram showing the fund at £10,000 towards a £20,000 target, and news of fundraising at the 25 x 1 mile relay and London Marathon. THE ONE LAP MONEY TARGET BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT FUND. There has been a substantial increase in the monies allocated to the BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT FUND since our last edition. In addition individuals and groups have made special attempts to raise money. For some reason however our plea for direct contributions to the FUND have not received much support. We believed it not too much to ask for a once and for all single payment from all who use Belgrave Hall and from our members who can no longer get there frequently. So if you have been meaning to write to Jim Heathfield at [address withheld] please do so now and give generously !!!!!! Our attempts to raise funds at the time of the Nike-Blackheath 25x1 Mile were reasonably successful. Top scorer was Gerry Sexton who has made a welcome return to racing this summer and may well be aiming to make our Junior teams this winter. Also very successful were Ross Martin, and the Richleys.(It's always the same people isn't it).Sponsership from the London Marathon also went very well with Bill Couzens raising over £300 and Paul Roche raising over £150. Well done too to the boys & colts who raised over £100. items.sum: Stop press reports on the ladies' winning first Southern League Division 3 match, the men's British League Division 5 win at Warley, and the men's Southern League team finishing equal last at Brighton.
items.s: STOP PRESS Stop press reports on the ladies' winning first Southern League Division 3 match, the men's British League Division 5 win at Warley, and the men's Southern League team finishing equal last at Brighton. STOP PRESS EARLY SEASON SUCCESSES. Our ladies got the Track and Field season off to an early and successful start when on April 16th they travelled to Withdean Stadium Brighton for their first Southern League Div.3 Match and came away with a sufficiently clear win to end the day top of the Div. ahead of Herne Hill. Everyone was a star but pride of place must go to Jackie Harman who gained the sprint double by a huge margin. This was Jackie's first League appearance for us and she could be a big factor in our promation chances. Our men were quick to follow the example of the ladies when on the 7th May our top team journeyed up the M1,M6 and M5 to Warley to take on the two teams promoted with us to Div.5 of the British League plus established British League competition. There were a few nerve racking moments as the coach rounded up members from various parts of London but eventually all arrived safely to post a series of excellent performances which left the opposition way behind. One of the intrigueing features of the British League is that we shall be meeting the same opposition 3 more times and if we finish in the first two places then we move up to Div. 4. No doubt the opposition will be working out ways of pulling back points but we still have a few cards up our sleeves - so please whatever you do,put the 3 remaining British League Matches well up your list of priorities. And the result of the first match? 1.BELGRAVE 301; 2.Windsor S&E 291; 3.Cannock Chase 248; 4.Bristol 247; 5.Hillingdon AC 219; 6.Met.Police 172; 7.Stretford 168; BUT MEN'S SOUTHERN LEAGUE TEAM DISAPPOINTS. Meanwhile on the 23rd April the men's Southern League team travelled also to Withdean Stadium at Brighton and it soon became clear that a shortage of Field events men would hamper our chances of a good result. In fact if it had not been for Reg Hopkins Jnr. and John Aska the final points total would have been even worse. There were some bright spots however. John Gladwin (eligible having missed our British League qualifying match last September) ran a lone 800m to record a fine early season 1;50.1,while first year Junior John Warren took 6 secs off his 1500m p.b. to clock 4:03. Despite such redoubtable efforts we finished equal last in a fairly close scoring match and there will need to be greater support if we are to achieve our objective of avoiding relagation. 1.Dartford 117½; 2. Sutton & Cheam 115; 3. Brighton & Hove 110½; 4 Equal. items.s: BELGRAVE MOVES UP THE RANKINGS. Note that Belgrave rose from 35th to 21st in the NUTS club track and field rankings for 1982. BELGRAVE MOVES UP THE RANKINGS. The Annual NUTS Club Track and Field Rankings for 1982 have been published recently and they reflect the improvements which resulted in last year's promotion to the British League. Topping the rankings with 19577 Pts was Wolverhampton & Bilston while Belgrave moved from its 1981 position of 35th. to a lofty 21st with 17032 Pts in 1982. This ranking puts us ahead of some well regarded 4th Division British League Clubs and not all that far behind some Division 2 Clubs. For example, Epsom & Ewell who were rated 17th with 17401 Pts and Aldershot F & D. who ranked 13th with 17560 Pts. As we have entered 1983 with a string of p.b's and a senior Club record in the Pole Vault we can look forward to something even better in next year's listings. items.label: April 1983
items.sum: Editorial explaining that the wider-page format has not cut the magazine below 44 pages as club activity grows, and arguing the club must review how it manages its affairs.
items.s: Catch 22 Editorial explaining that the wider-page format has not cut the magazine below 44 pages as club activity grows, and arguing the club must review how it manages its affairs. Catch 22 The introduction of the wider page 'Belgravian' was made with the hope of reducing pages and hence printing costs. By some strange coincidence the change in format occurred at a time when our whole range of activities expanded and try as I might I cannot provide an interesting and factual account of your activities in less than 44 pages. There was a time when your Hon. Editor could look forward to some kind of respite in the winter but what with the increasing interest of members in indoor competition as well as the despatch of teams onto the Continent no longer can the winter season be regarded as our quiet period. So what ? Well there is no doubt that the whole scope of our Club's work has increased and what with the new all weather Track at Battersea as well the planned improvements at Belgrave Hall things are likely to get even more demanding than hitherto. The time is not far away when we will have to review the way we manage our affairs. Anyone who has attended recent Committee meetings at which representatives of all Sections, Sub Committees , Working Parties and so on discuss and control the affairs of the Club will realise that decission making is becoming more and more drawn out as the numbers attending increase. Add to this the fact that as our membership increases so our turnover moves into the small business bracket and you will see that some thought should be given to these matters in the not too distant future. The problem is - who's got the time to sit back and produce a master plan for the future ? CATCH 22!! Battersea Belgrave Hall
