items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: the Dormans' marriage, Oliver Foote's relay form, John Bicourt's film career, ex-Surrey AC members Jimmy Green, Walter Batson and George Williams, athletes taking time off to train, Bill Downey's illness and a walking section award. grapevine Belated congratulations to Richard and Sonia Dorman on their marriage last June. Richard, who now lives in Nottingham, has made a welcome return to racing and is already well on the way to regaining his top form. Oliver Foote went into hospital at the beginning of March to have his wisdom teeth removed. Four weeks later he was our fastest long leg runner in the Haig-Belgrave relay and by a big margin! We wonder if this technique for shedding weight will catch on. While on the subject of improving racing performances it has not gone unnoticed that John Bicourt has started shaving his legs! We can report that this new development has something to do with John's new career in films and TV. Intrigued? Watch this space! Among ex-Surrey AC members receiving the last copy of the 'Belgravian' was P.W.(Jimmy) Green. No stranger to us for he competed in Belgrave colours during World War 2. Jimmy of course needs no introduction as the man who started Athletics Weekly' after the war. Jimmy is now in his 70's but still trains local athletes. Walter Batson, competitor in the first Barking to Southend Police walk, another former Surrey AC man and now a member of Belgrave is back on the road again after illness. George Williams, a wonderful stylist, former Belgrave walker and International was recently seen in Bournemouth and sent his regards to all his 60's compratriats; Messrs Middleton, Vickers, Hall, etc.., To reach the very top in todays athletics requires not only talent but complete dedication. Both John Gladwin and Stuart Paton have shown their commitment by changing occupations to give themselves more time for training. Mark Sinclair has gone one step further and, following a house move to Dorking is taking a 6 month sabatical to concentrate on his running. We wish all our dedicated young men the very best of good fortune in their endeavours. Another member reaching for the top but in a somewhat different context is Don Anderson. Don has taken 6 weeks leave from his teaching post to undertake a training holiday in Kenya - At an altitude of 12000 Ft. We knew Don was determined to make our Southern League team! Many of our regulars at Belgrave Hall have been asking after Bill Downey. Sadly soon after last years 25 by 1 mile relay Bill contracted a hepatic condition and has only recently resumed training. We wish him a speedy recovery. Following their widespread successes in this years County Champs our Walking Section was presented by the Surrey & South London Newspapers Group wit[illegible] the Victor City Outstanding Sports Achievement Award for February. NOTICES General secretary's notices: an extra Thameside League date on 10 August 1983, a call for officials for the Inter-Counties 20 at the Belgrave 20 on 16 July, and for helpers at the Rank Xerox Marathon finish on 5 June. HON. SECS. NOTICES You will have seen elsewhere in this issue details of the new Thameside League which Belgrave has established at Battersea Park. Unfortunately the fixture card omitted one of the fixture dates so will all officials as well as boys and colts please note the extra date :---SAT. AUGUST 10TH 1983. The Belgrave 20 on 16th July will be the venue for the Inter-Counties 20. In order to ensure that everything goes smoothly may I ask for the maximum support from all officials. Please ring me on [phone number withheld] to offer assistance. While on the subject of officials; We have been asked to provide help to man the finish of the RANK XEROX Marathon which is to be held on the 5th June. A field of around 800 is expected and the finish will be at Richmond Green.The Club is to receive a donation towards our building fund so once again I would ask you to make a special effort to help out. items.s: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Update on the Belgrave Hall Development Fund, now around £14000 of a £27000 target after a £4000 Sports Council grant, with a loan, rising team travel costs and a possible more modest scheme, illustrated by a track-shaped fund chart. BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT The Belgrave Hall Development Fund has been boosted by a grant of £4000 from The London & South East Region Sports Council. This brings our funds to around £14000 - well short of our target of £27000. Project Manager Ian Horton has also negotiated an interest free loan from the Sports Council totalling another £4000. A loan from the Southern Counties AAA's has also been negotiated but the level of interest is such that it would present too onerous a burden bearing in mind our present income. This state of affairs is less encouraging than we had hoped mainly due to the much higher cost of running our new Teams. Treasurer Jim Heathfield estimates that the travelling costs alone for the 2 Ladies teams, the Men's British & Southern League teams, plus the 2 Youths , Boys & Colts teams will this summer be around £1800 !!!!!So your 'Donations' are even more important In order to keep the momentum going Ian Horton is looking at the possibility of a more modest scheme so that at least we can get the first floor put in this year. It will be touch and go! items.sum: Obituary of Mrs E. R. Savage, widow of past president Dick Savage, club helper and Vice President, former Selsonia AC member and past president of Surrey County Womens AAA.
items.s: In Memorium — MRS E R SAVAGE Obituary of Mrs E. R. Savage, widow of past president Dick Savage, club helper and Vice President, former Selsonia AC member and past president of Surrey County Womens AAA. In Memorium MRS E R SAVAGE We were saddened late in November to learn from Win Shepherd that her mother had died recently in hospital. Mrs Savage was in her 80's and had not enjoyed good health over the last few years. Nevertheless her interest in the Club never flagged and on a number of occasions during the last few years we were able to welcome her to our meetings. Married to Past President the late Dick Savage she was a great worker for the Club, travelling with and supporting our teams. She was one of a gallant band of ladies who, half a century ago, cut piles of sandwiches and brewed gallons of tea for Belgrave socials which followed Club Championships. A supporter of womens athletics she was a member of Selsonia AC now disbanded and was a Past President of Surrey County Womens AAA. Until the formation of our Ladies Section we were a mens Club but that did not prevent us from honouring her by making her a Vice President for years of service to Belgrave. A number of old friends from Belgrave attended the funeral to say 'Goodbye' to a fine lady. Our sympathies are extended to our other lady Vice President -her daughter Win- and the family. Gordon Doubleday. Mrs E. R. items.s: W.C.JONES Obituary of Bill Jones, a member for over 30 years and formerly of Ashcombe AC, who died aged 82. W.C.JONES Bill Jones passed away recently at the age of 82. He was a keen member of the Club for over 30 years having previously been a member of Ashcombe AC for whom he raced with considerable success. Bill was of a very quiet nature. Although he was never involved in the running of the Club he was always willing to help out if asked. He won our Yacht 3 handicap when he was over 70 and up to 3 years ago he was running across the common on Saturday afternoons. We extend our sincere condolences to Mrs Jones , to son Dennis and daughter Sheila. Frank Webb. W.C. items.s: TOMMY GREEN CUP Stuart Paton received the Tommy Green Cup for winning the 1982 AAA Under 20 1500m in a club record, ahead of contenders Ernie Obeng, John Gladwin and Carl Lawton. TOMMY GREEN CUP For many, the highlight of our annual Dinner and Dance is the presentation of the Tommy Green Cup to the athlete achieving the most meritorious performance in the preceding year. Seldom has the choice been more difficult. First there was Ernie Obeng's fine 100m victory over Olympic Champ. Alan Wells ; Then there was John Gladwin's new 800m Club record of 1.46.46. Also in contention was Carl Lawton's great win in the 1981 London to Brighton walk. But pride of place went to Stuart Paton for his outstanding performance in winning the 1982 AAA's Under 20 1500m title in a new Club record. items.s: POOR TURNOUT AT DINNER DANCE Report that the annual Dinner and Dance drew about 50 fewer people than usual but the annual draw made £338, with next year's date set for 20 November at the Dog and Fox. POOR TURNOUT AT DINNER DANCE Some 50 people less than usual turned up for this years Dinner and Dance despite an excellent turnout by our new ex-Surrey AC members. This was a disappointment, not only for your committee, but also for Ron Langheim and his family who always work so hard to make the highlight of our social calender so successful. As usual the evening was a huge success and we hope for greater support this coming November. Particularly important for our fund raising efforts is the Annual Draw which Ron also organises and this year you all managed to sell even more tickets than usual so that despite cash prizes of more than £150 plus 10 other prizes a profit for the Club of £338 was achieved. Our thanks to Ron, his family and everyone else who contributed to a most successful evening. You may care to note now the date of this year's Dinner - Dance. It will be held at the Dog and Fox on Sat. 20th November. Your Committee is looking at ways of making it more attractive to our younger members. So if cost has proved a problem why not start saving a little regularly each week. We'd love to see you there next time!!! Ron Langheim Ron Langheim organises the Dinner and Dance and the Annual Draw Ron Langheim Ron Dinner and Dance Annual Draw Dog and Fox Surrey AC

e: Stock Exchange London to Brighton Walk
items.s: The Lupton Shuffle History feature on Tommy Green's 1932 Olympic 50km walk gold and James M.K. Lupton's newspaper letter dismissing race walking as a 'professional shuffle', later answered by Green, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson and Ray Hall on the London to Brighton course; the original letter is reproduced. The Lupton Shuffle At the Los Angeles Olympic Games of 1932 Tommy Green of Great Britain and Belgrave Harriers won the gold medal in the 50km walk. In the closing stages of a hard-fought race he beat the Latvian J. Dalinsch in a time of 4hrs 50mins 10 secs, after being nearly a minute down in third place at the three-quarter distance. Tommy was one of Britain's two gold medallists at that Games (Tommy Hampson was the other at 800metres) and he returned to a hero's welcome. The press hung on his every word. Prior to the 1933 London-Brighton Walk Tommy let it be known that he was out to be the first man to break the 8 hours barrier on the Brighton Road, and the Press got hold of the story. The publicity clearly upset James M.K. Lupton of London Athletic Club who could not resist writing to the Editor of the West London Observer with his views on race walking. He put himself out on a most precarious limb by describing such walking as "professional shuffles" and ridiculing the supposition that anyone could legitimately walk from London to Brighton in under eight hours. Well, Tommy won the race for the fourth time but failed by just 79 seconds to fulfill his target and prove Mr. Lupton wrong. And no one who saw Tommy Green walk competitively would question his mode of action. Two years later Mr. Lupton was made to eat his words by the impeccable stylist Harold Whitlock who clocked 7:53:50 and went on to repeat Tommy Green's achievement by taking the 50km Olympic Gold Medal the following year in Berlin - again one of only two gold medals for Britain. In 1957 the course was lengthened by ¾ mile to 53 miles 129 yards and another Olympic Gold Medallist-to-be, Don "Little Mouse" Thompson, set the sensational record of 7:35:12. If James M.K. Lupton was famous for anything, it was setting himself up to be shot down by three of this country's greatest walkers. Not to be outdone (and to make this story start and end on a Belgrave note) Past-President Ray Hall got in his own shot at Mr. Lupton in 1962 when he set a Stock Exchange record over the "Thompson" course of 7:58:38. C.S. SPORTS CORRESPONDENCE RACE WALKING, OR THE "PROFESSIONAL SHUFFLE." To the Editor, "W.L.O." Sir,—I notice in the Press that Mr. T. W. Green has expressed his determination to walk from the Clock Tower, Westminster, to Brighton Aquarium, a distance of 51 miles, 1607 yards, in eight hours in the Surrey Walking Club's race on September 9th. It makes anyone that knows what really legitimate walking is roar with laughter to think that any human being could cover the London to Brighton distance in eight hours. Fancy anyone walking a mile in six minutes, 22 seconds, the present so-called world's record, and eight miles, 438 yards, in the hour, both impossible feats. This race walking has been going on for a great number of years. It is not walking, but what used to be known in the eighties as the "Professional Shuffle." I have seen most of the so-called champions for the last half century, and I can say that I have never seen any honest walking amongst them. It is not walking, but a mix up between a walk, a run, a trot and a shuffle. It took A. F. H. Newton 5 hours, 53 minutes, 43 seconds on November 13th, 1924, to run the London to Brighton course, which at once makes any one walking the distance in eight hours an absurdity. All the walking records standing on the books to-day are nothing but "Professional Shuffles," and were never accomplished by fair and legitimate walking. It is a very great pity that the International Amateur Federation and the Amateur Athletic Association recognises this mode of progression as legitimate walking, but to those that know anything about walking, it is nothing but a burlesque.—Yours, etc., JAMES M. K. LUPTON. London Athletic Club, SPORTS CORRESPONDENCE — RACE WALKING, OR THE "PROFESSIONAL SHUFFLE." items.s: WALKING Walking section review by Carl Lawton of the 1982-83 winter season with race-by-race reports and results from September to November 1982 (Corby, Wimbledon, Leicester, Chippenham to Calne, Sleaford, Woodford Green, Bexley, Enfield, Battersea Park), with a photo of the start of the Belgrave Open 7. WALKING It has been an encouraging winter season with wins in all but one of the London "Opens" and we "drew" that one, but we lost hold of the Chippenham. Regrettably the Sectional Secretary was sidelined for three months, but he did discover that he was not indispensable. As usual thanks to those who gave assistance for the Belgrave Open 7 and especially those who donated to the prize fund. This year I shall endeavour to boost entries and I shall require more help that last year. In the middle of last summer I was contacted by Paul Warburton as he was interested in taking up walking as he had done a couple of 3kms races. His rise has been quite exceptional and as can be seen from results is now one of the team. Also we have had an assortment of individuals in team results, which bodes well for this year. With Nationals coming round again an all out effort will be required if we are to do well. Last year we slipped up for various reasons, this year things could be different if........... items.sum: Women's section report by Ladies Secretary Derek Jones on the winter's cross country and circuit training, newcomers, the senior squad, Julia McGrath's promise and Gail Porter's three championship wins, thanks to helpers, UK ranking places for Jackie Harman and Lydia Montoute, and hopes of promotion to Division 2.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Women's section report by Ladies Secretary Derek Jones on the winter's cross country and circuit training, newcomers, the senior squad, Julia McGrath's promise and Gail Porter's three championship wins, thanks to helpers, UK ranking places for Jackie Harman and Lydia Montoute, and hopes of promotion to Division 2. After the Euphoria of the summer season Cross Country Training got off to a very slow start, with only 4 runners turning up on occasions. However, events seem to have snowballed and whatever the weather, normally 12 girls (on one occasion 18) have turned up at Belgrave Hall on Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings for a run over Wimbledon Common. Some of them positively dislike Cross Country Training but have persisted and have found that the training is keeping them fit. Circuit Training at Heathbrook Centre, due mainly to a late start also began slowly but more girls are coming along for training. We have had a recruitment drive going with some of the local schools and a few useful links have been forged. Some of the schools seem to think that it is a good thing that their children are benefiting from our training. Of the newcomers to Belgrave real promise has been shown in competition and training by Jackie Stone, Anita Davison, Kim Marsh, Julie Godfrey, Trudy Attrell, Sarah Wotherspoon, Sarah King, Sian Davies, Tania Morrison and Andrea Coore. Determination in training too has been shown by Nikki Marsh, Lisa Davison, Rachael Parrott, Christina Gauge, Amanda Grant and Mo O'Connell (until she was injured). Steady progress has been shown by sprinter Jessica Palmer who is one of those who dislikes Cross Country Training but looks better for the training and also competition and probably surprised herself by finishing 7th in the Club Cross Country Championships. Suzanne Jordan and Tracey Johnson have been fairly regular in their training but more determination is required in both traing and competition. Unfortunately, the Senior Squad had been conspicuous by its absence but will be strengthened by the addition of Rosemary Honeychurch and Linda Sparks (regulars at Wimbledon and Heathbrook) Jackie Barclay has been a regular at Heathbrook but since moving house has found the trip to Wimbledon a bit far. Just to prove what a good all round athlete she is Jackie ran in the Surrey Road Relay and was second in the Club Cross Country Championships. Wendy Dunsford has not minded making the long trip from Harrow to train and compete on a number of occasions. Although not a member of Belgrave for reasons which will become clear, 11 year old Julia McGrath has shown really exceptional promise, coming 4th in the Wandsworth Cross Country Championships, 11th in London Inter-Schools Cross Country and 7th in the London Inter-Boroughs. Julia has competed for us but will be moving to Birmingham shortly and we wish her well. Pride of place must go to Gail Porter. Gail is now a triple champion and has shown determination and dedication in training. Her three wins were in the Wandsworth Schools Cross Country Championships (1st in 1981 and 3rd in 1980), the London Inter-Schools Cross Country Championships (7th in 1982) and the Junior Club Cross Country Champion (1st in 1982). All the races were won from the front and in the Wandsworth Schools at Morden Park she smashed the course record and finished well over a minute in front of the second placer. From the beginning of 1983, we have had good attendances at cross country meetings and what with a number of parents showing interest and being prepared to come along in cold weather as well as finding that they have enjoyed each others company, the Belgrave contingent has grown. For instance, at the Mitcham AC/Prestige Meeting at Morden Park at the end of January, the Belgrave party totalled over 40 (compared with 9 in 1982). Also, the junior field in our own Cross Country Championships was the largest we have ever had. Some of the girls who have joined us have been shy and reserved but just by training and competing have gained in confidence and have surprised themselves with their own ability. We now look forward to the summer season with some excitement and believe that with the additions to the squad we had last year, we are quite capable of gaining promotion to Division 2. Just saying "thank you" seems a bit inadequate, but my thanks go to Harry Porter for his efforts in Cross Country Training and also in Circuit Training. Harry leads the Cross Country Pack Runs and is always urging the girls to do better and most have responded. My thanks also to Frank Simmons who although not always enjoying the best of health has been to most Wednesday and Sunday sessions and whose advice has been invaluable. We still need help, however. So instead of sitting at home watching T.V. Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings why not come along and give a hand?. We need people to help especially at home meetings. Congratulations to 2 Belgrave girls for getting into the U.K. Ranking Lists:- Jackie Harman - 23rd in the U.K. Senior 100m (6th in the Inters). 21st in the U.K. Senior 200m (4th in the Inters). Lydia Montoute - 14th in the U.K. Junior 200m. Congratulations to Gail Porter and Julia McGrath who represented London in the English Schools Cross Country Championships on 26th March . items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track and field section introduction on the winter's indoor and open-meeting activity and the new Track and Field Committee, with contact details of the 1983 team managers. TRACK AND FIELD Winter is traditionally a quiet period for our track and field members interrupted only by the Boxing Day handicaps. This winter, however, has seen changes with a few of our younger members participating in sub-zero Open Meetings (and producing a spate of personal best's) while Phil Lovell, Colin Gaynor and Stu Paton have taken time out for indoor competition with Phil setting a new Club polevault record and Stu winning the AAA's indoor 1500m Championships thereby earning his first Senior Indoor International Vest against France. A Track and Field Committee has been set up in recognition of the more demanding commitments we face in 1983 due to having teams in Div.5 of the Southern League. It is with pleasure that we note that Stephen Crosbie (1983 General Track and Field Secretary) and Alan Mead (1983 joint Manager of our Southern League team) have returned to back up our Track and Field management team which is a follows:- General Track and Field Secretary: Stephen Crosbie - [phone number withheld] (work), [phone number withheld] (home). items.sum: Explanation that competing in a British League match only rules an athlete out of the next Southern League meeting, not the rest of the season.
items.s: NOTES ON TEAM SELECTION Explanation that competing in a British League match only rules an athlete out of the next Southern League meeting, not the rest of the season. NOTES ON TEAM SELECTION It is sometimes believed that participation in any one of the British League matches will preclude selection from Southern League competition for the rest of the season. This is not the case. If an athlete does compete in a British League match he is only precluded from the next Southern League meeting. Therefore all team members who competed in last September's qualifying match will not be eligable for the first Southern League Match whereas all those who did not compete will be eligible. It is, however, possible for Southern League athletes to compete in a subsequent British League Match without penalty. British Athletics League Southern League

items.s: JANUARY 29th 1983 - COSFORD - AAA INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS. Report of the AAA Indoor Championships at Cosford, where Stu Paton won the 1500m from Gary Staines (3rd), Colin Gaynor ran in the 60m and Phil Lovell set a club pole vault record of 4.50m. JANUARY 29th 1983 - COSFORD - AAA INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS. We were well represented at this year's AAA's Indoor Championships and the video recorders worked overtime as Stu Paton and his training partner/ 2nd claim Belgravian Gary Staines lined up against a good class field in the 1500m which contained 3 visiting Americans. Ian Archibald stretched the field through 800m in 2 minutes. Gary tried to follow and with 400m to go Stu looked to have settled for 3rd. Ever eager to outsprint Gary Stu put in a long surge with such effect that he passed Gary at 300m out and kept the momentum going to turn a 15m deficit on Archibald at the 200m out mark into victory by 2m. Gary held on well for 3rd and only just missed the European qualifying mark. Colin Gaynor showed early season form by running 12th fastest in the 60m while new signing Phil Lovell set a club polevault record with 4.50m to clinch 8th spot . 1500m: 1. S. Paton(Bel.) 3.46.65; 2. items.s: FEBRUARY 12th 1983 - COSFORD - GB v FRANCE - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. Report of the GB v France indoor international at Cosford, where Stu Paton ran fourth in the 1500m won by Seb Coe and Colin Gaynor was fourth in an invitation 60m. FEBRUARY 12th 1983 - COSFORD - GB v FRANCE - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. While our remaining juniors were gaining a team bronze in the Southern C.C. Championships, Stu Paton teamed up with Seb Coe in the 1500m against France. 2nd fastest this year on paper Stu was expected to split the French runners. This was not to be. Nerves and a disturbed nights sleep proved too much and Stu could not match a fast 3rd 400m. Seb Coe showed great thoughtfulness in encouraging our man afterwards. No doubt Stu will be even keener to set new records this summer. Also making an appearance in an invitation 200m and resplendant in his Belgrave vest was Colin Gaynor who improved on his seasons best 60m time to finish in 4th place. 1500m: 1. S. items.s: FEBRUARY 23rd 1983 - COSFORD - GB v RUSSIA - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. Report of the GB v Russia indoor international at Cosford, where Stu Paton and Gary Staines took part in Buckner's UK indoor mile record attempt. FEBRUARY 23rd 1983 - COSFORD - GB v RUSSIA - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. Still in the middle of their preparations for the National CC Championships Stu Paton and Gary Staines were called on at short notice to participate in the much published mile UK indoor attempt by Buckner. Gary towed the leading Russian through the ½ mile in around 1.56 and soon after eased off the track - his job done. Both Buckner and Stu faded as a result of the early pace but once again the experience was all part of the learning process for our men. One day later both Stu and Gary went down with virus infections. items.s: TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1982 Round-up of Belgravians' places in the 1982 Scottish, UK junior, UK senior and UK women's age-group track and field rankings. TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1982 The Scottish Association of Track Statisticians were the first to publish top rankings for the 1982 season. Belgravians were well placed in many events reflecting our growing strength. Stuart Paton ranked 3rd in the Senior 800m with 1.48.9 and 4th in the Senior 1500m with 3.42.86. He topped the Scottish Junior rankings in both the 800 and 1500. Steve Smullen ranked 15th in the 800m with 1.53.89, 17th in the 1500m with 3.53.2 and 9th in the 1 mile with 4.10.5 (All these performances were achieved prior to the Surrey AC amalgamation on August 31st 1982). Mark Lindsay-Bayley ranked 9th in the 110mH with 15.3, and 13th in the 400mH with 56.9. His 6.50m long jump was good enough for 13th place in the Scottish rankings. In the UK junior mens rankings for 82 Stuart Paton's times ranked him 5th in the 800 and 1st in the 1500. John Gladwin's 48.9 ranked him 20th in the 400, his 1.46.46 putting him top of the 800 Junior rankings. But the most impressive improvement was in the number of Belgravians featuring in the UK Senior mens top 50 Rankings. In the field events new member Phil Lovell's 4.70 was good enough to put him 10th in the pole vault with Mark Shippen's 4.30 being good enough for 30th. Derrick Williams ranked 18th in the long jump with 7.40 and 32nd in the triple jump with his 14.76. David Dawson ranked 49th in the shot with 14.27 and Ken Onagaluchi was equal 20th in the discus with 48.64. Our young ladies too are beginning to make an impression. Jackie Harman's 11.81 100m was good enough for 5th place in the UK Intermediate women's lists (in fact 3 of the faster times were 11.8 windy hand timings, so in our book Jackie was good enough for second). The fast Intermediate 200m was 23.97 and Jackie was not far behind with 24.14 for 4th place. Lydia Montout ranked 14th in the Junior 200m with 25.7. Explains how, after losing the Surrey AC slot in the Ebbisham League, Belgrave (led by Derek Crookes) formed the new Thameside League for colts and boys at the Battersea track. BELGRAVE FORM NEW COLTS AND BOYS LEAGUE. When the Surrey/Belgrave merger took place last year we had hoped to use the Surrey AC slot in the Ebbisham League to provide plenty of competition for our growing band of colts and boys. Mysteriously the Ebbisham League management decided that the Surrey slot should be relinquished. Not to worry we thought,Belgrave had been waiting to join for several years and so the vacancy would come to us anyway. Not on your nelly! We were passed over and so what to do? Well, to cut a short story even shorter, Derek Crookes came up with the idea of forming a new League based on the new all-weather track at Battersea. A quick advert in A.W. and we had a good enough response to get things going. The new League is to be known as the Thameside League- at least for this year. There are even more ambitious plans ahead. Several Clubs have indicated their interest in participating next year particularly if we include girls as well. Now that has the makings of a really good idea. Such a combined competition would create greater team spirit and would eliminate the expense of running separate teams to different venues. The GLC has been approached to see if they will support such a League and their initial response has been very encouraging We ask therefore that all colts and boys take full advantage of the chances offered by this new League and turn out in force for every match! (Also refer to the Hon. Secs. Notices on P.5). Derek Crookes Derek Crookes came up with the idea of the new Thameside League Ebbisham League Thameside League Battersea Surrey AC

items.s: BATTERSEA ALL WEATHER TRACK Progress report on the new all-weather track at Battersea Park, delayed by a Tilbury dock strike and a wet April but still due to open in June. BATTERSEA ALL WEATHER TRACK Those of you who have kept a close watch on the developments at Battersea Park will have seen the excellent start made by the contractors after Christmas aided by a spell of reasonably dry weather. Hopes were high that an early opening might be possible but fate was to take a hand during the latter stages first, as a dock strike at Tilbury held up the top surface and second, as we moved into the wettest April on record. It is to the credit of the contactors that the opening date is still planned for June with a big Ceremony on the 26th Battersea Park Tilbury

EARLY SEASON SUCCESSES No sooner had Steve Williams completed his comprehensive analysis of the existing Belgrave age records than the first results of the new outdoor Track and Field season arrived and almost immediately the records started to tumble.- A really good omen for the important season ahead. In the Senior ranks Phil Lovell pushed his p.b. and our Pole Vault record to 4.75m at a S.Counties,Loughborough Univ.,London Univ.,Civil Service match held at West London on Wed. 27th April. Paul Richley, also at the same meeting, lopped an astonishing 14 sec.s off his 3000m record to reduce our Junior best down to 8.14.5. In the same race Oliver Foote ran a p.b. 8.28.8, only 3 days after winning the Surrey 10000m title. The other early season record was Dick Addison's Youth 400m time of 49.9 set while winning the Surrey title. This eliminated John Gladwin's 50.5 but John was not idle having stretched to an easy 3.56 1500m in his first outing at West London Stadium. items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' winter season 1982-83, with commentary and race-by-race results for the colts (including the Surrey League first division title), boys and youths, and photographs of four young runners by Bill Laws. YOUNG ATHLETES This is the second season of the new management, mars bars and all and the following results show an improvement on overall and individual results far beyond our expectations. Before detailed analysis, I would like to thank all the young athletes for their efforts during the winter, running through often very tough conditions. I would like to thank Duncan, Reg, Ted, Rosemary and Claire for sharing the load, also the increasing band of parents for solving the transport logistics of ferrying indistinguishable boys and mud. I never thought I would attend a race where the support for the Bel-boys outnumbers even the 'host' clubs but it has happened regularly this winter. I am grateful for this and the friendly atmosphere that exits within which the boys have maintained often dramatic improvement while sustaining an obvious enjoyment of the sport. Reports by Ian Horton. COLTS We know if we want to eventually boast strong teams in each age group we must build from the base and therefore perhaps my greatest satisfaction at the completion of this season is to record we have 25 members in the colts section, the majority of whom have been active throughout the winter often fielding 3 teams. We have enjoyed 'many firsts'. We have fielded the first micro colts team and ran the first Belgrave mini colts championship, won by Adrian Ross and Second Russel Isles, both of whom (at the age of 10) have already made significant impact in the U.13 races. Teddy Davies is already an experienced campaigner and two years their junior, even so the age competition must be awarded to Stewart Booth, who at 7 ran a seasoned race at Canvey Island. The colts were the most prominent in striking firsts for the Bels, pride of place going to taking the Surrey League 1st division title, winning convincingly against distinguished clubs, including Herne Hill, Croydon, Ranelagh. The most satisfying aspect being that eight boys contributed to the scoring team, G. Allison, B. Leigh, J. Caines, D. Steward, G. Webb, D. Cunningham, A. Ross and P. Whiston. The first division individual title was won by Ben Leigh. Gareth Allison won the club championships, gained a creditable 8th in the Surrey C.C. Championship and represented Surrey County to finish 41st in the Inter-Counties 'B' race. From this base I am optimistic we can develop strong colts and boys teams next season. COLTS. So we travelled to Bournemouth with growing confidence and again were rewarded with an excellent third team place. Then on November 13th performed superbly in the Sutton & Cheam 4 x 1 mile relays with times of 4.40, 4.57, 4.50, and 4.52 averaging 4.52 miling( The course record previously averaged 5.02). Even so the team finished fourth to Bracknell. At that time we were not to know the ringing prediction in the past BELGRAVIAN (April 1982 P.29) was soon to be realised when injuries prevented this team running again for thr rest of the season. So it was left to John Warren to fly the banner often without support and it is therefore to his credit that he has put together a string of outstanding performances ( including the Club Championship and 1st in the Points League, 5th at Bournemouth, 2nd at Canvey, and 2nd in the Ranelagh Open). It is not surprising therefore that first and second year boys gave their support to maintain the combined Youths/Boys Surrey League position. Good luck to John in the next C.C. season Junior Section where a comparative effort undoubtedly will reap higher rewards. Congratulations also to David Palmer, performing well throughout his first season with the Club, gaining a second in the Club Championships and second in the points table. items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY The road and country captain's review of the 1982/83 season, lamenting poor support in key races and the failure to close a senior team in the National, while praising the juniors' retained Surrey title and individual runners. ROAD AND COUNTRY A quick summary of the 1982/83 season would probably read like a typical 'end of term' report- 'Has shown promise but could do better and currently lacks the determination to do really well' Yet once again I am to record that the lack of support in some of the key races has left us with a result that is not only disappointing and frustrating to those who have turned out and tried hard, but shows us in a position that that belies our true potential. This was climaxed by our performance (or rather lack of it) in the National where we failed to complete a senior team. The honours must undoubtedly go to our Juniors for bringing home what creditable results we did have, with a special mention for the marvellous way in which they retained the Surrey title. Again though one is left wondering what might have been achieved in the latter part of the season if they could all have been fit and together at the same time As the results show, for individual honours,congratulations are due to Stu Paton & Paul Richley for a string of top class performances throughout the season. Other noteworthy points include:- - The impact made by our older Juniors and the consistant runs from ; Oliver Foote, Peter Gilbey, Don Anderson & Derek Slann without whom things would have been much worse. - Don Andersons 'run of the season' by starting some 6 minutes behind the S of Thames Senior field and still finishing in the 200's. - David North, still recovering from illness , running himself to a stop in the Southern C.C. - The consistant runs of Simon Williamson & Leo Lyons until injury struck Leo. - The emerging talents of Adam Christie & Mike Nouch and not forgetting Mark Sinclair's first (of many we hope) Club Senior C.C. title. - Vet. International John Thresher flying from Canada to make our 12 stage relay team. John's interest & enthusiasm is a tonic to all who meet him on these visits. Finally my thanks to Bill Laws & Tom Carter for helping out with the transportation of our team on so many occasions GORDON BISC[illegible] Gordon Bisc[illegible] GORDON BISC[illegible] surname cut off at the scan edge after 'BISC' Stu Paton Stu Paton string of top class performances 1982/83 Paul Richley Paul Richley string of top class performances 1982/83 Oliver Foote Oliver Foote older junior Peter Gilbey Peter Gilbey older junior Don Anderson Don Anderson 'run of the season' in South of Thames, starting 6 minutes behind the senior field and finishing in the 200s Don Anderson Don Andersons Derek Slann Derek Slann David North David North ran in Southern C.C. while recovering from illness Simon Williamson Simon Williamson Leo Lyons Leo Lyons injured during season Leo Lyons Leo Adam Christie Adam Christie Mike Nouch Mike Nouch Mark Sinclair Mark Sinclair won first Club Senior C.C. title John Thresher John Thresher veteran international; flew from Canada to run in the 12 stage relay team John Thresher John's Bill Laws Bill Laws helped transport teams Tom Carter Tom Carter helped transport teams National Cross Country Championships Surrey Cross Country Championships South of Thames Cross Country Championships Southern Cross Country Championships Club Championship National 12 Stage Road Relay Canada

items.s: NOVEMBER 13th 1982 - WINDSOR - SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR C.C. CHAMPS. Report and Belgrave results from the South of Thames Junior cross country championships at Windsor, where Belgrave were 4th, their highest placing for many years, but missed victory through non-attendance. NOVEMBER 13th 1982 - WINDSOR - SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR C.C. CHAMPS. Some first class running from Oliver Foote and Peter Gilbey anchored us for our highest placing for many years, but what a lost opportunity and disappointment for all who were there. Just one more of our non-attendees in the first twenty and victory could have been ours. It is worth noting that all of our current team is eligible for next year's race, so as it too much of a dream to hope we can take it seriously enough to win on what will probably be our own course at Wimbledon. The IAC Crystal Palace International Cross Country race at Crystal Palace on 11th December clashed with our N. Surrey league feature and we were fortunate that only Stu Paton was asked to run. Stu did not hit his best form and finished 38th in 30.29 in a race won by David Taylor (Ireland) in 27.38. items.h: BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS.
items.sum: Light-hearted report by W.R.L. on the club's first Boxing Day fancy dress 3.2 mile handicap road race at Wimbledon, with the full 47-place result.
items.s: BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS. Light-hearted report by W.R.L. on the club's first Boxing Day fancy dress 3.2 mile handicap road race at Wimbledon, with the full 47-place result. BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS. When the idea of a Boxing Day Fancy Dress Handicap Road Race was first mooted there was little idea of the response it would attract from members. It is still not clear whether it was an excess of Xmas spirit; the desire to dress up; or just a bad bunch of programmes on the tele, but whatever the reason over 60 of our senior and junior members turned up in the most varied collection of costumes. Sigmund Freud would have had a field-day explaining the individual choices . There is little doubt of the terrific effort put in by all concerned. Indeed so good were some of the efforts that the HON. Handicapper could not identify them and Mick Gleaves cousin was heard to ask afterwards why he had not run!! The good people of Wimbledon could not believe it as 'Noddy' Biscoe set the slower entrants on their way. But soon they were joining in the fun and rushing indoors to get cameras to record the strange sights. The times were almost incidental but nonetheless the competitive edge showed as 'Father Christmas'-Paul Richley discarded his sack and 'Fly Me' stewardess John Gladwin threw away his handbag as they hauled in the early starters at sub 5 minute mile pace. Pete Gilbey as 3rd fastest was thought to have pulled a flanker as he was clad only in a nappy and large safety pin. Rubic Cube- Pete Staples got in some usefull resistance training but the Fancy Dress competition was taken apart by the Pritchard family with Simon 'JIMMY' gaining 1st prize, closely followed by big'FAIRY' Brian who again proved he is everyones favourite. Not to be outdone in suspenders and Black stockings(Yes I know this is a family mag. but you should have been there) was 'St. Trinian' - Maureen. The morning was concluded at Belgrave Hall with a hot punch bowl providing a fitting end to a really amusing event. It is rumoured that costumes are already being planned for next year. Me? Well I'm planning something, but on the other hand I might just take my camera along instead. I could make a fortune!!! W.R.L. (W) = Walker ** =Fred Bell. 1. C.Cross 19.27 2. D.Gordon 20.25 3. items.sum: David J. Mote's report on Belgrave's first appearance at the Hermes Club Oostende Wellington Medley Relays on 27 March 1983, finishing sixth of 50 teams, with a course diagram and the leg-by-leg team.
items.s: BELGRAVE CROSSES INTO EUROPE David J. Mote's report on Belgrave's first appearance at the Hermes Club Oostende Wellington Medley Relays on 27 March 1983, finishing sixth of 50 teams, with a course diagram and the leg-by-leg team. BELGRAVE CROSSES INTO EUROPE MARCH 27th 1983 - OSTENDE - WELLINGTON MEDLEY RELAYS. HERMES CLUB OOSTENDE have been organising the Wellington Medley Relays for 27 years and for the last 3 years a team from Surrey AC has crossed the Channel to compete. Hearing of our merger (how news travels) a Belgrave team was invited to compete along with 15 International Clubs to make up a total field of 50 teams. The race comprises of 12 legs ranging from 300 to 1200m. Due to the large number of competitors (600 in our race alone) the venue is a racecourse on the outskirts of Ostende and the race is held in front of the main grandstand to provide good viewing for a maximum capacity crowd and for the TV audience which follows these races with avid interest. The UK teams created much interest and apart from the Bels there were strong contingents from Blackheath and Aldershot. Our race started at 4pm with John Barry contesting the first 800m leg and he brought us in contention in 8th place. Everyone excelled themselves and the excitement rose as John Gladwin moved us into 2nd place on the 6th leg. The remaining runners tried desperately to take us into the lead as the race hotted up. For the spectators it was unbearable as the lead changed hands and after some 20 minutes only 10 seconds seperated the first 8 teams. The final surge saw Blackheath take victory in 20.08.6 with Belgrave 6th in 20.15.4 just one place ahead of Aldershot. It was great to see the team spirit as our top track speedmen lined with our middle distance specialists. We even had a small band of vocal supporters and thanks to the Couzens and Pritchards for their backing. And finally special thanks to Leo Coy and Bob Bridges who respectively managed the team and organised the travel arrangements. This year was an integration year where the team got it's feet under the table. I believe with the potential we have we can go back next year and turn the table over. Why not come and join us?? items.s: ROAD ROUNDUP Round-up of members' road race results from November 1982 to April 1983, largely compiled from John Wasbrough's reports, including John Tee's London to Brighton debut. This has made it increasingly difficult to keep abreast of results. Stu Barrett has written to draw our attention to John Tee's fine debut in last years Brighton run. items.h: APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY.
items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's report on the Belgrave Haig road relay at Wimbledon on 9 April 1983, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 23rd of 41, with stage times and team results.
items.s: APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY. Gordon Biscoe's report on the Belgrave Haig road relay at Wimbledon on 9 April 1983, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 23rd of 41, with stage times and team results. APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY. Up to seven days before the race we had the makings of a good team, one that would surely get us back into the first 9 places & hence qualify for the National 12 Stage Relay again. However once again it proved to be wishful thinking and during the ensueing week no less than 6 team changes and multiple variations to the running order had to be made. Injuries and illness accounted for most of the drop outs but not all, as even a race of this standard does not seem to have the attraction it once did in the days when people would give their back teeth to be in the team! However credit must go to those who still ran although one degree under. The race itself was blessed with fine weather and a record entry and with fine opening runs on long & short legs by Olly Foote and Mark Sinclair it looked as though we would still make it. However it was not to be and we gradually dropped down the field to finish 23rd out of 41 teams some 6 places lower than in 1982 but some 2½ minutes faster! I do not propose to analyse the team performance in great detail but the highlight of the race for us was seeing John Gladwin well and truly back in action on the 6th stage in recording 15m31s, the second fastest on that leg and equal fourth fastest of the day. Finally I would like to record my thanks to all those who helped to literally get the show on the road, from Bill Couzens who let me bully him into organising all the course markers-- once again a loyal band without whom the race just could not continue. To Clive Shippen and his equally able team who hardly ever see the race but who this year excelled themselves with a truly magnificent result sheet. Hope to see you all again next year!!! items.s: APRIL 17th 1983 LONDON MARATHON. Note on Belgrave runners in the 1983 London Marathon, highlighting G. Buchler's 2:23.03 and Simon Williamson's personal best. APRIL 17th 1983 LONDON MARATHON. It takes some time for all the results of the London Marathon to be collated and circulated and as we go to the printers the full lists have yet to be produced. However we know of two stirling performances from Belgravians. New member G.Buchler clocked a highly creditable 2:23.03 in 144th place while Simon Williamson ran a p.b. in 282nd place clocking 2.29.29 to squeeze into our all time top ten rankings for the marathon. G.Buchler G.Buchler new member; 144th, 2:23.03 Simon Williamson Simon Williamson 282nd, 2.29.29, personal best, into the club all-time top ten for the marathon London Marathon London

items.s: SPONSORSHIP Note on Channel 4 televising the English Schools championships and John Gladwin's selection for Peugeot Talbot Athletics Foundation sponsorship. SPONSORSHIP Channel 4 has signed a 3 year contract to televise the English Schools Athletics Championships. This July more than 40 minutes of the events from Plymouth will be televised which no doubt pleases sponsors - The National Dairy Council. Closer to home John Gladwin appeared on television following the announcement that he had been selected for special sponsorship by a panel which included both Brenden Foster and Dave Moorcroft. Eleven young athletes have already been selected for assistance via the Peugeot Talbot Athletics Foundation and a key factor in the choice of athlete has been that of ' high standards of dedication and self-discipline'. Peugeot Talbot plan to spend £25,000 on sponsorship over the next 3 years. items.s: RECORD SEASON Editorial hailing an amazing season of 32 new club records, track developments and the British League Division 5 win, and noting coaching sessions by Mike Winch and Judy Oakes at Belgrave Hall. This season has been truly amazing for we have seen a great burgeoning of our activities and achievements. On all fronts we are able to report advances. The Belgrave Hall Development is to proceed in January, Battersea Park track has become all weather, Norbiton track is likely to go all-weather in 1984 and our athletes have re-written our record books to confirm the progress for which you all have worked so hard. In this issue you will read of 32 new Club records!!! The strengthening of our British League team continues. We look forward next year to emulating our performance in winning this season's Division 5. Although we will face tougher opposition in Division 4 our performances this year would have placed us well up in Division 3. Winter training is essential for early season track and field successes and we are proud that UK Champions Mike Winch and Judy Oakes have started coaching sessions at Belgrave Hall as a prelude to building up a centre of excellence for strength and mobility training following our Belgrave Hall Development Programme. items.label: October 1983
items.sum: Editorial on the influx of top middle distance runners, urging that they race more on the road and in relays and proposing a Road Secretary.
items.s: ON THE RIGHT ROAD? Editorial on the influx of top middle distance runners, urging that they race more on the road and in relays and proposing a Road Secretary. You will also read in this issue of the influx of new top class middle distance runners. There is a fear that we will not be able to offer enough of them competition at the highest levels. It would seem that what with representative matches and controlled racing schedules many of our top middle distance men are not always available to turn out when needed. So in practice everyone will get a fair share of top Club competition. But, also it would seem that more could and indeed should be done to encourage our top middle distance men to race in open road races and in relays.Wouldn't it be great to see our road and country traditions re-established. We have the men, but we need to plan and organise our road activities better and it is time we considered appointing a Road Secretary.

items.sum: Club gossip column covering Philip Oppenheim's election as an MP, John Bicourt's TV work and steeplechasing, officials' elections, births, returning veterans, Graham Mackie's journey home to New Zealand and Kevin Sturman's film work.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip column covering Philip Oppenheim's election as an MP, John Bicourt's TV work and steeplechasing, officials' elections, births, returning veterans, Graham Mackie's journey home to New Zealand and Kevin Sturman's film work. Two years ago the Belgrave 100m Championship was won by Philip Oppenheim. 27year old Philip has been less active recently and no wonder! In June he became the youngest Member of Parliament. His views on capital punishment received widespread TV coverage. In his spare time he edits a specialist magazine on high technoloy subjects. For those of you watching the Helsinki World Champs on Channel 4 our comments about John Bicourt in the last Belgravian will have begun to make sense. Yes it's John who keeps taking Olympus kit 'To hell and back'. John's interest in steeplechasing has been re-kindled by new member Mike Hayes whom he is coaching. Both represented us in the last British League match and John is down to buy the drinks as Mike came home first by 6 secs. Congratulations to Carl Lawton on his election as President of the Southern Road Walking Assoc. and to Gordon Biscoe who is this year's President of The South of The Thames CCA. Mike Nouch is back running better than ever and we learn that he was married in the summer. It's worked wonders. There's always news on the stork front. Ann has presented John Rayner with their first son Jack, while Liz and Leo Lyons are counting their blessings because their second daughter, who was due in December, arrived 12weeks premature in September. Other new arrivals for Belgrave parents are; a son -Steven -for Alan and Ann Painter and a daughter -Heather- for Chris and Glynis Tapling. Colin Gaynor has gone up to Loughborough University for 1 year to study Recreational Management. In joining Ernest Obeng who is in the second year of his Doctorate and Mark Waller he strengthens the Belgrave supporters club. Our British League team to Crewe were intrigued to see one official cheering for them. He turned out to be Gerry Warr who walked for Belgrave from 1949 to the late 1950's. He is now a field referee and is Chairman of the Lancashire Schools AA's. He lives in the Wirrall and asks to be remembered to his past team mates. We are pleased to hear that Bill True is back on the road again after illness and injury. He caught a chill while officiating earlier this year and then strained a hamstring. He is now 76 and is planning to have a break from official duties. George Williams, mentioned in GRAPEVINE earlier this year, has put on his boots again and has competed for the first time in 16 years. He has again joined Belgrave and hopes to turn out in the coming winter. He was a British International in the early 60's. Albert Frost who joined us from Liverpool Pembroke just after the war and competed in our Southern and National teams was awarded the C.B.E. in the 1983 New Year's Honours list. Before retiring he was the Finance Director of ICI. We have received a most comprehensive account from Graham Mackie in New Zealand of the grand tour which he and Debbie took when returning home at the beginning of the year. While in Delhi he met Ranjit Bhatia and was well received. Graham bussed across India, Nepal; flew to Siam ,Indonesia and then on to the magic of Bali. He ran out of money in Australia and worked for two months to raise the funds to complete the journey back to Wellington. His aim this winter is to make the N.Z. cross country team. Following JB into the film business is Kevin Sturman. We can't say too much at present but there is a connection with Sean Connery and Greece. More next time! items.label: October 1983
items.sum: Tribute to Tom Carter on his election to a second term as club President, recalling his running career from 1930 and quoting his 1957 Belgravian message on the club motto.
items.s: The President. Tribute to Tom Carter on his election to a second term as club President, recalling his running career from 1930 and quoting his 1957 Belgravian message on the club motto. It is a very special set of circumstances which result in a Belgravian being elected for a second term of office as President. It is a very special person who would qualify for such an honour. Such a person is Tom Carter. Tom, now in his mid 70's,is still a 100% Belgravian devoting all his spare time to our Club and it is incredible to think that this devotion has been sustained for over 50 years through good times and through bad times. Whatever our fortunes Tom has been there giving advice and encouragement both to Officials and to new members alike and never failing to help out by transporting younger members to races plus helping out with all the usual jobs at races. There can be nobody better known to all Belgravians than our Tom and the debt we owe was only partly recognised in 1980 when we held a special '50 Anniversary Party' for him and of course Ethel who too has supported us for all this time. Behind every great man there is a great lady! Tom joined Belgrave in 1930 and almost immediately made an impact in our teams. He was in many of our medal winning National teams winning team gold in 1934. In 1936 Tom was 9th Englishman home in the National and gained an International vest running for England at Blackpool.In 1939 Tom won the Surrey 6 mile track Champs in a new record time. He also won the Southern CC title and the Southern 6 miles track title. He crowned a fine athletics career with other great performances including a 3rd place in the AAA's 10 mile track Championships. After such an illustrious career you might be forgiven for thinking that a spot of rest was in order. But not for Tom! He pitched in with training younger members after the war and worked through most of the jobs undertaken by our Officials. In 1957 Tom was honoured with the Belgrave Presidency. He wrote in the Jan. '57 Belgravian,words which are as relevant today as they were then. "Thank you all for the great honour which you have bestowed upon me in making me your President for this year. To me this wonderful Club of ours has no equal, for what other club can point to so many successes in all branches of athletics. I should like to draw members attention to our motto "Semper Paratus" which means "Always Ready". To me this means always ready for anything for our Club; I hope this means the same to you also." That's good enough for us. 'Rock on Tommy' in this your Presidential Year. items.label: October 1983
items.sum: Report of the 15 September 1983 AGM at Belgrave Hall covering the club accounts, Belgrave Hall finances, new subscription rates from July 1984 and the coming departure of Derek Crookes and Jim Heathfield from office.
items.s: AGM - GOOD AND BAD NEWS Report of the 15 September 1983 AGM at Belgrave Hall covering the club accounts, Belgrave Hall finances, new subscription rates from July 1984 and the coming departure of Derek Crookes and Jim Heathfield from office. This year's A.G.M. held at Belgrave Hall on September 15th was the best attended for many a year the numbers being swelled by several of our top track and field men plus a good turnout from our younger members and their parents. Those present were treated to an excellent review of the season's successes by Hon. Secretary and joint President - Derek Crookes followed by a detailed breakdown of the Club's accounts by Hon. Treasurer - Jim Heathfield. The successes are recorded elsewhere in this issue and so it is worth highlighting the key points from the published accounts and Jim's talk. Subscriptions for the year to June 1983 totalled £2712 thanks to the untiring efforts of Membership Secretary - Carl Lawton. This sum was only just topped by monies from donations, fund raising and grants so that our total revenue was £5440 and this sum just about met our total expenditure of £5447.By far the biggest single cost was that of running our mens, womens,young athletes and walking teams the overall figure reaching £2165. Next came printing, stationary, and postage at £1643 followed by prizes and medals which this year cost £647. So, once again subscriptions came nowhere to meeting the Club running costs thereby reinforcing the arguments of those wishing to see subs raised to more realistic levels. Those of you who keep an eye on the state of finances will know that Belgrave Hall is treated as a separate cost centre. This year the running expenses totalled £2926 and were met from bar profits and income from the hire of the Hall.We now pay the local Council £576 in rates and the ever watchfull Revenue around £200 as tax on Hall income. After all these deductions the net profit arising from the activities at the Hall was £1521. And so on to the cash balance which we carry forward to support the imminent Hall rebuilding programme. This now stands at a respectable £12411 and will be supplemented by Grants and Loans which have been promised by The Sports Council and several other Sporting Organisations. Increased income will be needed in the years ahead if the expansion of our activities is to continue. In recognition of this the Club's Committee and Trustees recommended to the A.G.M. that subs be increased from July 1st 1984 The present levels of subscriptions had remained constant for the last 4 years and the proposed increases were unanimously accepted by all present without a single dissenting voice. The new rates will be ; SENIORS £12(Was £10), UNDER 20 £9(£6), UNDER 17 £6(£3), ASSOCIATE AND SECOND CLAIM MEMBERS £6(£3) ........................................ And now for the bad news. Both Derek Crookes and Jim Heathfield indicated that the workload on behalf of the club had increased to such an extent that they would be forced to step down at the end of this years term of office. There is no doubt that many of our officials are rapidly approaching this situation and we must find ways of relieving the load of the hardest pressed of our management team. Derek Crookes Derek Crookes Hon. Secretary and joint President; to step down at end of term Jim Heathfield Jim Heathfield Hon. items.label: October 1983
items.sum: Report that the Belgrave Hall improvement programme will start in January 1984, describing the funding raised, the planned building works and facilities, and appealing for donations to Jim Heathfield.
items.s: BELGRAVE HALL Report that the Belgrave Hall improvement programme will start in January 1984, describing the funding raised, the planned building works and facilities, and appealing for donations to Jim Heathfield. Well we're doing it! The Belgrave Hall improvement programme is to proceed. Bill Couzens has cancelled his regular bookings for the Hall during the period January to March 1984 and builders will be moving in directly after Xmas. So far we have raised £29,000 of which £11,000 is in the form of loans from; The Sports Council,The Southern Counties AAA's,plus the London and the Surrey Playing Fields Associations The exact scope of the works to be carried out will depend whether or not we are able to obtain further monies ; and so we have 2 contingency plans both of which include the following; Extending the floor right across the Hall and building a new front entrance hall with an enclosed staircase leading up from the entrance area. The existing wooden staircase and store will also be deleted at this stage and a new partition wall built to separate the existing mens changing room from the gymnasium area. This work will start in January. But our hope is that further monies can indeed be found to still further improve the standard of the gymnasium and to incorporate sauna facilities plus a small office area which will be used to centralise Club records. In addition improved changing and shower facilities for the Ladies Section will be built on the ground floor to complete the full re-development of the Hall. It might be helpful at this point to remind you of the improved functions and facilities which the full development will provide. The Hall will provide a much wider range of activities than now and will have to earn extra money to pay off the loans which we have obtained. The Hall will be divided into upper and lower levels each of which will have their own entrances and toilets. Thus it will be possible to run separate activities on both the upper and lower levels at the same time. The upper floor will be used for art and recreational purposes during the day and social functions in the evenings and at weekends. The lower floor will be used to provide gymnasium, sauna and changing for Road and Cross Country training and the aim is for these facilities to be available to members at most times as opposed to the limited opening of the Hall as at present. Our aim then is to use the developed Hall to provide greater chances to use art,recreational and sports facilities by the people of South London. A key improvement will be due to the use of the gymnasium by Mike Winch and Judy Oakes who will for three days per week be running special strength and mobility sessions not only for athletes but also for other Sportsmen and members of the general public. We plan,with full support of Judy and Mike to make Belgrave Hall a major centre for training Field events athletes. In addition Mike and Judy have complete training schedules for all athletic specialities from sprints to the marathon. So, Please be patient during the re-building phase. We shall try to organise the works so that training will not be interrupted. In the meantime we still need donations so please be generous and send a'once and for all'substantial contribution to Jim Heathfield at [address withheld]. items.sum: Review of the walking season: disappointing team turnouts, the departures of Paul Warburton and Paul Blagg, Ron Day's Quadrathon attempt, John Keown's 25th Brighton and Gail Porter's girls championship medal.
items.s: WALKING Review of the walking season: disappointing team turnouts, the departures of Paul Warburton and Paul Blagg, Ron Day's Quadrathon attempt, John Keown's 25th Brighton and Gail Porter's girls championship medal. There are times in the annual cycle of walking when it is difficult to be unbiased or disinterested in activities. As a competitor it is hard to criticise the actions of a team member when one is in the position of possibly doing the same in the next race. With that in mind I extend my thanks to those who have tried and have done their bit this year, and that covers virtually all our walkers. We have not done as well as we could have in the Nationals but we've had that problem before of not getting it together on the day. We regretfully lose the services, hopefully only for 10 months, of Paul Warburton who has gone on an exchange to America. Also gone is Paul Blagg who has decided to go to pastures new for his own reasons. He had come from a junior to reach International class, but was not often available to turn out in team races so the effect on team results will be minimal. Team turnouts in the ultra distance events have this year been disappointing. We admittedly like other clubs seem to lack that dedicated group of long distance men and have to hope that the short distance men will fill the gap. We have picked up a few new members but if we are to lead we must find some method of attracting and keeping new talent. A word in passing on Ron Day. He was the only Belgravian to take part in the recent Quadrathon; 2 mile swim, 50 km walk,100 mile cycle and a 26.3 Marathon run. Unfortunately he was withdrawn after the cycle event having failed the medical check. But congratulations on getting that far. Incidentally three other walkers competed with distinction; Ed Shillabeer was 3rd, Arthur Eddlestone 4th and Stephen Till 6th. Congratulations also to John Keown on completing 25 consecutive ' Brightons ' 1300 Miles !!!! It is good to see our girls in action again thanks to Harry Porter and Dave Sharpe. Individually Gail Porter leads the way with 3rd in the Southern Counties WAAA Girls Championship. John Keown had competed in the previous three but this time reversed his role to stand on the road as a helper. Carl Lawton had acted as helper in the previous three but this time competed along with John Dunsford, Ron Day and John Morris. A pleasant evening start and a cool night followed with Ed Shillabeer taking a 20 minute lead by 30 miles and Carl 2nd. Ron Day, who had reached 50 miles before retiring in 1979 got through that point this time and John Dunsford was well on schedule for an improved time on last years Leicester 100. items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's season: a strong Southern League start that faded, club records, the growing junior walking and sprint squads, and thanks to helpers. It could have been a really great season and it started off better than anyone could have expected. However the best laid plans can often go wrong and they did. Following an excellent start in the Southern League we fell away especially in the Senior team although we still managed to establish several Club Records and personal best performances. Our Junior Walking team has been greatly strengthened by the improvement of Gail Porter who finished 3rd in the Surrey Championships, 3rd in the Southern Counties and 11th Nationally. She also broke 3 Club Walking records and with the backing of Rachael Parrott, Christina Gauge, Nikki Marsh, Tracey Johnson and Sarah O'Connell we look to be ready to make a big impact next year. Thanks for this must go to David Sharpe for his guidance and support. On the track side the junior sprint squad has grown in numbers led by Jessica Palmer and Andrea Coore. Our middle distance Juniors have grown in numbers and strength with notable performances from Gail Porter and Jackie Stone. In the other sections the enthusiasm of Rosemary Honeychurch has been outstanding and it is pleasing to see that she has set a new 3000m Senior Club racord. Wendy Dunsford and Veronica St Ange were the basis of our throwing squad backed by Julie Jones who has also developed into an excellent sprinter. Dawn McNeil and Janet Johnson were at avery meeting gaining valuable points. Just to say thanks must seem a bit tame but thanks go to Frank Simmonds (Despite having problems at the beginning of the summer) and to Harry Porter. A number of parents came along to help as well and found they enjoyed each others company and they also helped out where possible Ladies Secretary Derek Jones Derek Jones Derek Jones Ladies Secretary Gail Porter Gail Porter junior walker: 3rd Surrey Championships, 3rd Southern Counties, 11th Nationally; broke 3 club walking records; notable middle distance performances Rachael Parrott Rachael Parrott junior walker Christina Gauge Christina Gauge junior walker Nikki Marsh Nikki Marsh junior walker Tracey Johnson Tracey Johnson junior walker Sarah O'Connell Sarah O'Connell junior walker David Sharpe David Sharpe guided the junior walkers Jessica Palmer Jessica Palmer led the junior sprint squad Andrea Coore Andrea Coore led the junior sprint squad Jackie Stone Jackie Stone junior middle distance Rosemary Honeychurch Rosemary Honeychurch set new 3000m Senior Club record Wendy Dunsford Wendy Dunsford thrower Veronica St Ange Veronica St Ange thrower Julie Jones Julie Jones thrower and sprinter Dawn McNeil Dawn McNeil at every meeting Janet Johnson Janet Johnson at every meeting Frank Simmonds Frank Simmonds thanked for help Harry Porter Harry Porter thanked for help Southern League Surrey Championships Southern Counties Championships National Championships

items.s: Around The Schools Round-up of schools championship results by Belgrave's young women athletes, including Gail Porter in the English Schools walk and wins in Wandsworth, Hammersmith, Lambeth, Morden and London Schools events. In parallel with competing for Belgrave many of our younger members turned out in School Area Competitions and performed with distinction. Gail Porter finished 28th in the English Schools Walking Champs with a time for the Junior Girls 2500m of 14.33. Tracey Johnson was 64th in 17.04. Suzanne Jordan won the Wandsworth Schools 800m Juniors title in 2.35.5 with Gail Porter 2nd in 2.36.5 and Tracey Johnson 4th. Kim Marsh , not to be outdone, won the Hammersmith Junior 800m while in the Lambeth Schools Andrea Coore won the Junior 200m in 28.6 and the long jump in 4.48. Jackie Stone won the Morden Schools Girls 800m in 2.40.8 while in Part 2 of the Wandsworth Schools Sharon Martins won the Junior javelin with 25.02 and Gail Porter took the 1500m with an excellent 5.18.0. Jackie Harman won the Inter Girls 100m in 12.2 and the 400m in 60.1. Both Sharon and Jackie went on to repeat their wins in the London Schools Javelin and 200m while Gail improved her 1500m time to 5.16.1 but finished in 2nd place. items.s: ASTOUNDING PAM Note on veteran Pam Davies's 1983 marathons: London, a win at Norwich and second on the Isle of Wight. Veteran Pam Davies continues to astound with several fine marathon runs this year. Following her 3hr 10min run in April's London Marathon Pam ran 3hr 16.08 just two weeks later in winning the Norwich Marathon. Three weeks later on May 21st Pam finished 2nd in the tough Isle of Wight Marathon with 3hr 19.20. items.s: PRE-AAA'S Boxed historical snippet on the National Olympian Association's 1866 Crystal Palace meeting, where 18-year-old W.G. Grace won the hurdles. In 1866 the National Olympian Association, a forerunner of the A.A.A., held its first meeting on a grass track at the Crystal Palace. The meeting was notable for the appearance of an 18 year old cricketer in the high hurdles. Whilst "officially" fielding at the Oval, he won the hurdle race and then went back to the cricket ground to score a double century. His name - W.G. Grace! W.G. Grace W.G.
