items.sum: Review of the young athletes' 1983 season: new officials' arrangements, then Ted Moore's report on the Dunlop National Young Athletes League, English Schools selections and the new Thamesside League, with four photos.
items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Review of the young athletes' 1983 season: new officials' arrangements, then Ted Moore's report on the Dunlop National Young Athletes League, English Schools selections and the new Thamesside League, with four photos. With increased activity and competition for our younger members it has been necessary to try to give the right amount of support from officials by re-organising and co-opting new members to help out. The major change has been the setting up a team of people to help out during the summer. Geoff.Davis, in the year of his joint Presidency and coping with the marriage in the summer of his daughter, was actively involved in the organisation of officials and our home meetings. Ted Moore took over the tough job of managing and getting out the various teams ably supported by Jim Mote and, as the season progressed, by an increasing band of helpers to whom we must express our sincere thanks. Our other joint President Derek Crookes whose pet project - The new Thameside Leagu[illegible] - got under way and was a huge success, also put in a large number of hours to support the Young Athletes and this was greatly appreciated. Ian Horton, who will now concentrate mainly on managing the winter teams, also provided support together with coach Ted Warren and it was pleasing to see Duncan Ross helping out at all the boys and colts meetings. Ted Moore has prepared the following summary of what has turned out to be a very satisfactory season for our younger Belgravians. Following the merger between Belgrave and Surrey AC, Belgrave took over Surrey's place in the Dunlop National Young Athletes League. Last year Surrey were relegated from the Southern Premi[illegible] League to the South central League. As a result we were in a League comprising of 6 Clubs and met the same Clubs on each of 4 occasions. The first match at Norbiton highlighted the problems that the Club would face, i.e.,A lack of field events people. A look at the score sheet showed that Belgrave had no competitors in 25 out of the 74 events. Needless to say the result was a 4th place. there were some fine efforts and a total of 13 wins. The following achieved doubles;- Phil Gray in the Javelin end Discus([illegible] Andy Moore in the Youths 800m and long jump with the spectacular Adrian Ross at the age of 11 winning the colts 100m and 200m crossing the line with an enormous dip.(Shades of Ernest Obeng[illegible] The second match should have been held at Wimbledon Park but had to be postponed due to a doubl[illegible] booking. So the second match was at Portsmouth. The Belgrave cotingent competed this time in 62 of the 77 events and the tally of points rose from the previous matches 212 to a respectabl[illegible] 267. This put the team in 3rd place behind Portsmouth and Epsom & Ewell who scored 333 and 297 points respectively. The highlight of this match as far as we were concerned was Clive Gardine[illegible] winning the Best Performance Award. This award is made to the best overall athlete at each meeting but can only be won once otherwise no doubt Clive would have won it again at some of t[illegible] other matches. Clive won the Boys 80mH in 12.4 and the 200m in 23.9. The Southern Counties Championships were also held the same day resulting in only a small group of Youths turning ou[illegible] for the Club. A great number of points were lost as a result of this clash, but those who did turn out did very well recordind 10 wins. At Wimbledon, there was another clash of events, this time with the London Youth Games, and as a result our tally of points was restricted to 261 - sufficient for 3rd place. With 14 non-scores but 11 individual wins we had now climbed to 3rd in the League. The final match gave a glimpse of what might have been. This time we fielded a large group of Youths . This time we again finished in 3rd place but our points total improved to 318, to Epsom and Ewell's 337 and Portsmouth's 349. This time the number of Zero's on the score sheet had been reduced to 10. Dick Addison achieved 3 wins in the 200/400/800(Y) while Clive Gardine[illegible] also achieved a hat-trick of wins in the 100/PV/80H(B). There were 12 other winners. It is impossible here to list every winner nor is it possible to list the 12 or so new Club records which were broken during the course of the season. But I can say that during the year the Youngsters gave a lot of pleasure to a lot of supporters. It was great to see how many of of the parents came along to support the team. Congratulations are in order to the following who were selected to run in the English Schools Championship;Dick Addison, Richard O'Hara, Andrew Moore, Sean Richards, Philip Goedluck, and Clive Gardner. Further congratulations are due to Philip Goedluck for getting into the final of the 200m(Y) and to Clive Gardner who won the gold in the 80m(H). What a pity that only Clive competed in all the YAL meetings, while Andrew turned out in 2. Philip regrettably did not make any of our YAL meetings. There is no doubt that we had the strength to gain promation The younger members were also competing in Belgrave's new Thamesside League which started this year for Colts & Boys with the emphasis on track events. I hope this will be extended to include a full track and field programme next year. There were 4 matches. In 3, Bels were second to Camberley but in the last match Bels were 1st. As a result the final League position was that Camberley won by just a single match point ahead of Belgrave. The beauty of this competition was that a lot of boys and colts were able to try out other events and all enjoyed themselves, It is important to note that we started the season with an untried team against clubs who for years have fielded Young Athlete teams. Against this background the Club has done extremely well and the results point to many young members moving ever upwards eventually to enjoy athletics at senior level. Report By.........Ted. Moore. items.s: WELCOME Welcome to new middle-distance members recruited via cross country secretary Gordon Biscoe, with dates of birth, coaches, careers and personal bests for Anton Gayton, Mike Hayes, Andy Leyland, Alistair Morfey, Gary Staines and Kevin Sturman. Six photos of the newcomers follow across the page 26-27 spread, two of them spanning the gutter. Our Cross Country Secretary - Gordon Biscoe, surfaced in September after his summer sabatical and found that some Fairy Godfather had presented him with an array of new middle distance talent. For our track team managers the new additions had come as no surprise as they had been working hard to produce greater depth in our track and field squads. We are delighted to welcome to our ranks the following new members. Some will already be known to you as County Class and International athletes. We shall follow their careers with interest and wish them well for the future. ANTON GAYTON. D.o.b. 11.10.1964.Coached by Ted. Warren. Anton has been a second claim member for 2 years . One of the most amenable and pleasant guys you could wish to meet but when he's on the track he becomes 'An Animal'. (See next page). Anton was Surrey League Junior Cham[illegible] in 1981 and is the current Surrey Junior 2000s/c champion. P.B's. 400m 56.0(82), 800m 1.59.5(83), 1500m 4.07.5(83),2000s/c 6.30.8(83). MIKE HAYES. D.o.b. 25.12.60. Coached by John Bicourt. Formerly a member of Crewe and Nantwich Mike has represented Cheshire in the Inter-Counties C.C. Mike is a very promising Steeplechaser and has already strengthened our British League team. His progress under the tuition of John Bicourt has helped to renew John's interest in the event. P.B's. 1500m 3.57.2(82), 3000ms/c 9.18.3(83). ANDY LEYLAND. D.o.b. 18.10.63. Coached by Mick Dunphy. An outstanding youth who finished 2nd to Paul Richley in the 1981 Surrey Youths C.C.Champs Andy has been injured for the past year but this summer has shown a welcome return to form. P.B's. 800m 1.58.0(83), 1500m 4.00.94(4th 81 Scot Jun), 3000m 8.53.2(81). ALISTAIR MORFEY.D.o.b. 24.5.60.Coached by Mick Dunphy. Dogged by knee injuries at Camb.Univ. where he graduated in Mech Eng Alistair has returne[illegible] to athletics this year following an abortive attempt at a world tour when he picked up a particularly dangerous strain of maleria in Kenya. This year under Mick's guidance Alistair has set a string of p.b's and has performed with distinction in the GRE Cup and British League meetings. P.B's. 1500m 3.56.9(83), 3000m 8.30.0(83), 5000m 14.45.6(83). GARY STAINES.D.o.b. 3.7.63. Coached by Mick Dunphy. Gary will need no introduction having featured on the 'box' in both the indoor and outdoor seasons. Gary has been a 2nd claim member for some 18 months and decided to become first claim in the spring. A lover of fast cars Gary provides the wheels for the 'Dunphy Boys! Gary finished 7th in the 1980 Youths National, won the AAA's Under 20 indoor 3000m in '81 and was 2nd in the 81 Junior indoor 1500m. He is a GB under 20 International and an English Senior International. P.B's. 800m 1.52.0(81), 1000m 2.22.69(82), 1500m 3.44.87(82), 2000m 5.12.3(83), 3000m 8.12.00(83), 1mile 4.01.50(82). In 1981 Kevin was Surrey Junior 1500m Champion,and in 1979 he came 2nd in the Southern Youths 3000m and 3rd in the Youths 1500m. items.sum: Track and field team managers' review of the 1983 season, listing new club records and the British League Division 5 title win, and urging members to note next year's fixtures.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track and field team managers' review of the 1983 season, listing new club records and the British League Division 5 title win, and urging members to note next year's fixtures. With memories of some remarkable performances still fresh plus the wholesale re-writing of our record books it is with some pleasure that we can review the Track and Field season. One of the first differences from recent years emerged early on as our men presented themselves for competition in the Spring. Field event men were heavier and stronger than at the end of last season with John Aska and Ken Onuagaluchi atleast 30 lbs heavier and raring to go. Our plan to get everyone fit and ready by April ready for the first British League match payed off for we got a dream start and alerted the competition to our strengths. Things gradually became tougher but our men rose to the occasion each time and our early lead was never surrendered. By the season's end 2 Vets records had been broken by Charlie Gillett and Bill Treharne; 7 Senior records had been either broken or equalled by John Gladwin, Mark L Bayley, Jim Gregg, Phil Lovell Derek Williams, Ken Onuagaluchi and the 4x400m squad of Guy Sagar, John Gladwin, Stuart Paton, and Dave Mote. Our younger men who competed in the various senior competitions aquitted themselves well ;Chris Cornwall equalling the youths high jump record looks a good prospect for the years ahead while Philip Goedluck tied the youths 200m record and Richard Allison erased John Gladwin's 400m youth's time from the records. In winning Div. 5 of the British League our teams recorded performances which would have been good enough to win Division 4. Our efforts in the winter ahead will be directed to improving performances next year both through greater individual achievements and by raising standards in the few weak areas remaining. Our thanks to everyone who turned out to represent the Club during the summer. Your support has made us even more determined to provide you with the type of management and organisation which you and an up and coming team deserves. We can see no limit to how far the team can go provided we all continue to put the British League matches at the top end of our priority lists. Next year's fixture card has already been published and you are asked to make a note of these key dates. Have a good winter!!!! items.s: FIRST BRITISH LEAGUE WIN Match-by-match account, with Belgrave scorers, of the club's four British Athletics League Division 5 matches in 1983 (Warley, Crewe and two at Colindale), ending as division champions, with the final table and next year's Division 4 opponents. The Match 3 winners are printed as 'Hillington' in the result line but Hillingdon in the report. 7th MAY 1983 WARLEY MATCH 1 On a cold miserable day our B A L campaign got under way at Warley. We were aware of the strength of WSE and Hillingdon from last year but the others were unknown quantities. We need not have worried too much as our team responded magnificently to the challenge and ended up victors over WSE and Hillingdon finished a lowly 5th. The results showed that we recorded 11 wins and 6 second places. We won everthing from 100m to 400m including the relays!! Star of the day was Pat Lyttle having his first taste of 'the big time' and winning the 'B' 100 and 200 plus joining the winning sprint relay squad. Other good performances came from Colin Gaynor, Derek Williams(5events), and Stuart Paton. The coach journey back to London was a happy affair with little regard for the terrible weather outside which had persisted all day. The competition turned out to be much tougher than the first match with Hillingdon clearly determined to make amends for their poor result in the first match. We spent most of the afternoon , which again was cold and windy, in 3rd or 4th spot but with only a few events left we edged into the lead eventually winning by two points from Windsor. John Aska got the better of Ken in the shot with a P.B. of 12.50 and Mark Shippen won the pole vault with a fine4.20. This time Hillingdon turned out their strongest team and on a fine afternoon turned out easy winners. Again we battled with WSE and this time they shaded us by two points We missed Colin Gaynor and later discovered that a foot injury was to put him out for the rest of the season. Fortunately Ernest Obeng came down from Loughborough University to help out but he too had a back injury and could race a bend so missed the 200 but looked in sparkling form in the short sprint and relay. John Gladwin won the 800 in style and Stuart Paton won a hard 1500 having let a big gap develop.Alistair Morfey gained usefull points in the B 1500 and went through the 800 with Stu in 2mins dead. Derek Williams did his usual rescue job this time in the 200 and won the long and triple jumps. Jim Gregg made his first appearance this year in the high jump and Phil Lovell despite injury popped over in the pole vault to gain valuable points. Terry Welsh who has proved to be a really enthusiastic Belgravian took revenge over Bill Treharne in the hammer and picked up more points than we had a right to expect. So, with just one match to go , we still headed the Division one point clear of Windsor. Last minute shuffling, with a few new faces, produced a different looking team and some fantastic results were produced. The outcome was that we demolished the opposition and ended worthy Champions of B.A.L. Division 5. Our field men got us off to a great start with Terry Welsh 2nd in the hammer and Ken Onuagaluchi beating ex-International John Hillier inthe discus for the first time in a B.A.L. match. John Aska as usual gave sound support inthe throws. Phil Lovell and Mark Shippen provided a clean sweep in the pole vault asdid Derek Williams and Dr. Aham Amadi in the triple jump. Aham celebrated promotion to our top team with a P.B. Derek suffered a rare defeat in the long jump but Roy Vassall confirmed his breakthrough in this event by taking the 'B' event. On the track John Gladwin another majestic win in the 800 and Paul Richley gave us another clean sweep by taking the 'B' race. Newcomer Mike Hayes and John (To hell and back) Bicourt fought out the steeplechase and transformed the points from this event which had suffered in earlier matches from the lack of Pete Gilbey due to injury. Perhaps the star of the day was Stuart Paton who at the last minute returned from holiday and won the 'A' 400 from a standing start!!! Not to be outrun John Gladwin then ran a 47.9 split in the 400 relay squad which posted a very respectable 3.17.8. Imagine what the final victory would have been if Ernest Obeng had not been competing for Ghana in the Helsinki World Championships and Colin Gaynor had recovered from his injury. Right; Terry Welsh was the only member of the Irish Guards who remained in London when they were posted to Germany two years ago. It would be hard to find a first team man with greater enthusiasm for Belgrave and a feature of the season has been the support of our British League efforts by Terry and his family. Terry has helped the field men to hold their own in terms of points gained and he and Bill Treharne have together added respectability to the hammer. Sadly Terry is to join his Battalion early in 1984 and it looks as though we will be losing his services next season. Thanks for your support Terry. We look forward to your return to our ranks. items.sum: Note welcoming some 30 new members from the Grenadier Guards at Chelsea Barracks and reporting the Army Championships at Aldershot, won by the club's Irish Guards members ahead of its Grenadiers.
items.s: WELCOME THE GRENADIERS Note welcoming some 30 new members from the Grenadier Guards at Chelsea Barracks and reporting the Army Championships at Aldershot, won by the club's Irish Guards members ahead of its Grenadiers. Chelsea Barracks is always a source of new members and we have over the years recruited many of our field events men from the various Guards Battalions stationed there. During the summer we were pleased to introduce ourselves to the Grenadier Guards and were delighted to welcome to our ranks some 30 new members. The Army Championships held at the end of July at Aldershot were very much a Belgrave affair with our Irish Guards members winning and Narrowly beating our Grenadier Guards members into second place. The Grenadiers seem determined to reverse matters next year and if the determination of Ed Boyter is anything to go by the troops are in for a tough winter. We look forward to welcoming them to Belgrave hall before the season is out. Ed Boyter Ed Boyter Grenadier Guards Army Championships Chelsea Barracks Aldershot Grenadier Guards Irish Guards

items.s: PART2 SURREY TRACK AND FIELD CHAMPS Report of Belgrave medals in the second part of the Surrey Track and Field Championships at Motspur Park, 16-21 May 1983, including Derrick Williams's long jump win and Stuart Paton's 1500m victory. 21st MAY 1983 MOTSPUR PARK PART2 SURREY TRACK AND FIELD CHAMPS The large number of medals won by Belgravians in Part 1 of the Surrey Track and Field Championships was supplemented by further medals in the Second Part held in very variable conditions at Motspur Park during the week 16th - 21st May. In the Junior events Pat Lyttle and Mike Alleyne both got through to the final of the 200m but could only manage 4th and 5th respectively. John Warren won through to the finals of both the 800 and 1500 and was not pleased that only 1 hour separated the two finals. It was to his credit that he ran a 2.00.7 800m having fallen over , and than ran a pb 1500. in 4.05.00. Paul Richley was not pleased with his silver medal in the Junior 1500m. In the Senior events Derrick Williams won the long jump in slippery conditions with 7.08, while Phil Lovell gained silver in the pole vault with 4.60 and Mark Shippen finished in 6th place with 4.20. Dr Aham Amadi was 2nd in the triple jump while John Druce was 6th with with 13.73 while John Druce gained 6th place exactly 1m behind.More silvers came from Colin Gaynor in yhe 200m running an excellent 21.8, and from Oliver Foote in the 5000m. Oliver was only 0.9 sec. off the gold finishing in 14.33.9 tothe 14.33.0 of Ealing's Peter Barratt. Dave Mote won the bronze in the 400m with 49.4 while Stuart Paton won a tough 1500m in 3.47.8 with Mark Sinclair finishing in 6th with 3.55.8. Last but by no means least we saw Ken Onuagaluchi gain the silver in the discus behind coach Mike Winch and on the basis of this performance he was awarded his first Surrey vest for the forthcoming Inter Counties. items.s: Battersea Park Track Bill Laws's account of the delayed new all-weather track at Battersea Park and its re-opening meeting on 26 June 1983, with Belgrave personal bests and the individual winners. 26th JUNE 1983 BATTERSEA PARK RE-OPENING MEETING. In the last issue of the Belgravian we reported the good progress which was being made towards the early completion of the all-weather surface. Well, you guessed it we spoke too soon and instead of holding home fixtures in May and June as planned we found ourselves having to hastily re-arrange venues at the last minute. It was difficult to explain to those affected that the length of the delays were unpredictable due to first a strike at the docks which kept the essential materials shipbound and later to delays in finishing the surface within specification. Indeed the contractors and their Yugoslav labour were well and truly on their way when it was decided that the inside lane was well below the required thickness. As a result the track was again taken out of action in August for re-laying the inside lane and once again our Ladies Sec. was left at the last minute to book other tracks for League events. During all these problems the GLC people were terrific and we sympathised with their difficulties. And so to the grand opening. Everybody wanted to see the fine new facilities properly launched and the GLC made the necessary funds available to us to get the thing away in style. Because of the wish to try and open the track on the 26th June to co-incide with Capital radio's London Venture Day we had but three weeks to get things done. With over £1000 worth of prizes and the two 800m's organised by the BMC an advert in AW created an enormous response and on the day it was like an International affair. Then we had Seb Coe warming up before the start and the huge crowd were well entertained. All told 124 athletes competed including 32 Senior/Junior athletes of International fame. Athletes travelled from as far afield as Torquay, Isle of Wight,N. Wales, Manchester,Loughborough and Colchester to compete and posted an impressive set of tarck records. Fast times were recorded and the consensus view among the sprinters was that the Spurtan 'B' surface was very fast indeed and up to the best Continental ones. The pole vaulters too were particularly enthusiastic. Personal bests were set by 5 Belgrave athletes and Stuart Paton in winning the 800m won a TV set. Mark sinclair ran 1.56.3 in the 'B' 800m, Alistair Morfey ran 3.56.9 in the 1500m to finish just behind Gary Staines, Oliver Foote ran a 8.20.0 3000m. Roy Vassall achieved 7.00 to beat Derek Williams in the long jump and Mark Shippen vaulted a pb 4.40. Many of the top GLC people attended and were appreciative of our efforts. My thanks to all those who helped with the organising both before the event and on the day. Particular thanks to John Bicourt who organised the 3000m S/C and to Dave Mote who liaised with GLC officials and produced a really first class Souvenir Programme.(Copies may still be purchased to aid Club funds). Our thanks too to one very special non Belgravian- Dave Cocksedge who acted as announcer for the day and, armed with his stats books,managed to keep everyone informed about who was doing what. One thousand miles of travelling led us to five Southern League matches (our home match was rained off) in which we never placed higher than 4th. We were later disqualified from 2 matches for fielding a new member who had not resigned from his previous club and we were relegated to Division 3. Pretty dismal stuff you may think but we learnt a lot about running 2 sides, had an enjoyable time tackling 'Strange' events when short of competitors and by the end of the season had seen Surrey and Belgrave happily welded into one team. It only needs a cursory glance through the following results to spot the heroes, so let us now look towards 1984. We have already proved that we can nearly always cover every event and with a few more travelling reserves we can finish near the top of Division 3. The stronger our 'B' team the harder our 'A' team members will have to work to keep their places.. One or two points to bear in mind: 1. We have a large membership and when athletes drop out at the last minute it is not always easy to contact reserves who might want to compete.If you are interested in competing a phone call to Alan Mead or Bob Bridges will at least let us know who we can call on. 2. If you cannot make a match after being selected PLEASE let us know. To keep a coach full of athletes waiting for someone who may or may not turn up is inexcusable and also gives us no chance to contact reserves. 3. If you are usually an 'A' team competitor don't look upon a 'B' team outing as beneath you. We always need to field the best two teams we can and you will find that an afternoon out with our SL side is a pleasing experience where youngsters of 16 rub shoulders with the old stagers who are 'over the hill' and those who are shooting for first team status. items.sum: GRE Cup report: Belgrave reached the semi-finals by finishing second at Enfield on 12 June 1983, then were eighth at the Brighton semi-final on 7 August. The text contradicts itself: Ken Onuagaluchi is said to be 2nd in the shot while winning it at Enfield (results: 2nd SP, 1st DT and JT), and at Brighton both Ken and Phil Lovell are said to have won the discus (results: Ken 1st DT, Lovell 1st PV).
items.s: GRE CUP COMPETITION GRE Cup report: Belgrave reached the semi-finals by finishing second at Enfield on 12 June 1983, then were eighth at the Brighton semi-final on 7 August. The text contradicts itself: Ken Onuagaluchi is said to be 2nd in the shot while winning it at Enfield (results: 2nd SP, 1st DT and JT), and at Brighton both Ken and Phil Lovell are said to have won the discus (results: Ken 1st DT, Lovell 1st PV). 12th JUNE 1983 ENFIELD 2ND ROUND A small team went to Enfield to try and get through to the semi-finals and just did enough to achieve this. Ken Onuagaluchi had a field day in the throws getting 2nd in the shot and winning the shot and the discus. Roy Vassall ended up third in a classy long jump. Our other winners were new member Alistair Morfey in the 5000m, Mark Shippen in the Pole Vault and Mark Sinclair with a fine win in the 800m. 100m; 4.P.Lyttle 11.3, 200m; 4. However,on the morning of the match the team began to fall apart and in the event we did not do ourselves justice. Nonetheless the spirit was still there as demonstrated by John Gladwin who came down to support the team even though he had been taken to Hospital that morning for 8 stitches in a face wound from a bike accident. Tere were some bright spots to an otherwise forgettable day. Ken triumphed in the discus again confirming that he is now pushing International class, Phil Lovell won the discus and John Bicourt returned to the chase and recorded a fine 9.28.4. Welcome back John!! It is worth reflecting that with average performances from our best men we could have made the final. UK CHAMPIONSHIPS-MEADOWBANK 28/29 MAY-UK TITLE FOR GLADWIN-CLUB RECORD FOR LINDSAY-BAYLEY It was a reflection of improving standards in the club that we had five competitors in this championship. All of our men performed well but John Gladwin provided the highlight in winning the 1500 in his first race at the distance at this level. Always to the fore in a slowish race John took a clear lead going into the last lap and was never headed, running a wound up 54.2. Stuart Paton had also qualified for the final but a clash between out top two middle distance men did not materialise as Stu had to withdraw with a strained chest muscle. Colin Gaynor made the final of the 200m but drawn in the outside lane and with the man inside him having scratched, never got into the race. However his time in the semis was fast running into a headwind. Derrick Williams was only 7cm behind the winner in the Long Jump but it was good enough only for fourth place in a competition affected by the cold and wet conditions. Although not making the final, Mark Lindsay-Bayley hurdled to a personal best and club record (electrical timing) in the heats of the highs to round off his early season exploits north of the border 100.5sf C Gaynor 10.88(10.85Ht) 200.6. TVH OPEN-1 JUNE-ANOTHER JUNIOR RECORD FOR RICHLEY Paul Richley went to West London Stadium looking for a fast 5000m time with which to impress the selectors for the European Junior Championships later in the year. It wasn't an outstanding run by Paul's own standards but even so he managed to erase Peter Carton's name from the club record books with 15.02.2. UK v USSR-BIRMINGHAM-5 JUNE- JOHN SPLITS OLYMPIC MEDALLISTS Following his UK Championships victory, John Gladwin was selected for international duty over the mile against the Soviet Union with Seb Coe as his partner in the two a side match. Hopes were high for the first sub 4 minute clocking by a Belgravian but on a blustery day fast times were ruled out. Just after the bell (3.07.9) John was chopped by the guesting Turnbull of Gateshead and Coe and Kirov broke away. Several metres adrift he seemed unlikely to pull either of them back but as Coe went clear in the home straight the Russian faded and John came through strongly to give Britain maximum points,,1. Ernie Obeng sprinted to one of his fastest times (10.28) at Meadowbank aided by a +8.5m wind but found it only good enough for sixth as Mel Lattany ran the first sub 10 sec 100 in Britain. In yet another middle distance race affected by tripping and pushing John Gladwin was one of a number affected by tumbling runners. Tracking Ovett at around 300m in the 1000m he was lucky not to have been forced to the outside lanes like Ovett himself. It undoubtedley upset John's rhythm and a lap or so later he was not ideally placed when Elliott and Cook kicked for home. Nevertheless our man finished as quickly as the two ahead of him, if not as fast as Ovett who had rejoined the race, (Elliott 2.21.92 Cook 2.22.13 J Gladwin 2.23.18 Morrell 2.23.43 Ovett 2.23.81) ARMY v SURREY v HANTS - ALDERSHOT 6 JULY 3000Sc 3 T Kay 9.08.7 SP 2 D.Dawson 14.54 3 P.McKay 13.82 DT 2 K.Onuaguluchi 49.86 3 D.Dawson 42.54 OSLO GAMES 9 JULY - 1.46.46 AGAIN FOR JOHN! Returning to the scene of his 800pb and club record of last year, John Gladwin amazingly duplicated his time on that occasion to the hundredth in finishing 5th in one of the fast races of the European Circuit. Talk before the race was of the pace being made at 50 secs for the first lap, so planning to be several metres down for a 51, John placed to the rear at the break from lanes. However it turned out just a shade slower and John was through in 52 marginally more comfortable than expected. The result was he picked up several paces on the second lap as the field strung out chasing the talented young Cruz from Brazil. But the watch stopped when it did and we couldn't all have been shouting loudly enough at our TV sets! (Cruz 1.44.04 Cook 1.44.96, Guimares 1.45.15, Koskei 1.46.33 J Gladwin 1.46.46 Harkonen 1.47.56 Forbes 1.47.81). CAU CHAMPIONSHIPS-LEICESTER-10 JULY - NEW DISCUS RECORD BY KEN Four members contributed to the Surrey points total at the 'Inter-Counties' with Ernie Obeng scoring a maximum for a comfortable first place in the 100 in 10.5 (+1.1). In the mile, Stu Paton was also looking for the title and had the chance to be the first sub 4 Belgravian but he couldn't quite produce it on the day finishing 3rd in 4.05.9. Derrick Williams was a little below par in the long jump with 7.06 for 8th but Ken Onuaguluchi had an outstanding Discus competition placing 3rd in a new club record of 52.46 only 2.20 behind the winner. We congratulate Ken on a fine performance and hope it will be the first of many such championship and record breaking successes. GLC CHAMPIONS 3rd SEPTEMBER 1983 WEST LONDON STADIUM GLC CHAMPIONSHIPS While gale force winds were causing havoc elsewhere round the Country the GLC Championships took place in terrible conditions with winds of 10m/s against the runners in the home straight. Lap times were as a result between 2 and 3 seconds per lap down on normal which made John Gladwin's 800m time quite outstanding. Mark Sinclair ran the heat and final of the Senior 1500m in 80 minutes and beat some sub 3.50 men in gaining the bronze. Paul Richley won the junior 1500m and Ken Onuagaluchi clocked up his second win over John Hillier in the discus. All this plus a clean sweep in the 3000m walk gave us victory in the Pepper Trophy which is for senior and junior competitors. items.s: Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile Report on the Nike-sponsored Blackheath 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 25 September 1983, which Belgrave 'A' won in 1.53.36, with leg times for Belgrave's A, B, C and young athletes' teams. Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile 25th SEPTEMBER 1983 CRYSTAL PALACE NIKE - BLACKHEATH 25 X 1 MILE. The first 100 x 1 mile relay was held in 1969 to celebrate the Centenary year of Blackheath Harriers. Since that event after a break of several years the long distance track relays organised each year by Blackheath have become one of the family highlights of the track season In 1977 to celebrate the Silver Jubilee the relay was shortened to 25 x 1 miles and this format has proved to be the most poular since then. The organisation needed to get over 80 teams started at 8 separate venues around the Country is considerable and Blackheath rely on sponsors to help out by financing the effort needed to promote this event. This year Nike again provided this support with excellent prizes for the first three teams. The reward for winning was a Nike Greyhound suit for every member of the winning team and our track men realised that this year we could improve on last years third place and that we might even topple the mighty Alderhot team. On paper things looked good for our 'A' team and Bill Laws produced a prediction that not only could our strongest team win but that with reasonable times we could just shave Aldershot's U.K. record of 1hr 52.00.2. Well we almost made it! On the day illness prevented John Gladwin from running and Leo Coy had to travel abroad at short notice. Stu Paton and Paul Richley both had bad colds but turned out to support the team effort while John Barry travelled down from Redditch. We also saw Kevin Sturman in Belgrave colours for the first time and nobody would have guessed from his styllish run that this was also to be his first race since injury in the summer. It is always difficult to highlight individual perfomances but certain exceptional runs must be mentioned. To start at the beginning 17 year old John Warren gave us a better than expected 3rd place on the first leg and recorded our 4th fastest time with 4.21. 16 year old Richard O'Hara showed great maturity in recording 4.38 - some 2 seconds slower than namesake Laurie who at the age of 51 never fails to amaze. Gary Staines was our fastest man with 4.10 and this time made him fastest of the day so he picked up a pair of Nike spikes. Mark Sinclair recorded our 2nd fastest time and once again confirmed that not only has he broken through to a new level of performance but that he has the strength to string together several good runs in close succession. So, with all our 'A' team well under 5 minutes and an average of 4.32 miling we turned out easy winners with Aldershot just pipping TVH for 3rd place by the incredibly small margin of 0.9sec. It was pleasing to see some of our stalwarts such as Martin Lake contributing to this win and even more pleasing to see some of the 'B' team men turning in good times. Derek Clack and Mike Nouch continue to improve and young Andy North made a welcome return after a back injury which has put him out for the last year. Our young athletes easily broke the club age record for this event the average age being 13 yrs. Gary McGurren almost broke 5 minutes and 11 year old Adrian Ross who only knows how to run flat out recorded a quite astounding 5.41. items.sum: Report and results of the Open, Surrey and Inter-Counties 20 miles at Wimbledon on 16 July 1983, run in great heat, with Belgrave third in the Open team race, S.Smythe winning the Belgrave championship, and thanks from retiring race secretary Derek Crookes.
items.s: Inter-Counties '20' Report and results of the Open, Surrey and Inter-Counties 20 miles at Wimbledon on 16 July 1983, run in great heat, with Belgrave third in the Open team race, S.Smythe winning the Belgrave championship, and thanks from retiring race secretary Derek Crookes. Inter-Counties '20' 16th JULY 1983 WIMBLEDON 'OPEN' AND INTER-COUNTIES 20 MILES This race always seems to bring forth a hot day but this year must have provided a record, for out along the Kingston By-Pass shade temperatures in excess of 100deg. F were recorded. The race incorporated the Surrey 20 as usual, and for good measure this year the Inter-Counties '20' also.,Early leaders were J.Ashworth (Yorkshire) and Shotbolt (Bedford) and it was Ashworth who was still in the lead at 15 miles. The heat however had taken a lot out of the leader and in the closing stages of the race he was passed by Bill Cains of N.E.Counties. The Belgrave Championship was won by newcomer S.Smythe from E.Thomas (Also a newcomer) and R. Pearson. For the first time for some years BELS were placed in the Open team race - finishing 3rd behind SLH and Epsom and Ewell. These teams also finished in the same order in the Surrey Championships. The Inter Counties title was won by the home County - Surrey - much to the delight of team manager Derek Crookes. After being race secretary for the past 10 years Derek Crookes has persuaded Tony Grant to take over next year and he takes this opportunity to thank all those who have assisted him in one way or another over the last 10 years. Many, such as - Ron Langheime( marking the course ),Dudley Gordon, John Plummer, Peter Sutton, Bob Taylor, Arthur Penstone,(All Pointsmen), and Frank Webb Ted Stimpson, Gordon Biscoe, Bill Merryman, Norman Dewberry,(Recorders), have been present at all races during the last 10 years and we hope they will continue to give Tony Grant the help needed to make this race successful. This year the race was sponsored by; RON HILL SPORTS, NATIONWIDE BUILDING SOC., and DOUGLAS SPORTS. items.sum: Report and full result of the Belgrave 5¾ mile road race at Wimbledon on 17 September 1983, won by John Gladwin, with Bob Lettin winning the handicap.
items.s: GLADWIN'S ROAD WIN Report and full result of the Belgrave 5¾ mile road race at Wimbledon on 17 September 1983, won by John Gladwin, with Bob Lettin winning the handicap. GLADWIN'S ROAD WIN 17th SEPTEMBER 1983 WIMBLEDON BELGRAVE 5¾ MILE ROAD RACE With John Gladwin running what for him at this time of year was a long one there was considerable jockeying for positions on the first two mile laps. As a result a bunch of runners moved out towards Copse Hill at which point the speed men decided to take off. John soon opened a substantial gap from Mark Sinclair and Olly Foote. Mark faded up Cambridge as second claim runner Bob Lettin came through strongly and Olly was pleased to set a P.B so soon after his Greek holiday. Fine runs were recorded by Mike Nouch, Martin Lake and Eric Crutcher and Mike was considered by some to have been unlucky in not winning the handicap. Super Vet Keith Sinclair recorded a P.B and claimed a few useful scalps. items.s: 12 STAGE RELAY PROSPECTS Look ahead to the April 1984 Southern 12 Stage road relay, listing the best Belgrave long- and short-leg times on the course since 1973, which combined would beat Aldershot's course record. 12 STAGE RELAY PROSPECTS It is not unknown for Club members to round off Christmas day by retiring after a substantial nosh to re-read the October edition of the Belgravian. For some this represents a chance to remember summer glories while others plan ahead for the spring and summer competitions. For the team managers it represents a chance to dream about what might be if we were to turn out our strongest teams. The first major event of the road season will be the Belgrave Southern 12 Stage relay which is held over our home course every April. For many years we figured prominantly in this event and considered a medal of one sort or another as our right. In recent years we have not done too well but again in our dreams we see the chances of putting out such a strong team in 1984 that we could spring a few surprises. Getting into the 1984 team should be quite a challenge. At least we hope so. The present course has been used since 1973 and the best times set by Belgravians over this period would just break Aldershot's course record by 3 seconds if combined. =4.06.36. TOP POINTS SCORERS - NATIONAL C/C CHAMPIONSHIPS 1945-83 GERRY NORTH - TOPS The July '83 Edition of the'NUTS' journal contained the results of a study by Ian Hodge to determine the greatest English Cross Country runner of all time. The method he used was to allocate 50pts for a win in the English National down to 1pt for 50th place. On this method of scoring he placed none other than our own Gerry North in top spot followed closely by Bernie Ford. Bernie has still a good few Nationals in him and no doubt he will take over top spot in the next year or so. SO! items.sum: Coaching report on funding, the new Hon. Club Coach grade for Mike Dunphy, John Sullivan and Mike Winch, the club's coaches and squads, and Judy Oakes's weight training ahead of the Belgrave Hall gymnasium.
items.s: Coaching Coaching report on funding, the new Hon. Club Coach grade for Mike Dunphy, John Sullivan and Mike Winch, the club's coaches and squads, and Judy Oakes's weight training ahead of the Belgrave Hall gymnasium. Coaching With no income this year from the London and South East Sports Council but with a very welcome contribution from the Wandsworth Sports Council we have been able to provide some financial assistance to Club coaches as well as to individual athletes. We have also provided specialist equipment for some of our field event men. Much remains however to be done before every member seeking coaching can have the attention which will ensure maximum development. Unfortunately we are still unable to find sufficient people willing to embark on the Club Coaching Courses which really are not too demanding either in terms of time and content. In recognition of the work put in by top Coaches through our 'Masters Coaching Scheme' the Belgrave Committee has approved a new grade of membership - Hon. Club Coach - which has been offered to and accepted by Mike Dunphy , John Sullivan , and Mike Winch. Mike Dunphy has moved his middle distance squad to Battersea Park where Clive Shippen has also been active with a Pole Vault squad training every Tuesday evening. Our other Club coaches have continued to give stirling service with Frank Simmonds looking after the sprints both at Battersea and at Tooting Bec while Battersea was being relaid with its all weather surface. Ted Warren has worked wonders with our Colts and Boys and some fine performances have resulted. Also pleasing has been the way our A and B team members have helped out with Dave Mote, Alister Johnson and John Druce turning out whenever possible at Norbiton to help younger members. We continue to seek ways of improving our Coaching and a very important step forward is about to take place..... Judy Oakes is starting Wednesday evening Weight Training for any members seeking strength and agility workouts. This is a prelude to the Belgrave Hall developments. Early in 1984 when the development of Belgrave Hall has been completed both Mike Winch and Judy Oakes wil be running the newly constructed Gymnasium initially for 3 afternoons and evenings per week. As the planned scheme includes a Sauna and multi-gym we expect Belgrave Hall to become a centre of excellence for strength training in S.E. London. This can only help to further build our track and field teams. Mike Dunphy Mike Dunphy made Hon. Club Coach; moved his middle distance squad to Battersea Park John Sullivan John Sullivan made Hon. DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE We just missed promotion from the Dunlop Young Athletes League this year mainly due to the problems of getting our strongest teams together for the early season matches. Next year we shall try to implement the major single point we picked up that is that the most important step towards winning these matches is to have a sufficiently large team to cover all events both at 'A' and 'B' events. items.s: UK PREP SCHOOLS CHAMPION Note on 11-year-old Adrian Ross winning the London Area and National Prep Schools 400m titles in 1983. UK PREP SCHOOLS CHAMPION 11 year old Adrian Ross has put in some very useful sprint times this year and elsewhere you will read of his excellent leg in the 25x1 mile relay. It is perhaps to be expected that he would run a good 400m. Well he did. On June 20th at West London he won the London Area Prep. Schools title in 65.2. After this he was selected to run in the National Prep. Schools Champs where he improved to 64.4 in the semi-finals and then won the final in the excellent time of 64.0. items.label: April 1984 (printed as No. 207)
items.sum: Editorial celebrating Belgrave's national titles, including Gary Staines and Ernest Obeng at the 1984 AAA Indoors, and setting British League promotion as the summer target.
items.s: NATIONAL CHAMPIONS Editorial celebrating Belgrave's national titles, including Gary Staines and Ernest Obeng at the 1984 AAA Indoors, and setting British League promotion as the summer target. With greater interest being shown by Belgravians in indoor competition we waited for the results of the 1984 AAA's Indoor Championships with more than usual interest - and were not disappointed. As a result of wins by Gary Staines in the 3000m and Ernest Obeng in the 60m there was a brief moment when Belgrave members held a total of six National Titles. What with Stuart Paton's 83 1500m indoor win, John Gladwins 1500m UK Champs title and Paul Richley's 83 Junior 3000m win our increasing strength in middle distance events was well underlined. Add to this Carl Lawton's 83 35km National walk title and you have some measure of our current strengths. It is perhaps disappointing that these performances have not been widely publicised in the main Athletics Journals. It clearly takes time for our up and coming members to gain the general recognition they deserve. One sure fire way of attracting attention seems to be by winning team competitions whether on the road, country or track. Well we started 1984 in grand style when a team of twelve sprint and middle distance men travelled to the Wellington International Relays in Ostend and came away as only the second winning British team in the 28 years of the event. Our main target for this summer must be to gain promotion to Division 3 of the British League preferably as the clear winners of Division 4. Our pole vault and jumps teams rate second to none and the throws have been considerably strengthened by the formidable Ken Onuaguluchi who has wintered well under Mike Winch's tuition. Where we have gaps; high jump, hurdles, and back-up in the sprints and throws, we have a crop of most promising youngsters who we hope will be eager to experience the excitement of representing our Club in British League competition. The new Belgrave Hall Gymnasium will be opened in mid-July and with Mike Winch and Judy Oakes at the helm will provide exceptional facilities for building up our sprint and field men. We might have the occasional problems but these are to be expected. The progress is still inexorably upward!!! items.sum: Club gossip column covering members' news, from Chris Steer's Canadian and American running to Belgravians appearing as film extras and a bout of glandular fever.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip column covering members' news, from Chris Steer's Canadian and American running to Belgravians appearing as film extras and a bout of glandular fever. There can't be many runners qualified to compete in 3 Countries. Chris Steer, who won the Canadian Marathon back in 1969, now lives in Seattle, USA, but has retained Belgrave membership(and UK citizenship!). In March Chris was back on holiday and ran in several races to make first reserve for the 12 stage relay. But, back in November he won the Canadian Vets C.C.Champs and the next month led home his Seattle based Club to win the USA Vets C.C. Team title. Our man's been quite busy!!! Our 12 stage relay provided a good get together for members of our past winning teams. Gerry North, Tony Fairclough, Chris Steer, Colin Pearson, Pat O'Connor and Trevor Hart could all be seen in animated conversation. The subject was Trevor's 'See Through Outfit'. He says it suits his mature image. Pat reckons he got it from Oxfam. More news from across the Atlantic is that Peter Hardwick has run a very respectable 2.29.55 marathon in Ottowa. It's hard to believe this is the same athlete who was so slow round the Club 10 five years ago that he helped to pick up the flags on his last lap! Peter is rewarded with 14th place on our all-time list - one place ahead of Gerry North. If you hear the sounds of a melodeon with the jingling of bells and the banging of sticks around the Epsom area keep an eye open for Alan Mead, the Southern League T & F Sec. He has by all accounts discovered hidden talents as a Morris dancer. It seems a more refined form of exercise is now preferred to track reps. Since retiring out West Gordon Doubleday is busier than ever with time-keeping duties in and around Bath. He still manages to travel back to officiate at Belgrave fixtures. He has also joined Somer AC and is building up their activities with another Belgravian - Bob James - who will be remembered by those active in the late 1960's. Gordon still manages to address by hand all the 750 envelopes for despatching the Belgravian. John Bicourt has made a second TV advert for Olympus Sports. Ken Onuaguluchi, Derrick Williams and Keith Smith were among Belgrave athletes attending a sunny Crystal Palace on April 24th to provide background realism for a film called 'Gulag' which centres around the Moscow Olympics and involves political intrigue. It is due for general release later this year. Kevin Sturman spent 3 weeks before Xmas out in Greece selected as a mobile 'Look alike' for star Jason Connery, son of you know who! This film is an epic entitled 'The first Olympics' and Virginia McKenna, Bill Travers and Benedict Taylor are the stars . It looks as though we should be including Equity membership forms when we sign new members! Glandular Fever has struck-first, Junior John Warren who had already had his share of bad luck with a troublesome knee injury, and second Gary Staines who succumbed immediately after the 12 stage relay. Next might be Stuart Paton who was seen inspecting Gary's throat in some detail after that particular race. Alan Painter showed all the signs of a misspent youth on Dec 3rd when he landed a touch in the 1 o'clock at Chepstow and took the Denmark Pot in the evening. But he must have found time for training as he put one over the Hon. Handicapper in our 7½ mile CC Champs the same afternoon! items.sum: Report that the £45,000 Belgrave Hall development, helped by a GLC grant, is going ahead before VAT on building work, with a grand opening planned for June/July 1984.
items.s: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Report that the £45,000 Belgrave Hall development, helped by a GLC grant, is going ahead before VAT on building work, with a grand opening planned for June/July 1984. £45,000 BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT GETS THE GO AHEAD The Belgrave Hall Development will be nearly complete as this issue of the Club Mag. lands on your doormat. But it was touch and go whether or not it would proceed at all because the first tenders ranged from a staggering £48000 to an incredible £74000!! With only £31000 raised at the end of November 1983 things looked desparate. But, not for the first time our good supporters -The GLC- came to our rescue. A hastily prepared proposal, a presentation to the GLC's Arts & Recreation's Sports Committee(chaired by Peter Pitt) and we were given a maximum £14000 Grant for our size of Club. So, once again we went out to tender on a slightly reduced sheme and this time 2 quotes were within budget. The Finance and Trustees gave the 'Go Ahead'; the General Committee quickly approved and the contract was let against a 72 page Specification prepared by our Architect - David Lawson RIBA -. By a piece of good luck our rush proved worthwhile as the contract period which spans from 1st March to May 31st ends just 1 day prior to June 1st when VAT becomes chargeable on building works of the type we are undertaking. (Little did anyone dream that the spring Budget would bring in this unwecome bit of legislation). If we had delayed the development any further it would have cost a further £6000 for the VAT and would have effectively put and end to our plans for several years. The Hall Development represents the largest single investment ever by Belgrave and is a measure of our commitment to the future. Once the loans totalling £11000 have been paid off the Hall will be a source of substantial revenues which will be used to finance a range of ambitious projects each aimed at helping members to enjoy our Sport and to give everyone the best chance to develop their athletics carrers to the full. A lot of Members have put in a great deal of very hard work to see this development through and to raise the funds for this project. We owe each and everyone a great vote of thanks. One practical way will be for you to support all Hall activities organised by Bill Couzens and the 'Social' team and to use the Gym and Leisure facilities which will be available after JUNE 1984. Keep in touch for the date of the GRAND OPENING in June/ July. Peter Pitt Peter Pitt chairman, GLC Arts & Recreation's Sports Committee David Lawson David Lawson RIBA architect for the Belgrave Hall development Bill Couzens Bill Couzens organises Hall social activities Belgrave Hall

items.label: April 1984 (printed as No. 207)
items.sum: Look back to the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics, where Belgravian Tommy Green won the 50km walk and second-claim member Tom Hampson won the 800m.
items.s: 52 YEARS AGO Look back to the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics, where Belgravian Tommy Green won the 50km walk and second-claim member Tom Hampson won the 800m. With the 1984 Olympic Games to take place in Los Angeles, U.S.A. many will recall the 1932 Games held in that city. It was an expensive operation for Great Britain and a long journey for the team which travelled by sea and overland. We did not send our full complement - but Belgrave were represented. There had been no walking events in the previous Games at Amsterdam, prior to that walks had been held over the shorter distances. After strong representation by the Walking World it was decided to hold a walk on the road over a longer distance - 50 Kilometres. Our sole representative was Belgravian Tommy Green, undisputed winner of many famous place to place walks including the London to Brighton. Tommy won the race of his career in 4hrs 50m. 10secs. 7m 12secs. ahead of J. Dalinch, Lativia (now part of U.S.S.R.), probably the biggest winning margin in any Olympic Athletic Event. He presented the Club with a cup bearing his name, awarded annually to the best performance by a member. On the track Tom Hampson (Archilles Club) scored a great win in the 800m to crack the 1m 50sec. barrier by recording 1m 49.7sec. (rounded up to 1.49.8secs as times over this distance were only given in fifths of a second). Tom was a second-claim member of the Club and did much of his training at Battersea Park. Both these Champions have passed on but their performances are remembered with pride and admiration Tommy Green Tommy Green won 1932 Olympic 50km walk in 4hrs 50m. 10secs., 7m 12secs. ahead; London to Brighton winner; donor of the Tommy Green cup Tommy Green Tommy J. items.label: April 1984 (printed as No. 207)
items.sum: Obituary of T.H. (Tommy) Scrimshaw, 1930s international half miler, who died in March aged 73.
items.s: In Memorium Obituary of T.H. (Tommy) Scrimshaw, 1930s international half miler, who died in March aged 73. T.H. SCRIMSHAW High on the International Honours Board at Belgrave Hall is the name of Tommy Scrimshaw. We are sorry to learn that he died in March at the age of 73. He had been admitted to hospital for treatment when his condition worsened and he died. In the early thirties Tommy was one of the country's leading Half Milers, as his many International vests show. He also represented the A.A.A. on a number of occasions, also the County of Middlesex. He was a tower of strength in Club teams. One event popular in those days was the One Mile Medley Relay (880, 220, 220 and 440 yards), with Tommy on the first leg a good lead from him would give his team a great advantage. In 1933 he narrowly missed winning an A.A.A. Championship being beaten on the post. To reach the heights he did meant serious and devoted training and he prepared himself thoroughly for races at the top level. During the winter he would enjoy a spin over the country, and on Sundays would take part in an all day stroll over tough going in the Surrey Hills. He was also a regular at the Club's Social Functions. His representative appearances took him all over Britain and his gift for making friends brought him a wide circle of friends. Amongst these were countless Belgravians and many had the pleasure of meeting him over the last few years when he came along to Wimbledon to see the lads in action. The news of his death will bring back happy memories of the joy and fun which his running and friendship brought us. We extend our sympathies to his wife and family. A number of Belgravians attended his funeral at Randalls Park, Leatherhead. Tommy Scrimshaw T.H. SCRIMSHAW international half miler of the early 1930s; narrowly missed an A.A.A. title in 1933; died March 1984 aged 73 T.H. items.label: April 1984 (printed as No. 207)
items.sum: General Secretary's report: Ted Stimpson elected President of Middlesex County A.A.A., a call for a new secretariat, a welcome to Assistant Secretary Ron Severn, Bill Lucas on the AAA re-organisation working party, and thanks to fund-raiser Ron Langheim.
items.s: HON. SEC'S. REPORT General Secretary's report: Ted Stimpson elected President of Middlesex County A.A.A., a call for a new secretariat, a welcome to Assistant Secretary Ron Severn, Bill Lucas on the AAA re-organisation working party, and thanks to fund-raiser Ron Langheim. A 'FIRST' FOR TED STIMPSON I am sure members will wish to congratulate Ted Stimpson on being elected President of Middlesex County A.A.A. Ted, who was a Cross-Country International and a member of Belgrave Winning National Teams, was also member of the renowned Cadagon A.C. (which - not to get too involved - was a closed club within Belgrave for members who had a Middlesex Qualification) at the time when clubs could only affiliate to one county association. He was a member of many winning Cadagon teams in the Middlesex Champs. often on the same day as the rest of Belgrave were winning the Surrey Championship!! Although past General Secretary, Alf Harley, was President of Middlesex C. A.A.A. it was in his R.W.A. capacity that he was so elected. Ted is the first 'nominated committee' member of Belgrave to be elected to this office - well done - have a good year. NEW ERA - NEW SECRETARIATE As indicated at last years A.G.M. this is my last year as General Secretary - and with the development of the Hall leading to more work on the Licensing side of things, it is perhaps time for the whole question of the secretariate of the club (Social and Athletic) to be thought over and, in my view, broken down more than at present. Anyone who feels they may be able to give 5 or 10 hours a week to a new secretariate team should consult Derek Crookes ([phone number withheld]). It would not necessarily mean that everyone engaged in the above team would be committed to the General Committee meetings of the Club. WELCOME RON SEVERN Experienced Officials are few and far between and it take years of hard graft in Club Athletics to produce the kind of experience which can help sustain and create a Club's vitality. Club Officials generally come up through the ranks and naturally remain in the Club for a lifetime. Sometimes however Officials find that they are unable to carry on for various reasons and it mainly moving house that causes the biggest problems. Belgrave have been most fortunate in gaining the membership and support of Ron Severn who moved to Wimbledon from High Wycombe last year and has taken on the job of Assistant Secretary. In an athletics career which he says has been notable for it's mediocrity, he first began running while in the Navy where he won medals for cross-country and boxing. After a lapse of several years he joined Wycombe Phoenix Harriers, where he says his level of non achievement continued. He did however become in turn; Secretary, Trustee and Chairman of Wycombe Phoenix eventually giving up in the late 1960's. His two satisfying achievements were a Road Runners Club 2nd Class certificate(at 10,15, and 20miles), and his association with the once famous Wycombe 'Furniture-Five' Road Race. When Ron first became involved with it, it was a small, fairly local event. When he left it , it had become a major Southern race which all the top Clubs contested from as far afield as Bristol, Portsmouth and of course Belgrave. In private life Ron is a solicitor, a chartered accountant and is a Company and Commercial accountant with his own practice. He is retained by a major firm of Chartered Accountants in London. We welcome him to our management team and hope that he will be able to devote his undoubted knowledge of the Athletic scene as well as his personal talents to the continuing development of Belgrave. AAA'S - BIG SHAKE UP PROPOSED - BILL LUCAS INVOLVED At present Athletics in the U,K, & N.Ireland is controlled by 19 separate bodies and a quick glance at Belgrave's letter heading will confirm that we are affiliated to 12 of them in order to conduct the affairs of our members. From time to time plans have been prepared aimed at simplifying the organisation of the U.K's Athletics activities. The last major report on this topic was prepared 15 years ago by the Byers working party and although it recommended the setting up of a single Governing Body little progress has been made due to the reluctance of the various Area Bodies to relinquish power. Recently pressure from certain Clubs has led to the AAA's setting up another working party to study the thorny problem of re-organisation. Chairing the working party is Dr Mike Turner -ex English International and of particular interest to Belgravian's is that our own Past President Bill Lucas was included in the total of 10 members. Other members include; Dave Moorcroft plus representatives from the BAAB, Welsh AAA's, Northern Counties AAA, Midland AAA's, and the AAA's itself. Not surprisingly the Turner Report follows closely the Byers Report and proposes a simpler Administrative Structure. Belgrave has set up a 5 man Study Group to review the recommendations as they affect us. What they conclude and how BEL'S use their 5 votes at the AAA's E.G.M. which is to be held in June will be reported in the next Belgravian. RON LANGHEIM - FUND RAISER In 1979 Ron Langheim announced a record profit of £279 for the Club Draw which he organises along with the Dinner and Dance. Over the years this profit has increased until in 1983 Ron was able to point to a figure of £429. Over the last six years Ron has raised a total of nearly £2000 for the Club by this means and we owe him a big vote of thanks. In addition Ron has organised the Dinner and Dance for the last 4 years but sadly he is to step down and this year Brian Pritchard and Bill Couzens are taking over. They have booked Bourne Hall - A really delightful place in the heart of Ewell Village. Dining and Dancing facilities are excellent and we strongly recommend you start saving now for the 3rd Friday in November. items.sum: Walking section report on the winter's form of Belgrave walkers and team prospects, with race-by-race results from September 1983 to April 1984, including the team win in the National 10 Mile Championship at Southend, Richard Dorman's first G.B. vest, and wins in the Met. 20km, Southern 20km and South Western 20 km.
items.s: WALKING Walking section report on the winter's form of Belgrave walkers and team prospects, with race-by-race results from September 1983 to April 1984, including the team win in the National 10 Mile Championship at Southend, Richard Dorman's first G.B. vest, and wins in the Met. 20km, Southern 20km and South Western 20 km. It has been a good winter, almost a clean sweep -the Enfield being the slight upset. Richard Dorman has regained form temporarily lost and backing up strength is certainly on the up. Team spirit seems to be also at an excellent level. One just hopes that we can put it together for this year and all the year. Stephen Marshall's form should be an inspiration to all, two years ago his time was 95 minutes in the Belgrave 10, this year 75 mins, a 20 minutes improvement! Again mentioning Richard Dorman all his races have been done on trips down from Nottingham - not for him a ½ hour journey. Mike Scamell has promised to train this year! Newcomer John Llewellin, he won the handicap at Enfield, with a sub 56 for 7 in his 1st Open., Neil Foster, although at College in Liverpool has managed trips back for races as well as various meetings up North, and Michael Feighan another with great prospects have all been well up in the finishing orders.. Those of you who competed with George Williams will be pleased to know that his return has now gone unnoticed. Although not quite as fast as he used to be. As a result of his rejuvenation he has formed a Post Office walking section in Bournemouth. By the time this is published Graham Seatter who 6 years ago was one of our leading lights will have re-appeared in competition. He made his return to England in December and has been training hard since. With the possibility of another addition in a few months one can be fairly certain that nobody can guarantee a team place. Although shorter distance events should prove no problem in turning out teams, we could still have difficulties in the ultra distances but not if we can all pull together. On a similar front we are not doing too much on the Younger Age Groups. We did have two girls teams in the Nationals but 2 out of 7 is not all that good. Once again the Annual Belgrave 7. The event which I could not continue to provide the prizes without the excellent donations from so many Belgravians. My thanks to you. NATIONAL WIN — For Team. 24th March 1984 Southend National 10 Mile Championship A few weeks before this race it was thought that there was a chance of snatching a win, but things fell apart with Stephen Marshall suffering with an ankle injury followed with 2 stints in the Midlands(Picket Duty - Ed.) which restricted his training and he eventually missed the race. That left a weaker team with little chance, but the other Clubs gave us a helping hand and we finished up.... Team Winners!!! It can't be said that we packed well, but with Richard Dorman achieving a P.B. and Graham Seatter showing what 3 months good quality training can do it was left to Carl Lawton and John Hall to back up for a 5 points win. John Llewellin came through for 5th. man with a P.B. In the Inter-Counties race held in conjunction good packing by Surrey (4 in 16) should have given a clear win but an objection concerning Graham's eligibility for Surrey caused him to be withdrawn. No reference was made by the objector or the referee to the rule book which would have confirmed that underAAA'S Rules he was in fact eligible!!! Richard Dorman won his first full G.B vest when he walked in the Spanish 20kms on Sunday 8th April. items.s: NEW MEMBERS ADD STRENGTH Note that new members Derek Brown and Tony Parmah become eligible at the end of May to strengthen the British and Southern League teams, with their best performances. Our British and Southern League teams will be considerably strengthened after the end of May when Derek Brown and Tony Parmah become eligible to compete for us in open competition. Last year as a youth Derek long jumped 6.38m and triple jumped 13.26. His training is being guided by British League Field Captain Derrick Williams. Tony is 20 years old and after dabbling at Karate took up athletics just 3 years ago. His progress has been rapid and his P.B.'s are; 11.6 @ 100m, 23.1 @ 200m, 50.2 @ 400m, 1.56.9 @ 800m, 15.9 @ 110mH, 54.0 @ 400mH and a 49.8 400m relay leg. Tony won the 1982 Junior Inter Counties 400mH, and in 1983 was 3rd in the Senior Boys English Schools 400mH. Tony will greatly strengthen our British League Team. items.sum: Ian Horton's report on the young athletes' 1983-84 cross-country season: Youths, Boys and Colts results in the Herne Hill League, Epsom Downs League, Surrey League, club championships, Surrey championships and the Ranelagh Open, with photos of Nadir Khan and Gary McGurren, ending with the Mini Colts results (third in the Epsom Downs League, winners of the Ranelagh Open).
items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Ian Horton's report on the young athletes' 1983-84 cross-country season: Youths, Boys and Colts results in the Herne Hill League, Epsom Downs League, Surrey League, club championships, Surrey championships and the Ranelagh Open, with photos of Nadir Khan and Gary McGurren, ending with the Mini Colts results (third in the Epsom Downs League, winners of the Ranelagh Open). This is the third winter season under the 'new management' and again it has proved to be the most successful to date. It was obvious from the beginning that in order to create strong sections in each age group, it would be necessary to build at the base with the Colts. Therefore, requiring a five year term. After three years we are well on target, borne out in detail by the following results challenging the exalted company of Mitcham, Camberley, Dartford and Aldershot. Look out Tonbridge - here we come! The mark of this season has been a more ambitious set of fixtures, taking up a place in the Downs League, consequently representing Belgrave in three major leagues and, together with carefully selected open events, young Bels. Vests could be seen buzzing at no less than 18 separate venues. We have learnt a lot at the Downs. Probably the most important aspect is that each age group runs over the same course distance at separate times, therefore providing information which can be correlated for broader use. Reports by Ian Horton YOUTHS Compared to our younger members, the Youths have had some undistinguished results this season. I am, therefore, delighted that John Booth has joined us First Claim, not only bringing his running talents but also his understanding of what is trying to be achieved. We look forward to his support next winter. 1st OCTOBER 1983 BROCKWELL PARK HERNE HILL LEAGUE MATCH 1 1. S.Fury (Elliot ) 24.48; BELS 'A': 43.J.Biesty 29.53; 44.R.Mann 29.53. Gary McGURREN, Glynn Tiernan and Matthew Kinane have been mainly responsible for this effort, finishing each race with barely a vest between them all season. Again well supported by first year boys, Bassam Zriek, Dan Steward, Justin Caines and fast improving Allen Owen. Welcome also to new member Duncan Ward, who in the last few races, clearly demonstrated that he will make a major contribution next winter. I hope that Adam Horton and Kevin McDowagh can also shake off their long spells of injury and sickness and return again to support the Youth squad next season. Team Result Winners: BELGRAVE COLTS Probably the most rewarding aspect of this section has been the large numbers of boys producing sparkling runs throughout the season - Gavin Webb, David Ashford and Kevin Biesty shouldered the responsibility for most of the winter - well supported by Nadir Khan, Adrian Ross and Saul Herbert, then in the latter part of the season Aaron Bacon, Russell Isles and Steven Lambert came good - watch out for this trio next season. This squad combined to achieve 2nd in the Epsom Downs League to the Surrey Champions. 4th in the Herne Hill League (Note - here 34 teams participated) and retained the Surrey League Title. The final Surrey Match (18.2.1984) must be a club record when the first 16 places were filled by Bels. Boys. Congratulations to Nadir Khan for lifting the individual title with consistent running. Congratulations also to Gavin, David, Kevin, Steven and Aaron gaining representative honours. The climax of the Colts season must be to win the Ranelagh Open, seeing off strong opposition including Hercules Wimbledon and Camberley, who were second and third respectively in the Surrey Championships - sweet revenge!! 1st OCTOBER 1983 BROCKWELL PARK HERNE HILL LEAGUE MATCH 1 1.S.Wilson (Dartford) 13.57; BELS 'A': 14.G.Webb 14.51; 16.D.Ashford 14.57; 17.K.Biesty 15.12; 18.D.Cunningham 15.15; 51.S.Herbert 15.57. items.sum: Schools news: Stephen Lambert and David Ashford third in the London Schools cross-country championships, and Gary McGurren's wins in the London Federation of Boys Clubs races and the London Schools Champs.
items.s: Around The Schools Schools news: Stephen Lambert and David Ashford third in the London Schools cross-country championships, and Gary McGurren's wins in the London Federation of Boys Clubs races and the London Schools Champs. In the London SchoolsC.C.Championships held at Morden Park Stephen Lambert was 3rd in the 1st year Boys category in 13.40 while in the 2nd year Boys David Ashford was also 3rd in a time of 12.58 for the 4000m course. In the 5 races held through the winter by the London Federation of Boys Clubs, Gary McGurren finished 3rd in the first one but his improvement through the winter was reflected in his following performances- he won the other 4 races!!! Gary also won the London Schools Champs on 2nd Feb at Wimbledon Common and ran for London in an Inter-Counties Match held on the 10th March when he finished in 31st place. items.s: THE VANISHING PINT Story of Bill Laws's lost bet with John Bicourt over a 2000m steeplechase at Battersea, where the track markings proved 16m too long. Last year Bill Laws bet John Bicourt a pint he wouldn't better 6min for the 2000m s/c. At Battersea John ran 6.00.8 soon after the opening of the all weather surface. The pint was not forthcoming as John said he was"looking into it". You'll never guess what he came up with. He found out that the distance was marked 16m too far. The markings have now been altered and John wants his pint. Bill says he's "looking into it"!!! items.sum: Cross-country captain Don Anderson's overview of the 1983/84 road and country season, highlighting third place in Surrey League Division 1 and Belgrave becoming the second British club ever to win the men's race at the Wellington International Relays in Ostend.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY Cross-country captain Don Anderson's overview of the 1983/84 road and country season, highlighting third place in Surrey League Division 1 and Belgrave becoming the second British club ever to win the men's race at the Wellington International Relays in Ostend. Looking back at the Road and Country results for the 1983/84 season it can be seen that performances were patchy but better than in recent years. We started off very badly in the first Surrey League match and the Surrey Road Relay, but ended up in 3rd position in Division 1 of the Surrey League behind Aldershot and Herne Hill. On the road we picked up our first team relay medal -in the Cambridge Harriers Bexley race - for nearly 10 years. On the Country our peak performance came from our middle distance and speed men who travelled to the Wellington International Relays at Ostend in March and not only became the 2nd ever British Club to win the Men's race but did so in a time exactly 1 minute inside last year's winning time. We can improve on these performances next season by keeping our Road Running side going during the summer and I look forward to all those not actively involved in our track teams to contact Tony Grant who will this summer be looking to get teams out at major races in the hope that we can pick some more team medals. Finally a word of thanks to Tom Carter, Colin Pearson and Gordon Biscoe for all their support during the winter season. Don Anderson Don Anderson C.C. SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE - DIVISION 1 After a disasterous start in our home fixture which was the first League match we were very nearly last but we finished strongly in 3rd place matching Aldershot and Herne Hill for quality but not quantity. Having Gary Staines up front on three occasions and Stuart Paton well placed twice plus a fine debut run by Kevin Sturman in the last race provided a most welcome boost to the rest of the team making every place gained that much more valuable. Of our scoring team men only Mike Hayes Simon Williamson and Derek Clack turned out for all 4 matches. 15th OCTOBER 1983 WIMBLEDON MATCH 1 Alister Morfey excelled in this race but as it turned out he damaged a knee and the injury was eventually to put him out for the rest of the season. items.sum: Light-hearted piece on the team's and supporters' three days in Ostend for the Wellington Relays, posed as a list of unanswered 'Soap'-style questions, beside an uncaptioned snapshot.
items.s: 'BELGRAVE SOAP' Light-hearted piece on the team's and supporters' three days in Ostend for the Wellington Relays, posed as a list of unanswered 'Soap'-style questions, beside an uncaptioned snapshot. The team and supporters spent 3 days and 2 hilarious nights in Ostend. While the opposition were preparing for the afternoon's race our lot were engaged in pedal car races down the main high street. Things didn't get much better in the evenings and perhaps the least said the better. To the older supporters it seemed a lot like the crazy TV series 'SOAP'. If you're a fan of that programme you'll know that after a succession of unbelievable events it always poses more questions than it answers. The Ostend trip had many such similarities and we could imagine the closing questions to that episode!!! Why has John taken an interest in trains? Why did Stuart bare all? Why did Oliver's bed collapse? Who locked Keith out of his bedroom? Why would Dave rather be a Bromley Lady than a Blackheath Man? Why were 5 'A' team runners found in a wardrobe? and. Why did Don buy a round of drinks? Intrigued? Well, read the next edition of 'BELGRAVE SOAP' when these and many other questions on the Belgium trip will be answered. Aldershot were as usual weaker in this race as their teams are divided between Surrey and Hampshire. However we only finished in 6th position. Dave North was first man hoem in 16th place with Kevin Sturman in 22nd position. New member Marcus Clarke ran as a guest and finished just ahead of Dave North. Paul Richley kept up our run of good performances in the junior event and won as he pleased some 25 seconds in front of the next man. It was a great disappointment that we couldn't finish a complete Junior team though.
