Report and results of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Parliament Hill, with Paul Richley 3rd in the junior race and Belgrave 43rd in the seniors. Our star of these races was Paul Richley who, after suffering a bad patch in the middle of the Junior race moved through the field to finish an excellent 3rd in a time of 30.55. This must be a disappointig result, espacially for the older members who can remember the past glorious days of our winning National teams. This is one race in particular where we should be doing better. Paul Richley had another brilliant run finishing 8th in the Juniors and missing out on selection for the New York World Champs by some 2 months on age. In the Senior event Kevin Sturman had a blinder in 63rd place and Dave North put his Southern run behind him to beat some good men in 157th position. items.s: THREE IN A ROW FOR OLIVER FOOTE Report and full result of the club 5¾ mile road championship at Wimbledon, won by Oliver Foote for the third successive year, with the handicap won by Chris Taplin. 10th MARCH 1984 WIMBLEDON 5¾ MILE ROAD CHAMPIONSHIPS The times in this race were better than in recent years and it was Oliver Foote, after 6 months out with a tendon injury , who came back to knock 26 seconds off his p.b. for this race to clinch his third successive Road Title. Also well up in the field was Peter Gilbey making an impressive return after being sidelined for almost a full year with a serious groin injury. We were pleased to see how well Laurie O'Hara is going again and John Bicourt too. Welcome also to Ed.Boytle[illegible] who was making a bid for the 12 stage relay team. Veteran Chris Steer over from Seattle also showed why he has been making a big impact on the North American Vets scene. The handicap race was taking place mid way down the field with Chris Tapling, Keith Duckett and Bill Laws proving most successful at beating the handicapper. items.sum: Report on Stuart Paton's 16th place in the Scottish cross-country championship, narrowly missing selection for the World Championships in New York; Nat Muir won.
items.s: PATON PIPPED Report on Stuart Paton's 16th place in the Scottish cross-country championship, narrowly missing selection for the World Championships in New York; Nat Muir won. Deep down Stuart Paton probably realised that he had not put in enough quality races to stand a real chance to make the Scottish Team for the World C.C.Champs. in New York. Nonetheless he came mighty close and was clear of some class track men such as John Robson and Graham Williamson in finishing in 16th place out of a record field of 985 starters. Nat Muir won all the plaudits with a fine 5th successive title but our man continued to bring home the point that with greater strength allied to his natural speed he is going to be a force to be reckoned with in the summer. items.s: Belgrave First Report and result of the 28th Wellington International Relay at Ostend, won by Belgrave in 19.08.0, a minute inside the previous year's winning time; the team photos are on pages 24-25. 25th MARCH 1984 OSTEND 28th WELLINGTON INTERNATIONAL RELAY Last year Blackheath became the first British Club to win the famous Wellington International Relay organised by the Hermes Club Oostende. Last year we were 6th and Team Manager-Leo Coy- was determined that we would produce a much better performance this year. But other teams had the same idea and both Aldershot and Blackheath seemed confident that they had brought the men to win. The organisers were not so sure and predicted a close race between Dutch and German teams who were fielding several Internationals. Before the race our strong group of loyal supporters were busy looking for bookmakers to get a sidebet on our'Unknowns' but without luck.No doubt the odds on us will be poor and the chance to supplement costs via the bookies have disappeared for next year. On to the race itself; The turf was heavy and rough after overnight rain.With 16 International teams and 39 Club teams the first stage was like the charge of the Light Brigade. Mark Sinclair kept well out of trouble away from the rails and by the end of the 800m stage had worked up to a useful 7th place. Stuart Paton zipped through the next 600m leg handing over to Dave Mote in 3rd place and the Team Captain kept us in that place for his 200m stint. Mike Allayne is big and tough and there was no way he was going to lose a position on his 350m leg. Pat Lyttle tied up a bit over the next 300m but although we slipped to 4th the field in front was being pulled back. The next stage changed everything. Leo had predicted that the 3 long legs would settle it and it was John Gladwin who put the issue beyond doubt on the 6th stage of 1200m. His sustained pace hauled in the 3rd place man almost immediately and he drifted round the tight turn at full stretch to take the lead in front of a full and clearly impressed grandstand of spectators. By the time he handed over to Gary Staines on the next 1200m leg we were 9secs. clear and Gary, followed by Kevin Sturman(1100m) - Paul Richley(800m) - Richard Addison(400m) - Guy Sagar(400m) - and Derrick Williams(200m) each maintained that margin as the strolled round lapping up the multi-lingual commentary which was very compimentary about their efforts. And so we were all pleased -not because the winning time was exactly 1 minute faster than last years- but because our men ran for each other and were impressive as a Team! The evening was quite something with the supporters laying on the right kind of celebration in an English owned bar. As far as the other goings on we refer you dear reader to the Centre Pages of this Edition Result; 7750m. 1.BELGRAVE 19.08.0, 2.Vlierzele Sportief 19.16.5, 3.Ajax S.V. 19.19.5, 4.Daring Leuven 19.31.7, 5.Houtland 19.34.7, 6. items.sum: Report and result of the Belgrave-organised Southern 12 Stage Relay at Wimbledon, newly sponsored by Brooks, where Belgrave's young team finished 10th and qualified for the National 12 stage.
items.s: GREAT IMPROVEMENT IN 12 STAGE PERFORMANCE Report and result of the Belgrave-organised Southern 12 Stage Relay at Wimbledon, newly sponsored by Brooks, where Belgrave's young team finished 10th and qualified for the National 12 stage. 7th APRIL 1984 WIMBLEDON BELGRAVE/BROOKS/SOUTHERN 12 STAGE RELAY To the outside world this race was the same well organised affair that it has always been. To us things were very different. Gone were Haig whiskey to be replaced by new sponsors BROOKS who have agreed to at least a 3 year term. Add to this the decision by the Southern Counties to at last make this event an Official Area Championship and we had an air increased expectation. Clive Shippen, who in Gordon Biscoe's absense, masterminded the whole affair valiantly dealt with over 70 entry applications and gradually whittled the field down to 45 with no 'B' teams. Bill Couzens had moments of panic as first the Police insisted on a new course which had to be measured only to find the day before the race that road works made it impassable. So, at the 11th hour we reverted to the old course and everyone was delighted as it enabled times to be compared with previous years. Generally as we count down to the race injuries occur and people drop out. This year the team was decided on the Sunday before and Chris Steer who delayed his return to the USA remained as reserve. Only Kevin Sturman and John Bicourt were unavailable and our youngest ever team(with the exception of 'Super Lol') did all that we had hoped for running 8 minutes faster than last year, qualifying for the National 12 stage, and producing a time that would have been good enough for 2nd place 4 years ago. Inevitably every leg was discussed in great detail for the following few days. With all our track stars on the short leg we achieved the distinction of being the only team with 3 men under 16 mins on the short stage,with Mark Sinclair only just outside. But for most the outstanding run was from Andy North, who,having shaken off a niggling injury which has dogged him for 3 years, has shown rapid progress. Of the long leg men Peter Gilbey showed how rapidly he has recovered from his injury as he ran 2nd fastest time behind Oliver Foote. Many of the team knew they could have run better and it would not have taken much to close the two min. 39sec gap between our 10th and Elliott's 3rd place. Maybe next year!!!! items.s: 1983 25 X 1 MILE RELAY Note giving the amended official result of the 1983 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace, won by Belgrave, with Sale moving up to second. Just as the October '83 Edition of the Belgravian went to the printers we received the Official results which showed that enbeknown to everyone at the Crystal Palace Sale Harriers had managed to ease into second place but still some 1½ mins behind our winning time. TVH therefore lost out on third spot by just 0.9 sec. Pretty tight after 25 miles!!!! Our successful team collected over £660 of kit from NIKE and already people are sharpening up for the '84 event.It looks as though the target time to stand any chance of making our 'A' team will be sub 4.35 and if all goes to plan the UK record held by Aldershot will be in danger. items.s: BRITISH LEAGUE BITS Track and Field section opener with British League news: the new division structure from 1985, Belgrave's three Division 5 records of 1983, the Division 4 record marks to beat, and John Bicourt's 14 years of League competition. TRACK AND FIELD The British League has decided that from 1985 there will be 8 Teams in Div.1 and that 6 teams will be retained in each of Div,s 2 to 5. The big worry was the ability to keep a reasonable timetable particularly in the throws. Our experience in 1983 with 7 teams in Div. 5(a once off exercise) showed that the javelin was often still in progress after the relays had finished. No doubt the BAL Officials feel they can sharpen up in this area. So, in 1984 the top 3 teams in Divs 2 to 5 will all be promoted and only 1 team will be demoted. Two extra teams will enter Div 5 raising the total number of British League Clubs to 32. Belgrave men set 3 new Div 5 records last year. Ernest Obeng posted a new 100m best with 10.6, Derrick Williams a new long jump record with 7.50, and our 4x400m squad of Stuart Paton,John Gladwin,Guy Sagar and Dave Mote set a classy time with their 3.17.8. For anyone wishing to get their name on the Div 4 record book these are the targets you'll have to beat. Leo Coy points out that John Bicourt achieved the rare distinction of spanning 14 years of League competition for Belgrave. In 1969 he was a member of our team that contested the first National League(as it was then known) and in 1983 he made a welcome return to our steeplechase squad. In addition to John there are still several members who are actively helping the Club in one way or another; Snowy Brooks, Charlie Gillett,Tony Fairclough, Bill Couzens,Laurie O'Hara, Alan Mead, Bob items.sum: Review of the 1983 track and field rankings: Belgrave rose to 9th in John Lunn's club rankings, with individual Scottish and UK rankings for Belgrave athletes listed.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1983 Review of the 1983 track and field rankings: Belgrave rose to 9th in John Lunn's club rankings, with individual Scottish and UK rankings for Belgrave athletes listed. Clubs. In 1981 Belgrave ranked 35th , in 1982 we were 21st and we knew that our 1983 performances were good enough to improve on that. And so we awaited the 1983 Track and Field Rankings with a good deal of pleasant anticipation. This year John Lunn's rankings of the top 200 Clubs was based on the 3 best performances for each event excluding the 10000m. Leading the rankings for 1983 were Haringay with 48,839 pts followed by Birchfield with 47,813 and Shaftesbury with 47,093. Belgrave moved up to an excellent 9th place with 43,833 pts. Our rivals in this years British League Div.4 will provide stiff competition judging by their 1983 performances; Aldershot 16th 42,541, Enfield 14th 43,251, Sheffield 15th 43,013, Windsor S&E 22nd 41,649, and Woodford Green 42, 017 in 19th spot. Our local rivals did not fare so well with Epsom & E 23rd, H.H.H. 28th, Hercules Wimbledon 57th, Croydon 60th,Sutton & Cheam 78th and S.L.H. 89th. Individuals. Stuart Paton ranked 9th in the Scottish 400m with his 48.9 mark; 5th in the 800m with 1.49.9, 5th in the 1500m with 3.43.27 and 7th in the mile with 4.05.9. Mark Lindsay Bayley's 15.35 110mH time gave him 4th spot in the Scottish Lists while his 56.1 400mH was good enough for 11th place and his 6.65m long jump was also sufficient for 11th spot. In the UK Rankings Ernest Obeng featured in 8th place with his 10.28(W) 100m while Colin Gaynor's 10.56(W) made 17th spot in an injury plagued season. Ernest avoided the big 200m races because of back injury and Colin's early season's 21.68 was good enough for 38th place. In the 800m John Gladwin's 1.46.46 was good enough only for 10th place in this star packed event and Stuart's time made 35th. In the 1500m the order was reversed with Stuart in 22nd spot followed by Gary Staines in 42nd(3.44.94) and John 44th with 3.45.09. In the mile John was 30th with a 4.02.2 timing. Tim Kay our Irish Guards steeplechaser was top for us with 9.08.7 in 46th place while MLB made 40th in the 110mH. Our field men showed great improvement. In the high jump Jim Gregg ranked 21st with 2.05,while in the long jump Derrick Williams filled 11th spot with 7.52 and followed this with 29th in the triple jump with 14.98m(W). Our Pole Vaulting strength was evident with Phil Lovell in 7th place with 4.90m and Mark Shippen in 17th with 4.40. Dave Dawson(another of our Irish Guards) made 24th in the shot with 14.96 while Ken Onuaguluchi finished in 10th position in the discus with 52.46m. His guest appearance in the first Southern Counties rep match and 52.60 throw seems to have gone unrecorded. Our Youths also performed with distinction. Philip Goedluck ranked 20th in the 200m with 22.5, and Richard Allison's 400m County record of 49.9 was worth 18th spot one place behind a certain Ade Mafe. We look forward to further improvements this coming season with particular attention to those moving up to junior and senior ranks. Good Luck!!!! items.label: April 1984 (printed as No. 207)
items.sum: Steve Williams's review of the 1983/84 indoor season, with AAA titles for Ernest Obeng (60m) and Gary Staines (3000m), Staines's first GB vests, and AAA youth medals for Philip Goedluck and Sean Richards.
items.s: INDOOR ROUND UP Steve Williams's review of the 1983/84 indoor season, with AAA titles for Ernest Obeng (60m) and Gary Staines (3000m), Staines's first GB vests, and AAA youth medals for Philip Goedluck and Sean Richards. The 1983/1984 Indoor Season saw a number of tremendous performances from Belgrave track and field men including AAA Championship victories for Ernest Obeng and Gary Staines, AAA Under 20 medals for Philip Goedluck and Sean Richards in the Youths Championship, a club indoor best vault from Phil Lovell - all capped by Gary's double International selection for Great Britain for his first senior 'vests'. It hadn't been Gary's long term objective to go for the AAA 3000 metres but a last minute decision to test how the Winter's training was going provided a bonus when he took the title from Billy Dee and ten others in a pb and new club indoor best of 8.04.72. Gary thus added the Senior Championship to his AAA Under 20 victory of two years previously. As a result of this fine win he was selected for the Indoor Internationals against the GDR at Cosford on 1st February and France in Vittel on 4th February over the same distance. In the first match, the East Germans wound up the race from half way and Gary couldn't quite hold on in the closing laps. He modestly said he had been outclassed on the day but he was less than 6 seconds behind the winner and recorded another good time of 8.07.3( in even 2.42 splits ) for a very creditable senior debut. Just 3 days later in France, on an acutely angled track under a low glass roof which created an uncomfortable muggy atmosphere, Gary, like most of the Brits, could find nothing against the fresher home opposition and he finished 3rd in 8.19.99. While Gary was taking the longest track event in the AAA's, Ernest Obeng made it a double celebration for Belgrave by winning the shortest event, the 60 metres, in 6.79 ahead of Buster Watson and Cameron Sharp. Ernie was even a shade faster in the semis with 6.77 - 4/100ths away from his best. This result confirmed Ernie's supremacy on the boards for he had already beaten Sharp in 6.8 the week previously at the Cosford Games on 7 January. Phil Lovell and Colin Gaynor also took the opportunity to sharpen up indoors, competing in both the Cosford Games and the AAA's. Phil - in transitional stage between 170lb and 175lb poles - vaulted an indoor best of 4.75 for 5th place in the Cosford using the softer pole before going out at 4.90. In the AAA he warmed up with the 175, looking for a competitive height, but he encountered problems and had to revert to the old pole to clear 4.50. He couldn't then get it together to go any further and finished in 9th place but Phil says he hopes to go over 5.10 or even 5.20 when he gets used to the extra tension of the 175. Colin Gaynor shaped up with 7.0 and 6.99 over 60m but was unfortunately eliminated in the preliminaries of both events. Not to be totally outdone by their seniors our more than promising young sprint triumvirate of Philip Goedluck, Sean Richards and Andrew Rodney were also in action to considerable effect. Phil ran some exceptional 200m times for a Youth indoors; 23.0 to win the Youths event at the Cosford Open on 19 November and 23.15( 23.04sf) for a marvellous silver medal in the AAA Youth Championship on 17/18 February. We have no knowledge of any faster indoor times by a Belgravian so Phil's 23.04 goes down as a club best. Hardly a stride behind Phil in the AAA's was Sean Richards with 23.28 for a fine 3rd place. Sean also went one better in the 400m with a silver medal in 51.67 - a magnificent double effort. Over 60m Andrew Rodney three times recorded 7.2. during the winter and peaked in the AAA Junior preliminaries with a fast 7.12 electrical timing. All in all a season to whet the appetite for the summer ahead. S.R.W. Steve Williams Steve Williams Steve Williams S.R.W. items.label: April 1984 (printed as No. 207)
items.sum: The Ladies Secretary's winter review of the Ladies Section: training, four district schools cross-country champions, injuries, record-breaking walkers Gail Porter and Rachael Parrott, and thanks to helpers.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES The Ladies Secretary's winter review of the Ladies Section: training, four district schools cross-country champions, injuries, record-breaking walkers Gail Porter and Rachael Parrott, and thanks to helpers. During the winter we have been based at Belgrave Hall on Saturday afternoons and a fair number have been coming along either for cross country training or a gentle jog across Wimbledon Common. Sunday mornings has seen us at Battersea Park and again a good crowd has been coming along for training with Frank Simmons. My thanks to Frank and to Ted Weldin and Graham Thom for their help and taking some of the work load off Frank. Words, cannot express my gratitude for the work done by Harry Porter and David Sharpe. Our circuit training sessions started later than we intended, but thanks to the help of Merton Council we were able to use a School gymnasium in Wimbledon. We always had a good crowd coming along to be put through their paces and finishing off the sessions with a game of Netball (really a cross between Netball, Basketball and at times all-in-wrestling). Definitely not for the nervous or faint hearted. We have four District Cross Country Champions. Kim Marsh started the ball rolling with an emphatic win in the first ever Hammersmith & Chelsea Schools event at Wormwood Scrubbs. Gail Porter completed a hat-trick of wins in the Wandsworth Schools (this time in the Intermediates). Mary Anna O'Connell did well to win the Chelsea Schools as did Jackie Stone in the Morden Schools who also beat girls two years older than herself. Although we did not have as many turning out in Cross-Country races as we did last year we did have regular attendances with good performances in the Girls from Jackie Stone, Isobel Young, Christina Gauge and Mary Anna O'Connell before she was injured. In the Juniors, because of the injury to Gail Porter, Davina Cameron was our only regular middle distance and cross country competitor and she was always trying hard. The other runners came along for training purposes and it seemed they enjoyed doing this, as there was no pressure on them. Injuries affected Gail Porter, Joanne McGroder and Mary Anna O'Connell and 'flu', mumps and various other illnesses hit everybody at some stage during the season. Rosemary Honeychurch was our only regular Senior Cross-Country runner, but she always battled away well in races and gave of her best, always turning up for training with an infectious enthusiasm that is very refreshing. Leaving the best till last, our walkers have been doing well in the Walking League and various other races that they have been in The Record Book has been completely rewritten by Gail Porter in the Juniors and Rachael Parrott in the Girls. Rachael now holds all four Girls Records and could probably lower these even more. There was good backing from Joanne McGroder, Kim Marsh, Isobel Young, Nikki Marsh, Charlotte Christou, and once again Rosemary Honeychurch improved on her times. 8½ year old Sarah O'Connell showed a lot of determination. The resurgence of interest in Walking has been helped by the enthusiasm of David Sharpe. Our trips to Southend, Highams Park and Birmingham were very enjoyable despite the bad weather on the last two. Thanks to all who have helped and supported the Ladies Section and I feel that a special thank you should go to Sue Parrott and Margaret O'Connell for their help and suggestions. Also, of course, thanks to Harry for driving the Mini-Bus, to training sessions and meetings as well as to Sue and Ken Parrott, Arthur O'Connell and Peter McGroder for providing transport as well. Harry, will probably be happier when he has a new navigator. Sorry Harry. We now look forward to a good summer season and hope that we are able to challenge for promotion this year. Support is welcome on Southern League trips and details of these and our other league matches appear later in this report. items.sum: Opening of Vets Corner: a round-up of Laurie O'Hara's winter road and cross-country results as the club's top veteran in his 52nd year.
items.s: VETS. CORNER Opening of Vets Corner: a round-up of Laurie O'Hara's winter road and cross-country results as the club's top veteran in his 52nd year. VETS. CORNER Apart from his successes in Area Championships Laurie O'Hara, who is now in his 52nd year, has once again put together a string of very impressive performances which confirm him as our top Veteran once again. On the 7th October in the Windsor Half Marathon he finished in 5th place overall and first O/50 with 1hr 14. On the 3rd December he was 8th in the Eastcote 6 mile Open C.C. race, while on New Year's day he once again ran the London Wall 10 mile road race and placed 33nd overall and was first O/50 with a remarkable 53.40 timing. He ran two other Half Marathons during the winter finishing in 4th place in the Harrow race on the 6th November in 1:12:30, and in 6th place in the Hillingdon event on the 25th March 1984 in 1:13:05. In both races he won the vets titles. The Hillingdon race was only 2 days after he had finished in 29th place in the Feltham 5 miler in a time of 26.19. No wonder he made our 12 stage relay team. Each year we say Laurie must start to slow down. To save speculation he could perhaps drop us a line so that the other Vets can get down to some serious training!!! Laurie O'Hara Laurie O'Hara top veteran in his 52nd year: 5th and first O/50 Windsor Half Marathon 1hr 14; 8th Eastcote 6 mile; 33rd and first O/50 London Wall 10 mile 53.40; 4th Harrow Half Marathon 1:12:30; 6th Hillingdon Half Marathon 1:13:05; 29th Feltham 5 miler 26.19 Laurie O'Hara Laurie Windsor Half Marathon Eastcote 6 mile Open C.C. race London Wall 10 mile road race Harrow Half Marathon Hillingdon Half Marathon Feltham 5 miler Southern 12 Stage Relay Windsor Eastcote London Wall Harrow Hillingdon Feltham

items.s: BAD LUCK FOR VETS Vets Corner report and results of the Surrey Vets cross-country championships at Richmond Park, where Belgrave were second over-40 team behind Croydon and won the over-50 team title. BAD LUCK FOR VETS 13th NOVEMBER 1983 RICHMOND PARK SURREY VETS C.C. CHAMPS. For the last 5 years we have been trying to pip Herne Hill's team in this event with a singular lack of success finishing on several occasions second to their winning teams. This year we did it, only to be beaten by Croydon but had the satisfaction of seeing our rivals back in third spot. It is about time that an event like this which can now attract entries of over 100 should have 4 to score. In suggesting this we must confess that on such a method of scoring we would have finished first team with 4th man home Keith Sinclair closing in ahead of the third placed men for both Croydon and HHH. For our Vet readers an interesting confrontation was that of Mick Gowan (HHH) and our own Tony Fairclough which reminded us all of those halcyon days of 20 years ago. items.s: Letter from past president Tom Morrell, a member for 57 years, explaining why the wartime 'B' vest was never made and listing post-war kit prices, with the editor's thanks. From; Past President - Tom Morrell. Having been a member for 57 years(so far) and living as I do in the sticks, I always look forward to receiving my Belgravian. I would refer to your item in the last Edition concerning Club Vests in the last war. The proposed design with a big letter 'B' stitched on was never implemented. The reason for the suggestion at the time was that labour was in short supply and sewing on the gold band was too time consuming. While on the subject of clothing younger members may be interested to know the prices charged for various items of kit after the war. Sleeveless vests 8/6d(42½p), long sleeve vests 10/6d(52½p), vest badges 2/6d(12½p), gold braided blazer badge £1.2.6p (£1.12½). Made to measure shoes; track, country or road were available from Sandy Law, a Club member, at £1.2.6p per pair. By the way, from your excellent photo's I don't see many members with the Club badge sewn to the gold band. Can I take this opportunity of wishing the Bels evey success in 1984. Tom Morrell. " Tom , many thanks for your kind comments concerning the Magazine. They make the effort worthwhile" Ed. items.sum: Letter from John Thresher in Winnipeg, Canada, on the club's successes, his 20-year-old club mile record, his own 1983 races and a donation to the Belgrave Hall fund.
items.s: Letter from John Thresher in Winnipeg, Canada, on the club's successes, his 20-year-old club mile record, his own 1983 races and a donation to the Belgrave Hall fund. From; John Thresher. Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. I have just received the recent Belgravian. It was really heartwarming to read of the successes and the new young Belgravians coming through. I still receive the Athletics Weekly so I was well aware of the exploits of John Gladwin and Stu' Paton, but the British League and the 25x1 mile relay results were so well worth reading. I was pleased of course to see my Club mile record surviving into 1984 making it a round 20 years. I predict now however that 3 Belgravians will break 4 minutes for the mile in 1984 and I wonder if Gary Staines will beat the two favourites to become the first. I had a good Spring(1983). In May I ran 32.16 for an accurate 10km road race in a temperature of -6deg C! and then 2:33:10 for a marathon in June. I injured myself in the marathon and haven't raced since. I don't intend to run another marathon and just want to run again. Time is running out as I am now turned 44!! I enclose a small donation towards the Belgrave Hall Development fund. Best wishes, good health and happiness to all the Bels. John Thresher. items.sum: Letter from Ranjit Bhatia in Delhi on 32 years as an athlete, the Belgrave Hall renovations and his hopes to run for the Bels vets, with the editor's reply recalling his 1960 road circuit record.
items.s: Letter from Ranjit Bhatia in Delhi on 32 years as an athlete, the Belgrave Hall renovations and his hopes to run for the Bels vets, with the editor's reply recalling his 1960 road circuit record. From; Ranjit Bhatia. Delhi, India. The new President of Belgrave is part of the gentry at Belgrave Hall to whom I owe so much. It is really through their guidance and encouragement that I have managed to survive as an athlete for 32 years now. I like to feel that is an achievement of a sort. As the years add on the annual list of attainments gets gradually diminished. But so what? Running can be more fun as we get older than ever it was. I am delighted to read about the renovations at Belgrave Hall. I shall be sending a donation towards the project. I always think of the wonderful fraternity at Belgrave Hall which represents the best aspects of the Athletic movement I was running reasonably well last season and managed a 1:23 half marathon on October 25th. This spurred me on to more training and then suddenly everything came to a halt due to pressure of work. If my plans for Los Angeles materialise I hope to be in the UK in July and aim to run for the Bels Vets. I am delighted to see that Bill Lucas was recently President of the Southern Counties AAA's. All good wishes to fellow Belgravians. Warmest regards. Ranjit Bhatia. " It is always pleasing to hear from our overseas members and good to see that Ranjit is going strong. Our newer members will not be aware that back in March 1960 Ranjit set a new record round the 5¾mile road circuit of 27min 56 secs. Our stars of today will need to go a bit to beat that. Ranjit is also involved on the admin. side and in October 1983 was manager of an Indian team that toured Japan. In between all that he is Professor of Mathematics at Delhi University. Once a year he visits the UK to take his place as the Indian represenative at Oxford University on the Rhode's Scholarship Selection Panel. We look forward to welcoming him to our rejuvinated Belgrave Hall this summer." Ed. items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Editorial on the growing television and sponsorship money in athletics and the need for it to reach clubs, officials and grass-roots support.
items.s: CHANGES AHEAD Editorial on the growing television and sponsorship money in athletics and the need for it to reach clubs, officials and grass-roots support. CHANGES AHEAD While at grass roots level little seems to be changing in the athletics world, at International level the gradual march towards Semi-Professionalism goes on unabated. The money which will come into our sport in the years ahead will pose special problems for Clubs and it is far from clear how it will all end. Take for example the pulling power of Televised events. From 1985 onwards the AAA's and BAAB will receive over a 5 year period monies exceeding £13.5 million from TV and sponsorship deals. Somehow much of this must come through to the Clubs and the AAA's recognise that without the support of Clubs, their officials, organising expertise and not least of all the support of the athletes themselves the whole thing could go badly wrong. The year ahead should see many points resolved and it is important that Belgrave has a view and a say in these important decisions. Whatever the outcome we must realise that our top athletes will be part of a world which we have not seen before. Let us hope that their hard work, dedication and talent will be fairly rewarded. Let us also hope that they will remember their roots and continue to support all those who have supported them in the past and who will continue to support them in the future. AAA's BAAB

items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Grapevine club gossip column: Tom Carter's presidential year, a birth for the Biscoes, John Gladwin's club 1500m record and drug test, members leaving for US universities, Charlie Gillett's music career and other personal news, Andy North and Michael Blackmore, and a new Gleave on the way.
items.s: grapevine Grapevine club gossip column: Tom Carter's presidential year, a birth for the Biscoes, John Gladwin's club 1500m record and drug test, members leaving for US universities, Charlie Gillett's music career and other personal news, Andy North and Michael Blackmore, and a new Gleave on the way. grapevine We were delighted to see President Tom Carter and Ethel at our British League home fixture in August. Ethel is making a rapid recovery following a stroke earlier in the year which required a brief period of hospitalisation. Although Tom must have found his Presidential year very demanding he has not missed any of our important meetings and visited members at Belgrave Hall at least 3 times per week. Getting results and news items from Gordon Biscoe has not always proved the easiest of tasks for your Editor. Not surprising, therefore, that the Belgravian of last April contained no details of a forthcoming happy event for Margaret and Gordon. On August 31st at Epsom District Hospital, Richard Dennis Edward Biscoe weighed in at a healthy 5lb 15oz. Congratulations from your many friends at Belgrave. Stuart Paton's Club 1500m record has been bettered several times this year by Stuart himself, Gary Staines and John Gladwin. When John finally reduced it to 3:39.47 at Meadowbank he also set another Belgrave first. Along with Steve Cram and Alan Wells, John was selected for drug testing. Training at the Belgrave Hall bar proved invaluable as John downed 7 lagers before obliging!! Kevin Sturman and Paul Richley departed our shores mid-summer for life at U.S. Universities. Kevin has returned to South Ilinois while Paul has gone to Iowa State with his sparring partner from Windsor - Andrew Pettigrew. Gordon Doubleday still visits us from Bath whenever possible. Gordon has recently been elected a Life Member of Somer A.C. and in September was re-elected President of "The Centurians" whose membership is confined to those walkers who have covered 100 miles in 24 hours. Our Vet sprints record holder - Charlie Gillett's hidden talents surfaced in a recent edition of The Sunday Telegraph's Colour Supplement. To quote the summary of a revealing 3 page article 'He is one of rock music's unsung heroes; an authoritative writer and broadcaster, a sharp talent spotter (he championed Elvis Costello and Dire Straights). His book, "The sound of the City", published in 1970 and now revised and re-issued, was a classic in a field which then hardly existed.' Funny how conversations with strangers often turn to running. A recent chat with a Leatherhead football club supporter revealed he had shared a bunkroom with Ted Stimpson in the 1940-41 war. 'Taffy' Jones sends his best wishes to Sargent Ted of 345 Heavy Anti Aircraft Battery - Royal Artillery. Taffy remembers "Ted was always dashing off somewhere to race a mile". Honary Coaching member Mike Dunphy and wife Ann are moving house from Welwyn Garden City to High Wycombe. Mike who has coached many of our fine middle distance men will be cutting back on some of his coaching commitments. We wish them happiness in their new house. Simon Williamson indicated to Bob Bridges that he would be unavailable for Southern League duties this summer. On being pressed he revealed that wedding bells in September were the reason. We wish the bride and groom good fortune. Remember those promising Youths -Andy North and Michael Blackmore? We hear that Andy has been invited to Michael's wedding in January but as it clashes with the Surreys we will have to lay on some high speed transport if our top Junior is to make both events. We also hear that there is another little Gleave on the way. Congrats and best wishes to Mum and Dad. items.s: MEMBERS HONOURED Report that the September AGM made Colin Pearson and Brian Gorman life members and elected Ernest Obeng, Harry Porter and Leo Coy Vice Presidents. MEMBERS HONOURED At the September AGM, Colin Pearson and Brian Gorman were voted life members for services to the Club. Colin has been active over the last 10 years or so providing support to Gordon Biscoe in running the Road and Cross Country Section. Brian Gorman is widely known for initiating new members to the joys of training over Wimbledon common. In addition he has looked after teas and sandwiches at Belgrave Hall every Saturday afternoon for many years and lays on a special spread for visiting teams. Truly one of our backroom boys' Unusually too we saw this year the election of 3 Vice Presidents at the AGM; Ernest Obeng for his services to the Club and for many years of International Standard performances, Harry Porter for his enormous work output as part of the small team building up our Ladies Section and Leo Coy who for 10 years has been responsible for compiling the U.K. 5000m, 1000m and 3000m S/C Rankings for NUTS. In addition Leo has been Results Secretary for the Southern League for the last 8 years and as joint team manager has played a major part in the building up of our 'A' track and field side which has gained promotion in each of the last 3 seasons. We are fortunate in having men of this quality taking on greater responsibilities for the future. items.s: DINNER DANCE Report on the oversubscribed club Dinner/Dance at Bourne Hall, Ewell, organised by Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard. DINNER DANCE A new organising duo, a change of date plus a change of venue provided the backdrop for this years Dinner/Dance. It was with some trepidation therefore, that Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard awaited the response as tickets went on sale. They need not have worried. By September the 175 places were over-subscribed with a waiting list for cancellations. So why such enthusiasm? Well the venue seemed a big attraction. Bourne Hall in Ewell provides extensive dining and separate dancing facilities in a village setting. Add to that music supplied by the popular 'Jaguars' and with the equally popular Ann and Bernie Ford as principal guests you have the formula for success. Our younger members were well represented and it was perhaps inevitable that our 3 fastest 1500m men would be among the unofficial 'cabaret' provided by the middle distance team. The raffle must surely have lost money (although 'No!' says Bill) as the glittering prizes were topped by non-other than a colour television. The evening proved a great success. Jenny and John Martin travelled all the way from Gloucestershire and Jenny's many Belgrave friends were delighted to see that she is now recovering from a period in hospital. Evelyn and Ted Stimpson were also official guests - a fitting honour in the year when Ted is honoured as President of the Middlesex AAA's. Congratulations then to Bill and Brian. We're already booking tickets for next year! items.s: COLD COMFORT Humorous note on John Rayner's triathlon in Leicester, where competitors changed in the open air after a cold quarry swim. COLD COMFORT John Rayner recently completed a couple of Triathlon's. After the first stage of an event in Leicester - a half mile swim in a deep quarry - all competitors (male and female) discarded their wet costumes together in the open air in preparation for the bike stage. At this point, one lady competitor commented that she didn't think the chaps were up to much. Apparently this was not a reference to their efforts in the swim, but rather to other factors brought about by the cold water! John Rayner John Rayner completed two triathlons Leicester

items.s: JOE COLEMAN - PRESIDENT Profile of new club President Joe Coleman, a member since 1927, walker and Grade 1 judge, with a photo of the Walking Section congratulating him. JOE COLEMAN - PRESIDENT Joe Coleman was elected a member on the 6th October 1927. From early days he was involved in all aspects of the Club and performed with distinction at Track and Field. In the mid thirty's he was scoring in our top Walking teams. He gained a first class standard in the 1938 AAA's Championships and won the coveted 'Fowler Dixon' style award. In 38 and 39 he was 3rd in our Open walk behind Harry Churcher. He achieved National 'fame' in 1939 when he and brother Len deadheated in the RWA National 10 mile Championship, and led Belgrave to a team win. Like many top class athletes his career was interrupted by the 2nd World War but he came back to score again in many of our Walking teams. In 1952 Joe was elected a Vice President of Surrey CAAA for whom he had competed in the Inter County Championships in earlier years. His experience and knowledge was passed on to many young athletes when he became a Grade 1 Judge in the early 1950's. Since then Joe has enhanced the reputation of Belgrave in the Walking World as he has travelled the Country judging top class events. A life time spent with the club and now the holder of its highest Office we can be certain that Belgravians will benefit from his vast experience and knowledge of the athletic world in the year ahead. items.sum: New President Joe Coleman's message thanking members for his election and calling for effort to revive the cross-country team and support the Ladies section.
items.s: From the President New President Joe Coleman's message thanking members for his election and calling for effort to revive the cross-country team and support the Ladies section. From the President Fellow Belgravians, Firstly, let me thank the council of P.P's who sorted me out for nomination and to the members at the A.G.M. who confirmed their nomination of me as the President of Belgrave Harriers for the coming year. I value this office very much, and since joining the Club in 1927 I have had great pleasure in rubbing shoulders with many fine men as athletes, officials and supporters of our club. We have enjoyed many successes, individually and teamwise in both running and walking sections of the club, and whilst the walkers have managed to maintain their winning ways, the X-Country men have not managed to match our pre-war and early post-war achievements not for the lack of endeavour but I do feel that if we made a real effort to harness our resources we could get the Bels singing again. The Track men have had some fine results likewise the younger age groups but Ladies section requires all the help and support we can give. The Roll of Presidents on the board at Belgrave Hall is an impressive one, and I will try to live up to the traditions that these men have set. Here's to the coming year, let us make it one to remember. Good Luck and every success to all members and sections of the Club. Joe Coleman. Joe Coleman Joe Coleman new club President; joined the club in 1927 AGM Belgrave Hall

items.sum: Tribute to W.G. 'Bill' Webb on his 90th birthday, recalling his cross-country running for Belgrave from 1927, with a photo of him holding a decanter.
e: South of Thames Cross Country Championships
items.s: W.G. 'BILL' WEBB - 90 YEARS YOUNG Tribute to W.G. 'Bill' Webb on his 90th birthday, recalling his cross-country running for Belgrave from 1927, with a photo of him holding a decanter. W.G. 'BILL' WEBB - 90 YEARS YOUNG On 9 August 1984 Bill Webb celebrated his 90th birthday. As he himself said, "There is nothing particularly meritorious in reaching 90, I just happened to be born with the right genes!" But he was also born with a charm which has endeared him to successive generations of Belgravians. Bill Webb joined Belgrave in 1927, following a period of six years at Polytechnic Harriers and several traumatic wasted years in the first World War. At 33 years of age he was a mature newcomer who made his mark immediately by finishing 8th in the Yacht '3' that year with 15:55 (off 25 secs). In only his second match for Belgrave he closed-in our scoring team just behind first-team regulars Wally Bayliss and Micky Pyer. The Belgravian Scribe was induced to write "The runners have lately been joined by W.G.Webb and A.Robertshaw and I suggest that the presence of these valuable men gives our team a new impetus of enthusiasm." Webb and Robertshaw were just the injection Belgrave needed and they celebrated by gaining bronze team medals in the South of Thames Senior of 1928 - our first medals in the event for 24 years! Bill went on to be our second scorer in the "Southern" and our first man home in the "National" at Leamington. A final flourish in the London-Brighton Relay and he had in one season established himself as a remarkably consistent runner who would always respond to the occasion. Within a year he was elected Captain. Bill Webb's charming disposition concealed a very determined athlete, but it also revealed a willing Belgravian prepared to step into the shoes of W.H.Hare who had done so much to improve our finances. In 1943 he was elected Honorary Treasurer, a post he held for 14 years, the longest on record. His service to the Club was first acknowledged in 1948 when he was elected President for two years. His 90th birthday was the occasion for fellow-Belgravians to make a further acknowledgement. At Belgrave Hall on Saturday 11 August a large gathering of members enjoyed a social evening in the company of Bill Webb who enraptured his audience with a lucid account of those early days. To mark the occasion our President, Tom Carter, presented him with a cut-glass decanter bearing a silver necklace engraved with the good wishes of the Club to which he has remained so loyal. W.G. items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Letter from Bill Webb to the President thanking fellow Belgravians for the gifts and gathering marking his 90th birthday.
items.s: Letter from Bill Webb to the President thanking fellow Belgravians for the gifts and gathering marking his 90th birthday. Dear Mr. President, I am only now recovering from the series of events occasioned by my reaching the age of 90 on the 9th August, 1984. I was overwhelmed with kindness, congratulations and good wishes which helped to make my day a very happy one. None more so than those wishes sent by fellow Belgravians, and the more tangible symbol of those wishes which you so graciously presented to me, on their behalf, at the special social gathering at the Belgrave Hall. It was a memorable and most emotive evening to me, and one which will be inscribed indelibly in my memory. Through you, Mr. President, I should like to express my humble and sincere thanks to all who so kindly and generously contributed to this most wonderful and truly Belgravian gesture. I do not apologise for having reached this specific age. Belgrave is partly responsible. I came to the club at the relative old age of 38, following what had been a traumatic period of my life. The club accepted me, rehabilitated me and made me feel younger and younger. I was proud to play a small part in a wonderful team whose ultimate goal was to win the highest honours in the field of athletics, and to own their own headquarters. They achieved both. I am happy to observe the quality and efficiency of our existing teams, to whom we all owe a debt of gratitude for the continuity of the Belgrave Tradition of "service to the club to the advantage of the whole". They will leave a bright light shining to guide their successors on their way. Bidding continued success to the Club. Sincerely, W.G. (Bill) Webb W.G. 'Bill' Webb W.G. (Bill) Webb reached 90 on 9 August 1984; says he joined the club aged 38 Belgrave Hall

items.s: MEMBERSHIP SECRETARY'S NOTES Membership Secretary's notes on club growth past 700 members and a plea for prompt subscriptions and address changes. MEMBERSHIP SECRETARY'S NOTES The growth of the Club has been quite noticeable during the last few years. Obviously with the influx of marathons we have picked up members on this front, but having done their "one off" retire to oblivion and are eventually deleted from our records. Despite this we have breached the genuine 700 members mark and are now heading to 800. I have, since taking over the job, requested efficiency in sending in subscriptions, change of address etc. but like most clubs, suffer from some who think reminders and requests do not apply to them. With that in mind, I should like every member to consider himself or herself as a link in the chain and not just a pebble on the beach.

items.sum: Report on the club's new committee and sub-committee structure approved at an EGM, and the changes of officers at the September AGM, with profiles of retiring Hon. Gen. Sec. Derek Crookes and his successor Bill Laws, and of retiring Hon. Treasurer Jim Heathfield and his successor Ron Severn.
items.s: OFFICIAL CHANGES Report on the club's new committee and sub-committee structure approved at an EGM, and the changes of officers at the September AGM, with profiles of retiring Hon. Gen. Sec. Derek Crookes and his successor Bill Laws, and of retiring Hon. Treasurer Jim Heathfield and his successor Ron Severn. OFFICIAL CHANGES Structure Our growing membership has resulted in greater activity in all sections and over the last few years it has become increasingly difficult to handle all Club business at monthly Committee meetings. Derek Crookes has been looking at ways of streamlining operations and his master plan was put to an EGM in the summer which approved the new arrangements. From now on the Committee will comprise of all Sectional Secretaries (or nominees) plus the Club's Trustees and 5 members elected at the AGM. Past Presidents may attend in a non-voting capacity and there will be many occasions when their specific past experiences and knowledge will be sought. In parallel with this re-organisation a series of Sub-Committees will be set up based on separate Sectional activities and interests. These groups will be charged with promoting their Sections activities and will produce plans, targets and budgets. It is intended that as our finances move back into a healthier state following the Belgrave Hall re-development programme, each Section will be provided with its own monies following approval by the Committee of individual Section's targets and budget plans. In this way individual Sectional Secretaries and Team Managers will have greater freedom in day to day operations and financial matters. Naturally proper accounting will be required and at the end of each year results will be compared with targets. It will be up to each Section to argue its case and get the funding it needs. We will need to feel our way into these new arrangements. New people are coming into the Management side. There will be difficulties but with our usual tolerance and understanding problems will be quickly ironed out and we can move to a simpler and more effective management system. People Each year at the September AGM we say farewell to the retiring President and welcome the new one. A hearty vote of thanks was given to Tom Carter for all his work during a year of office made particularly difficult by Ethel's illness. The meeting was particularly sad as both Derek Crookes and Jim Heathfield stepped down from office following terms of service spanning a period of time during which Belgrave's fortunes have seen a quite remarkable upturn. HON. GEN. SEC. Derek Crookes took over the post of Hon. Gen.Sec. in September 1978 and played an active and major part in the amalgamation plans. It was mainly Derek's efforts which resulted in the influx of the fine athletes and officials from Surrey A.C. who now play an important part in our expanding activities. During his 6 year period as Hon.Gen.Sec. Derek was elected President in 1981 and the following year served as joint President with Geoff Davis. In his final year of office he took the initiative in proposing and developing the re-organised Management Structure which has now come into operation. His services will not be lost completely as he has taken on the vacant post of Coaching Secretary. We can expect that there will soon be improvements to our Club Coaching arrangements once Derek has turned his full attention to the problems which currently exist. (For further details of Derek refer to the October 81 Belgravian). Bill Laws takes over as Ho.Gen.Sec. on the promise that the new Organisational Structure will make the job less onerous. Bill joined Belgrave in 1952 while at Emanuel School. His membership lapsed when he moved North and he rejoined in 1963. He became a Committee member in 1974 and organised the Dinner/Dance for 5 years. His forte is looking after special projects. He negotiated the Sports Council Grants for the 1976 Hall improvement and the G.L.C. Grants for the latest Hall developments. In 1982 Bill spent quite a lot of time persuading the GLC to invest in putting the all weather track at our home track in Battersea Park. Bill gained a first in Mech. Engineering at Brunel University. He is a Chartered Engineer and is a Fellow of the Institute of Mechanical Engineers and a Fellow of the Institute of Energy. He was Project Manager for Belgrave on the latest Hall Development. In his spare time he has Edited the Belgravian since September 1979 and after producing the last 10 Editions is looking for someone else to ease into the job over the next year or so. HON. TREASURER Jim Heathfield took over the job of Hon. Treasurer in September 1979 and under his careful control funds soon grew to a level which permitted the recent Hall development project to proceed. Whereas most Club Officials perform duties different from their business activities, with Jim Belgrave work was very much an additional burden as he is an Accountant within the Ministry of Defence! With turnover now well into 5 figures keeping all the Accounts and cash flows under control, is practically a full time occupation, and it is much to Jim's credit that he managed to convey an air of complete calm during periods of difficulty. Unlike many Accountants, Jim was always anxious that our hard won savings should be put to work for the Club's future and his wholehearted support for our development projects has been an essential part of the success story. Sadly Jim is 'resting down' due to pressure of work but hopes to become involved again in the not to distant future. We thank him for all his efforts on our behalf. Ron Severn has taken up the mantle of Hon. Treasurer and it would be difficult to find someone better qualified. A lawyer and Accountant by profession he has already made an impact in the short period he has been with Belgrave (see the April 84 Belgravian for a full C.V.!). Ron has been posing the sort of questions about our aims and aspirations which someone fresh to the scene can do. We welcome Ron to his first Belgrave Office and wish him good luck in the year ahead. items.sum: Report on the completed redevelopment of Belgrave Hall: the refurbished upstairs club room, remodelled changing rooms and busy new gymnasium, with thanks to the volunteers, the architect and donors to the Appeal Fund.
items.s: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Report on the completed redevelopment of Belgrave Hall: the refurbished upstairs club room, remodelled changing rooms and busy new gymnasium, with thanks to the volunteers, the architect and donors to the Appeal Fund. BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Well, its finished! And everyone who visits Belgrave Hall is amazed at the transformation of our Headquarters. Upstairs we have created one of the finest club rooms you could wish to find. With; new windows faithfully repeating the original pattern, a £6000 maple floor lovingly sanded and polished by Harry Porter, new gas fired radiators plus velvet curtains and carpets in club colours, we have a most fitting setting for the Club Honours Boards. Add to this delicate colouring scheme to augment the soft furnishings and it is no wonder that Bill Couzens has been inundated with requests to hire the new facility. Already bookings from Art and Exercise classes are near capacity and our investment is beginning to show the cash returns which the Finance Committee was predicting two years ago. Downstairs the mens changing facilities have been remodelled to give a slightly larger floor area following the removal of the old staircase. The interest in the new Gymnasium has been fantastic. Within three weeks of opening Mike Winch and Judy Oakes reported full capacity with opening on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m. International athletes from as far afield as St. Albans make the trek to Belgrave Hall to obtain the benefit of the new facilities. Many of our members including nine of our British League team now train regularly in the Gymnasium with Mike and we look forward to big improvements in their 1985 performances. Interspersed with the specialist training sessions are strength and fitness classes for ladies and other members of the public. All this is again providing a big boost to our income. Now that the operating patterns are getting sorted out following the inevitable teething problems, we can look forward to a good social calendar and hopefully you will come along and take advantage of your Club's facilities. We are indeed fortunate that a major scheme of this nature can be planned, financed and progressed solely through the voluntary work so freely given by a few of our loyal members. Let us, therefore, through the pages of the Belgravian thank all who gave so much of their time and efforts and in particular; Ian Horton whose original conceptual designs formed the basis for the scheme as it has evolved, Tom Carter who has acted as Clerk of the Works making frequent site visits to check progress, Bill Couzens who has been responsible for specifying and procuring the various services, Bill Laws who was Project Manager and finally Harry Porter who has saved the Club so much money by putting the finishing touches to the Contractor's structural work. We also owe a big debt of thanks to our Architect - David Lawton, R.I.B.A. who fulfilled the targets we set with great dedication and professionalism and at a fee especially reduced as his contribution to this worthwhile project. And finally a big thank you to all those who have contributed to the Development by responding to our Appeal Fund. Over the two years to June 1984 donations totalled £1,496 but were swelled in September following a direct appeal by Past President Charlie Manning which added a further £1,085 to the funds for the Hall development. items.s: 1983/84 ACCOUNTS Summary of the club's 1983/84 annual accounts, with a table showing net income of £10,587 against expenses of £9,709 and a surplus of £878 (the text itself calls £10,587 the year's running expenses). 1983/84 ACCOUNTS At one time our Annual Accounts could be summarised on two sheets of paper. This year it took four sheets including five separate schedules to detail Jim Heathfield's report to the 1984 A.G.M. During the year to July 1st 1984 our total running expenses had reached a record £10,587 while income from subscriptions achieved a record - but far from adequate - £3,417. The shortfall as usual was met from income derived by those hardworking members who freely devote so much of their time to club activities. The only area where there was a reduction in income this year was that of Hall Hire. Revenue from letting reduced to zero during the re-building of Belgrave Hall which started in March 1984. The 1984 Accounts can be summarized as follows:- Leaving a surplus for the year of £878 on the Revenue Account. A most satisfactory achievement considering the cash flow requirements associated with the Hall Development. items.s: Gordon Doubleday's note on meeting veteran member Edmund Donovan, O.B.E., a Belgravian since before the First World War, on a visit to London from New York. Gordon Doubleday recently made a lightning trip from Bath to London to meet Edmund Donovan who is visiting London from the U.S.A. with wife Daye. Gordon writes - "One of our oldest members, Edmund Donovan, O.B.E. was recently over here from New York where he lives. He was a Belgravian before the 1914-18 War, afterwards he went to the U.S.A. Unfortunately an accident to his hip has left him mostly confined to an invalid chair. His interest in the Club is undiminished and he always looks forward to reading the "Belgravian". He was accompanied by his charming wife Daye who originated from Fulham. Edmund is intensely proud of being a Belgravian and sings our praises in the U.S.A. He recalled C.C. runs from the "Spenser Arms" and the "Green Man" from former Club H.Q's and of course, Battersea Park. He sends his regards to all, particularly those who he knows." items.s: WALKING Carl Lawton's review of the walking section's year: a National 10 win and other team placings, Graham Seatter's Leicester Mercury win, British vests for Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall, and the Ladies Section led by Rachel Parrott. WALKING Casting ones thoughts back to the beginning of the year, we visualised having the strongest distance team for many years. But it did not materialize. We were unable to have our fittest teams out when needed and things did not work out. However, we did have partial success - the win in the National 10 was followed by 2nd in the 20kms and 2nd in the 35kms, but 7th in the 50kms with a team average age of 45 was not something to write home about. Regretably we ended up having to have only John Keown flying the flag for us in the Hastings and the Brighton which I fear is no credit to us by not being able to turn out teams. Maybe next year will be different. Paul Warburton has returned to England after his 12 months in America and he hopefully replaces, in person, if not speed, Graham Seatter who has helped Belgrave to various placings during the year, and not forgetting his win in the Leicester Mercury in 2:26.56. Congratulations to Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall on gaining British Vests during the year. Regretably Stephen has had his year torn apart due to work commitments. One must not forget that we have a Ladies Section and although not quite as prolific as the men we have been turning out teams and individuals at various events with Rachel Parrott cleaning up all age club records. items.s: 14th JULY 1984 KENDAL NATIONAL 50km. National 50km walk at Kendal, where after Carl Lawton withdrew four Belgrave Johns finished to give the team seventh place. 14th JULY 1984 KENDAL NATIONAL 50km. The long journey north to the pleasant lakeland region, which despite early complaints, only took 3 hours on the train, proved rather disappointing following our placings in the previous three championships. With only five starters and the withdrawal of Carl Lawton after 35kms, it was left to the four Johns to bring home a team average age 45! John Hall got the better of John Llewellin, while John Dunsford, not on his best form, kept going too ahead of John Keown. items.sum: Introduction to the track and field section, noting promotion of the 'A' team to Division 3 of the British Athletics League and the 'B' team to Division 2 of the Southern League, and naming the report writers.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Introduction to the track and field section, noting promotion of the 'A' team to Division 3 of the British Athletics League and the 'B' team to Division 2 of the Southern League, and naming the report writers. TRACK AND FIELD Our track and field management teams seem to be coping well with the burgeoning* activities of our Track and Field activities. You will see from the following reports that on all fronts our Senior Men are setting new high standards and we have seen for the first time promotion of our 'A' team to Division 3 of the GRE sponsored British Athletics League plus the promotion of our 'B' team to Division 2 of the Southern League following an astounding year when they have gained maximum possible match points. The British League and GRE Cup reports have been prepared by joint team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws, the Southern League reports by joint team managers Bob Bridges and Alan Mead. Add to this the 'Steve Williams' roundup and we think you will find entertaining reading. * This is Stuart Paton's 'Word of the month'!!!! Leo Coy Leo Coy joint British League team manager Bill Laws Bill Laws joint British League team manager Bob Bridges Bob Bridges joint Southern League team manager Alan Mead Alan Mead joint Southern League team manager Steve Williams Steve Williams writer of a roundup Stuart Paton Stuart Paton British Athletics League Southern League GRE Cup

items.s: BRITISH LEAGUE ROUNDUP British Athletics League match 1 at Cleckheaton, where a depleted Belgrave team finished fourth, 13 points behind winners Windsor, with full results. BRITISH LEAGUE ROUNDUP 12th MAY 1984 CLECKHEATON GRE/BAL MATCH 1 The prospect of a 500 mile return trip must have proved unpalatable for 5 of our Team who missed the luxury coach booked for this fixture near Leeds. As it was the decimated team of 18 of our 'A' team men plus Andy Paton drafted in from the large group of supporters only missed winning this first fixture by 13 points, but so close was the match that we finished in 4th place. Windsor who had travelled up the night before, turned out as victors and there is little doubt for future long journeys, we must plan an overnight stay. Pat Lyttle was our only recognised sprinter but having competed for a point in the 'B' hammer, fatigue took its toll and our sprint results were poor. Ken Onuaguluchi, Phil Lovell, Mark Shippen, Aham Amadi and Derrick Williams added respectability to the field events while in the middle distance, Stu Paton won the 400 and John Gladwin got outkicked by a certain Steve Crabb! Andy Paton, Chris Cornwall made their debut in the BAL. Note: Aham beat Derrick in the triple by 14 cms. Read on ..... items.sum: British Athletics League match 2 at Enfield, a wet day of mishaps in which Belgrave finished third, with full results.
items.s: 17th JUNE 1984 ENFIELD GRE/BAL MATCH 2 British Athletics League match 2 at Enfield, a wet day of mishaps in which Belgrave finished third, with full results. 17th JUNE 1984 ENFIELD GRE/BAL MATCH 2 Following our fourth place at Cleckheaton, the Bels. Team had a much better look for Match 2. The day turned out wet and thundery and matched the appearance of the team managers as we had a years quota of disasters in one match. We got off to a flying start with new member Tony Pamah winning the 400m in style and Mark backing up well in the 'B' with 2nd place. Dave Armstrong's blocks slipped in the 100, Phil Lovell fell foul of an over zealous judge and the weather in the pole vault and failed his opening height, and John Aska despite a dash by taxi just missed the hammer. Apart from the disasters this meeting was one of the best that we have been involved in to date - the competition was fierce, especially the 400 and 400 relay with John Gladwin running 49.1 and finishing 5th. In the 400 relay we recorded one of our best times for years and finished last. Our other wins came from Gary (800m), Stu (1500), John (5000 B), Derek and Aham (Triple), Ken (discus and shot) also worth recording was Vince Cornibert, who threw a marvellous 60 metres in the Javelin and Phillip Goedluck who ran a great 200m and short relay. Andrew Rodney, Dave Armstrong, Phillip Goedluck, Tony Pamah, Derek Brown and Snowy Brooks (15 years since his debut in the British League) all made their first appearance. Note: Derrick beat Aham in the triple jump by 2 cms. Read on ..... items.s: 8th July 1984 WINDSOR GRE/BAL MATCH 3 British Athletics League match 3 at Windsor, which Belgrave won with 273 points in probably their best ever team performance, assuring promotion to Division 3; with full results. 8th July 1984 WINDSOR GRE/BAL MATCH 3 After Enfield we were in 3rd spot in the League and if we stayed there then we would be in Division three in 1985. At Windsor we aimed to consolidate this position. As it turned out this was probably the greatest team ever fielded by Belgrave and the best result in any T & F Match in our long history. Colin Gaynor returned to strengthen our sprints despite having problems with his hamstring. This made an enormous difference to our sprints. The remainder of the team were superb. It is worth reading the results in detail. Andrew Rodney, Phillip Goedluck won the 'B' sprints in style - Jeremy Levine gave a boost to the high jump - Vince won the javelin, beating in style those who had been in front of him all season. Jeremy Levine, Steve Smullen and Henry Cooper all made their British League debut. Promotion to Div.3 was assured as a result of this victory, and there remained an outside chance of victory. items.s: 18th AUGUST 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE/BAL MATCH 4 British Athletics League match 4, a Belgrave home promotion at Battersea Park, where a weakened team recorded a record 15 event wins but finished second to Windsor; with full results. 18th AUGUST 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE/BAL MATCH 4 After our great win at Windsor, the last round match was a Belgrave home promotion at Battersea and what a great day it was - Geoff Davis did an amazing job - we had more officials than in the Coliseum, L.A. The GLC also did us proud with Battersea looking in great shape. Our Team was in great shape too, but with the Nike Classic claiming Stu Paton, John Gladwin and Ernest Obeng and holidays accounting for Ken Onuaguluchi and Vince Cornibert, plus Paul Richley off to the U.S. we were just a bit short of our top men. Nevertheless we recorded 15 wins, our highest ever, but we were pipped by Windsor on the day. Mark Sinclair chased Gary in the 1500 and both recorded good times - Mark ran a P.B. just missing sub 3.50. John Bicourt won the S/C in 9:05.5 a brilliant run for a 38 year old youngster! Neil Phillips won the 'B' discus as did Snowy in the 'B' shot. A great day with the Bels. still on the up - Div. 3 next year! Thanks to all athletes, officials, recorders, groundsmen and helpers for a meeting that was typically Belgrave - just perfect. Neil Phillips made his debut in the BAL team. Note: Aham beat Derrick in the triple jump by 1cm! to make it 3:1 for the series. items.s: For Your Diary. BRITISH LEAGUE FIXTURES FOR 1985 Notice of the 1985 British Athletics League Division 3 fixtures and the GRE Cup semi-final and final dates. For Your Diary. BRITISH LEAGUE FIXTURES FOR 1985 As we go to the printers we learn of the fixtures and venues for the 1985 B.A.L. Div.3 Matches. These dates may seem a long way off but for all our 'A' team men please note in particular the first date - 11th May at Enfield. We know from this summer that we will need to make a better start in Div.3 if we are to have any chance of promotion to Div.2. (* or Battersea Park if Tooting isn't ready) Please note there's a 6 week gap in July/August between matches and hopefully holidays can be fitted in to avoid these important B.A.L. fixtures. The GRE Cup Semi-Finals will be held on Sunday, 4th August with the final on Saturday 31st August/Sunday 1st September at Copthal Stadium. items.s: GRE CUP ROUNDUP Round-up of Belgrave's 1984 GRE Cup campaign, second in the second round at Battersea Park but a disappointing seventh in the semi-final at Copthall, with event-by-event results from both matches. GRE CUP ROUNDUP While our quarter final match at Battersea provided a result which promised well for the semi's, we failed to make the finals finishing a dismal 7th at Copthall following the late withdrawal of several of our top performers. Our throws were depleted with with Kenny 'O' taking a well deserved holiday in Nigeria and Derrick Williams was forced to withdraw from the jumps as a result of being knocked over by a car the day before. The main problem with Cup Matches is that with only one athlete per event it is difficult to get travelling reserves to attend away matches. Consequently when our sprint representative failed to appear for the 200 and sprint relay we were hard pressed to make up the numbers. 28th MAY 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE CUP 2ND ROUND 100m 2.A.Rodney 11.2; 200m 3.S.Richards 22.9; 400m 3.G.Sagar 50.4; 800m 4.P.Richley 1:57.0; 1500m 1.P.Ric[illegible]ley 3:55.5; 5000m 5.M.Lake 15:41.4; 10,000m 3.D.Jenkins 33:43.8; 3000m S/C 1.M.Hayes 9:17.2; 110H 1.A.Pamah 15.5; 400H 1.A.Pamah 54.8; DT 1.K.Onuaguluchi 52.68; SP 1.K.Onuaguluchi 14.06; HT 4.H.Cooper 39.10; JT 3.D.Mole 50.64; HJ =3 C.Cornwell 1.75; TJ 6.D.Hollingworth 11.65; PV 1.P.Lovell 4.60; 4x100 2.BELS. 44.3; 4x400 2.BELS 3:26.0. items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1984 Southern League season, in which the team won every match to gain promotion straight back to Division 2.
items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP Review of Belgrave's 1984 Southern League season, in which the team won every match to gain promotion straight back to Division 2. SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP After the disappointing 1983 season when the 'B' team slipped to Division 3 in the Southern League, the Bels came roaring back in 1984 to win every single match and have bounced straight into Division 2. Not only did every match result in victory but the points scores were phenomenal - our highest being a massive 160 out of a possible 180 (which would need a win in every event, 'A' and 'B'). Our average score over the season was as high as we have ever attained in any single Southern League match over the past 15 years. Why the change in our Fortunes? The reason surely is our increasing depth of good performers in virtually all events, and here we must thank Eddie Bojtler for pushing so many athletes in our direction. Now that our 4th, 5th and 6th ranked men can produce 40 metre hammer throws, run sub-23 200 metres etc., it means that even with athletes barred through 'A' team duty in the National League side, or on holiday or injured, we can still turn out an impressive 'B' side. Now it's time to think of 1985. Can we go straight through Division 2 to the Southern League's premier competition? Its possible. And with members now having to prove themselves to get an outing with our 'B' side, perhaps we should start thinking seriously about a 'C' team - if we can find the officials to get it going! Eddie Bojtler Eddie Bojtler thanked for bringing many athletes to the club Southern League

items.s: 26th AUGUST 1984 NORMAN PARK INTER-CLUB Report and results of an inter-club meeting at Norman Park, hosted by Blackheath, against visiting Belgian club Hermes Oostende. 26th AUGUST 1984 NORMAN PARK INTER-CLUB When we sent a 12 man team to Ostend last March we knew that Hermes Oostende would be visiting the U.K. for a Track and Field meeting. Blackheath were hosts this year and at short notice we managed to pull together a respectable team which turned in some good performances. Our new 16 year old sprinter Marcus Adam ran well in his first outing in Belgrave colours, while in the field events new member Tony Featherstone set some markers, which reflected his lack of competition for the last 2 years, and no doubt he will be seeking to annihilate them next year.
