items.h: TRACK AND FIELD ROUNDUP - NON LEAGUE MEETS
items.sum: Steve Williams' round-up of Belgrave performances at non-league meetings in 1984, including Stuart Paton's SCAAA 800m title, three Inter-Counties champions, and the club 1500m record falling to Paton and then John Gladwin, with all-time 1500m list and record progression.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD ROUNDUP - NON LEAGUE MEETS Steve Williams' round-up of Belgrave performances at non-league meetings in 1984, including Stuart Paton's SCAAA 800m title, three Inter-Counties champions, and the club 1500m record falling to Paton and then John Gladwin, with all-time 1500m list and record progression. TRACK AND FIELD ROUNDUP - NON LEAGUE MEETS BY STEVE WILLIAMS Some Early Season Odds and Ends 1 Feb TVH 3000m 1 J Gladwin 8.19.3 25 Apr SCAAA Rep Match TJ D Williams 14.60 DT K Onuaguluchi 50.00 SCAAA 3000m Champs. P Richley 8.20.90 29 Apr Enf 400mh A Pamah 55.2 2 May SCAAA Rep Match 800m 1 J Gladwin 1.48.6 DT K Onuaguluchi 51.14 1500m Gst. M Sinclair 3.51.5 6 May UAU Champs 200m C Gaynor 22.0 9 May BMC 1500m 1 J Gladwin 3.49.0, M Sinclair 3.53.1 16 May Lough v Bor Rd 100/200 E Obeng 10.5/21.4 PV P Lovell 4.60 LJ D Williams 7.01 23 May Civ Serv Rep LJ/TJ D Williams 6.98/14.66 27 May UK Champs 1500m S Paton 3.52.72Ht G Staines 4.00.45Ht SCAAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - C/PALACE - 1/2 JUNE - STUART PATON - 800M CHAMPION There was an excellent turn out for this year's 'Southern' and plenty of good performances with Stuart Paton topping the bill by taking his first Southern Championship in his 'second' event - the 800m. Stuart always looked the danger man in what was a slow race early on as he covered every move of the leader. As they entered the final straight Stu' quickly opened a gap on the rest and comfortably held it to the line for an impressive win. In the field, there were fine silver medals for Phil Lovell, who duplicated his performance of last year, and Ken Onuaguluchi, whose Discus series included 53.80 for a further improvement in our club record. Other pb's came from Mike Hayes- who made virtually all the running to win the 'standards' steeplechase (why he didn't meet the championship 'cut off' is something of a mystery) and from Aham Amadi in the Triple Jump. 400m P Lyttle 51.26ht G Sagar 50.17ht,50.44sf 800m 1 S Paton 1.50.49 1500m 11 G Staines 3.54.61 (3.48.49ht) P Richley 3.49.72ht M Sinclair 3.52.70ht 3000mSc(Standards) 1 M Hayes 9.13.76 400mh A Pamah 55.94ht PV 2 P Lovell 4.60 5= M Shippen 4.20 TJ 9 A Amadi 14.63 DT 2 K Onuaguluchi 53.80. HFC OLYMPIC TRIALS - C/PALACE - 6 JUNE:- Qualifying conditions were certainly tough for our two men-John Gladwin and Phil Lovell-but rightly so with Olympic places at stake. John faced an 800m final 2 1/4 hours after running 1.47.46 in the heats to qualify as a fastest loser- and that after a recent bout of illness. Sadly, he had little left to offer for the final and finished 8th in 1.49.46. Meanwhile,Phil faced an opening height of 4.80 in the vault- only 10cm below his best of last year. He gave it three good shots but made his exit. AAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - C/PALACE - 23/24 JUNE - STUART PATON TAKES 1500M RECORD DOWN A NOTCH 100m- Ernest Obeng had been running into form with 10.47/21.25 for Loughbro' v AAA on 17 June and 10.55 to win an invitation meet in Belfast two days later, but he was below par here and didn't make the final. 11.07ht, 10.80sf. 800m- John Gladwin's heat time of 1.47.51 saw him through to the final as a fastest loser. The next day, John seemed without confidence at the start and he brought up the rear until the final straight when he found a way past Brown and Billy on the inside - but the medals were beyond recall. (1 Cram 1.46.84 6 J Gladwin 1.47.47.) 1500m- In the public eye, this event was notable for Elliott's defeat of the eventual Olympic Champion but for Belgrave supporters, attention was focused on Stuart Paton's attempt to make up for his disappointment of last year when not fully fit. With only 2 to go through from each heat by right, making the final was tough enough but Stu' was well placed throughout and produced the fastest finish to snatch first place on the line from Williamson - it may only have been a heat but nobody was sparing themselves at the end. The time - a new club record of 3.42.69. Of course it all had to be done again the next day and Stu' couldn't get up to the sharp end of a very tactical race. Nevertheless he recorded another 3.42 - and no doubt gained a lot from the experience. ( 1 Elliott 3.39.66 2 Coe 3.39.79 10 S Paton 3.42.98.) Pole Vault- Phil Lovell seemed stuck on 4.60 upto this stage of the season and that was again the height he achieved here in 7th place. Nevertheless a fine placing in a national championship. Discus- Ken Onuaguluchi was seen lofting out his warm up throws a long way but he couldn't catch a really big one in the competition. His best was a solid 52.58 and put him also in 7th place. --------------------- Paul Richley made a long trip up to Stretford worthwhile on 26 June by running an excellent 3.48.7 in a BMC 1500m while Gary Staines took his 800m pb down to 1.50.0 in a BMC race at West London on 4 July. INTER COUNTIES CHAMPIONSHIPS - BIRMINGHAM - 1 JULY - THREE CHAMPIONS More Belgravians than ever before found their way to these championships as County selections. Titles were taken by Ernie Obeng(Sy)100m in 10.25w, a CBP and Ernie's 5th win in 7 years - a magnificent record; by Gary Staines(Herts)- the Mile in 4.09.53 - and Phil Lovell, finding some improved form (4.75) in the Pole Vault. Good points were also earned by Tony Pamah(Kent) 4th in the 400mh in 55.4 and Ken Onuaguluchi(Sy) 2nd in the Discus with 52.16. After a 4.11.15 heat in the mile, Stu' Paton dropped to 4.16.90 in the final for 9th place. LAURISTON MILE - BATTERSEA PARK - 4 JULY:- This annual event saw three Bels way ahead of the field. Mark Sinclair took the lead straight away aiming for a fast run and John Warren made every use of the pace on Mark's shoulder. John had to let Mark go just before the bell as Mark kicked on to win in a useful 4.13.6 but John was rewarded with a pb of 4.18.7 in 2nd. Dave North completed the trio with 4.21.4. ENGLAND v SPAIN v SWEDEN - GATESHEAD 6 JULY - JOHN (AND GARY) TAKE STUART'S RECORD John Gladwin won further International selection for England over 1500m in this match and Gary Staines received a late invitation to run as a guest following his Inter-Counties win. So there was special interest as these two clashed for the first time. As usual, Gary got stuck in with the leaders straight away with John tucked in behind. In the final sprint, John squeezed past Gary but four others were just ahead in a blanket finish. Both men dipped under Stu's recent mark and the middle distance record spree was truly underway.(1 Theriot 3.41.28 2 Hutchings 3.41.33 5 J Gladwin 3.41.45 6 G Staines 3.41.76).Ernie Obeng ran as a guest in the 100m placing 2nd to McFarlane in 10.5. PEUGEOT/TALBOT GAMES - C/PALACE - 13 JULY - 1000m RECORD:- John Gladwin took our club record for 1000m down to 2.19.14 although not helped by some uneven pacemaking, while Stu' Paton was also inside the previous best - which he held - with 2.21.37. Ernie Obeng was ahead of a former World record holder (Williams) and a former Olympic champion (Crawford) as he took 3rd place in the 100m in 10.69. EDINBURGH GAMES - MEADOWBANK - 17 JULY - JOHN GOES UNDER 3.40 WITH STUART JUST BEHIND Four days after their meeting in London, John and Stuart were brought together again for an invitation 1500m on Stu's 'home' track and both men again earned pb's - a couple of classy times (shown at the top of the All Time list) and forward placings in a large field behind the World Record holder who won in 3.36.90. Both men finished well and will go faster when hanging on further up the front of one of these pace made races. items.label: October 1984
items.h: GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD
items.sum: Notes on Gary Staines equalling the club mile record at West London Stadium and running well in a gale at Jarrow, and John Gladwin winning an international 1500m in Taipei.
items.s: GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD Notes on Gary Staines equalling the club mile record at West London Stadium and running well in a gale at Jarrow, and John Gladwin winning an international 1500m in Taipei. GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD GARY STAINES equalled the club mile record at West London Stadium on 5 September when winning the Open Graded 'A' race in 4.02.1 on one of the first cold evenings of the late Summer. But those weather conditions were nothing compared to the gale force winds he had to contend with four days later at a meeting to open the new Jarrow track. That Gary should run 4.03.67 was therefore an exceptional effort. Cram and Walker were less than 6, and 5, seconds ahead, respectively and if you reckon on them being worth 3.49/3.50 normally , it shows the true merit of Gary's run. ------------ Members of this club have competed in many parts of the World but new ground must have been broken by John Gladwin when he won an International 1500m in Taipei in September in 3.52.25 and took second place in the 800 in 1.48.92. So if you get offered a job lot of training shoes - made in Taiwan - you'll know where they came from! items.label: October 1984
items.h: ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS
items.sum: Account of Ernest Obeng's 1984 season, including his expulsion from the Los Angeles Olympics by Ghanaian officials and his late-season return to form, with a photograph from the Peugeot Games.
items.s: ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS Account of Ernest Obeng's 1984 season, including his expulsion from the Los Angeles Olympics by Ghanaian officials and his late-season return to form, with a photograph from the Peugeot Games. ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS 1984 was a year of mixed fortune for our leading sprinter. He struggled to find his best form early on but it was Olympic year and, having missed out on Moscow, Ernie was encouraged enough to pay his own way to LA for probably his last chance to compete in the great event. Well no doubt you know the story of Ernie's expulsion from the Games by Ghanaian officials in what seems an incredible case of victimisation. It was obviously a great disappointment to him not to be able to compete and the character assassination that went with the affair added insult to injury. It was perhaps some small consolation to Ernie that he should hit some of his best ever form in August - as if to show that he would have performed with great credit to his country in LA. For following a couple of ordinary clockings at the Nike Classic and in Budapest when still coping with jet lag, he flew to a 10.25 timing (his 3rd fastest legal mark) in Zurich on 22 August, only headed by Olympic Bronze Medallist Ben Johnson and Osvaldo Lara - winner of the Eastern Block 'Friendship' Games. Then in Rieti,Italy on 2 September he recorded 10.32 (+0.7) behind Penalver and Lara. At the IAC/Coca-Cola meeting on 7 September, Ernie gave us at home the first glimpse of this return to form. He snapped away from the blocks to win his heat easing up in 10.45 into a slight headwind - but what a pity the start of the final was such a shambles with McFarlane getting a clear flyer and the race not being recalled by the starter. Although Lara's pick-up enabled him to win, Ernie,at a disadvantage with his own fast start pre-empted, couldn't quite make up the deficit and he finished 3rd in 10.38. Ernest Obeng's Belgrave Honours badge well to the fore in the Peugeot Games held at the Crystal Palace on July 13th, - probably the last occasion he will wear Ghana's colours as he has vowed not to compete again for the Country which treated him so shabbily in Los Angeles Olympics. Wells won in 10.46. Press Association Photo. items.sum: Bill Laws' report on the 1984 Nike 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace, where Belgrave's A team finished second nationally to Sale, with the leg times of all four Belgrave teams.
items.s: Nike Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile Bill Laws' report on the 1984 Nike 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace, where Belgrave's A team finished second nationally to Sale, with the leg times of all four Belgrave teams. Nike Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile 29th SEPTEMBER 1984 CRYSTAL PALACE NIKE 25x1 MILE RELAY Last year's first ever win in this Nationwide event led us to hope that with a better team (on paper) we could repeat our success. Sale running at Manchester had other ideas and as our 'A' team turned in times just marginally slower than we had anticipated Sale improved on their efforts of last year. We ran as usual at the Crystal Palace venue while 80 or so teams competed at 8 other venues. The race was close right up to the 18 mile mark when Pat Chester running for TVH ran a 4.08 effort to snatch the lead from the Bels. Nigel Clarke got a bit carried away on the next leg as the excitement built and ran his first 400 in 57.7! It was left to Peter Gilbey to take us into a lead which increased to 3 minutes over TVH over the next 5 miles. Everyone had been blaming the cold windy conditions for the 'slow' times, but either they were wrong or Gary Staines' 4.06 on the last leg was really something special. Running at even pace Gary finished in great style and even had to contend with being baulked by 2 Croydon runners who ran right in front of him as they changed the baton at the 2 lap mark. Several of our 'A' team men had just returned from holidays and it showed in their times. Our youngsters though ran superbly with Youths John Booth and Glyn Tiernan performing well as did Junior Richard O'Hara who is beginning to look a class runner. In the 'B' team Francis Ward, who has returned from 2 years in the U.S.A. proved fastest with Andy Moore close behind. Our 'D' team comprised young members having an average age of 13 years and their general high level of performance promises well for the future. Our thanks to Bill Couzens, Brian Pritchard and Derek Jones plus their families who put up with the trying conditions while organising and recording through the morning and afternoon sessions. Jim and Dave Mote organised the Young Athletes and yours truly the 'A'. Bill Laws Result: 1.Sale H 1:53.42; 2.BELGRAVE (A) 1:54.19; 3.Aldershot F & D 1:56.41; 4.T.V.H. 1:56.46; 5.S.L.H. 1:58.38. items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1984 Rosenheim League season, with seniors and Youths results from four matches and the Youths' second place in the final behind Herne Hill.
items.s: ROSENHEIM LEAGUE Review of Belgrave's 1984 Rosenheim League season, with seniors and Youths results from four matches and the Youths' second place in the final behind Herne Hill. ROSENHEIM LEAGUE (Non-scoring performances in brackets) The Rosenheim League again provided some essential competition for rising and falling stars alike (and those who never made it). The Senior team was always short of one or two of our better men to compete with the likes of Herne Hill and South London who take the League more seriously than ourselves but the Youths performed with credit to make the final where they finished second to Herne Hill despite being without a specialist sprinter. Notable performances over the season came from Pat Lyttle (22.0) Steve Smullen (3.53.6) and Mark Sinclair (8.21.2). Also Mike Hayes and John Bicourt, under 6 minutes for the 2km chase. First year Youth, Clive Gardner ran a fast 23.6 200m while Glyn Tiernan, the same age, looked impressive in the middle distances. Youths field eventers, Julian Mole and Festos Ogwuda, were both over 12 metres in the triple jump - which is good jumping. But perhaps the best performance of all came from 12 year old Adrian Ross who zipped round one lap in 61.1 for a remarkable new club colts record. items.s: Anecdote about sprinter Pat Lyttle's mis-recorded time in the 25 x 1 mile relay, which led him to run again in the B team. Sprinter Pat Lyttle couldn't accept his 6.57 timing in the 25 x 1 mile relay C team. It seemed there was an arithmetic error but the mistake wasn't apparent. So Pat stayed for the afternoon's B team and ran 5.51!! The morning's figures were then re-checked and sure enough it was 5.57. Sorry Pat - they said. Anyway Pat got 2 p.b's in 1 day. Not bad! There will be no excuses for not running a 48.5, 400m next season. Pat Lyttle Pat Lyttle ran 5.51 for 1 mile in the B team after a mis-timed 5.57 in the C team Nike 25x1 Mile Relay

items.sum: Note on Gary Staines' week in July 1984 in which he ran five top races, including winning the Inter-Counties mile and racing for England at Gateshead.
items.s: GARY STAINES' EXTRAORDINARY WEEK. Note on Gary Staines' week in July 1984 in which he ran five top races, including winning the Inter-Counties mile and racing for England at Gateshead. GARY STAINES' EXTRAORDINARY WEEK. Team spirit has been a particular part of our continueing upward path in the British Athletics League. Perhaps the most remarkable example was the case of Gary Staines who in one hectic week in July ran 5 top class races. On the Sunday he ran a heat and won the final of the Inter-Counties 1 mile. On the Wednesday in an Open Meeting he ran a p.b. 800m in 1.50.0. On the Friday he worked in the morning and then dashed up to Gateshead to guest in the England v Spain v Sweden International where he ducked under Stuart's 1500m Club record and was prominant on Television as he led for 3 laps . And on the Saturday he travelled with the BAL team to Windsor and won the 800m as we achieved a massive points win over our rivals. With support like that our Officials know that all the hard work behind the scenes is worthwhile! Gary Staines Gary Staines won Inter-Counties 1 mile; 800m p.b. 1.50.0; broke club 1500m record in England v Spain v Sweden at Gateshead; won BAL 800m at Windsor Stuart Stuart previous holder of club 1500m record British Athletics League Inter-Counties England v Spain v Sweden Gateshead Windsor

items.h: OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST
items.sum: Report and full results of the Yacht 3 handicap at Wimbledon on 6 October 1984, won from scratch by Oliver Foote with the 4th fastest time ever on the course behind Gerry North's three.
items.s: OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST Report and full results of the Yacht 3 handicap at Wimbledon on 6 October 1984, won from scratch by Oliver Foote with the 4th fastest time ever on the course behind Gerry North's three. OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST 6th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON YACHT 3 HANDICAP It is very seldom that the speedy scratch markers take the handicapper to the cleaners in this event. Generally a few of our slower runners manage to leg it off an over-generous mark. This year it was different due to some exceptionally fine runs from our faster men. Chris Millbank showed what progress a year's training can provide as he knocked a remarkable 2½ minutes off last years debut time. First year Junior, Richard O'Hara translated his recent track form to a fine first run round this course as too did Marcello Bizio. Leo Lyons showed a return to form after prolonged injury while 15 year old Gary McGurren ran an exceptional 16.16 in his first attempt at this event. But pride of place must go to Oliver Foote who took the field apart as he moved from scratch through to take the lead at Wimbledon Village after which he coasted to a 9 sec. lead. His time of 14.34 was the 4th fastest ever round this traditional Club course, the first three all being recorded by Gerry North (14.15, 14.21, and 14.21). Gerry's 14.15 clocking was in 1962 - the year he won the English Senior National Cross Country Champs. As Steve Williams remarked - "This was Oliver's finest win to date". Several ladies competed in this years race, fastest of whom was new member Jill Davies. H = Handicap or watch time A = Actual Time B = Boy, Y = Youth, J = Junior, L = Lady H A H A H A 1. SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE - DIVISION 1 13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON SURREY C.C. LEAGUE - DIV.I A marginally better performance than last year's opening disaster. Gary Staines cut his foot and was forced to retire while Oliver Foote fell over and did well to get up to 8th place. Andy North turned in a good performance and is beginning to make a few people sit up and take notice as too is Martin Lake. The race was notable for the number of top class second claim members running for other teams. Julian Goater (Shafts) finished 5th in AFD colours while Omega had drafted in two top Welsh runners. Its about time this league was restricted to bona fide clubmen. With only 91 pts. separating the bottom 5 Clubs, the next 3 matches assume even greater importance so lets hope Gordon can get a strong team out next time. items.h: FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY
items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's win in the inaugural 'Zatopek' 6 x 4½km Thames Relay in the City of London on 21 October 1984, organised by Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford, with a photo of anchor John Gladwin.
items.s: FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY Report and results of Belgrave's win in the inaugural 'Zatopek' 6 x 4½km Thames Relay in the City of London on 21 October 1984, organised by Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford, with a photo of anchor John Gladwin. FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY 21st OCTOBER 1984 CITY OF LONDON 'ZATOPEK' 6x4½km THAMES RELAY This inaugural race organised by ex 10,000m world record holders Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford was well publicised in the Local and National press and despite the previous day's National 6 stage relay received a great response from athletes and spectators. The course, chosen to keep clear of traffic, was not up to Championship Standards involving as it did several flights of steps. Nevertheless the atmosphere was there with commentary by Capital Radio's Kelly Temple and this coupled with free lunch and a drink plus party made the day memorable particularly for the loyal lady supporters. But to the race. This was the first time we had got our strongest 6 together. Not all were fully fit and with many still beginning a gradual build up we weren't certain if the established relay stars would prove too strong for us. The start saw 60 runners streaming over Southwark Bridge with Oliver Foote tucked in in about 12th place. As the fast pace began to bite a group of 3 broke away and at the first change over Oliver was only 3 seconds down on Enfield's leader Keith Doulton. Dave North took it steadily moving into second spot as a gap of around 8 seconds opened between him and the leader. Looking more relaxed than usual and picking up the pace our man gradually pulled back the difference to hand over to Gary Staines in the lead. Gary moved off fast opened up a gap of 15 seconds, relaxed and then had a fright as Andy Catton of Ilford stormed past at the 2 mile mark. Not to be put off Gary knuckled down to some hard work and needed his sprint finish to put us back in the lead. Stuart Paton looked to be moving well as he opened the gap to around 25 seconds which Mark Sinclair needed as Kevin Steer of Ilford took off after him on the 5th leg. The race bubbled at this point as Kevin gradually reduced the gap to get within 3 seconds of Mark 600m out. It was at this point that Mark kicked and the Ilford mans efforts had been in vain. John Gladwin took off as though he was in a fast 1500 and broke Ilfords last stage runner to such an extent that they drifted back to 4th as Keith Palmer ran the fastest leg of the day to bring Highgate into second place 50 seconds adrift. Our'B' team men put up some good times to make a great day for Belgrave. STOP PRESS Just as we close for the printers the results have arrived of the South of the Thames "Junior" C.C. Champs held at Windsor Great Park on Saturday 10th November. items.s: VETS. CORNER Vets Corner column on Belgrave veterans' 1984 season, including Laurie O'Hara's UK over-50 1500m record and Southern 10 miles over-50 title, and results of several veterans' road races. VETS. CORNER There were varying fortunes for our Vets on the track and road. With the European Vets T & F Championships being held in Brighton this year we could have expected some medal successes, but it was not to be. Laurie O'Hara who earlier in the year had established a U.K. over 50's 1500m record with 4:13.9 only managed 4th at Brighton as he recorded 4:15.1 just 0.1 sec. off the bronze in a close finish. If he had opted for the 5000m there would have been gold but with an entry fee of £5 plus £5 per event it didn't encourage doubling up. Snowy Brooker also travelled hopefully to Brighton, having put in some excellent performances in our British League team but despite some first class marks in the early events he managed 3 'no-throws' in the discus and was eliminated. Laurie later went on to win the Southern 10 Miles Vets Champs. with a remarkable 53.36 as he led our Vets to a team Silver. 26th MAY 1984 WIMBLEDON VETS A.C. 10 MILES Course now accurately measured to ten miles. 1.F.Bell (Woking) 54.15; 2.J.Froud (Woking) 54.26; 3.T.Ryan (N.London) 54.51. items.s: DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE Report on Belgrave's four 1984 Dunlop Young Athletes League matches (Battersea Park, Guildford, Redhill, Portsmouth), with outstanding performances, match results and final league positions (Belgrave third). YOUNG ATHLETES DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE This years league competition has been an up and down affair, with successes being sandwiched between disappointments. The following are short reports covering our four matches, highlighting the outstanding performances from these meetings. 6th MAY 1984 BATTERSEA PARK MATCH 1 As our first meeting dawned we found ourselves in disarray after the long winter break. Our weaknesses were startingly apparent in the technical field events where absences let down our extremely strong track team. At the end of the day we scored 17 wins, 16 seconds, 4 thirds and 17 other places, leaving 18 events not covered. The failure to cover these events caused our immediate loss of a minimum of 18 points. Outstanding performances - P.Goedluck Y.200 (23.3) & 100 (11.5); G.Warr Y(B) 200 (24.7) & 100 (11.9) R.Iles C(A) 1500 (5.08.7); D.Ward B(A) 1500 (4.42.1); D.Steward B(B) 1500 (4.35.2); S.Richards Y(A) 400 (54.8); D.Ashford B(A) 3000 (10.28.1); J.Caines B(B) 3000 (11.24); B.Zreik B(B) HJ:(1.50) & B(A) 800 (2:17.5); A.Ross C(A) 800 (2:25.3); C.Gardener Y(A) 100H (15.1). Youths 4x100 (46.2). Results: 1.Sutton & Cheam 248; 2.Surrey Beagles 228; 3.Fareham 202 4.BELGRAVE 186; 5.Walton 147. 3rd JUNE 1984 GUILDFORD MATCH 2 A warm but blustery day greeted us at Guildford. Our team had been dramatically strengthened since the match at Battersea Park and particularly in the field we felt in a far better state to face the competition. The match was very close with several athletes doubling up to cover empty places in some events, and at the end of the day it was these commendable actions added to the other impressive individual results which gave us the day by ½ a point. On this occasion we notched up 18 wins, 15 seconds, 11 thirds and 20 other places leaving only 8 events empty. Outstanding performances - B.Zriek B(A) 400 (56.7) & (A) LJ (5.44); S.Richards Y(A) 200 (24.3); G.Warr Y(B) 200 (25.4) & (B) 100 (12.1); R.Iles C(A) 1500 (5:09.4); C.Cornwell Y(A) HJ (1.75); M.Reece Y(B) HJ (1.70); D.Sewell B(A) SP (11.75); S.Warr B(B) SP (7.58); D.Rose Y(B) LJ (4.78); C.Gardiner Y(A) 100H (15.1); J.Mole Y(B) 100H (17.3); O.Olufuneo B(B) HJ (1.40); M.Dooley Y(A) LJ (5.32) & Y(A) 100 (11.9); G.Allison B(A) HJ (1.60); Youths 4x100 (46.5). Results: 1.BELGRAVE 219; 2.Camberley 218½; 3.Sutton & Cheam 210½; 4.Fareham 190½; 5.Guildford 189½. 24th JUNE 1984 REDHILL MATCH 3 Redhill was the first meeting at which we fielded a team selected by the newly formed Young Athletes Committee. The weather was warm and the athletics hot. With athletes now able to concentrate on their specialist events results were impressive with 23 wins, 19 seconds, 12 thirds and 12 other places. 6 events were still empty but this was understandable when one realises that 12 of the team were representing Surrey and London in the School's Triangular match and were therefore unable to compete for us. Outstanding performances - D.Ashford B(A) PV (1.75); D.McCarthy B(B) PB (1.30) & (B) JT (20.60); G.Warr Y(A) 200 (24.0) & (A) 100 (11.7); G.Pastana Y(B) 200 (24.5); D.Maloney B(B) 200 (27.0); I.Gilley C(A) 200 (27.7); A.Ross C(B) 200 (28.4) & (A) 100 (13.8); J.Mole Y(A) TJ (11.42); G.Tiernan Y(A) 1500 (4:35.7); G.Allison B(A) 80H (12.8) & (A) HJ (1.50); J.Beasty Y(A) 3000 (10.14.4); K.McDonagh Y(B) 3000 (10:15.4) & (B) 1500SC (5:34.7); D.Rose Y(B) 100H (18.6); S.Sbicca B(B) HJ (1.30); S.Beaumont Y(A) 800 (2.10.1). Colts 4x100 (57.2) Youths 4x100 (50.2) & 4x400 (3:52.4). These results gave us our second win, this time by a clear 24 points. Results: 1.BELGRAVE 258; 2.Surrey Beagles 222; 3.Guildford 211; 4.Camberley 165; 5.Walton 121. This moved us up into second place in the league behind Sutton & Cheam. All we needed was an average team performance in our last meeting and we would be guaranteed a place in the promotion qualifying meeting at our home track, Battersea Park. As we left Redhill, hopes were high that we could join our senior teams in their promotion celebrations. 29th JULY 1984 PORTSMOUTH MATCH 4 Tomorrow never comes. Our team for Portsmouth, devastatingly depleted by unavoidable holidays and sickness, was just a poor shadow of the team at Redhill. Our athletes pushed themselves to the maximum, almost all competing in their statutory 4 events. Team morale remained high though unfortunately morale alone doesn't win meetings and with no competitors in 23 out of 72 events a poor result was unavoidable. However all credit must go to the athletes and parents who attended on what was a beautiful day at an excellent facility. Outstanding performances - I.Gilley C(A) 200 (27.7); G.Warr Y(A) 200 (24.5) & (A) 100 (12.4); D.Sewell B(A) ST (12.06) & (A) JAV (76.58); G.Allison B(A) 80H (13.0) & (A) 800 (2.17.6); J.Mole Y(B) TJ (11.80). items.s: THAMESIDE LEAGUE Report on the 1984 Thameside League for boys and colts, expanded to include women's teams, with final positions and special mention of Gavin Warr and Gareth Allison. THAMESIDE LEAGUE This Belgrave brainchild, created ostensibly to provide competition for boys up to 14 years of age, was successfully expanded this year to incorporate five women's teams, whose exploits are reported in the Women's Section. In addition to the inter-club events it includes numerous non-scoring competitions in a relaxed atmosphere, where boys can experiment with new events. When reporting the results of our Boys and Colts in this competition it must be said that they appear disappointing because both teams finished near to the bottom of their leagues. This is because, in many cases, this year the emphasis has been to provide club competition for those boys who only occasionally have the opportunity to take part in the Young Athletes League, while at the same time providing a series of non-scoring races for others. Both these objectives were achieved, but at the expense of the league position. It was gratifying also to see the popularity of this venture grow with each meeting with the numbers of competitors in June and July, before the holidays began to thin the ranks, threatening to swamp the organisers. All in all it has been a happy and (with the aforementioned qualification) successful season. With all competing clubs already booking their places for next year we look forward to even greater achievements. Our congratulations go to Croydon Harriers Boys and Camberley A.C. Colts, but warn them, we shall be after the trophies next year. The individual performances are too numerous to mention in this report, but the final league tables were as follows THAMESIDE LEAGUE - FINAL POSITIONS. COLTS; 1. Camberley 22pts., 2. Croydon 18pts., 3. Twick.& Ran. 15pts., 4. HHH 14pts., 5. BELGRAVE 8pts., 6. Queens Park H 7pts. BOYS; 1. Croydon 22pts., 2. HHH 21pts., 3. Camberley 17pts., 4. BELGRAVE 10pts., 5. Queens Pk 8pts., 6. Twick.& Ran. 6pts. In summing up the season special mention must be made of the exploits of Gavin Warr (Youth) and Gareth Allison (Boy). Gavin competed in every Young Athletes League and won every race in which he competed. Gareth competed in both Young Athletes and Thameside Leagues and proved to be the club's only high-jumping middle-distance hurdler. Finally the Young Athletes sub committee wish to thank all the parents and officials who supported us so consistently throughout the season. Reports by Jim & Dave Mote. items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's 1984 season: 7th in the Womens Southern League, Midweek League win, county vests and medals, individual progress, and thanks to helpers.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's 1984 season: 7th in the Womens Southern League, Midweek League win, county vests and medals, individual progress, and thanks to helpers. WITH THE LADIES It has been quite an exciting season, with us finishing in 7th position in the Womens Southern League. This was our best position since 1980. In this League after 4 3rd placings we were lying 12th and we won the last 2. The last meeting was against strong opposition and we beat Aldershot, a team we had never beaten before so that was really pleasing. The Thameside League was a good replacement for the Lily B League and we hope that this will be continued for next season, especially as the athletes seemed to enjoy the competition. After a period of 6 years we re-entered the Midweek League (very similar in content to the Rosenheim League) and as we won every match we won the League very convincingly. There were plenty of places for the Non-scorers and everyone who came along was able to get competition. Our Junior relay team was unbeaten in all 6 Southern League, all 4 Thameside League and all 6 Midweek League races which is another good record. During the Season Club records were broken on at least 40 occasions. Three of our athletes gained their county vests. Wendy Dunsford represented Middlesex in a meeting in May held at Motspur Park, whilst Veronica St. Ange competed for Surrey in a representative match in July at Copthall and Rosemary Honeychurch represented Surrey in the Southern Womens Inter Counties Championships in August held at Crystal Palace. Three of our athletes also won Gold in County Championships. Rosemary Honeychurch won the 3000m in the Surrey Championships, whilst Cindy James and Angela Abrams won the 100m and Hurdles in the Middlesex Championships. Our total tally of medals in both County Championships was 12, with 6 Silvers and 3 Bronzes. So congratulations to all the medal winners and all those who took part. This was our best haul of medals in County Championships as well. Our walkers were well represented in the English Schools Walking Championships with London being represented by Gail Porter, Kim Marsh, Isobel Young and Charlotte Chirstou and Surrey and Essex being represented by Rachael Parrott and Joanne McGroder respectively. Picking out individuals it is worth noting that Jessica Palmer has continued the improvement she showed from last season and was joined in the Sprints by Yvette Edward Cindy James, Angela Abrams and Andrea Abrams, Nina Christou and Tracy Ritson. Angela Abrams and Nina Christou, both improved their Hurdles technique and had good backing from Cindy James. Cindy proved to be a good all-round athlete with improvements to her Shot and Discus. We were a bit short of junior middle distance runners, but those who did the events tried their best but the improvement shown by Jackie Stone was very encouraging as well as winning Silver in the Surrey Championships. Angela Abrams and her twin sister Andrea improved their marks in the Long Jump and Andrea began to do better in the high jump but must learn to concentrate harder. The record book has been re-written by Rachael Parrott in the walks and now holds all the Girls records as well as improving upon the Girls Javelin record. In the Seniors the middle distance team of Rosemary Honeychurch who has knocked over a minute off her 3000m record this season and there is probably more to come, Vicky Mitchell, Gail Porter ably backed by Davina Cameron and Georgina Tura did well. The Sprinters did not do as well as the Middle Distance runners but Andrea Coore, Shirley Daure, Penny Garnons-Williams well backed by Dezrine Conard, Adele Peck, and when they were able to come to meetings Erica Goldson and Susan Wilkinson Our Throwing team of Wendy Dunsford, Debbie Roberts, Veronica St. Ange as well as Perrican Bayar when she was available proved almost unbeatable. They won through although not always at their best and Veronica competed with broken bones in her foot. It is perhaps worth noting that we have competed in 40 Southern League fixtures since 1977 and Wendy has only missed 2 of them. She has been ever-present since June 1979 and in the Shot in the 30 matches since we were promoted to Division 3 has scored 139 points out of a possible 150. Our Walkers have kept Belgrave vests to the fore and these have been led very well by Rachael Parrott ably backed by Isobel Young, Charlotte Christou and were ably backed by Kelly Owen, Julie Field and Teresa Thirlwall. For all these results thanks must go to a great number of people who have helped me no end this season. Among those who should be mentioned are Ted Weldin, Dave Wenham, and Graham Thom for their help in the Hurdles, Jumps and Sprints. Also for his efforts in the Walks, thanks must go to Dave Sharpe, who has turned up at Battersea Park from Dagenham despite having a number of problems during the summer. Thanks to Derek Crookes too for also helping with the Middle Distance girls during the back end of the season. Last, but not least my thanks must go to Harry Porter and Frank Simmons for the work they do and their help and advice during the Season. Thanks to all the parents who come along and help and support and have made friends with each other and thanks to Sue Parrott for taking over the Press Representative's job. It is very pleasant to have so many people eager and willing to help and to those who come along to help judge at meetings as well. We could have done with a few more of these. After all we are here to help and encourage athletes and athletics and this cannot be done by not supporting BELGRAVE. We need help especially at Home Matches and even recording helps as Wyn Sheppard who was at all our home matches doing just that, or serving teas. Every little helps, so why not come and enjoy a day out seeing youngsters enjoy themselves. If I have missed anybody in my thanks during the season, then the omission was not really intentional. Thanks to all who have helped and encouraged or brought their children along to meetings by car. items.s: WOMEN'S SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Battersea Park on 14 April 1984, Belgrave third, with four club records. WOMEN'S SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 3 SOUTH 14th APRIL 1984 BATTERSEA PARK SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Teams: 1.Ashford A.C. 183; 2.Redhill & Reigate A.C. 172; 3.BELGRAVE 161½; 4.Eastbourne Rovers 93½; 5.Walton A.C. 83. A fine day, sunny and warm and Battersea Park looking really splendid. This was always going to be a tough match, with Ashford having been relegated and Redhill just missing promotion. There were some really great performances, with 4 new club records,1 club record being equalled and about 20 personal best performances being set. Excellent runs in the 1500m and 3000m by Rosemary Honeychurch, breaking her own 3000m record by some 24 seconds. Our Turkish national champion Perrican Bayar improved the Discus record by over 9 metres, Veronica St. Ange broke the Javelin record and Andrea Coore broke the Inters High Jump record and equalled the Senior record. It is perhaps worth noting that this was Wendy Dunsford's 28th consecutive Southern League meeting since June 1979. The English Schools Walking Championships took place on the same day and that took away some, whilst others were injured and some waited for the coach in the wrong place. However, some arm twisting by Rosemary Honeychurch on the journey down meant that we were covered in most Junior events and 2 of the Seniors ended up doing 4 individual events and a relay. 3 more Club records fell and 18 more personal bests were set and some were doing events unfamiliar to them, but with those results what more could have been asked of anybody. Fresh from her triumphs in the Surrey Championships Rosemary Honeychurch broke her club record still further and ran a personal best in the 1500m. The Senior Discus and Junior Discus records were both broken. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Yeovil on 21 July 1984, Belgrave third after a coach breakdown; the second senior relay is printed as 4x100m though its time and team suggest 4x400m. 21st JULY 1984 YEOVIL SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH 1.Yeovil Olympiades A.C. 182; 2.Bognor Reg. & Chich.A.C. 160; 3.BELGRAVE 141½; 4.Boro.of Kingston A.C. 129; 5.Horsham Blue Star Harriers 103½. Such are the peculiarities of these leagues that we had to travel down to Somerset to meet near neighbours Kingston, whom we had already met three days earlier in another league. Quite an eventful trip with an articulated lorry jack-knifing in front of us and the coach breaking down about 2 miles from the track. As luck had it, the Kingston coach passed us just as we were starting to walk and came back for us. We repaid this kindness by pushing them into 4th spot. Andrea Coore broke the Intermediate 400m Hurdle record at only her second attempt at the distance. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Portsmouth on 11 August 1984, won by Belgrave with six club records. 11th AUGUST 1984 PORTSMOUTH SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH 1.BELGRAVE 166; 2.Hastings A.C. 164; 3.Weymouth St.Pauls 156; 4.Winchester & Dist.A.C. 103½; 5.Portsmouth Atalanta A.C. 101½. This is a match we should have won as after the fourth match we were above the other teams we met here. However, with 6 new club records being set and 7 personal best performances, this was the time to give of their best. Commiserations to Andrea Coore who broke the Intermediate 400m Hurdles record only to see it snatched away 2 minutes later by Vicky Mitchell. The other records came from Cindy James in the Discus (also breaking the Intermediate record) Tracy Ritson in the Girls Javelin (this erases a record that had stood for 7 years) and a fine win in the 4 x 400m Relay to knock 3 seconds off the old record. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 (S) Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Dartford on 1 September 1984, won by Belgrave, securing 7th place in the division; it calls this the first win over Aldershot, though the season review says the same of an earlier match. 1st SEPTEMBER 1984 DARTFORD SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 (S) Results: 1.BELGRAVE 178; 2.Ald.Farn.& Dist. 176½; 3.Dartford H.148; 4.Basingstoke A.C. 145½; 5.Fleet & Crookham A.C. 37. This was a really splendid result for us as two of the teams we beat were in 5th and 6th position in the Division. This also was the first time that we have beaten Aldershot so that result was even more pleasing. This result meant that we finished in 7th position in the Division which is the best that we have done since 1980. It also means that we finish well above Hercules Wimbledon and with the last result just pushed Kingston back into 8th place. items.s: Arthur Penny, Commonwealth 6 miles champion fifty years earlier, is presented with an inscribed silver salver by Clive Shippen at Bill Webb's 90th birthday celebrations. Fifty years ago Arthur Penny won the Commonwealth 6 miles Championship Still hearty and in fine form Arthur is a frequent visitor to Belgrave Hall. He was pleasantly surprised when he attended the celebrations for Bill Webb's 90th Birthday for at the end of the proceedings Clive Shippen presented Arthur with an inscribed silver salver commemorating his fine win of fifty years ago. items.label: October 1985
items.sum: The editor's farewell after six years and twelve editions, contrasting the club's thin results of six years earlier with its present growth and success.
items.s: 'MAMMOTH' FAREWELL The editor's farewell after six years and twelve editions, contrasting the club's thin results of six years earlier with its present growth and success. This mammoth edition of the Belgravian represents for your Editor a final fling. For after 6 years and 12 editions it is time for a new face. As we progress towards our Centenary year we are moving into a period when naturally there will be a great deal of reminiscing about past glories. But in the role as Editor, where every aspect of Club activities is scrutinised and sifted before being recorded, it has become apparent that the Belgrave of today is in many ways far removed from that of 30 or even 10 years ago. I well remember 6 years ago searching desparately for decent copy on athletic achievements. Apart from the up and coming young squad of Dave North, Mark Sinclair, Mark Waller, Paul Richley, Stuart Paton and John Gladwin, plus the ever successful walkers , there was very little to give hope for the future. Our track team was about to be relegated to Div. 2 of the Southern League and the Road and Country team were desparately short of star performers. Today all that has been transformed. The problem with producing the Club magazine now is that in all Sections there has been a massive increase in active members and an incredible increase in athletic performances. Unfortunately because costs and Editorial time have to be kept within reasonable limits many items now have to be omitted. Behind all this success has been a growing team of enthusiastic officials and helpers all willing to give generously of their time to help our young, active and up and coming members. It is because of them that we can look forward to a well planned and exciting future. A future that will see many of our members rising to the top levels of International competition with all the financial rewards which such achievements deserve. I hope that the Belgravian will continue to record these successes and will provide interesting and stimulating reading for all members whether young or old, rabbits or stars. I wish my successor well. The place of our magazine in Club life cannot be overestimated. items.sum: Club gossip notes: members' radio appearances, marriages, engagements, injuries, a Toga party and a Valentine's Day aerial stunt.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip notes: members' radio appearances, marriages, engagements, injuries, a Toga party and a Valentine's Day aerial stunt. grapevine Leo Coy hit the airwaves in January when he appeared as the final questioner on Radio 4's Sports Review and Quiz. Graham Macky has written from New Zealand. He and Debbie were married last year and it suits him. After a fine second place in the N.Z. Marathon Championship he ran in the IAAF World Championship in Hiroshima on 14th April and finished 46th in 2:16.17. We also hear that there will be a new addition to the family early in 1986. Congratulations. Dave Mote's tendon operation proved successful and he has now to decide whether to resume his athletes career or become a full time dilettante. The omens are not good. His 25th birthday Toga party at Belgrave Hall showed all the usual signs of creeping decadence. The North brothers also displayed a couple of dirty habits despite which their Fan Club organised by our younger Ladies seems to be growing! John Aska at Walton track in September. Nothing strange you may think. But no' Our field events man has transformed into a top American Football star. Nicknamed 'Crusher' he helped a G.B. team defeat France 7-0 in the first International between these two countries. Doesn't qualify for the International Honours Board though! Remember Paul Richley and Kevin Sturman left our shores for U.S. Universities in August '84. Almost immediately both suffered injuries which put them out of action for the season. Thereafter their lives followed strangely similar patterns. Kevin married Anita in May 1985 and its doubtful if we will see them back here on a permanent basis. Paul returned early in 1985 and announced his engagement to Tina Couzens. Congratulations and best wishes to all. You'll read elsewhere of Mike Alleynes great 400m improvements this year. It may be a coincidence but at the middle of the year he got engaged. We wish him and Erica all happiness in the future. But in 1984 the wedding was that of Chris Everett to founding member of our Ladies Section, Jane Pritchard. Most of us can't remember exactly what happened at the celebrations and its costing an arm and a leg to suppress Brian's video. Chris has moved to the Bahamas to further his career as a croupier. Jane joined him in the summer. Maggie Thatcher and The Queen followed in October! February 14th - Valentine's Day saw a light aircraft circling South London/N.E.Surrey with an appropriate message in tow. The local press finally tracked down the instigator. Yes you've guessed - Charlie Manning! Can we afford for this boy to take charge of our Centenary Year promotional campaign? items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Humorous account of Oliver Foote being bitten by a dog on the Kingston-By-Pass, his £28 compensation, and his faster finishing since.
items.s: A BUM DEAL! Humorous account of Oliver Foote being bitten by a dog on the Kingston-By-Pass, his £28 compensation, and his faster finishing since. A BUM DEAL! Have you noticed that since the jogging boom dogs have become a lot more tolerant towards your average runner. There remain a few who find the nippier mortal irresistable and one of these had a good go at our top distance man Oliver Foote just at the start of the track season. The setting was the Kingston-By-Pass, Oliver was working up a nice pace mid-way between the Coombe Lane Bridge and the Robin Hood Roundabout when a particular ferocious specimen hurtled out of the riding stables and sank its nashers into his rear end. Our hero limped along to Kingston Hospital where the injury was much admired by the duty nurses as they drew lots to administer the compulsory anti-tetanus injection. Next on to the local cop shop where the matter was investigated by the boys in blue who eventually located the animal plus its owner. Negotiations for compensation began. No doubt Seb Coe would have commanded a good fee. our man settled for £28. As it turned out the adventure had its brighter side. We now notice that Oliver has acquired a noticeable acceleration - a change of pace which led to a 58 sec. last lap as he gained the Surrey 5000m Silver medal in mid-May (and in a p.b.). This fact has not gone unnoticed by some of our middle distance coaches and it is rumoured that as dust falls on Wimbledon Common, some can be heard practising their barking and growling techniques - based on second hand instruction books by Percy Edwards. So next time you think you're being chased by a Doberman - check twice - it might be Jim Webster!!!!! Oliver Foote Oliver Foote bitten by a dog while training; Surrey 5000m silver medal in a p.b. items.sum: Obituary of Leslie J. Cohen, Belgrave middle distance runner from 1934 and leading athletics administrator who became club president and a life vice president of the AAA.
items.s: LESLIE J. COHEN Obituary of Leslie J. Cohen, Belgrave middle distance runner from 1934 and leading athletics administrator who became club president and a life vice president of the AAA. In Memorium LESLIE J. COHEN Long, lean and hungry looking and striding purposefully over a cross country course dressed in 'Wellies' and oilskins - that is how I prefer to remember him, for that was when he was at his happiest. Born in South London in October 1908, he first graced the athletic scene in the '20s as a member of Ashcombe (later to be Ashcombe St. Georges AC), but it was as a Belgrave Harrier (from 1934) that he flourished into an excellent middle distance runner of near international standard with pre-war successes on track, road and country. After the War he threw himself into athletic administration with such enthusiasm and energy that he was known to everyone in the sport for his organising ability. For many years he was secretary and/or championship secretary to the AAA, Southern AAA, Southern Cross Country Association, South of the Thames Cross Country Association, CAU and London Business Houses AA, besides other appointments associated with those organisations and with Belgrave Harriers, who are forever grateful for his fund raising initiative, which led to the development of their headquarters in Wimbledon to the standard they are today. All this work led him, perhaps a little reluctantly, to the presidencies of Belgrave, South of the Thames, Southern AAA, Southern CCA, ECCU, and ultimately to a life vice presidency of the AAA. It is a privilege to have been associated with this man and to have competed and served with him over a long period of time. We have missed him during the past few years when his health prevented him from carrying on in his usual energetic and spirited way, but he was not forgotten. Wherever his colleagues met his name cropped up and will continue to do so - we will remember him. Our sympathies and condolences go to his wife Mary (nee Hutchins), who in her early days was also a distinguished athlete with Spartan Ladies. W.E. Lucas, Leslie J. Cohen LESLIE J. items.s: ETHEL M. CARTER Obituary of Ethel M. Carter, long-time Belgrave supporter and wife of Tom Carter, who died on 10 October. ETHEL M. CARTER On 10th October we lost one of our dearest and best loved supporters. Ethel who two years ago suffered a partial stroke and had been making a steady recovery, passed away peacefully. We have lost a great friend. Ethel was keenly interested in all of Belgrave's activities starting back in the 1930's when she first met Tom and encouraged him in his many successes. Tom and Ethel have been a part of the Belgrave scene for over 50 years providing a constant source of help and encouragement to generations of young athletes. Floral tributes both from the Club and from over 40 Belgravians said far more than words to convey our deep respect and love for Ethel. Our thoughts and support are with Tom at this sad time. items.sum: Profile of new club President Gordon Biscoe: his running career from 1953, road running, his long service as Road and Cross Country Secretary, and his organising of club races.
items.s: GORDON BISCOE - PRESIDENT Profile of new club President Gordon Biscoe: his running career from 1953, road running, his long service as Road and Cross Country Secretary, and his organising of club races. GORDON BISCOE - PRESIDENT Gordon Biscoe joined Belgrave in 1953 after a period of service with the R.A.F. His athletics career began at school and continued during R.A.F. Service where he shared in many team successes over the country, including the winning of the Shropshire Championship in 1952. Although Gordon's career with Belgrave never hit the dizzy heights of individual stardom, he was one of the engine room men sharing in the successes of the 50's and 60's teams, when you had to fight to get into the Surrey, Southern,National and major relays. Gordon's first love was always the road, achieving much better success than in the track where his best times were 2.06 for 880 yds, 4.35 for the Mile and just inside 15m for 3 Miles. In humerous vein he lists amongst his achievements on the road as being the only known person to run the famous 'Bridges Race' on the Thames Embankment in two left shoes; and being selected the most number of times as first reserve for the Brighton Relay! His first official role in the Club was as Road Running Captain from 1964 to 1967, a period when our senior teams were the scourge of the road, when he then took over from Derek Crooks as Road Secretary. In 1969 he then took over from Bill Laws as Cross Country Secretary, a position he has now held for 17 years. In addition during the late 60's he was Social Secretary for 2 years, when he organised a number of successful socials. Gordon has always preferred to devote what time he has got to Belgrave rather than seek honours in the outside world of athletics, but he has served on the general committee of the Surrey AAA as well as the South of the Thames C.C.A. for many years, culminating this service by being elected President of the South of the Thames in 1983/84. He He is also a graded timekeeper. His organisational abilities are now well known having built up a large experience (and store of amusing anecdotes) over the years, from organising ordinary club races to major championships on behalf of the Club. He organised our 20m Road Race for 6 years with the 1975 event being his most memorable one, as being the occasion he first met Margaret, now his wife, who at the time was Centre Organiser of the Wimbledon Red Cross who always attend this event. When they were married in 1979 Gordon confessed that it was then he realised he wasn't running fast enough any more! Like many Belgrave wives Margaret now helps out in many 'behind the scenes' activities, such as making cross country marker flags, or collating race entries etc. Gordon's longest running epic is now the Belgrave 12 Stage Road Relay which he has masterminded for 17 years in to the premier race that it is today carrying Southern Counties AAA Championship status and commercial sponsorship. Away from Belgrave, Gordon is a Chartered Electrical Engineer working for a research association. In his spare time, what there is left from Belgrave duties, business commitments (often abroad) and helping look after a young son, Richard of fourteen months, Gordon lists amongst his hobbies, gardening and Jazz - having been a very keen follower of Chris Barber and Humphrey Lyttleton. items.label: October 1985
items.sum: New President Gordon Biscoe's message thanking members and calling for a stronger, financially secure and united club ahead of the centenary.
items.s: From the President New President Gordon Biscoe's message thanking members and calling for a stronger, financially secure and united club ahead of the centenary. From the President May I first take this opportunity to say a sincere thank you to you all for the honour of being elected President of this great club; it is one which I shall always cherish. In my seventeen years as Cross Country Secretary some previous Presidents have called for efforts to be made to achieve some athletic goal during their term of office, like winning the National Cross Country Championship, but while these goals are of course always desirable, they have sometimes been unrealistic. During this coming year I would, therefore, like to set a goal for all members, which is perhaps less spectacular in the short term, but is very desirable, very necessary and at the same time achievable - it is for us all to work harder and closer together to make Belgrave even greater. It is desirable in that we will be in our 99th year and what better way to celebrate the following centenary year and fulfil all the plans being made than with a thriving club. It is necessary for, as most of you know, in the world of athletics times are changing fast and in order to keep pace with these changes it must be our objective to work for a stronger and more financially secure club with ever improving facilities to meet the needs of all our athletes. It will mean forgetting some of the parochial attitudes that sometimes exist between the various sections, and working for the Club as a whole; it will mean recruiting 'new blood' to our organizational and management ranks to ease the burden of some of these already in office; and for our active athletes, particularly 'A Team' members, it will sometimes mean putting Club requirements before personal desires, in order to get team success. It is as teams that we will invariably get our victories and we are capable of far more than we do, if only our teams were properly supported. Success breeds success! and surely our efforts in the British League this summer are a fitting example. Good Luck and best wishes in all your efforts in the year ahead. GORDON BISCOE Gordon Biscoe GORDON BISCOE President; Cross Country Secretary for seventeen years National Cross Country Championships British Athletics League

items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Anecdote of Marcello Bizio, laid up with a hernia after three road race wins in Italy, being urged by Colin to run anyway.
items.s: CRACKER! Anecdote of Marcello Bizio, laid up with a hernia after three road race wins in Italy, being urged by Colin to run anyway. CRACKER! There's a story doing the rounds that may well be apocryphal but is worth telling nonetheless. Following a substantial reduction in weight and victories in three road races in Italy, Marcello Bizio has become hot property. If one of the first team men is missing Marcello is your man. Unfortunately all this activity brought on a groin strain which has required surgery. Just before the operation Marcello was contacted by our Assistant Cross Country Sec. who urged him to turn out for the following weeks race. Now Marcello's English is improving by leaps and bounds. "Sorry", said our hero, "I can't run, I am with Hernia". "Don't worry old son", says Colin, "First claim membership of a foreign Club doesn't count!". What a cracker! Anyway what we're trying to say is "Get well soon Marcello? The team needs you back as soon as possible" Marcello Bizio Marcello Bizio won three road races in Italy; groin surgery Marcello Bizio Marcello Colin Colin Assistant Cross Country Secretary Italy

items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Report on the official opening of the rebuilt Belgrave Hall and new gym, conducted by AAA Secretary Mike Farrell, with thanks to Peter Pitt for a GLC grant.
items.s: BELGRAVE HALL Report on the official opening of the rebuilt Belgrave Hall and new gym, conducted by AAA Secretary Mike Farrell, with thanks to Peter Pitt for a GLC grant. BELGRAVE HALL Although Mike Winch and Judy Oakes had started operations at the new Gym as far back as October 1984 it wasn't until February that the rest of the Hall had been finished to a standard ready for the official opening.The Official Opening Ceremony was conducted by AAA's Secretary - Mike Farrell who was able to confirm that the AAA's would be contributing specialist equipment for strength training.Local dignitaries including the Major and Majoress of Wimbledon were in attendance and we were particularly pleased to welcome representatives of the Southern AAA's, the London and South East Regional Sports Council,the London and Surrey playing Fields Association. Present too was our biggest supporter - Peter Pitt-who you will recall stepped in at the last minute to provide a GLC grant of £14000 when the development project was foundering due to cost escallation and the introduction of VAT mid way through the the building programme. Past Presidents travelled from all over the UK to see the conclusion of a project that many had helped start with the purchase of the Hall way back in the 1930's. All were able to admire the new developments which have resulted in the Hall now being used for some 70 hours per week and open for training 7 days each week. items.sum: Changes of officials at the AGM, including Joe Coleman as General Secretary, and a tribute to Bill Couzens on stepping down after building up the bar and hall lettings.
items.s: OFFICIAL CHANGES Changes of officials at the AGM, including Joe Coleman as General Secretary, and a tribute to Bill Couzens on stepping down after building up the bar and hall lettings. OFFICIAL CHANGES This years Annual General Meeting saw a substantial change round in our Official line-up. Joe Coleman fresh from an active Presidential year has taken over the mantle of Gen. Hon. Sec. while Eric Crutcher backed by Keith Duckett has taken over the role of Gen. Hon. Sec. Social. Harry Porter has extended his involvement with the Ladies Section taking over the Track and Field Sec. job as well as the Country while on the Vets side Keith Sinclair has moved into the Secretaries seat and we are delighted to see a new face on the management side. Elected members included on the Committee are; Dave Mote, Andy Paton,Keith Duckett,Sue Parrott and Bill Laws. Bill Couzens. With Bill Couzens stepping down from the Gen. Sec. Admin. job we see an end of an era. It is difficult to overstate Bill's contribution to the improvement in Belgrave's fortunes over the last 5 years. It was he alone who built up the bar activities and the hall letting from nothing to a point where they provided a major contribution to the overall monies coming into the Club. In addition to running the business side Bill also undertook all the odd jobs needed to keep the facilities in good repair. It was not unusual for him to be called out of bed during the small hors of the morning and most Saturday mornings until quite recently he could be seen cleaning the Hall and generally undertaking those thousand and one jobs needed to keep everything running smoothly. Spare moments at home were taken up with book-keeping but probably Bill's best efforts were reserved the beer itself. Without doubt the best drop of Guiness in South London can be had at the Hall and that does not happen by accident. It is a measure of Bill's contribution that his job has been split into four parts because it would be practically impossible to find anyone who could devote enough time to what in reality could be considered a full time job. The Club owes Bill a great deal - and you can bet he would be the first to deny it. But we know Better!! Thanks Bill. Joe Coleman Joe Coleman Gen. Hon. items.s: FINANCIAL MATTERS Treasurer Ron Severn's report of a £2,095 surplus for the year despite the Hall rebuild. FINANCIAL MATTERS Ron Severn reported on his first year as Hon Treasurer at the September AGM. Last year we had been warned that because the Hall would be out of action for 6 months during the rebuild and because we would need to start repaying the loans in 1985 there would be little likelihood of a profit. Surprise therefore when we learned of a substantial surplus of £2,095 for the year. The signs for 1986 are even better with lettings near to capacity. Things really seem to be in good shape and in capable hands. Ron Severn Ron Severn Hon Treasurer Belgrave Hall

items.s: INDIAN SUMMER Leo Coy's visit to Ranjit Bhatia in Delhi and Bhatia's run in a 250km multi-day race from Agra to Delhi. INDIAN SUMMER Leo Coy has recently returned from a business trip to India and while in Delhi was royaly entertained by Ranjit Bhatia. Ranjit is expecting another Belgravian in the near future when Bob Taylor travels to India in November on holiday. Super Vet Ranjit moved into the area of ultra long distance competition recently when he competed in the 250km race from Agra to Delhi. The race started at 7am on October 4th 1985 and 40km was covered before lunch with a further 25km in the afternoon. In the following days they covered 55km, 55km,65km, finishing with a short sprint of 15km into Delhi. Out of 256 starters over 200 finished the course and the event attracted Nationwide T.V. coverage. items.sum: Carl Lawton's review of the Belgrave walking section, on squad depth, the 20-30 age gap and the season of individual walkers including Graham Seatter's National and Inter-Counties medals.
items.s: WALKING Carl Lawton's review of the Belgrave walking section, on squad depth, the 20-30 age gap and the season of individual walkers including Graham Seatter's National and Inter-Counties medals. One of the advantages of being a member of a strong section is that even if you are a 'good' club man' usually finishing in 7th or 8th in the team there is always the chance that you may get the odd 4th spot when some cannot turn out and still get in the prizes. With a weak section you may always be in the team but the team is not good enough to gain prizes. With this in mind a glance through the results will show how many have been in the scoring teams during the winter months, especially the London 10 miles. We still, however, must endeavour to encourage more people, not just to come into the sport but to stay in. The wastage of 'talent' is something we should all be concerned about, there is at the moment a gap in the 20-30 age group. Why else do you see a lot of the same faces heading fields that were there 10 years ago? Meanwhile to the present. A good winter, but so was last year. Wins at Cambridge, Pewsey Cup, Belgrave and Imber Court, generally with good packing and never our best team out. Graham Seatter finished off his year back with us turning out when he could and showing Murray Day the ropes. During the year Graham collected two National medals and an Inter Counties team medal, not a bad achievement for someone who had given up walking for the last three years. Richard Dorman had his good raves, not as good as he had hoped but he is still a 'youngster', and his trips down from Nottingham for races should be an example to us all. Paul Warburton, back from his years sabatical in America, wasted little time in getting back into team placings, although the change in climate here did not suit him. Richard Tanner has almost returned to his standard of 7 years ago, not bad for someone who did not expect to take up walking again. John Newnham has not been at his best for a while but has still collected the odd team prize. Which brings me to the 'youngsters', Neil Foster, 3rd in the SCAAA 10kms and 2nd in the Club 10m, Michael Feighan (likened in style to Stan Vickers, but not quite the speed yet) and Murray Day. There is little one needs to say of Murray. Results say all that. And there is Stephen Marshall too, who, having had his work commitments reduced should be back in the spotlight. John Hall has had to lie low for a while due to varicose vein problems but is now back on the road. items.s: LONDON 10M CHAMPIONSHIP Report and results of the snow-hit London 10 mile walk championship at Battersea Park on 9 February 1985, won by Richard Tanner with Belgrave the winning team. 9th FEBRUARY 1985 BATTERSEA PARK LONDON 10M CHAMPIONSHIP This almost proved to be a non-event. Snow during the previous night reduced the number of starters to an embarrassingly low number of 16. Whether it should have been held is debatable, but had it been cancelled then it would have been unjust to those who turned up, many of whom had travelled from the outer limits of the boundary. Any way it was held with teams reduced to 3 a side, enabling 3 teams to start, Belgrave were the only team to start 4, but within a mile Paul Warburron was on the side-lines, having discovered that some walkers cannot cope with slippery surface. So it was left to Richard Tanner to not only bring home the team but to win overall with John Hall 2nd and Doug Fotheringham 5th. (The latter both did times faster than in the Belgrave). So it was another win for Belgrave, much to the pleasure of the Wandsworth Mayor who presented the awards. Commiserations to Richard Dorman who, having travelled down from Nottingham the previous evening, failed to make Battersea from Wimbledon due to train cancellations. 1.R.Tanner 79.41; 2.J.Hall 83.14; 3.N.Carmody (C.H.) 85.33; 5.D.Fotheringham 87.48. items.s: DOUG FOTHERINGHAM'S SEASON Tribute to veteran walker Doug Fotheringham's season: team medals, two European veterans silver medals in Rome and the Veterans A.C. 5 mile Grand Prix. Doug Fotheringham, one of Belgrave's Super Vets has undoubtedly had one of his best seasons, in various races Doug has collected winning team medals, GLC, Southern 20 miles, Southern 20 Kms and Track Competition. In addition to this he won two Silver medals in the European Championships in Rome and as a result of the Veterans A.C. 5 mile meetings at Battersea during the summer, came away as overall Grand Prise winner. Doug Fotheringham Doug Fotheringham veteran walker; two silver medals at the European (veterans) Championships in Rome; overall winner of Veterans A.C. 5 mile Grand Prix 1985 Doug Fotheringham Doug GLC Championships Southern 20 Miles Walk Championship Southern 20km Walk Championship Southern Track Walking Competition European Veterans Championships Veterans A.C. 5 Miles Grand Prix Rome Battersea Veterans A.C.

items.sum: Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' season, in which the boys reached the 1981 five-year plan target of being the most successful Y.A. club in Surrey, with three team medals at the Surrey Championships.
items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' season, in which the boys reached the 1981 five-year plan target of being the most successful Y.A. club in Surrey, with three team medals at the Surrey Championships. Last year I referred to the fact that we had completed the third term of a five year plan. I can now unveil the plan launched in 1981 in the knowledge that the boys have achieved that target this winter "to be regarded as the most successful Y.A. Club in Surrey". In 1981 this was ambitious as we had only 6 cross country runners in all age groups! But the most satisfying aspect is that 5 are still running and one of those has won an English Vest. A glance at the following will confirm the outstanding results recorded in the three leagues in all age groups. Then the perfect peak culminating in the Surrey Championships when we took Silver, Bronze and Gold Team Medals respectively, to confirm the best overall performance by any Surrey Club. Incidentally 'Belgrave Historians' have said this is the best result in the history of Belgrave. The athletes still credit their collective success to the Mars Bars, but all credit for this effort must go to the boys after many years of hard work and they are duly recognised in their respective sections. At the same time I know the boys would also wish to thank the increasing band of supporters, braving all weather conditions to make timely appearances around the course which strengthened everybodies resolve when the going got really tough. Also thanks to those who helped organise, transport and carry out co-operative duties. Not least appreciation to Rosemary for 100% attendance, recognised as the number pinning, track suit hanger, Mars Bar Lady. Thanks to every body, above all to the boys who made this season the most enjoyable yet. And for the future - readers can be confident we have amended our plan. IAN HORTON Ian Horton IAN HORTON Rosemary Rosemary 100% attendance; number pinning, track suit hanger, 'Mars Bar Lady' Surrey Cross Country Championships

MINI COLTS The efforts of these youngsters force their own place of recognition. In preparation to receive the mantle from the successful Colts for next season there are no faint hearts in this squad. Battling on the often bleak Epsom Downs they took second place in the League. A special note of Babs Khan and Teddy Davies for their consistently high performances, also rapidly improving Reece Wilkins and Stewart Booth. Welcome to Neil Webster and Ben Brown who clearly showed talent that will make next season exciting. Also a special mention to Ben Cooper who, as our youngest runner (8), closed the team at the Ranelagh Open to secure his first ever Team Medal and with three more years as a Mini-Colt certainly not the last. 10th NOVEMBER 1984 SUTTON & CHEAM OPEN 1 MILE (4 to score) 1.R.Fletcher (Reigate) 6.15; 9.B.Khan 6.50; 20.T.Davies 7.07; 47.S.Booth 7.42; 56.G.Cox 7.54. items.s: COLTS Colts section of the young athletes' review: their best season, with the Downs League and a third successive Surrey League title, Surrey Championships silver, 5th in the Herne Hill League, and 1984-85 cross country results. COLTS Predictably the Colts had by far their best season with four of the squad representing their county in the Inter-Counties. Very early signs of their imminent success showed at the Collingwood Open when they finished a close 3rd to Woking and Shaftsbury. They went on to win the Downs League with Matthew Egerickx taking the individual title. Frankly it must be said there was little opposition to the Colts taking the Surrey League title for the third consecutive year. So to the best day in the Bels Y.A. history when at the Surrey Championships this squad ran out of their skins to take the Silver close behind Woking with all 4 scorers in top 15. They finished 5th in the Herne Hill League, which is generally recognised as one of the highest quality leagues in the south. Congratulations to Matthew, Steven, Alexander, Aaron, Dan W., Robert, all gaining representative honours. 13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON COMMON SURREY LEAGUE (1) 2¼ MILES (5 to score) 1.E.Barker (Ranelagh) 16.51; 2.A.Ross 17.05; 3.S.Lambert 17.14; 4.A.Bacon 17.44; 6.D.Winson 18.14; 7.B.Ambrose 18.19; Also ran 8.D.Parr; 11.B.Khan; 12.M.Harrod; 18.T.Davies. items.s: BOYS Boys section of the young athletes' review: a young squad that won the Downs League, took Surrey Championships bronze and won the Ranelagh Open, with 1984-85 cross country results. BOYS The Boys were expected to struggle as a consequence of virtually all the regular runners being in their first year. Their character was under-estimated as any concern proved unjustified by the results. Due mainly to some superb runs by Duncan Ward, consistently supported by David Ashford. Gareth Allison also Dean Cunningham and the notable improvement of Nadir Khan and Saul Herbert. These combined to take the Downs League Title, eighth in the Herne Hill League and Bronze Medal in the Surrey Championships, with a superb individual second place by Duncan Ward (robbed of the title by some indifferent marshalling when he was sent off course while leading, but to go on to take 18th place in the Southern Counties. The boys closed their season with a clear victory in the Ranelagh Open.
