items.s: YOUTHS Youths section of the young athletes' review: a mainly first-year squad that won the Surrey Championship team title, took Herne Hill League bronze and 2nd in the Ranelagh Open, with 1984-85 cross country results. YOUTHS This squad reached the level of achievement expected of them this season. Coincidentally as with the boys shouldering the imbalance of being predominantly a 'first year team' (it was hardly noticeable!) Even so, I do not overlook the invaluable contribution John Booth made, especially early season. Welcome also to Graham Adams and Simon Maynard, too late to effectively strengthen the squad, but a glance at the December 8th Surrey League result showed what is possible. Good luck to these three next season as Juniors. The most significant team result was stealing a highly contested Surrey Championship title with a fine individual 4th from Garry McGurren, backed by Matthew Kinane (flying in from Switzerland hours before), Simon Beaumont and Glynn Tiernan. Not to be outdone the 'B string' runners showed consistent form to nail the Bronze in the Herne Hill League, largely from the efforts of Matthew Smith, Adam Horton and Robert Mann. It was not surprising that the same trio together with Brian Carlton should also take 2nd place in the Ranelagh Open. Congratulations to Matthew, Glyn, John, Simon and Adam gain representative honours, also Garry for gaining a National Vest for an International Catholic Schools Race. 13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON COMMON SURREY LEAGUE (1) 2¼ MILES (5 to score) 1.M.Rendell (A.F.D.) 14.28; 7.J.Booth 14.51; 15.K.McDonagh 15.54; 17.R.Mann 16.16; 18.D.Mavoney 16.20; 19.B.Carlton 16.24; Also ran 23.G.Webb; 24.N.Khan; 26.D.Cunningham; 30.A.St.Horton; 31.T.Palmer; 35.S.Herbert; 37.P.Whiston. items.s: NEW MEMBERS WELCOMED New members welcomed: profiles of Simon Smith, Graham Adams, Simon Maynard and Steven Webster, four athletes who moved from Mitcham A.C. in late 1984, with photos. NEW MEMBERS WELCOMED SIMON SMITH: Aged 18 yrs. D.O.B. 18.8.66. Simons athletic interests encompass a number of disciplines and to encourage his wide base interest he came to Belgrave in December 1984 from Mitcham A.C. Personal bests include a 2710 Pentathlon score: 1.75 HJ; 5.37 LJ; 33m JT; 37.5 2kg Discus; 2.05' 800; 4.30.6 1500; 10.37 3000 S/C. He trains and competes regularly over the country and has a Surrey County Youth Team Bronze from Road Relays. The athletic energy demands being so high for simon it is most fortunate for his family that he is a 1st Commis Chef at the Royal Lancaster Hotel, Hyde Park a la carte Restaurant where he gets first class fare to match. GRAHAM ADAMS: Aged 16 yrs. D.O.B. 10.6.68. Graham is a young athlete of great potential with a range from 400H to Cross Country and Road. He joined Belgrave in December 1984, an ex Mitcham A.C. member. An excellent steeplechaser he won the Surrey Youth title in 1983 as a 14 year old. A favourite to retain the championship in 1984 he unfortunately had to miss the event, and the bulk of the track season, with a mystery virus condition effecting the blood. We have to look back to 1983 and to early 1984 for his best track and country performances. These include placing, 4th as a first year youth, in the county event and an excellent 71st in the National at Newark. 1983 Personal bests of 2.06.5 800; 4.19.8 1500; 9.16.6 3000 mark his existing potential, and his success over the steeplechase barriers is matched with useful prowess over 400H where he has notched 61 sec. SIMON MAYNARD: Aged 17 yrs. D.O.B. 8.12.67. Following a move from Mitcham A.C. in December 1984 Simon almost immediately showed his worth with a 3rd placing in the Surrey County Youths X.C. Champs at a time when training, which started late in November, pointed to only 90% readyness. February and March saw him fully fit but frustrated over his ineligibility to enter major events, such as Southerns and Nationals, owing to a first claim rule that keeps him off the Belgrave score sheet until 4.9.85. County vests at cross country and track, have been an annual bonus for a lad who has a superlative record in every age group, mini colt upwards. He is also a Steeplechaser of note with a County Youths Silver Medal in recognition. Best performances have so far come on the country and over the barriers, but he hopes to soon improve his 1984 3000 p.b. of 9.07 and expects in 1985 to get close to 2 min. for 800 and 4 min. at 1500. The following Cross Country season will be welcomed, particularly the prospect of high class team competition with his new friends at Belgrave. STEVEN WEBSTER: Aged 14 yrs. D.O.B. 27.5.70. Steve joined Belgrave in November 1984, the youngest of four athletes moving over from Mitcham A.C. A schoolboy at Wilsons he feels he is treading a familiar athletic path at a school that has produced the Paton brothers; Dave Swain (E & E); Aidrian Izatt (SLH) in recent years. There has been some early success including a win at the I.A.C. Cross Country (Crystal Palace) 1982: The year in which he ranked 4th in the U.K. 1500 Colts list. October 1983 saw him corner a small piece of athletic history when he became the youngest ever male recipient of a AAA Championship Gold medal. A member of the successful Mitcham A.C. team in the inaugural AAA Championship (at this age group) road relays at Sutton Park West Midlands, Steve entered the record books in some style recording the fastest anchor leg in the event, and 4th fastest overall. 1984 brought a sixth place in the SCAAA Boys 1500 final at Crystal Palace in a time of 4.20.63. He also posted a 9.19.3 3000 on a freezing late February evening at Crystal Palace. In the lead. Simon Maynard(l) & Graham Adams(r). Photo.Bill Laws. Steven Webster in the Surrey C.C.Champs. items.s: Anecdote of Steven Webster's Capital Radio prize flight with Simon Maynard being called off for weather, after which Maynard won the club 5000m senior championship in a personal best. Back in May Steven won a Boys race in Battersea Park organised by Capital Radio. The prize was a trip in the Company's Flying Eye early morning traffic jam spotter plane. The only problem was the starting time - 6.30am. Anyway, it was too good to miss and as the prize included for a friend to go along also it was at 5.30 am that Steven and Simon Maynard set off with Jim Webster acting as chauffer. The destination was Levesden airport near Watford. Gale force winds and torrential rain looked as though they would provide a bumpy flight and it was with mixed feelings that the lads received the news that there would be a delay in proceedings. And so it went on. The flight would have to be another day. So back to south London and for Simon it was time to prepare himself for his first Club Championship - the 5000m Senior Champs at Battersea Park. And what a consolation! Yes the day turned out fine for Simon for he beat all our Seniors to win the 5000 in a personal best time of 15.21.6. items.sum: Report on South African-born Ian Gilley's colts club records set during a summer stay in England, and even better marks since his return to South Africa.
items.s: IAN GILLEY SETS EXTRAORDINARY COLTS RECORDS Report on South African-born Ian Gilley's colts club records set during a summer stay in England, and even better marks since his return to South Africa. When the last issue of the Belgravian went to print we were aware that some good performances from our younger members had not reached the editorial office but we didn't realise that the missing marks put up by South African born Ian Gilley, during his stay in this country last Summer, were quite so remarkable. Well, Ian's father Rod has now provided us with a summary of Ian's English results. He competed in 17 colts events, all of which he won,2 youths events placing 2nd and 4th and 1 senior event, placing 3rd. His best performances amongst these were 100m-12.1, 200m-25.5, 400m-58.6 and Long Jump-5.08m - all of which established new club records. But apparently we hadn't seen anything, for, on his return to South Africa, Ian has recorded the following astonishing marks:- 9.90(80m) 12.0(100m) 18.04(150m) 24.6(200m) 56.6(400m) and 5.41(Long Jump)!!! Ian's family plan to bring him to the U.K. during the Summer of 1986 to compete in the Boys Age Group when doubtless we shall see more records tumble to this exceptional young man. items.s: DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE Jim and David Mote's review of Belgrave's 1985 young athletes season: the four Dunlop Young Athletes League matches (2nd at Battersea Park, Worthing and Redhill, 3rd at Ewell Court; 8th of 16 overall), victory in the H.A.C. Memorial Trophy at Battersea Park, the Thameside League, and tributes to leading young athletes. This was another year when we promised so much as a team but eventually had to be content with outstandingly consistent individual performances. Once again we suffered because we were unable to cover all events and to a degree this was caused by lack of control by management. We needed more helpers both in the lead up to matches and in management of the three sections on the day. However, we hope we will learn by our mistakes and they will not be repeated next year. I have been asked to take charge of the Young Athletes Section again next year and would welcome help in contacting athletes and organising them at matches. We have a considerable depth of talent in our section and it is up to us to make the best use of it. The season was to comprise of five matches, but in fact was reduced to four because the final meeting at Redhill was called off because the track was flooded. The following are short reports covering the four matches, highlighting the outstanding performances from these meetings. 12th MAY 1985 BATTERSEA PARK MATCH 1 In preparing for the opening meeting we were full of confidence in our ability to crush all opposition but were dismayed to realise on the day that the Surrey Championships were to start on the following day and for obvious reasons many of our middle-distance runners declined to compete. As some of these athletes also double up on field events we found ourselves with more gaps in our team. Nevertheless we were able to give a good account of ourselves and scored 28 wins, 13 seconds, 8 thirds and 4 other places leaving 24 events not covered and a consequent minimum loss of 24 points. This time 'A' level studies reduced our team and again we had to be content with second place. There were, however, two outstanding features in this match in that we won all but three track races A and B in the Boys and Youths teams, but missed out where we had no competitors and Festus Ogwuda cleared 14.17 metres in the Youths Triple Jump to win the Dunlop Award for the outstanding feat in the match. We were of course delighted that so many of our athletes were honoured by selection for their Districts, but it played havoc with our League team. Not downhearted the rest of the section competed with commendable spirit, doubling up wherever possible and achieving a very good result in the face of adversity. Special mention must be made of Festus Ogwuda who had competed in the morning session of the competitions at Crystal Palace and then made his own way to Redhill and arrived in time to add his considerable talent to the efforts of our depleted team. Nevertheless it was sad at the end of the day to find that we (who boast the fastest Youths 4x100 Relay Team in the South of England) had insufficient athletes available to enter a team in this event. Our achievements were 20 wins, 13 seconds, 8 thirds and 2 other places. We had no competitor in 34 events. MEMORIAL TROPHY After our sad reports about depleted team it is a pleasure to report the turn-out of Boys and Youths for this competition. On this occasion we were embarrassed with talent with athletes competing for places in the team. This reflected in the results which showed Belgrave way ahead of all other competing teams including a very strong one representing our hosts, Hercules Wimbledon. It was an undoubted pleasure to see our Youths Captain, Mark Dooley presented with the trophy at the end of the meeting. THAMESIDE LEAGUE This very popular competition again gave our Boys & Colts plenty to aim for. As a team we did not have much success, but individually the athletes competed with great spirit and many surprised themselves with their achievements in events where they had not hitherto considered themselves accomplished. It was interesting to see middle distance runners hurdling, sprinters jumping, and nearly everyone having a try at the field events at one time or another. In summing up, having already mentioned the exploits of Festus Ogwuda. Mention must also be made of our Youths first choice sprint squad of Gavin Warr, Joe Minetti and Mark Dooley who competed whenever possible and were never beaten in the Young Athletes League sprints. When joined by Clive Gardner who is primarily a hurdler, but is also a class sprinter, they made up the relay squad that won the Surrey AAA, Youth 4x100m and ran the remarkable 44.9 at Ewell Court. Julian Mole also competed unstintingly providing valuable back up to Clive in the hurdles and Festus in the triple jump and taking over the 'A' competition when they were not available. Julian never missed a Young Athletes match and won every hurdles race and triple jump competition in which he competed 'A' and 'B'. Finally, I will commend one boy who competed in every match - Young Athletes and Thameside Leagues - always completed three events and stood by for the relay if required. I of course refer to our middle distance hammer and discus throwing hurdler - John Coy. Well done all of you, we look forward to another exciting season in 1986. items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's record-breaking team win (16 points) in the South of the Thames Junior Cross Country Championship at Windsor on 10 November 1984, led by individual winner Oliver Foote.
items.s: UNIQUE RECORD WIN Report and results of Belgrave's record-breaking team win (16 points) in the South of the Thames Junior Cross Country Championship at Windsor on 10 November 1984, led by individual winner Oliver Foote. 10th NOVEMBER 1984 WINDSOR SOUTH OF THAMES - JUNIOR The South of the Thames 'Junior' Cross Country Championship is a senior event with barring conditions. Of our top men Pete Gilbey and Stuart Paton were not eligible. With Gary Staines injured we still felt we had enough fire power to worry the opposition. And so it turned out. Although the 5½ mile course was wet the stoney paths helped the faster track men to a good start and after 2 miles the 250 strong field was led by 4 Belgravians - Oliver Foote, Mark Sinclair, John Gladwin and Dave North, with Andy North and Francis Ward not far behind. Oliver opened up a gap from John with about 1 mile to go and won by 8 seconds followed by John, Mark in 6th and Dave 7th. The winning team's point score of 16 was the lowest ever beating the 19 pts record set by Belgrave in 1945 and the lads are now barred from this race. But the backing team could well repeat the victory next year with Andy North finishing a fine 13th and Francis Ward in 28th place. So a great day for Belgrave and Oliver having the satisfaction of adding his name to a cup with such greats as Chris Chataway (1949), Tim Johnson (1959), Dave Holt (1964), Pete Standing (1968), Dave Clarke (1977) and Roger Hackney (1978). Richard Partridge and Bob Treadwell had their own private battle for first. Partridge won on the day but was later disqualified as it was found that his residential qualification was not yet valid - so Oliver gained Silver - our best performance since Gerry North's days. Our senior men's team looked good for Bronze but fell away over the last 2 miles. In the Juniors Andy North almost ran up to the form he had displayed in the Surrey league as he finished 5th to get a Surrey vest. Again the Juniors got 4th team and with a bit of luck could have got Silver. items.s: INTER COUNTIES Report on Belgrave's Surrey representatives at the 1985 Inter-Counties Cross Country at Braunceston Park, Leicester. Two weeks after the Surreys our County representatives travelled to Braunceston Park Leicester to contest the Inter-Counties. In the Senior race a few overseas competitors added a bit of spice while Steve Cram was running to a fine 6th place to confirm his new winter training programme. Oliver Foote finished 46th in 37.07 but not finding the snow and ice to his liking. In the Junior race Andy North proved he should have had a Surrey medal as he finished in 55th place with 33.27 to be the second Surrey Junior man home. In the Youth race Simon Maynard was well in the 20's but faded to 45th in 20.31 as his lack of winter preparation showed. But what a promising young man he looks. items.sum: Report and results of the 1985 National Cross Country Championships at Milton Keynes, where Oliver Foote was 59th senior and Andy North 20th junior.
items.s: OLIVER AND ANDY EXCEL Report and results of the 1985 National Cross Country Championships at Milton Keynes, where Oliver Foote was 59th senior and Andy North 20th junior. 3rd MARCH 1985 MILTON KEYNES NATIONAL C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP It was cold, wet and unbelievably muddy at Milton Keynes as nearly 2000 Senior runners tackled the toughest race of the winter season. Each season the field gets bigger and this year saw 194 teams completing the course with Belgrave managing 45th place. Mike Hayes again gave an indication that he is over illness as he moved steadily through while Dave North who had succumbed to 'flu the week before battled gamely through to finish. Martin Lake too ran brilliantly on a reported 30 miles a week training schedule. Leo Lyons missed the start! But pride of place went again to Oliver Foote. Not known to like muddy courses he had a battle royal with Karl Harrison (who was to feature so well in 10k Road Races in the summer) with Karl finishing in 56th place and Oliver in 59th. And as for the Juniors - what can you say of Andy North's run. While others sank to their knees Andy floated across the mud and reminded many of us who were fortunate to see his run of another great North of some 30 years earlier! His 14th in the Southern should have equated to around 60th in the National (indeed local rival Mark Slowikowski finished 65th) but Andy seems to do better the harder the race. And so it was 20th place and some well known scalps to his credit. items.s: CAMBRIDGE H ROAD RELAY Report and results of the Cambridge Harriers road relay at Bexley on 17 March 1985, where Belgrave were third and Gary Staines ran the fastest time of the day. 17th MARCH 1985 BEXLEY CAMBRIDGE H ROAD RELAY Mike Hayes was the only member of last year's bronze medal team to return to Bexley and it is a measure of our increasing strength that we again came third narrowly failing to pip Aldershot for silver. Gary Staines was eager to run leg 1 and it soon became clear that he is moving into excellent form as at 2 miles he stretched away to record 15.42 for this near 3½ mile course and in so doing ran the fastest time of the day. Andy North took over 16 seconds in the lead and ran 32 seconds faster than last year (he was in the 'B' team then) to hand over still 14 seconds clear. Junior, John Warren, showed that he has now overcome illness and injury to record an excellent 16.53 and kept us in contention as we slipped to 3rd place. Steve Smullen, who a week earlier had run a 1.57 800m, slipped further back to 4th, but Stuart Paton pulled us back with a useful 16.27. As Mike Hayes took off 51 seconds behind the second placed Aldershot man he waited to see if he would be caught by the clan following Windsor and Invicta men. Imagine the surprise as he came into view of the finish breathing down the neck of the Aldershot man. Alas his early effort proved too much. But we had some first class performances to look back on. Particularly noteworthy was Chris Millbank's 'B' team run following his previous days win in the 5¼. items.s: SOUTHERN 12 STAGE RELAY Report and results of the Southern 12 Stage Road Relay hosted from Belgrave Hall at Wimbledon on 14 April 1985, where Belgrave finished 21st. 14th APRIL 1985 WIMBLEDON SOUTHERN 12 STAGE RELAY Last minute efforts by Clive Shippen helped prevent the Southern 12 Stage Relay being switched by the SCAAA's to the unpopular Thamesmead site. With a rejuvinated Belgrave Hall we were able to provide a worthy base for this year's race and it is to be hoped that we will be honoured with this event in the years ahead. Sadly our team couldn't match the hopes of our supporters and as in most recent years our top men reported unfit for duty although some of them jogging around the course seemed pretty fit to the casual observers. Andy North proved fastest of the short leg runners with the amazing 53 year old Laurie O'Hara second best. On the long leg Oliver showed little sign of his previous days 10km p.b. while Mike Hayes again ran exceptionally well. items.h: AND WHERE WAS THE CROSS COUNTRY CAPTAIN THIS WINTER ?
items.sum: Cross country captain Don Anderson's account of trekking to Annapurna base camp in the Himalayas after injury, being robbed on the descent and cycling and hitching back to Delhi.
items.s: AND WHERE WAS THE CROSS COUNTRY CAPTAIN THIS WINTER ? Cross country captain Don Anderson's account of trekking to Annapurna base camp in the Himalayas after injury, being robbed on the descent and cycling and hitching back to Delhi. Having not run for most of 1984, due to injury, I decided something positive was needed to "Bump start" my body back into action, so I chose to go trekking in the Himalayan mountains. This would be of little benefit for the road or track, but would be a good reminder of what hard work and endurance was all about. So off I set from Pakhora, a village in the valley, with tent, sleeping bag and back-pack weighing 26 kilograms, to Annapurna base camp, some 17,000 feet above sea level. Food and chlorinated water were essential items, as the area was rife with hepatitis, spinal meningitis and amoebic dysentery, not to mention sickness and diarrhoea; after all I was here to gain fitness not lose it. The first two days were a pleasant trek up to 3,000 feet, but the map I used was very inaccurate. It led me up the creek, so I scaled the mountainside in order to reach the village of Kanre, some 5,400 feet above sea level, to put me back on the right course. After that it was steady trekking to Tikedhunga. The paths were well used by donkey trains - the only means of transporting supplies to outlying villages but they carved the paths up making the going uneven and difficult. Back in the Khala valley it was nice to stop for a bath in the glacier fed river. It was cold, but certainly refreshed the parts that weren't often reached. Pressing on to the village of Shorepani, 9,300 feet above sea level, the snow settled on the tent at night and made the inside freezing. On to the village of Shanrung, which is above 10,000 feet. The view was breathtaking with the morning sun radiating the snow capped Annapurna peak and Machapuckhie (fish tail) mountains like forbidding gods. The next was the village of Chomrong, still climbing. By this time I was running short of time, so I decided to leave my kit at one of the lodges and run up to Annapurna base camp wearing only running kit. The view from the mountain was again breathtaking, and well worth the 5,000 mile trip. The adventure was by no means over, for during my descent to Kathmandu, I was robbed of my money and passport. The British Embassy refused to help me and so I had to resort to my own initiative to get back to Delhi, India. So I borrowed a bicycle and cycled hundreds of miles relying solely on local hospitality to provide me with food and accommodation. After some wheeling and dealing I crossed the border into India. From there to Delhi I hitched a lift on the footplate of a steam train, where we had tea and chapaties cooked on the train's boiler. The British High Commission in Delhi were more sympathetic to my cause and issued me with an emergency passport and lent me some cash whilst I waited for my flight to London. It was a very interesting trip, but in future, I shall limit my altitude training to Box Hill! Don Anderson Don Anderson Don Anderson cross country captain; injured most of 1984; trekked to Annapurna base camp. It is now over 10 years since the Belgravian reproduced the top 100 performances over our 5 3/4 mile road course. And there is good reason why this particular bunch of statistics has laid dormant for so long - there have been hardly any runs inside the 100th best mark of 10 years ago! In fact, just one run apiece from Messrs O'Hara, Weller, Stow, Duncan, Bicourt and Foote. items.s: 29TH WELLINGTON INTERN. RELAY Report and results of the 29th Wellington International Relay at Ostend on 31 March 1985, where a young Belgrave team finished third of 53 teams. 31st MARCH 1985 OSTEND 29TH WELLINGTON INTERN. RELAY For a variety of reasons only Dave Mote, Guy Sagar, Mark Sinclair and Derrick Williams of last years winning 12 made the return journey for this years International Relay held on the Wellington race-course at Ostend. We took the opportunity to "blood" the youngsters and new members. With Oliver Foote and Mike Hayes adding experience over the longer legs and superb runs from Steve Smullen and Mark Sinclair we finished in bronze position. A truly splendid performance in this elite company with Aldershot and Blackheath left trailing. Every run was impressive and it was great to see our new 400m squadies - Mike Bazire and Will Willson doing so well. Dave Mote looked as though he's over injury and attacked into gale force winds. Guy Sagar produced his usual gutty run- while Junior, Simon Maynard made a fine debut at this level of competition. The team was grateful for the vociferous encouragement from 13 loyal supporters who were rewarded with fine sunshine, but gale force winds which managed to suit a Hovercraft at Dover!! And thanks to Don Anderson. Forced to work nights he travelled over on the day of the race just to cheer on the team, and then rushed straight back well satisfied with our efforts. FRANCIS IMPROVES Francis Ward, back in Ireland for a 6 month University training course, used the opportunity to get in some high quality races. On March 24th at Straffan in a 10k Road Race he finished 12th out of a field of 500 in a creditable 32.49. Two months later in the 1985 Irish Universities Championships he lowered his track 10k p.b. to 31:33.2 just missing out on a bronze medal as he finished a tired but happy fourth. items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Introduction to the issue's track and field section reviewing a record-breaking year, with a list of report writers. An eventful 12 months with many individual and team successes plus a considerable number of personal best performances. Almost all of our senior Club Records were under threat and several fell; with John Regis taking Ernest's 200m time, John Gladwin bettering his own 800m time, Ken O extended his discus record and Gary Staines became our first sub 4 minute miler. Ernest became our first AAA's track champ winning an exciting 100m in a year when he has given unstinting support to our British League Side. If you're of an excitable nature skip this Section ! items.h: INDOOR ROUND-UP - GREAT SPRINTING FROM ERNEST OBENG AND JOHN REGIS
items.sum: Steve Williams's review of the 1985 indoor season, led by Ernest Obeng's 6.63 60m club record and John Regis's AAA Under 20 200m win, with a UK all-time indoor 200m list.
items.s: INDOOR ROUND-UP - GREAT SPRINTING FROM ERNEST OBENG AND JOHN REGIS Steve Williams's review of the 1985 indoor season, led by Ernest Obeng's 6.63 60m club record and John Regis's AAA Under 20 200m win, with a UK all-time indoor 200m list. With the middle distance boys giving the indoor season a miss, it was mainly the sprinters who kept the Belgrave name to the fore on the boards in 1985. Ernest Obeng began what must be his most significant indoor campaign on 12 January at the Cosford Games when he sprinted to a fine p.b. over 60m - 6.68 - just shaded by the eventual European Champion, Mike McFarlane but ahead of some useful domestic competition in Watson, Asquith and Sharp. Phil Lovell was another Belgravian in 2nd place with a 4.70 pole vault behind Jeff Gutteridge. Two weeks later, Ernest lined up again at Cosford to defend his AAA's title. Amongst those alongside him were McFarlane again and Desruelles of Belgium and although he was away as well as these two, he lost out in the pick up from 30 metres and had to be content with the bronze medal. Nevertheless his time of 6.71 was still faster than he had run prior to this season. Mike Alleyne had also travelled up for this event and recorded 7.18 in the heats. Unfortunately, Phil Lovell no heighted in the vault this time. Ernest then departed for a short visit to the continent and took advantage of the better indoor surface at Sindelfingen, W.G., where, on 1st February, he won the 60m event in a fabulous new club record of 6.63 which is one of the fastest times ever in the World - the third fastest by a Commonwealth athlete before McFarlane's European run! Two days later Ernie backed this up with a 6.65 at Karlsruhe. Great sprinting! The Juniors next took the stage at Cosford on 17 March at the AAA Under 20 Championships and more medals fell to the claret and gold as our new sprinter, John Regis, demonstrated some real quality with a tremendous victory at 200m in a CBP of 21.93, which is some sprinting round the tight bends of an indoor track. In fact, this run placed John as the 8th fastest ever UK indoor performer! John had previously placed 2nd in the 60m championship in 6.90 and although 200m seems his specialist distance we can anticipate some good things from him over 100m as well. Phil Goedluck, in his first year as a Junior recorded 7.07 and 22.63 in the heats, which made him the fastest 17 year old, and Phil can look forward to two more attempts at these titles! At the other end of the age range, our 'new' Vet, Snowy Brooks, was in good form at the British Veterans Championships held at Cosford on 23 March. Snowy won the 60mH in 9.3 and the Long Jump in a new UK Best performance of 6.14. He also placed 5th in the 60m in 7.8 (7.7ht) and recorded 25.4 in the heats of the 200m. items.s: EARLY BIRDS Round-up of Belgrave early-season track bests in spring 1985, led by Michael Allayne's sprinting and Mark Sinclair and Mike Hayes in the steeplechase. EARLY BIRDS Following several low key performances last summer it seemed as though Michael Allayne was approaching the 1985 Track and Field season with renewed enthusiasm. We first spotted his 7.18 sec. 60m effort in the 1985 AAA's Cosford Indoor Champs. This was soon followed by an excellent 35.1 300m at an open meeting at Dartford. In March he ran a p.b. 49.5 sec 400m at an open meeting at the Crystal Palace and it is in this event that his many Belgrave fans believe he has the greatest potential. A sub 48.0 this season is a real possibility. Other impressive early season results are to hand. Several Belgravians have notched up p.b's which indicate a fine year ahead for many of our established Stars. On the 20th April at Battersea Park, Mark Sinclair ran his first 2000 S/C and won in 5.54.8 closely followed by Mike Hayes in 5.57.7. Four days later Mike won a Southern Counties Match 3000 S/C at Crystal Palace with a huge p.b. in 9.03.9 while the following Saturday Mark won the Surrey 3000 S/C in 9.12.0 at the Croydon Arena 'dust bowl'. Oliver Foote and David North - our mainstays for the British League 5000m - confirmed early season form with p.b's of 8.17.3 and 8.26.6 at the Southern Counties match while a week later in a graded meeting Mark Sinclair also ran a p.b. 3000 in 8.20.1. While this was going on 16 year old Graham Adams ran 60.7 for the 400H - again a big p.b. while 20 year old John Warren lowered his 3000 p.b. to 8.37.2. items.s: NIKE BLACKHEATH H 25 x 1 MILE - 1984 Note that Belgrave were awarded the 1984 Nike Blackheath 25 x 1 mile relay after Sale's disqualification, with Gary Staines fastest in 4.06, and a call for runners for 22 September. NIKE BLACKHEATH H 25 x 1 MILE - 1984 The official results of the 1984 25 x 1 Mile Relay were a long time coming and with good reason. After extensive debate between Blackheath and sponsors Nike, Sale were disqualified from 1st spot as a result of some runners competing without Club vests while others were paced. As a result Belgrave repeated their 1983 victory and the winning team each received a pair of Nike Transit trainers while Gary Staines, who recorded the days fastest time with 4.06 also won a pair of spikes. With so many up and coming youngsters it should take 4.35 to make the team this year. The date is Sunday, September 22nd at Crystal Palace and a UK record by Belgrave is on the cards if everyone turns out. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP Introduction to the 1985 Southern League season, thanking the 68 athletes who competed and noting club records by Andy North and Glynn Tieoran. SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP First of all, I would like to thank all those who turned out in the Southern League this season, all 68 of them ! I think this proves that we are giving as many people as possible competition at this level. With the strong likelihood of a 'C' team next season there is room for even more. So never think you are not good enough. We try to fit every one in somewhere and don't forget there are non scoring races at 200m and 1500m at every meeting. A look through the results will show who did what and where and quite a few of the 'A' team will be looking over their shoulders at the quality of some of them. Those that stand out are the two club records that were set; Andy North's junior 5,000 record of 14:55:8 at Battersea on 25th May and Glynn Tieoran's 1500 youth record of 4:02:8 also at Battersea on 3rd August. There were also a host of p.b.'s set throughout the season. So with a few more people willing to travel to away matches and prepared to "race" on cinder, we may have two teams in their respective premier divisions in our centenary year. items.s: SIMON MAYNARD'S FIRST TITLE Report and results of the club championships at Battersea Park on 8 May 1985, where 17-year-old Simon Maynard won the 5000m on his debut at the distance. SIMON MAYNARD'S FIRST TITLE 8th MAY 1985 BATTERSEA PARK CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP Our first Club Championship of the season coincided with the 40th Anniversary of VE day and for 17 year old Simon Maynard his 5000m debut turned into a dream. Showing great maturity he sat on the leaders throughout taking the lead only in the finishing straight as he eventually overcame the strength of Martin Lake while the first five home all recorded p.b's. The supporting events were all well attended. In the 800 John Booth looked impressive as he followed Steve Smullen through the bell in 56 secs and also recorded a p.b. In the throws Ken, Tony Featherstone and Mike Small came together for the first time confirming our growing strength in the field events. 5000m: 1.S.Maynard (J) 15:21.6; 2.M.Lake 15:22.4, 3.L.Lyons 15:37.5; 4.D.Clack 15:42.0; 5.C.Millbank 15:46.0; 6.E.Boytler 15:47.0; 7.M.Donahue 16.01; 8.M.Bizio 16.08; 9.B.MacRae 16.29; 10.L.Coy 16.50, 11.E.Bird 17.06; 12.A.Pollit 17.11; 13.D.Maughan 17.26; 14.C.Howard 17.35; 15.A.Stone 17.36; 16.A.Grant 17.46; 17.S.Smith 17.56; 18.T.Eden 18.00; 19.R.Bale 18.05; 20.L.Mclean 18.06; 21.J.Rayner 18.55; 22.L.Mann 19.01; 23.D.Davies 19.13; 800m 'A': 1.S.Smullen 1:55.7; 2.J.Booth (Y) 1:58.3; 3.A.Painter 2:01.0; 4.S.Williams 2:03.0; 5.K.Green 2:03.0; 6.A.Gayton 2:03.1; 7.M.Leeson 2:03.9; 8.D.North 2:06.0; 800m 'B': 1.P.Halliday 2:02.7; 2.M.Johnson 2:04.0; 3.A.North 2:05.8; 4.A.Ludlow 2:08.6; 5 - 2:10.3; 6.B.Hall 2:15.4; DT: 1.K.Onuaguluchi 51.34; 2.A.Featherstone 43.76; 3.M.Small 41.46; 4.M.Hill 35.82. items.s: SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS (PART 2) Report and Belgrave results from part two of the Surrey County Championships at Motspur Park on 13-18 May 1985, highlighted by Glyn Tiernan's championship best in the youths 1500m. 13-18th MAY 1985 MOTSPUR PARK SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS (PART 2) With several members chosing not to compete we were nonetheless splendidly represented with a host of medals. Mark Sinclair failed by a whisker to win the 1500m where heats and final were run within 2 hours due to the earlier heats being washed out. Mark Shippen finally got it together in the pole vault. Derrick Williams showed some impressive speed and looks set for a best ever season. Oliver Foote too surprised with a fast last 800m in the 5000 being recorded at 57 secs for the final 400m as he gained a silver in a p.b. But pride of place must go to the Youths with Gavin Warr clocking a fine 23.1 in the 200m final and Glyn Tiernan breaking a 15 year old Championship Best Performance to win the Youths 1500m by a huge margin. (Historians may note that the previous record was held by none other than Belgrave's Bill Custin who ran 4:07.1 in 1970). items.s: Note that Gary Staines and Mark Sinclair ran for the AAA in a representative match at Crystal Palace on 15 May 1985. On Wednesday 15th May Gary Staines and Mark Sinclair gained AAA's vests in a representative match at Crystal Palace. Gary confirmed his early season form with a 3:47.2 1500m timing despite arriving only 10 minutes before the race while Mark Sinclair fell in the 2000m S/C and was badly spiked. Nonetheless he got up and finished in 5:57.1. items.s: BRITISH LEAGUE - DIVISION 3 RESULTS - MATCH 1 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 1 at Enfield on 11 May 1985, where Belgrave finished second, two points behind WSE. BRITISH LEAGUE - DIVISION 3 RESULTS 11th MAY 1985 ENFIELD MATCH 1 With last years visit to Enfield in mind - bad weather and a third place - we hoped that both would improve in this the first match in Division 3. Sadly, the weather was much worse, but our performances warmed everybody as we achieved a solid second place - having led Windsor by two points with one relay to go! Bels had eight individual wins - Ernest, having been caught by St. Louis in the 100, won the 200, Stuart and Gary had fine double wins in the 800, Mark Sinclair outkicked the field to win the 1500 and he was backed up well by Steve Smullen, who won the 'B' event. Pete Gilbey won the 'B' S/C, having avoided the elbow to elbow tactics of Large (S & E) and Mike Hayes. Ken won the discus in very unfavourable conditions and our 4x100 team had a comfortable win. Mike Bazire and Tony Featherstone made their BAL debuts, in a very satisfactory start to the season. items.sum: Report and results of British League Division 3 match 2 at Windsor on 1 June 1985, where Belgrave were third after being pipped by Windsor in the last relay.
items.s: MATCH 2 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 2 at Windsor on 1 June 1985, where Belgrave were third after being pipped by Windsor in the last relay. 1st JUNE 1985 WINDSOR MATCH 2 Glorious weather was the order of the day at Windsor and hopes were high of a repeat of last years fine win. Unfortunately Southampton and Windsor turned out very strong teams and we had to be content with third place. We again headed Windsor by two points with just the last relay left and they again managed to pip us at the post. Ernest, thought that he had nicked the 100 from Todd Bennett as they crossed the line together, but the S & E man was given the verdict. Gary almost caught the England Captain on the line in a fine 800 metres race. Stuart won the 'B' event and John Regis made his BAL debut by winning the 'B' 100, but unfortunately an injury kept him out of the short relay, despite this the 4x100 team equaled the Club Record. In the Long Jump Derrick Williams led the field with a good 7.15 metres and he also won the 'B' TJ. Ken again triumphed in the discus and almost sneaked a win in the shot. Will Willson, Dave Catling, Leo Lyons and Nigel Clarke competing in the BAL for the first time, all performed exceptionally well. items.sum: Report and results of British League Division 3 match 3 at Brighton on 30 June 1985, which Belgrave won by half a point to go top of the division.
items.s: MATCH 3 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 3 at Brighton on 30 June 1985, which Belgrave won by half a point to go top of the division. 30th JUNE 1985 BRIGHTON MATCH 3 At the half way stage in the League, the promotion battle was between Windsor, Bels and Southampton while Enfield, Brighton and local rivals HHH all had to fight to avoid the drop. Brighton, the home club had never finished lower than second in all their previous home BAL Matches. Southampton were getting their act together following their win at Windsor and WSE were determined to keep their lead at the top of Div.III. It promised to be a great day and that is how it turned out. We were always in the first three throughout the afternoon and did not lead until very late. Our double wins in the 5000 (Olly and Mark both with p.b's) and the Pole Vault (Phil and Mark) pushed us into the lead that we did not lose although it was very close with just ½ a point between Southampton and ourselves after an exciting final relay. Enfield did us a favour by tying with Windsor and this resulted in the Bels heading Div.III after a memorable day. Individual performances that should be mentioned are Mark Lindsay-Bayley who filled in for Derrick Williams in the Triple after Derrick had injured himself in the first round of the Long Jump. Derrick was also a key member of the Relay team and Aham volunteered to run in his place and he also had a go at the High Jump! Andy Paton came along as a spectator and in borrowed gear ran a storming first leg in the Long Relay. Mike Bazire pushed himself to the limit as he gave all in both relays. With this tremendous team spirit we won a match where we could have easily finished third. The other heroes of the day were the throwers - they really excelled. Mike Small in his first BAL Match for us had a great afternoon. Ken threw the hammer for the first time and Tony Featherstone threw 46 metres in the discus, to get a p.b. by a large margin. Ernest broke Peter Radfords ground record in the 100 and left Todd Bennett for dead as he scorched to a fine win. MLB and Dave Sheldon ran p.b's in the Long Hurdles and Alan Benn made his debut in the BAL. items.sum: Report and results of British League Division 3 match 4 at Southwark Park on 10 August 1985, won by Belgrave with 256 points and a club and league record 41.1 in the 4x100 relay.
items.s: MATCH 4 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 4 at Southwark Park on 10 August 1985, won by Belgrave with 256 points and a club and league record 41.1 in the 4x100 relay. 10th AUGUST 1985 SOUTHWARK PARK MATCH 4 This last match was switched from Tooting and despite protests was held at Southwark Park. The afternoon got off to a stormy start as most of the vaulters refused to take part as the conditions were dangerous. The match followed the same pattern as before with the Bels never out of the first three and we took the lead with just a few events to go. It turned out to be a memorable day for the Club and its many supporters - they drowned the other teams supporters with their noise. Our throwers were again magnificent - out of eight events they recorded 4 wins, 3 seconds and a third place. It was good to see Vincent Cornibert again and he certainly shook-up the Javelin competition. 16 year old Graham Adams came into the team at the last minute and ran really well to finish 3rd in the 'B' 800. Tom Taylor also made his BAL debut for us and had two splendid second places. Chris Cornwell equalled the Club Record and became our first 2.00 High Jumper in BAL Competition. Another performance that went unnoticed was that of Derrick Williams in the Triple Jump. Both he and Aham were struggling below their best when with one jump left he produced a magnificent 14.75 to completely change the points position for the event. Pride of place must go to the 4x100 Relay team who recorded a new Club and Div.3 League record with a spectacular 41.1 with a good second in the 4x400 Relay it rounded off a marvellous afternoon for the Club. Our winning points score of 256 was the highest of the 4 matches despite the absence of the pole vault result in which we normally amass around 20 points. items.s: Photo of the 4x100 relay changeovers in the final BAL match, with Ernest Obeng handing to Phil Goedluck and Todd Bennett to Roger Black. A highlight of this years BAL matches has been the sprints and relays with Todd Bennett turning out for Southampton and Ernest for Belgrave. items.s: From Brian Pritchard Letter from Brian Pritchard congratulating the club on winning British League Division 3 and thanking team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws. LETTERS From Brian Pritchard I would like to congratulate the Club on their achievement of winning Division 3 of the British League. Having followed our team very closely during the past five years, I believe our rise in consecutive seasons from Div.5 to Div.2 is quite remarkable considering the very high standard of the British League. I would firstly like to congratulate the team on their superb achievement and in the way they have responded when asked to turn out for the Club, and secondly to thank Leo Coy and Bill Laws for the magnificent way they have managed the team, and I can not think of anyone else who could have done the job as well. I look forward to next season with anticipation. I am sure I speak for all the supporters who have turned up at the meetings, in wishing the team, Leo and Bill the best of luck for next year. Brian Pritchard Brian Pritchard Leo Coy Leo Coy British League team manager Leo Coy Leo Bill Laws Bill Laws British League team manager Bill Laws Bill British Athletics League

items.sum: Letter from Derrick Williams describing a day in Watford filming a long jump coaching video with Lyn Davies, with a photo of him jumping.
items.s: From Derrick Williams Letter from Derrick Williams describing a day in Watford filming a long jump coaching video with Lyn Davies, with a photo of him jumping. From Derrick Williams As promised a few lines about my latest filming exploits. The saga starts one Friday morning, going about my usual days work when I received a 'phone call from Jim Alford who wanted to know if I was available for a few days, as they were in the process of making a series of videos for coaching consisting of all the events in track and field. My involvement was slightly different in that with the other video they had an experienced athlete e.g. Seb Coe, David Hemery etc. to both demonstrate and talk about the techniques involved in their events, but I came into the story because for the long jump they had Lyn Davies who was quite able to coach, but because of a long-standing injury didn't feel able to run and jump. So a replacement was called for. Not being able to get an exact double they searched for the next best thing - a tall very handsome and capable athlete. But failure again left them with just one option ... me. So my day began at seven thirty a.m. Taxi to wisk me off to the film location which was not L.A. as I had hoped, but sunny Watford. Arrived at around 8.45 a.m. and met everyone involved; the director Tony Maylam who made the "Super Milers", the film crew, Lyn Davies and the young athletes who were all still at school. The day began with Lyn breaking down the preparation for any session, warm up stretching, drills etc. Then with the aid of the youngsters he did the approach run, take off, movement through the air and landing. All the youngsters performed very well. They were of different standards which was lucky as they showed common faults any beginner would have. By 3 o'clock they had done the maximum work their tired bodies would allow. So I was told to make ready for my entrance. I had been sitting to one side up to this point watching and learning all the little points Lyn Davies mentioned. I was supposed to be the finished article, with the technique the youngsters should hope to one day emulate, so for the next three hours I was running flat out and jumping into a pit littered with camera men and equipment. They were filming with three different cameras so I was at it time after time after time and at around 6 o'clock I was wondering how much longer when those magic words sung out "Just one more take Derrick". I thought we'll have to make this a good one. So using my 'fabled speed" I sprinted to the board and launched myself high into the air and to the horror of the camera men landed less than six inches from the cameras sending sand over everyone. Thankfully they saw the funny side. And so ended a memorable days work, very hard but also very rewarding, meeting Lyn Davies was an honour. With best wishes to all. Jumping With style! Derrick Williams immaculate technique has now been captured in a series of coaching videos made for the I.F.A. which is to be distributed to over 140 Countries. items.s: THE STEVE WILLIAMS' ROUND-UP Steve Williams's round-up of Belgrave international, championship and representative performances in 1985, including Ernest Obeng's AAA 100m title, Gary Staines's first sub-4-minute mile by a Belgravian and John Regis's European Junior medals. THE STEVE WILLIAMS' ROUND-UP ROUND-UP OF THE BEST OF BELS INTERNATIONAL, CHAMPIONSHIP AND REPRESENTATIVE PERFORMANCES As has become usual in recent years, we were well represented in the early SCAAA matches at Crystal Palace. On 24 April, Olly Foote (8.17.3) and Dave North (8.26.5) ran pb's over 3000m while Mike Hayes placed 2nd in the 'chase in 9.03.9, also a fine pb; Phil Lovell won the Pole Vault at 4.80 and Ken Onuaguluchi placed 2nd in the Discus with 51.34. On 1 May, Stu' Paton was 2nd over 800m in 1.53.5, Mark Sinclair 2nd in the Southern 'Standards' 3000m in a pb of 8.20.1, and Phil again won the vault with 4.80 and, this time, Ken, the Discus with 49.88.// AAA's representative vests were won by four Bels on 15 May at C/Palace where John Regis won the 200m in 21.8, Gary Staines was 4th over 1500m in 3.47.5, Mark Sinclair 6th in the 2km 'chase in 5.57.2 and Phil Lovell 3rd in the Vault again at 4.80.// On 21 May Stuart Paton was over in Norway where he ran what turned out to be a seasons best 1500m in 3.48.57. * * * UK Championships - Antrim - 25/26 May - JOHN REGIS shares 200m title:- A trip over the Irish Sea paid handsome dividends for John Regis, Gary Staines and Phil Lovell who all collected medals. John brought home Gold from his dead heat with Linford Christie in the 200m in a magnificent 21.59 (club jnr. rec.) despite carrying a hamstring problem, and backed this up with Silver in the 100m in 10.5, also a club jnr. rec. A feature of John's running was his remarkable finishing speed. Gary took Bronze in the 1500m in a typically gutsy run (3.44.22) and Phil found his consistency at 4.80 bringing Silver in the vault - a fine performance in miserable conditions. Also competing were Mike Hayes - 9.12.4 for 14th in the 'chase and Stu' Paton 3.54.17 in the 1500m heats. * * * At the Glasgow Games on 9 June, Ernie Obeng held off Sharp and Watson over 100m in 10.3 and, representing Loughbro' against AAA's, three days later, won at 100m in 10.45w and placed 2nd over 200m in 21.22w. * * * SCAAA Championships - C/Palace - 14/15 June - GARY STAINES wins 1500m:- Our highlight was undoubtedly Gary's win in the 1500m. It was his first major championship outdoors and his determined final 200m in a closing lap of 56.9 showed improved finishing. Well done Gary. Medals were also won by Stu' Paton - close to his best time over 800m but too far off the pace when the winner jumped the field; Phil Lovell, 3rd in the Pole Vault and Ken Onuaguluchi 2nd in the Discus - a medal in these championships is becoming a nice habit for these two. Results:100m D Williams 11.15ht 200m M Alleyne 22.47ht, P Lyttle 23.03ht 400m G Sagar 52.30ht 800m 3rd S Paton 1.49.03, 5th J Gladwin 1.50.35(1.49.85sf), N Clarke 1.55.39ht-pb 1500m 1st G Staines 3.42.89 5000m O Foote 14.53.26 3000mSc 12th M Hayes 9.14.54 PV 3rd P Lovell 4.80 LJ 8th D Williams 7.03 TJ 10th A Amadi 14.34 SP 6th K Onuaguluchi 14.89pb DT 2nd K Onuaguluchi 54.56. * * * On 21st June, JOHN REGIS became the latest Belgrave International when selected to run 200m against the USA at Birmingham. This was something of a firey baptism for an athlete still a junior and John should not be too unhappy with his 6th place (21.68) in company which included the Olympic Bronze medallist, the World Silver medallist and a 20.07 performer in the US team! *** GARY STAINES ran 3.44.77 in Poland on 24 June. *** On 30th June, STUART PATON was an International winner for Scotland against Ireland and Catalonia, using that great acceleration to swamp Paul Forbes amongst others in the 800m in 1.50.97.*** At the World Veterans Championships in Rome at the end of June, SNOWY BROOKS was a match for the best with a Silver Medal in the Long Jump (6.42) and Bronze in the Pentathlon (3475 pts). * * * Surrey v Army v Hants - Aldershot - 3 July: 3000mSc 5th M Sinclair 9.24.0; 110mH 3rd T Taylor 15.3, 5th M Lindsay-Bayley 15.4; PV 1st P Lovell 4.60; LJ 1st T Taylor 6.99; TJ 1st A Amadi 14.42; SP 3rd D Dawson 14.18, 4th P McKay 14.15. * * * English Schools Championships - Hull - 12/13 July:- Snr Boys 200m 2nd M Adams 21.9(21.6sf) 5th P Goedluck 22.3(22.1sf): Inter Boys 200m G Warr 23.0sf TJ F Ogwuda 13.57qual. ERNEST OBENG AAA'S CHAMP. AAA Championships - C/Pal - 13/14 July - ERNEST OBENG 100m CHAMPION:- Third in 1978, second in 1981 and now first in 1985, Ernest Obeng has become only the second Belgrave runner to win a Senior AAA title by taking the 100m championship this year (his only predecessor being Bill Nankeville who won the Mile in 1948). Coming comfortably through his heat and semi-final in 10.51 and 10.42 respectively, Ernie looked an obvious medal prospect, although the American 10.10 performer, Darwin Cook, who had already beaten Ernie in the Ulster Games, must have been favourite. And it was Cook who got the best start in the final with Ernie, suprisingly one of the last away. So with what is usually the best part of Ernie's race over, observers could have been forgiven for thinking our man would be run out of it - but, maintaining his form wonderfully through the last 20 metres in a storming finish, Ernie just edged ahead when it counted. Only 5/100ths covered the first 5 across the line but Ernie was in no doubt he had made it, celebrating with one arm raised aloft as he ran through. Well done Ernest! The full result for posterity:-1st E OBENG 10.44; 2nd D Cook(USA) 10.45; 3rd Imoh(Nig) 10.46; 4th L Asquith 10.49; 5th B Watson 10.56; 6th D Reid 10.72 (McFarlane 10.46 disq.,Christie dnf) The wind was 1.4m/s against./// Our other top men in action were John Gladwin - first Briton home in the 800m in 5th place with 1.47.08, the start of a great series of runs from him, lasting to the end of the season; Gary Staines - a pb of 3.41.48 in qualifying for the 1500m final where he placed 10th in 3.44.45; Phil Lovell =8th in the Vault with 4.80 and Ken Onuaguluchi 6th in the Discus with 51.88. Also Mike Alleyne - 400m ht of 49.32 and Stuart Paton - 1.50.01 800m ht. * * * At the Peugeot Talbot Games at C/Pal on 19/20 July Ernest Obeng confirmed his AAA form with Imoh and Asquith, winning the 100m in 10.39 while John Gladwin was the winner of the 1000m from a good domestic field in 2.19.69. It was also at this meeting that we saw the FIRST SUB 4 MINUTE MILE BY A BELGRAVIAN when Gary Staines chased home Steve Cram in a time of 3.59.24. Stu' Paton ran 4.07.89. * * * Edinburgh Games-23 July:100m E Obeng 4th 10.48 * * * The Bislett Stadium again did the trick for JOHN GLADWIN, who reduced his 800m best to 1.46.11 in the process of winning the Oslo Games event on 27 July in a dip finish with Moussa Fall, following the disqualification of Mack. And John's verdict on the new surface is that it's not as fast as the old one! * * * At the Inter-Counties Championships held at Thurrock on 28 July, Ernie Obeng retained his 100m title from McFarlane in 10.9 into a strong wind as did Gary Staines in the Mile with 4.12.3. And, going one better than in the last two years, Ken Onuaguluchi made it a great Belgrave hat-trick by taking the Discus with a throw of 52.20. * * * At the IAC Grand Prix at C\Palace on 2 August, KEN ONUAGULUCHI just missed his own club record in the Discus with a fine throw of 55.18 in 4th place. * * * Budapest Grand Prix-4 Aug:Ernest Obeng maintained his good form with a 10.36 clocking behind Nagy and Lara, while John Gladwin ran what he admitted was probably his worst ever tactical race, placing 6th in 1.47.92. Then, over 2000m, there was an outstanding run not only from Steve Cram but also from Gary Staines who finished 6th in a remarkable 5.02.67, indicating that whatever Gary has achieved so far, he can surely reach greater heights over 3000m and 5000m eventually. * * * SCAAA v Comb. Serv. v Welsh AAA v Achilles - 7 Aug - C\Pal:3000mSc 3rd M Sinclair 8.56.9 - a great personal best from Mark who can make a big impact in this event. PV 1st P Lovell 4.90 - equals Phil's own club record. LJ\TJ T Taylor 1st\5th 7.43\14.37 SP\HT 4th\6th P McKay 13.91\46.54 DT 1st K Onuaguluchi 53.34. Kodak Classic - Gateshead -9 August:100m 2nd E Obeng 10.58;DT 3rd K Onuaguluchi 54.62 U\20 Inter County Match-11 August: Jnrs: 100m'B' 1st P Goedluck 11.2; 200m 1st M Adams 22.1;3000m 4th A North 8.50.7. Yths: 100m'B' 2nd G Warr 12.0; 200m'B' 5th M Dooley 23.8; 1500m 3rd G Tiernan 4.11.8; 3000m 7th M Kinane 9.14.7; TJ 4th F Ogwuda 13.50. * * * At the AAA's U\20 Championships in Birmingham, John Regis placed a magnificent 2nd over 100m in 10.46w (10.45w ht) a run which clinched his selection for the European Junior Championships. Equally impressive was Marcus Adams with 3rd over 200m in 22.08 into a 4.56w!! And, backing these two up, we had Phil Goedluck running his fastest ever times - 10.79w for 7th in the 100 (10.75w ht) and 22.40 for 6th in the 200m (22.12 ht). Fast Juniors indeed! Our promising Triple Jumper, Festus Ogwuda placed 5th in the Youths event with 13.62, a fine performance. * * * At a Nottingham Open Combined Events meeting on 17/18 August, Festus Ogwuda completed a Decathlon with Junior implements in a club record score of 5010 points. * * * Home Junior International-Meadowbank-21 Aug: 100m 1st J Regis 10.87 200m 1st M Adams 21.54 (This was a further improvement in the Club Junior Record and an amazing run from a 17 year old into an unhelpful headwind!) * * * In one of the best kept secrets of the Europa Cup Final weekend, England 'B' were taking on France in Le Touquet. John Gladwin won selection for the 800m where he had a comfortable win in 1.46.88.*** Ernest Obeng ran a season's best of 10.28 in Zurich on 21 August, going on to 7th in the final in 10.43. * * * European Junior Championships, Cottbus, East Germany - 22/25 August - "Ein Kurzstreckenlauf Fantastisch": Well, what can one say about an individual Bronze Medal and Relay Gold by JOHN REGIS at these Championships. No doubt most of you were watching on TV and saw the way he ate up the ground in the last 30 metres of the 100m to come through to 3rd place behind Elliot Bunney and Havas of Hungary, in another Club Junior Record, after a cautious start because of a still tender hamstring. It was a fabulous run in any circumstances let alone those but perhaps John was even better on the final leg of the 4x100m where he brought the team home to the Gold Medal in a new UK Junior record of 39.80! I believe he must have come close to the club high jump record with that leap in front of the UK team in the stands at the end!! * * * At Crystal Palace on 26 August, JOHN GLADWIN completely dominated an International 800m for England against Poland, Hungary and Czechoslovakia, leading all the way to a time of 1.47.77. What with a victory lap in front of the home crowd and signing autographs afterwards, this was an afternoon for him to savour. * * * Tooting Bec Re-Opening Meeting - 24 August: KEN ONUAGULUCHI 56.08 - ANOTHER CLUB RECORD Leading Bels results:- 400m'B' 3. M Kinane 2.01.8 * * * Whistlestop 100's from Ernie: Koblenz-28 Aug-6th 10.52: Riccione-31 Aug-3rd 10.53: Rieti-4 Sept-3rd 10.39.*** On 15 Sept at C\Palace Phil Goedluck won over 100m at the U\20 Inter Area match in 11.03. * * * John Gladwin and Gary Staines brought their most successful seasons to a close on a short tour of China with the England U/23 team. In Beijing on 8 September, John won the 800m in 1.47.35 with the European Champion in his wake, while Gary won over 1500m in a tactical 3.51.15. Then, 3 days later in Nanjing, John completed a fine double in his second fastest time - 1.46.42 with Ferner again behind, while Mark Rowland, this time reversed placings with Gary in the 1500m, Gary clocking 3.54.10 in another slow race. OLIVER SOUTHERN 10 KM SILVER It was inevitable that when Oliver Foote found himself in a higher class 10k field than the County Championships he would come up with something a little closer to his potential. And so it was at the Southern Counties Championship at Crystal Palace on 11 September where he ran to a fine Silver Medal and a time of 29.49.4 - fastest by a Belgravian for 17 years! It was also at this meeting that Matthew Kinane confirmed his progress this year by breaking the longstanding Club Youths Mile Record with 4.26.0 in 7th place in the Peter Coe mile. * * * International Youth Friendship Games - Crystal Palace - 29 September - JOHN REGIS 20.78!!! John Regis was really in a purple patch at the end of the season and his final race produced a brilliant 20.78 clocking over 200m to succeed Ernie Obeng as Club record holder; I believe that only 3 British Juniors have ever gone faster. And in case you didn't know it, John is still a Junior next season!! Another spectacular performance came in the 4x200m when Mike Bazire, Phil Goedluck and Marcus Adams joined John to clock a time that only 2 UK National teams and a Haringey club side, amongst British teams, have ever beaten. There were some other pretty good performances as well - if that's not an understatement - with Marcus Adams, Phil Goedluck and Youth Joe Minetti all sprinting magnificently. items.s: How the Club Mile Record Has Progressed Box listing the progression of the Belgrave club mile record from Len Herbert's 4.21.0 in 1939 to Gary Staines's 3.59.24 in 1985. How the Club Mile Record Has Progressed Club records were not formalised until after 1950 and our early history is a little short on details such as times. However, it is reported that A H N Edward, Hon. Sec of the club from 1887-1898, was "a sound 4.30 miler" and A D Pyer is believed to have run 4.22 in the early 1920's.(Confirmation of any times from this period would be welcomed).But the following is probably accurate:- Len Herbert 4.21.0 ( 8.7.39) Bill Nankeville 4.14.2 ( 48) Jack Brown 4.13.6 (21.6.52) " 4.13.4 (10.9.52) " 4.12.0 (10.7.53) " 4.11.8 ( 7.54) Brian Hallowell 4.10.6 ( 6.56) John Davies 4.10.6 ( 6.58) Ranjit Bhatia 4.08.7 ( 4.60) Mal Robinson 4.08.3 ( 62) " 4.07.1 (30.3.63) John Thresher 4.05.5 (26.5.64) " 4.02.1 (22.7.64) Gary Staines 4.02.1 ( 5.9.84) " 3.59.24 (20.7.85) A H N Edward A H N Edward Hon. items.s: WITH THE LADIES Harry Porter's winter report on the Belgrave women's section: first inter-counties representatives, county and Surrey League team medals, the walkers and winter training. WITH THE LADIES It has been quite an exciting winter. This year was the first time we had had representatives (Rosemary Honeychurch, Vicky Mitchell and Jenny Webb) in the Southern Inter Counties and National Inter Counties Cross Country Championships. Also the first time we have gained team medals in County Cross Country Championships (the Surrey Intermediate Team of Jenny Webb, Gail Porter and Andrea Coore who finished 3rd team). The first time we had had an individual winner in the Surrey League Cross Country Championships (Rosemary Honeychurch) and also we had team winners in the same race (Rosemary Honeychurch, Vicky Mitchell, Jenny Webb and Debbie Hankins). We also finished a Senior Team in the National Cross Country Championships (37th). In the Surrey League Rosemary Honeychurch finished 3rd individual over the 4 races and in the Inters Jenny Webb was 5th and Vicky Mitchell was 6th. Our Walkers have been doing well with Gail Porter and Rachael Parrott (who won a race in the Cambridge Harriers Walking League) well to the fore. Our winter training has been quite well attended with good attendances on Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings at Belgrave Hall, and Sunday mornings at Battersea Park and Wednesday Evening Circuit Training Sessions have also been well attended. items.s: 'DYNAMITE' ROSE Profile of Rosemary Honeychurch, the women's section's leading middle-distance runner, and her big 1984 improvements at 1500m and 3000m. 'DYNAMITE' ROSE ROSEMARY HONEYCHURCH: Alias "Dynamite Rose" is "Belles" leading middle distance star, and is a 21 year old student at Whitelands College where she is studying for a degree in sociology. How many of you have taken 32 secs. and 65 secs. off your P.B.s for 1500m and 3000m in one season? "Dynamite" did just that!! At the start of the 1984 season her best 1500m was 5.17 - at the end - 4.45. Her best 3000m was 11.07 - at the end - 10.02. Her coach (since last April), Derek Crookes says she is a "Dedicated trainer" who does everything laid down in training schedules, and is an out and out fighter. 1984 saw her win the Surrey County Senior 3000m and this was followed up by representing Surrey in the same event. Her winter "hobby" is trying to run her coach into the deck over a hard 3 to 4 mile run most Saturdays at Wimbledon. She represented Surrey in the Inter-Counties C.C.Champs 1985 but her best run was to chase Ann Ford in the C.P. 6km road race at the end of December. Rosemary Honeychurch ROSEMARY HONEYCHURCH student at Whitelands College; 1984 improved 1500m 5.17 to 4.45 and 3000m 11.07 to 10.02; won Surrey County Senior 3000m 1984; represented Surrey in Inter-Counties C.C. 1985 ROSEMARY HONEYCHURCH Dynamite Rose Dynamite Derek Crookes Derek Crookes Rosemary Honeychurch's coach since April 1984 Ann Ford Ann Ford Surrey County Championships Inter-Counties Crystal Palace Open Road Race Whitelands College Wimbledon Crystal Palace Surrey

items.s: SUMMER ROUNDUP Derek Jones's farewell summer round-up as Ladies Secretary: the women's team's promotion to Southern League Division 2, Wendy Dunsford's loyalty, the junior relay squad, and thanks to coaches and his successor Harry Porter. SUMMER ROUNDUP After the good winter season with the Seniors coming 2nd in the Surrey Cross Country League and finishing a team in the National, the start of the Track season was a bit disappointing. In our two warm up meetings we finished 5th out of 6 and 6th out of 7 and we were a disappointing 2nd in our first Southern League to put us in 9th spot in the table. Even after the 2nd Southern League we were 7th and in the next 3 matches we had to meet all the teams above us. However, everybody got stuck in and competed out of their skins in the last four matches with the result that we did what we wanted to do and got promotion to Division 2. So well done to all concerned. It really was a fantastic result, especially those last 4 matches in the Southern League. I would like to mention the determination of Wendy Dunsford who, over the 6 years has competed in a remarkable 44 Southern League meetings out of a total of 46. The September meeting was her 39th consecutive Southern League. In the Thameside League the girls finished 5th, but the Juniors were level on League points with Camberley and just lost out on insufficient match points (by about 7½). Just one mention which I almost forgot and that is the Junior Relay squad who in the last 2 seasons crossed the line in first place in League Races (Southern & Thameside) and Inter Club matches on no less than 22 occasions. (Unfortunately one resulted in a disqualification). They also gained a Bronze in the Southern Counties Womens AAA as well as coming 5th in the WAAA Championships. Finally, I would like to thank everybody who came along to give their help and support. Please keep it coming. I would also like to thank everybody who has contributed over the six years I have been Ladies Secretary. I think I can safely say that I leave the section in a healthy state, which is no thanks to me, but to the efforts of all the athletes and those who have helped. I would like to thank Frank Simmons and John Gould for their help and coaching skills. To my successor Harry Porter I wish Good Luck and thank you for the help you have given me over the past few seasons. I hope you get the same co-operation as I do. I will certainly be on hand with help and advice. Good Luck for 1986. items.sum: Profile of New Zealand-born former GB high jumper Joanne Hilliard, who switched to the discus under Mike Winch and joined Belgrave in 1985, with her personal bests and club records.
items.s: JOANNE HILLIARD Profile of New Zealand-born former GB high jumper Joanne Hilliard, who switched to the discus under Mike Winch and joined Belgrave in 1985, with her personal bests and club records. JOANNE HILLIARD Born in New Zealand on 1st March 1962 Joanne Hilliard moved to the U.K. at the age of 7. She became interested in athletics and started competing at club level at the age of 16, starting as an all-rounder before progressing on to training specifically for the high jump She trained with Ron Murrey for 5 years and gained her first International vest in July 1983 when she represented Great Britain in the G.B v France match. Further International appearances followed including a match in Norway in August 1983. It is perhaps surprising that with this background and a p.b. of 1.83 that the following April she should decide to give up the high jump. In September 1984 she decided to take up the discus and joined Mike Winches squad. She was among the first of Mike's group to start training in the Belgrave Hall gymnasium and set the travelling record by commuting three nights per week from St. Albans to Wimbledon for strength training. It was a natural progression when she moved to London early in 1985 that she should join Belgrave. Soon after she became engaged to another of Mike's squad- Blackheath Harrier and 80m+ javelin thrower Daryl Brand. Joanne has shown great promise in the discus and it is on the cards that both she and Daryl will see International competition in 1986. Biographical details, Height - 6'2", Weight - Mind your own business! P.B's. High Jump - 1.83(1983). 1.80(1985). Club Record. Discus - 47.80(1985). Club Record Shot - 12.36(1985). items.label: October 1986
items.sum: The new editor's opening ramblings, crediting Bill Laws's last mammoth issue, looking ahead to the centenary year, recalling sixty years as a Belgravian, and appealing for officials, fund-raising support and publicity.
items.s: EDITORIAL RAMBLINGS The new editor's opening ramblings, crediting Bill Laws's last mammoth issue, looking ahead to the centenary year, recalling sixty years as a Belgravian, and appealing for officials, fund-raising support and publicity. The Mammoth is not extinct!! It has in fact raised another mammoth edition of the Belgrave Bible. Bill Laws in his final fling as Editor dubbed the issue mammoth in the context of its bulk. He modestly failed to mention the mammoth task (not tusk) in the preparation of the tome, and I, because nobody else came forward agreed to try to keep things going and maintain the continuity. Bill has a very professional attitude in the jobs that he undertakes, and The Belgravian was no exception and I only hope that my efforts somewhat match up to his. This is Belgrave centenary year and a great deal of preparation work has been done by a band of members led by Clive Shippen to make it a real celebration and I am certain that if we all enter into the spirit of things and support all of the promotions to the utmost, it will be a year to remember. T.C.(Charlie) Jones and I are celebrating our 60th year as Belgravians as also I believe is Norman Dewberry (born 1902) and we have a vast store of memories and can well recall the halcyon days prior to World War II when the Walking Section, the Cross-Country and Road Relay Runners had won all of the National Championships plus many other major events whilst the Track and Field men had, with the exception of a few flashes of success, generally met with moderate success. Now the emphasis has gradually turned and the major successes have gone to the Track and Field men and this year has been stupendous for both Team and Individuals. Details, results for the year are to be found in this issue. For many years the club had, as compared with today, few summer inter-club committments. With men-only membership we had two annual inter-club fixtures - one with T.V.H. and Ashcombe A.C. for The Doris Shield which was one of the highlights of the season and also a triangular match with Mitcham AC and Croydon A.C. plus inter-club matches with such clubs as L.A.C. and Cambridge Harriers and invitations to the Kinnaird Trophy and Waddilove Bowl, all of these events were more or less limited to 6 or 7 flat events with 2 jumps and sometimes a couple of field events, but now it is reaching saturation point - multi team leagues for male and female - all age groups and whole gambit of track and field disciplines. We have a large active membership and we usually meet our committments but these very heavy fixtures require considerably more people to organise and officiate. So thats the rub - we have the athletes, but we need many more members to do the official and supernumerary jobs. The athletic success of the club is one thing, but the financial success is another. Ron Severn our intrepid Treasurer does a super job balancing the accounts, but to perform the miracles demanded of him we need a lot more hard cash, so we earnestly ask you all to support to the utmost, any of the fund raising schemes that will be launched for the club's benefit. Then to publicity. The club has 3 Press Officers who regularly send reports etc. to up to 10 different newspapers, but the number who take any notice is very small and whilst enhanced reports are agreeable, fair comment is always acceptable, so if anybody out there knows the way in - let's hear from you. Advertising time on television is very expensive to hire, but if all our athletes who are fortunate enough to be appearing at events shown on colour television would wear the Claret & Gold - when at all possible, that would be a bit of free advertising for the Club. J.G.Coleman Editor Bill Laws Bill Laws previous editor of The Belgravian Clive Shippen Clive Shippen leading centenary preparations T.C. items.h: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL?
items.sum: Appeal for members to train as track and field technical officials, with Clive Shippen as the contact.
items.s: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL? Appeal for members to train as track and field technical officials, with Clive Shippen as the contact. Our Club is suffering from an acute shortage of technical officials. Our track and field programme each summer covers young athletes, ladies, and men's fixtures in a variety of leagues and other competitions. In every case we have an obligation to provide technical officials. Why not try your hand at helping in this way? No previous experience is necessary and you may choose from the pre-season fixture list those meetings at which you are prepared to assist. All judges are only too happy to help newcomers learn the ropes. The following categories are used in track and field athletics :- Track Judge Field Judge Starter Marksman Timekeeper In November each year the Surrey County AAA give an evening's introductory lecture in Wimbledon for newcomers in all these disciplines. If you wish you may take a Grade 4 test the following week, but it is not necessary. All you need is a copy of the A.A.A. rule book, which all officials need to refer to from time to time. Officiating can be a most rewarding and enjoyable part of the athletics scene. Why not give it a try? For all the advice you need telephone CLIVE SHIPPEN on [phone number withheld]. Clive Shippen CLIVE SHIPPEN contact for would-be technical officials Wimbledon Surrey County AAA
