England v USA-Gateshead-27 June: 100m 6th E Obeng 10.70; 200m 5th J Regis 21.38; 800m 2nd J Gladwin 1.46.34 Ulster Games - 30 June: 200m 3rd J Regis 21.14; Mile 14th G Staines (pacemaker) 4.03.04 Stockholm/Helsinki Grands Prix - 1/7 July E Obeng 100m 5/5 10.67/10.58 Inter Counties - Corby - 5 July: 400mH A Pamah 54.9ht Peugeot Talbot Games Crystal Palace 11 July: 100m 4th E Obeng 10.44 200m 6th J Regis 21.42 Mile 13th G Staines 4.00.00 BANK OF ENGLAND INVITATION MEETING - ROEHAMPTON - 16 JULY: 100m A 3 J Busk 11.2; B 4 A Paton 11.9 200m A 3 J Busk 23.2 B 4 P Walker 24.6 400m A 5 J Booth 53.2 B 1 G Adams 53.5 800m A 1 S Paton 1.55.0 B 1 M Hayes 2.02.6 (n/s J Chaston 2.01.7, A North 2.06.4, A Gayton 2.13.7) 1500m A 2 J Chaston 4.07.4 B 1 M Hayes 4.09.4 (n/s S Maynard 4.12.0, M Bizio 4.20.0, S Webster 4.22.8) 5000m A 2 J Wright 15.06.0 B 1 A McIntosh 15.24.0 4x400m 1 (R O'Hara, G Tiernan, G Adams, S Paton) 3.27.2 (n/s 3.31.6)Team 5th 75 pts.(Guy Sagar competing for the Bank did 11.9(100m) 2.70(LJ) & 34.20(JT) * * * * * At the Pearl Assurance International meeting held in Birmingham on 19 July, John Gladwin improved the club 800m record to 1.46.09 behind Steve Cram, having fought off 1.42 man Koskei down the home straight. Then in Paris 3 days later he improved still further, to a classy 1.45.14. At the Birmingham event Ernie Obeng ran 10.49 over 100m. * * * * * At the inaugural World Junior Championships held in Athens from 16-20 July, Philip Goedluck proved himself to be one of the best in the World at his age when taking a fine 5th place in the 200m final in 21.38. Such was the competition that 2 rounds and semis were necessary and held on the same day. It is a tribute to Phil and his coach that he came up with his best form to date for this big event. All four of his times were faster than his previous legal best- 21.36ht 21.25 Rd2 & 21.32sf. Phil actually beat the eventual Bronze medallist in one round so it was a pity he missed out on an individual medal. However some compensation was in store when he contributed a great backstraight leg to the winning UK 4x100m effort which equalled the UK Junior record (you'll remember John Regis helped set it last year). But it was a good job Phil had a long arm to stretch to the flying Kirton for their changeover; every hundredth counted at the end with 3 teams hardly separable by the human eye. * * * * * At the AAA U/20 Championships in Birmingham on 9/10 August, Marcus Adam and Phil Goedluck gave further proof of their status as the most exciting junior sprint prospects in the country with double medal winning performances. Well done to both, particularly Marcus on this occasion for getting the win in the 200m. If only he could have been at the World Juniors too! Marcus may be interested to know that a Belgravian already has his name on this trophy for Alan Sexton twice won the then 220 yards title in 1948 and 1949, his 22.1 on the latter occasion constituting a AAA Junior record. Perhaps Marcus will emulate that feat next season! Results:- 100m 2nd M Adam 10.63; 3rd P Goedluck 10.78 200m 1st M Adam 21.09; 2nd P Goedluck 21.21 * * * * * U/20 Inter Counties Match - 3 August 200m 1st M Adam 21.2; 2000mSc 1st S Maynard 6.01.4 *** IAC Int.3 Aug 100m 5th E Obeng 10.45; 800m 5th J Gladwin 1.46.12:*** Budapest 11 Aug E Obeng 10.45ht SCAAA Match 6 Aug-1500m 3rd S Paton 3.49.85; 3000m 3rd M Sinclair 8.12.01; 3000mSc 6th M Hayes 9.23.77; PV 1st P Lovell 4.80; TJ 4th D Browne 14.64; SP 3rd A Ekoku 14.23; DT 1st K Onuaguluchi 54.44:*** Zurich 13 Aug B100m 4th E Obeng 10.55; B800m 4th J Gladwin 1.45.72 *** SCAAA Match 13 Aug 1500m 3rd S Paton 3.52.7; 3000m 4th K Sturman 8.15.9; PV 3rd P Lovell 4.60; TJ 3rd D Browne 14.05; HT 5th M Small 47.86.*** Marcus Adam produced a very fine sprint double for GB Juniors v WG Juniors in Gottingen on 16 Aug with 10.82 and 21.10, while Phil Goedluck nearly did the same in a Home Junior International at Meadowbank the same day! 100/200 2/1 10.6w/21.28w * * * * * At the Dairy Crest Games in Birmingham on 19 August, Ernie Obeng (10.46 3rd in the BR Sprinter Trophy) John Regis (20.98) and Gary Staines (3.59.97 Mile) returned to something nearer their best form while Marcus and Phil took 2nd and 3rd in the BR Junior Sprinter Trophy final. But the special mention on this occasion goes to Mark Sinclair who mixed it with some of the best men in the World in a 2000mSc, finishing not too far behind the Commonwealth Champion in a time of 5.33.59, and only just shy of John Bicourt's club best set in the year John ran his 8.22 ! JOHN GLADWIN'S Commonwealth games performance and his consistently good record over the season gave him a further major Games selection for Stuttgart and the 14th European Championships held at the end of August. John qualified for the final by winning his heat in a fast but comfortable 3.36.85 and based on that run and the efforts of the other qualifiers, had much more than an outside chance of a medal despite the presence of Cram and Coe. So when John was run into 5th place (3.42.57) after a very fast last lap - John himself ran it in 53.0 - he was somewhat disappointed. But then John set about getting in some fast races to finish the season and he showed himself to still be in the tremendous form he has exhibited since April by setting further club records for 1500m in Brussels - 3.35.26 - and the Mile at Crystal Palace - 3.54.52. Congratulations John on a marvellous season. SCAAA Matches:- 31.8 5000m 4th K Sturman 14.28.0; 14.9 200m 1st P Goedluck 21.6 At a meeting to open a new track in Staffs, Phil Lovell again equalled the club Pole Vault record with 4.90.** That elegant stylist, Kevin Sturman ran one of the fastest ever 10000m times by a Belgravian (29.48.3) in taking 6th place in the Southern Championships on 10 Sept.** John Regis took 3rd place behind Wells and Christie over 100m at Crystal Palace on 12 Sept, John's time of 10.43 was another pb and one hopes to see him competing more over this distance in future as a complement to his 200m running. Three centimetres separated Abi Ekoku from the club shot record at Crystal Palace on 27 September when he put a mighty 15.75 to win at the Croydon Field and Hurdles meeting. This record has stood since 1959 and at long last looks ready for revision next season. At the same meeting Ken won the Discus, Mike Small took third in the Hammer with 49.06 and Marcello Bizio recorded a steeplechase pb. STOP PRESS?? ABI EKOKU has since raised the Club Shot Putt record to a mighter 15.94 metres J.G.C. Edt Derrick Williams all-round talents have never been in doubt. Over the years he has been our 'A' string in the 100m, 200m, LJ, HJ, TJ and part of the 4 x 100 and 4 x 400 squads. He has even won the Surrey Decathlon Championship. In our last BAL Div.2 Match at Battersea he ran his first 400m Hurdles more of a series of hops if this photo is to be believed - and recorded a quite remarkable 55sec. in his debut. What if he took it seriously and cleared the hurdle and not the railings. John Barry has backed up our middle distance men this year and secured his 'B' spot in our BAL 1500m squad with some good performances. Jay Busk. With an improvement of over 1 sec. this year, Jay Busk has made a big contribution to our 400m performances winning the 'B' string BAL event at Cardiff with a 48.85 Adrian Ross rounded off a fine season, which saw him capture the Berkshire County Boys 400m and 800m titles and the Berkshire Schools 800m, by running the remarkable time of 2.03.79 in a Boys Invitation 800m at Crystal Palace on 14 September. This mark constitutes a club record and finally removes a number of venerable 880 yards performances from the books. items.s: SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS - 26/27 APRIL - 17 MAY 1986 Boxed report and results of the 1986 Surrey County Championships, where Belgrave seniors broke five championship records, John Gladwin setting new 800m and 1500m bests. SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS - 26/27 APRIL - 17 MAY 1986 It's not every day that a County Championship record is broken. This year our senior men broke 5 with John Gladwin setting new records in both the 800m and 1500m within the space of 3 hours. His efforts erased times set as long ago as 1971 and 1969 and provided an early season glimpse of the results of a solid Winter's training. Mark Sinclair's steeplechase season got underway with his CBP, while in the Discus, Ken's new CBP was almost overshadowed by Abi's breakthrough into +50 meter throwing. Mike Small threw a pb in the Hammer and is nudging the Club record. But top honours go to our 800m men who placed 4 in the first 5 with Richard O'Hara taking a big slice off his pb as too did new member Phil Walker. Good efforts by the Juniors with a fistfull of medals but where oh where were the Colts and Boys? WRL COLTS: 1500m 10 N Webster 5.17.2 BOYS: 400m 5 A Ross 55.6; Hts. M Bowers 58.1 800m Hts. items.h: AAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - CRYSTAL PALACE - 20/21 JUNE 1986 WORLD CLASS PERFORMANCES FROM THE TWO JOHNS
items.sum: Boxed report of the 1986 AAA Championships at Crystal Palace, where John Regis won the 200m and John Gladwin the 1500m in a championship best, with other Belgrave performances.
items.s: AAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - CRYSTAL PALACE - 20/21 JUNE 1986 WORLD CLASS PERFORMANCES FROM THE TWO JOHNS Boxed report of the 1986 AAA Championships at Crystal Palace, where John Regis won the 200m and John Gladwin the 1500m in a championship best, with other Belgrave performances. AAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - CRYSTAL PALACE - 20/21 JUNE 1986 WORLD CLASS PERFORMANCES FROM THE TWO JOHNS We'd waited a long time between AAA track titles before Ernie's victory last year - but now we had 2 Champions in the space of 2 hours! At about 3.30 on Saturday afternoon, John Regis lined up alongside Linford Christie, Todd Bennett, Ade Mafe et al for the 200m final; 20.41 seconds later he was punching the air in celebration of a superb win. Christie, drawn in the lane inside John was first into top gear and he led our man by a metre coming off the bend with the rest in a line just behind But that wasn't enough for the UK 100m record holder. John powered down the straight and turned that deficit into a metre advantage with a supreme demonstration of aggressive but relaxed sprinting. Up went both arms before the line and that ample chest, resplendent in club colours, stopped the electronic timer in the third fastest ever time by a Briton, a UK teenage best and, very obviously, a club record. Quite magnificent! Commonwealth selection was ensured and at the end of the afternoon, John received the Mumm Champagne award for the best performance of the afternoon from none other than our own Arthur Penny. Of course that decision must have been difficult for any Belgravian to make as later on there was a special 1500m! John Gladwin needed to avenge that 'UK' defeat by Harrison, and win, to be sure of a Commonwealth spot, while Gary Staines, with a new pb from the week before, could also look for a prominent showing. The early pace was respectable with Gary taking it up at about 680m and hitting the 2 lap mark in 1.57.6. But John had been biding his time on the outside of the bunch and with 600m left he took off for home. The "Cram type approach" worked to perfection. Nobody could go with him (not surprising when you consider his closing speed - the last 3x200 in 28.3, 27.9 and 27.2 successively!) and he came home nearly 20 metres to the good in 3.35.93, a new Championship Best Performance and John's umpteenth club record. This was the 106th running of the event and there can have been few more dominant displays. No finer compliment can be paid to our two than to list a handful of previous winners of these titles. 220yds/200m - Eric Liddell, McDonald Bailey, Steve Riddick, Don Quarrie, Mel Lattany and Stanley Floyd. Mile/1500m - Jack Lovelock, Sydney Wooderson, Roger Bannister, Eamonn Coghlan, Dave Moorcroft, Steve Ovett and Steve Cram. Results: 200m 1 J Regis 20.41; 2 T Bennett 20.50; 3 L Christie 20.51 1500m 1 J Gladwin 3.35.93; 2 S Crabb 3.38.04; 3 P Larkins 3.38.19 The two Johns then were the stars of the weekend but others were competing with success as well. Phil Goedluck and Marcus Adam were flying in the sprints. Phil was in great form with pb's of 10.55 and 10.48w in the 100m heats and semis and 21.22w in the 200m heats, close up with those of bigger reputation, while Marcus was near his best with a 21.55w heat. Both men later qualified from the first semi final of the British Rail Sprinter Trophy for Juniors over 100m, Marcus getting the jump on Phil 10.53 to 10.67, as they took 2nd and 3rd places. In the Triple Jump, Derek Browne bounded out to another pb of 14.77, the first time he had used a 15 stride approach instead of 9, and that obviously worked, while Mike Hayes was a creditable 9th in the steeplechase with 8.53.16. The rest of our lads were perhaps not quite up to scratch and did not perform as we know they can. Ernie Obeng won his 100m heat in 10.45w but missed out on progress from the semis by the thickness of a vest. Also Mike Alleyne, 49.79 400m ht; Phil Lovell 4.70 and 11th place (PV); Derrick Williams, three fouls after a 7.19w Long Jump qualifier; Abi Ekoku, 17th in the Discus with 45.50; Mark Sinclair, retiring from the 'chase after starting with a heavy cold and then cracking a knee badly on a barrier. And, rounding off that 1500m, Gary, who would have hoped for something better than his 8th place in 3.45.29 after his promising early laps. items.h: XIII COMMONWEALTH GAMES - EDINBURGH - 24 JULY/2 AUGUST 1986
items.sum: Boxed report of the 1986 Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh: John Gladwin's 1500m silver behind Steve Cram, John Regis eighth in the 200m final, and Ernie Obeng left out of the England relay squad.
items.s: XIII COMMONWEALTH GAMES - EDINBURGH - 24 JULY/2 AUGUST 1986 Boxed report of the 1986 Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh: John Gladwin's 1500m silver behind Steve Cram, John Regis eighth in the 200m final, and Ernie Obeng left out of the England relay squad. XIII COMMONWEALTH GAMES - EDINBURGH - 24 JULY/2 AUGUST 1986 "Second, and the winner of the Silver Medal - John Gladwin, representing England" No doubt our 23 year old club record holder will long remember those words from the medal presentation ceremony, along with his remarkable performance in the 1500 metres final........... A slow handclap greeted the opening lap when nobody was willing to take it on on a very windy day so some people present couldn't have realised this wasn't a Grand Prix meeting! 800 metres passed in 2.15 - maybe that wouldn't distress too many in the Rosenheim League but every second was absorbing - and in the next 50 metres John jostled his way to the outside in order to execute a pre race plan to run for home 500 metres out. Just before the home straight he took off. Giving it everything into the bell and round to the backstraight - a 200m he covered in 24.6! - John opened up a gap that was scarcely believable in this class of field. He really had taken everyone by surprise and for a few moments it looked like he would even do the impossible and beat Cram. It wasn't to be though as with 160m left, the World No.1, who later admitted to being a worried man, finally caught John. But our man wasn't letting his hard work count for nothing and he kept hard on Cram's heels for a magnificent Silver medal. Taking a place on the lap of honour John had to survive an almighty embrace from Keith Sinclair before later receiving his medal from The Duke of Edinburgh and then enjoying the closing ceremony celebrations. That evening, at an alcoholic establishment close by the Games Village, John rounded off the day in company with a group of friends from Belgrave and Lauriston, the imbibing going on into the wee small hours! 1st S Cram 3.50.87 2nd John Gladwin 3.52.17 3rd D Campbell (Can) 3.54.06 Earlier in the week we had seen John Regis progress fairly comfortably to the 200m final (3rd ht 21.26, 2nd sf 21.23) although seemingly not quite firing on all cylinders and, for the semis and final, he had his left thigh heavily strapped as a precautionary matter. John took 8th place in the final (21.08) behind some of the best sprinters in the World, and, if that wasn't John's top form, it was still a fine performance for a teenager who can look forward to further Games selections in the years ahead. Ernie Obeng, who was looking forward to his third Games was unfortunately kept out of the England 4x100 squad by the good form of others. items.sum: Match-by-match account of Belgrave's four GRE/British League Division II fixtures of 1986 (West London, Cwmbran, Meadowbank and Battersea Park), ending in promotion to Division 1.
items.s: GRE/BRITISH LEAGUE DIVISION II 1986 Match-by-match account of Belgrave's four GRE/British League Division II fixtures of 1986 (West London, Cwmbran, Meadowbank and Battersea Park), ending in promotion to Division 1. GRE/BRITISH LEAGUE DIVISION II 1986 10th MAY 1986 WEST LONDON MATCH 1 Our 1986 British League campaign got off to a flying start at West London on a damp and very windy day. TVH got a clear lead and held it throughout the afternoon, but gradually the 'Belgrave Machine' roared into action and with the relays to come, we were one point ahead. The 4x100 team sealed our victory and the 4x400 made certain. Highlights of our win included 12 winners. Simon Maynard and Abi Ekoku won on their BAL debuts. John Regis and Marcus Adam in his debut put the frighteners on Linford Christie. John Gladwin cruised round the 1500 and was chased home by John Barry. Stuart Paton, Derrick William, Ken, Phil Goedluck, David North all won their events with good performances. Phil Lovell won the vault on his last attempt at 4.60 (phew!). A great start to the season! 31st MAY 1986 CWMBRAN MATCH 2 A large contingent travelled to Wales for our Second Round Match. Our supporters were in good voice and got noisier as we scored a comfortable victory. TVH lost ground and Cardiff did us a favour by finishing 3rd. The Scottish Challenge never materialised and it was left to Southampton to finish 2nd on the day. Twelve wins were again recorded and included Gary Staines running away from Dave Baptiste, Phil Goedluck, Mark Sinclair, Derrick Williams (Long and Triple), Ken and Abi in the Discus, Phil Lovell and Mike Hayes and Simon Maynard in the Chase. John Regis was beaten on the dip by Colin Jackson and Todd Bennett in the 100 and Marcus was given the same treatment in the 200. But the 4x100 recorded a magnificent win in 41.26. Abi beat Ken in the Shot by 1cm. Derek Browne continued his fine improvement in the Triple. Mike Alleyne and Dave Sheldon recorded p.b's. Richard O'Hara and Phil McKay made their debuts as also did Jay Busk who was the star of the day with his win in the 400 B, and recording a p.b. 48.85. At the end of two matches we were top of the league by three clear points. 5th JULY 1986 MEADOWBANK MATCH 3 Most of the team were air lifted by B.Cal to Edinburgh for the third match, in the impressive Meadowbank Stadium. Edinburgh Southern fielded their strongest team and won comfortably. We managed a safe second place with the other four teams finishing with just four points between them. Star of the day was Ernest Obeng who broke Alan Wells' League Record in the 100 with 10.39. Marcus made it a double by winning the 'B', and also the 200 'B'. The short relay was another fine win with Mike Alleyne taking the injured Derrick Williams place. Mike Small finished 2nd in the Hammer behind Chris Black. Ken and Abi again won the Discus and Phil Lovell easily won the Vault with another fine display. In the Shot Abi was 2nd in the 'A' just ahead of Ken who won the 'B'. Vince recorded his best throw of the season in the Javelin. So, after three matches promotion to Division 1 was almost assured. Mark Lindsay-Bayley organised the evening meal, and Belgrave took over Dario's Restaurant for the evening. A quick dash was made across Edinburgh to see John Gladwin on T.V. A good weekend was had by all, except TVH. 23rd AUGUST 1986 BATTERSEA PARK MATCH 4 The final match for this season and again we turned out a strong team. TVH had to beat Southampton by two places to gain promotion. They did beat Southampton, but not by enough. So, Southampton will join us in Division 1 next year. Mike Small got off to a great start by finishing second in the Hammer with 49.50, ably backed by Terry Welsh. Phil Lovell again won the Vault, and Abi and Ken won the Discus. Derek Browne improving all season scored a great win in the Triple, and he was backed by Abi! Derrick Williams made a sensational debut in the 400H, as did Chris Millbank in his first BAL S/C. Not content to do a p.b. Chris had a rest at the last barrier! Just behind him Simon Maynard had another great run and a p.b. Kev Sturman ran the 1500 and was unlucky to finish 4th. Abi recorded a p.b. of 15.51 in the Shot. Our four top sprinters were all competing with ernest just pipped by Nigel Walker in the 100 and John, Marcus and Phil all winning their events. The sprinters combined to form a powerful squad in the 4x100, but shaky changes ruled out a very fast time, but still equalling the club record. Mark Sinclair ran a brilliant 5000, with the best time by a club athlete for many years. Star of the day was John Gladwin, who on the eve of his departure to the Europeans, smashed the league record for the 800. The 4x400 squad also ran the fastest metric time ever recorded by Belgrave. Battersea Park looked splendid thanks to great work by Clive Shippen, Charlie Manning and Wandsworth Council. It was a fitting end to a great season. PHOTOS FROM THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Joe Minetti (33) completes a sprint double by winning the 200m from Stuart Paton who clocked a nippy 22.9 - not bad for a middle distance man! Others in shot , left to right, are Mike Scott, Andy Paton, Phil Smith and Pat Lyttle Jay Busk (1) is about to unleash the fastest one lap performance in the Championships since Clive Ryan's 48.7 for 440 yards four years before Jay was born! Guy Sagar (lane 2) took second. In lane 3 is Gareth Allison who set a Youths club record for 400mH a couple of weeks later. No, you're not seeing things! It's Ken to Abi in the 4x1 - lane 2 at Battersea will never be the same again as about 8 hundredweight of throwing power dented the track in a semi serious, sorry make that deadly serious relay! The changeover at the bottom bend involved Mike Small and Vince Cornibert. Gordon Biscoe appears to be looking at the watch in disbelief but it was a comfortable 58 at the bell for Richard O'Hara who ran out an easy winner. Alan Painter, a youngster of 39, was the only other runner inside 2 minutes. Pat Lyttle is still in touch at this point but his legs are about to part company with the rest of his body any second! items.s: Round Up SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 2 Bob Bridges' round-up of Belgrave's 1986 Southern League Division 2 season, finishing 6th and missing promotion by one point, with match reports from Battersea, Stevenage, Brighton, Havering, Portsmouth and Guildford (the last continued on page 52). Round Up SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 2 I will start by thanking all of those who turned out this year, be it to compete or officiate, thus making it an enjoyable and successful season. Once again we saw an improvement in our performances over the previous year, this time finishing 6th in Division 2 and missing promotion by 1 league point with the top 5 going up. It is not only our individual performances that are up - our team spirit is riding high. I think this is shown by our commitment in the long relay which we won 5 times out of 6. It is not only the British League that provides entertainment and excitement; you should have heard the cheer which greeted our last victory by one point on the cinders at Guildford. Having said that, a look through the results will show that we were still missing a few competitors in the less 'popular' events and don't forget that at every match there is one sprint and one middle distance non-scoring event. So do come along and enjoy yourself, be it to partake or spectate. The Southern League is proving to be a good 'feeder' for the British League and if we continue to make progress as we have, we should gain promotion into Division 1 next season, our centenary year. Bob Bridges Match Reports The first match at Battersea saw us successful by a healthy margin of 16.5 points from the next club with our superiority over local rivals SLH being particularly noteworthy. Admittedly a few of our 'A' team men were on view, with John Barry scoring an easy 1500 win and Abi Ekoku giving us maximum points in the Shot and Discus, but we had no 'B' competitor in two events and the selected 'B' 1500m runner didn't turn up so we were still giving away points unnecessarily. Personal bests were set by Joe Minetti (100) Jay Busk (400) Richard O'Hara (800) Simon Maynard (5000) and Marcello Bizio ('chase) while those two stalwarts John Bicourt and Snowy Brooks gave quite a few years and a beating to most of their rivals. We had a few defectors for the match on cinders at Stevenage but it didn't make much difference; we took 2nd place. The throwers again excelled with Mike Small scoring 15 points and Snowy Brooks was only a metre or so shy of his best ever Discus throw set some 8 years ago. Again we took the 'A' races from 100m through 1500m and at the halfway stage in the season we were in 4th place in the division behind Woking, Oxford and Bedford. The match at Brighton gave us an even bigger win with 18 individual firsts. The throwers were in good form with Neil Phillips winning 3 events and Tony Featherstone 2. Roy Vassall came up with his best Long Jump for a while and also improved in the Pole Vault reportedly using the pole climbing technique that was banned by the AAA in 1920! Nice one Roy. Mike Bazire notched a sprint double and Jay Busk dipped under 50 seconds in the 400m for the first time. Debutants Phil Walker and Chris Knight won impressively in their respective events while Paul Richley found some of his old sub 4 form in the 1500m, with Graham Adams running a pb just behind. The bubble eventually burst at Havering in July when we could only scrape up 4th place with a team containing too many people in non specialist events. Even so we had some winners with Stu' Paton maintaining our 400m 'A' record and helping us to victory in the long relay. Chris Knight continued to do a good job in the low hurdles with good back up from Gareth Allison who found he could high hurdle as well and competed in 5 events during the afternoon. Kevin McCallion, a new Irish Guards member won the Pole Vault. The match at Portsmouth proved to be a Navy benefit day and we lost further ground in the league. Stu' Paton continued to strengthen our team and again he anchored the 4x4 effort in fine style. Andy Moore came in for his first race of the season and proved his good form with Richard O'Hara too strong as a 'B' man in this class of competition. Jim Gregg brought repectability to our High Jumping and Gareth Allison set a club Youth's record in the 400mH. The whole match was of very high standard which also saw Roy Vassall finish only 4th in the Long Jump with 6.61, a distance good enough to win most other matches. --- Continued at bottom of P. 52. Continued from the Southern League Report on P.54. We returned to winning ways at Guildford but it was just too late for our promotion hopes. Still, Chris Knight showed the sort of form that could see him knocking on the door for BAL selection next year while the improving Chris Millbank upset the form book by taking the 'A' scoring spot away from John Bicourt in the 'chase. Aham Amadi made a welcome return after injury and helped us to a 'Triple' double with John Druce. Our Javelin pair also scored a maximum and we believe Guy Sagar would be even better with a 400m run up! This match also saw Errol Roofe make his Southern League debut for us and although 'not fit' he managed to win the 100m 'A' and help the short relay to victory. The highlight of the match and perhaps the season was the 4x400m relay which we had to win and did to take the match by 1 point from our friendly hosts, Guildford. items.s: ROSENHEIM LEAGUE 1986 Review and run-on results of Belgrave's 1986 Rosenheim League season (five league matches at Tooting, Croydon and Battersea plus the final at Tooting, where the seniors placed 4th), with final league positions. ROSENHEIM LEAGUE 1986 For the first time this year, the final was held on an 8 lane track and so only one team from each division needed elimination through the five league matches. Surrey Beagles were the unlucky ones from our division. The overall standard in the final was possibly the best ever and despite a reasonable Senior team we could only finish 4th. Needless to say it was the 'A' team members who turned out through the season who provided the best quality performances and mention must once again be made of the support and efforts of Mike Small. However tucked away in the results you'll find confirmation of the improvement of many of our younger members with the fine 3000m times of Juniors, Graham Adams and Simon Maynard, and Youth, Steve Webster - a new club record - the most notable. You'll also notice the return to Belgrave of Eric Barker, one of our best ever throwers, and of Alan McIntosh, our double cross country champion from 1979/80. Note for next year:- If you think you might be needed as a scorer in any event, please turn up as early as you can to assist the team manager with selections. We might not take the league that seriously but we might as well do our best! items.s: The Ladies. Harry Porter's review of the Belgrave ladies' 1985-86 season across cross country, road running, race walking and the Southern League, GRE Cup and county championships. The Ladies. After the euphoria of gaining promotion to Division 2 of the Southern League in September, the Winter Season was rather an anti-climax. Over the country in the Surrey Womens League the seniors were unable to repeat the result of the previous season although we had a few more turning out, but injuries and illness to some runners meant that we were short at times. Having said that the Juniors finished in 3rd place after the 4 races and the Inters, who were having a separate race for the first time were 5th. The Seniors were 7th and the Girls 10th. In the County Championships we only had 2 representatives in the Middlesex and our Surrey team was depleted with no Senior representative. In the Juniors Jacqui Smiter was 13th and Natalie Fenyoe (Middlesex) was 17th Girl home. A new name appeared on the Senior Club Cross Country cup. Well done to Vicky Mitchell and another win in the Juniors for Jackie Stone. Our Road Runners have been strengthened by the addition of Frances Guy, who broke several existing records quite considerably and was 2nd in the Mitcham A.C. 25Km Road Race and 2nd in the St. Albans Marathon. Meanwhile and I won't let on about her age, but Pam Davies keeps on going. Our walkers too put in some good times with Rachael Parrott and Charlotte Christou in the Juniors and some excellent Walking from Susan Kew as well as Gail Porter (3rd in the Enfield Open 7 Miles). During the winter season Wendy Dunsford's shot putting had improved considerably indoors and was putting over 12 metres. Team Selection was going to be difficult as we had 5 Senior shot putters all over 10 metres. Turning to the summer season we started off very slowly and after our 3rd Match found ourselves in 23rd place in the table. Unfortunately we went down to Cambourne with a good team, but the match was rained off. We won our last 2 fixtures though and finished 9th. For the first time and as an experiment, we had a 2nd team and they finished 15th. Also we got through to the Semi Final of the GRE Cup for the first time and although we were 7th there were 3 club records that afternoon. We were also invited by Adidas to an International Athletes Club Field Events Championship at Birmingham where we finished 4th. In the Thameside League the girls and juniors did well also and over all we won the Midweek League again. The experiment of running a 2nd Southern League team was reasonably successful and will be continued for next season. We had 4 County Championship winners - Wendy Dunsford (Middlesex-Shot), Helen Kemp (Surrey-Shot), Joanne Hilliard (Kent-High Jump) and Charlotte Christou (Middlesex 2500m Walk) all these plus Cindy James (Silver Medal in the Middlesex Shot) represented their county's in the Inter County Championships. In the Southern Championships Joanne Hilliard was our only medal winner coming 3rd in the High Jump. On the roads Frances Guy continued her winning ways with firsts in the Edinburgh Marathon, the Poly Marathon and the Belgrave 20 Mile Road Race. Well done to everybody for a good summer season, but we look forward to promotion to Division 1 and Division 3 in our Centenary Year (1987). Thanks to all those people who came along to help and support (officials, parents etc.) and all in all with good team work from all quarters of the section without which we would find it very difficult. So, once again, thanks to all those concerned. items.label: June 1987
items.sum: The centenary president, Bill Lucas, reviews the centenary year so far (New Year's Eve party, January cross country event, 12 stage relay, first National League match, London Marathon), regrets the club's absence from the National 12 stage relay at Sutton Coldfield and lists the year's remaining events.
items.s: Message from the President The centenary president, Bill Lucas, reviews the centenary year so far (New Year's Eve party, January cross country event, 12 stage relay, first National League match, London Marathon), regrets the club's absence from the National 12 stage relay at Sutton Coldfield and lists the year's remaining events. Message from the President We are now well into our Centenary Year and after a very successful opening party on New Year's Eve we followed with an equally successful cross country event in very adverse conditions on 17th January. The Belgrave 12 stage relay on 4th April brought commendations from all concerns (except perhaps Hercules Wimbledon) and despite a wet day (a rare occurrence for this event) we can be satisfied that the race was well up to its usual high standard. My grateful thanks go to the many club members who have worked so hard to ensure that our centenary is one to remember and particularly I would thanks the Centenary Committee, ably led by Clive Shippen, who have formed the working base for our success. The first match in Division 1 of the National League was held at Portsmouth on 9th May and we finished sixth of the eight teams. This is highly commendable in the face of the best opposition in the country especially as we were short of our best sprinters and a couple of hiccups probably lost us the few points necessary to have finished fourth. I could only watch the London Marathon on television but was delighted to see a large club banner, a preponderance of new club hats and a very prominent club bag - well done supporters!!! I thought the commentators could have been more liberal with their remarks about our centenary. (Continued P.4) Message from the President (cont.) I must confess to a few disappointments in the running field. We narrowly missed success in the Senior Surrey Cross Country Championship held late in 1986 and were only a few points away from winning the South of the Thames race on our own course on 24th January. Following this we were seventh in our own 12 stage relay which although one place lower than last year was nevertheless a good achievement and qualified us for the National event at Sutton Coldfield. My disappointment arises from our inability to send a representative team fot this race. I realise that our athletes have many commitments but so do the athletes of Gateshead, Birchfield Tipton etc who all fielded teams strong enough to fill the first three places. I can only assume that their runners plan their year to include such events and I would like to see our own athletes, in conjunction with their coaches, planning in similar fashion. Perhaps 1988 could see us as prominent in the Winter programme as we are during the Summer. We still have many events to come in 1987 including Club Championships on 11th July (a gala day for everyone), the Belgrave "20" on 18th July (incorporating the Southern championship), a river trip on 25th July (a night to be remembered we hope), the club dinner on 14th November which promises to be an extra special evening, the Open Walk on 28th November and the final events of the year incorporating our Boxing Day extravaganza and the closing party on New Year's Eve. Much work goes into the organisation of such promotions - please support them to the full. We look forward to seeing everyone who can possibly attend whether actively, officially or as a passive spectator. Good wishes to you all for our continuing success. Bill Lucas President Bill Lucas Bill Lucas President Clive Shippen Clive Shippen leads the Centenary Committee Belgrave 12 stage relay National League London Marathon Surrey Cross Country Championships South of the Thames National 12 stage relay Club Championships Belgrave "20" Southern Championships Open Walk Boxing Day Portsmouth Sutton Coldfield Hercules Wimbledon Gateshead Birchfield Tipton

items.sum: The treasurer suggests members donate the odd pence from their bank balance, or the difference to the nearest multiple of 5, to the club.
items.s: RON'S MASTERPLAN The treasurer suggests members donate the odd pence from their bank balance, or the difference to the nearest multiple of 5, to the club. RON'S MASTERPLAN Donations: Some members of the Club would like to make donations to its funds from time to time, but feel than an amount they could afford would, perhaps, be too little to be worthwhile. This is fully understood. At the last A.G.M. I made a suggestion which all members may like to adopt. I put forward the idea that when a member gets his or her bank statement from the bank, they might send me a cheque, made payable to the Club, for the odd pence in the final balance. Thus, if that balance were, say, £118.76 their cheque would be for 76p. A further suggestion on this is that if they felt able to, their cheque could be for the difference between the balance and the nearest multiple of 5. In the example I have given, the cheque would be for the difference between £120 and £118.76 namely, £1.24p. If, however, the balance were to be, say, £116.50p the cheque would be for the difference between that figure and £115, i.e. £1.50. These may not seem very large amounts in themselves, but I am sure you will appreciate that if enough members did it, the gain to the Club would be quite substantial. It would also, I hope, be painless for members. I look forward to receiving hundreds of cheques from you. Don't bother with covering letters. Perhaps I can thank you in advance? [address withheld] RON SEVERN Hon. Treasurer Ron Severn RON SEVERN Hon. Treasurer

items.label: June 1987
items.sum: Grapevine column: visits by past presidents Tom Morrell and Gordon Doubleday to the 12-stage relay, Jack Stubbs' memories of Paul Khlopin, Mike Porter's recollections, Jack Goswell's operations, Daye Donovan's gift in memory of Edmund Donovan, research into John Garnett (killed on the Somme 1916) with a 1914 club group photo, and Leo Coy and Rangit Bhatia racing in Delhi, plus the birth of Carly to Jane and Chris Everett.
items.s: grapevine Grapevine column: visits by past presidents Tom Morrell and Gordon Doubleday to the 12-stage relay, Jack Stubbs' memories of Paul Khlopin, Mike Porter's recollections, Jack Goswell's operations, Daye Donovan's gift in memory of Edmund Donovan, research into John Garnett (killed on the Somme 1916) with a 1914 club group photo, and Leo Coy and Rangit Bhatia racing in Delhi, plus the birth of Carly to Jane and Chris Everett. grapevine It was good to see Tom Morrell again at the 12-stage relay on 4th April. Tom was our President back in 1954-55 and had travelled down from Norfolk with his daughter and son-in-law Eric Hall to see the relay. What a day to pick! It rained incessantly, but Tom enjoyed being back in the Belgrave fold again. He was secretary of the Belgrave Hall sub-committee from 1948 to 1970 so was particularly interested in the alterations to our head-quarters. He reckons we have done well to get a quart into a pint pot but will not surprise anyone with the view that our changing rooms and showers need attention. Tom sends his congratulations to all those involved with organising the event and only wishes that he could have been involved too. By the way, Tom is not completely absent from centenary celebrations, his local bowls club is also celebrating its Centenary this year! Another of our Past-Presidents, Gordon Doubleday (1969-70) was up from Bath to time-keep at the 12-stage relay. Gordon was particularly pleased to see Exeter's fine performance in our race (they were second) because he was a member of Exeter from 1939 to 1942. Gordon discovered on April 4th that Keith Jennings of Exeter was a grandson of Belgrave walker R. "Jock" Martin who was a member of our winning London to Brighton Walk teams before the war and who became a Centurion in 1946 in a 24 hours event at White City. These Belgravians get everywhere! * * * * * Some members will recall that two years ago the Club presented a silver salver to Jack Stubbs of SLH to commemmorate 20 years as Chief Timekeeper at our Relay. Well, although he has retired from most officiating, Jack continues to appear as a timekeeper at this promotion. He is now well into his eighties. On race day at Belgrave Hall he caught the smell of liniment from the dressing room and recounted how Paul Khlopin, a Belgravian who came from Russia at the end of the first World War, used to anoint himself with a mixture of olive oil, wintergreen and vinegar. Any left over in his special bottle he would drink! Our older members will remember the stench of pre-war dressing rooms. Perhaps they can recall other peculiar recipes. * * * * * The RRC Newsletter recently asked early members to drop the Editior a line. One of the first to reply was Mike Porter who was a member of Belgrave from 1948 to 1953 before moving back to Manchester. He wrote "I have many happy memories of Belgrave. Once a 'Bel' always a 'Bel'. We used to train on Tuesdays and Thursdays from Chelsea Barracks, tearing it up on the Hyde Park horse rides, plus the Saturday Inter-Club races, or training runs over the country; from those days I remember, Tom Carter, Bill Lucas, Bert Footer, Steve Charlton and many others". Mike has been heavily involved in the veterans movement for some years now. JACK GOSWELL, Former President, Walking Secretary and now 200 Club Organiser has recently undergone a couple of uncomfortable operations. He is now back on his feet and wish him a quick and full recovery. At the end of January your President, Gordon Doubleday and Clive Shippen were invited to lunch by DAYE DONOVAN at her London hotel. Although it was a pleasure to meet Daye again the occasion was rather sad because she would normally have been accompanied on her journey from New York by EDMUND, one of our most fervent vice-presidents, who sadly passed away at the end of last year. He would dearly have loved to take part in the centenary celebrations of the club he joined no less than 75 years ago, but it was not to be. As a token of Edmund Donovan's esteem for Belgrave Harriers Daye presented our President with a cheque for about £1,200. It was a gesture that the Club deeply appreciates. We have every hope of seeing Daye amongst our official guests at the Centenary Dinner in November. * * * * Within a few months of Edmund's death the Club received a letter from a Lt.Col. J.A. Garnett who was seeking information concerning his uncle J.E. GARNETT who he knew was a Belgravian prior to his death on the Somme in September 1916. Our researches were able to show that John Garnett joined the club in August 1911, exactly a year before Edmund Donovan, that they were team-mates on many occasions and that our own mile/1500 club championship trophy is named after the same John Garnett. Our photograph shows John and Edmund in a club group at St. Saviour's Church Hall, Raynes Park just prior to the Blackstaffe and Murphy Shield races of early 1914. Offen, - Clark, T Helm, J White, O Horwood, - . Researches also showed that John's brother, T.W. Garnett, was elected in 1915 and was the father of the enquiring colonel. He was to became Major T.W. Garnett MBE and a Military Knight of Windsor; he died in 1976. It is probable that he was the donor of the mile cup in memory of his brother. Apparently he maintained a very great interest in athletics right up to his death. But the thought still lingers....if only the enquiry had come a few years earlier, Edmund could have revealed so much more than cold researches can achieve. Sunday, March 15th, saw Leo Coy racing against Rangit Bhatia; but not in England as you might have expected. Leo was visiting Delhi on one of his business trips and was a willing volunteer to participate in Delhi's weekly 6.5 km race. We don't know the result and suspect that Leo's tummy was not too keen on the experience. Rangit writes to say that he lunched with Vir Chauhan (Ex-Belgrave 1974) and Leo during his visit and regarded it as his own little Centenary celebration. He hopes to visit Belgrave again in June and be fit enough to race a few times. Rangit in now over-50. Grapevine Congratulations to Jane and Chris Everett on the arrival of baby daughter Carly. Jane took an extended holiday in the UK for the delivery choosing the coldest part of the winter. Grandad Brian Pritchard says he can't get used to sleeping with a Grandmother! The pictures below show the front and back of cigarette card No.40 of the series "Sporting Events & Stars" which could be found in a packet of 10 Senior Service in the 1930's, priced 6 pence. How about that reference to Belgrave Harriers!! WALKING - T. W. GREEN SPORTING EVENTS AND STARS SERIES OF 96. No. 40 T. W. GREEN. A Railway worker who prefers to walk. The greatest "hiker" in the world to-day. Member of the most successful Athletic Club in British history—Belgrave Harriers. Olympic Champion, Los Angeles, U.S.A., 1932, winning the 50,000 metre walk in 4 hrs. 50 mins. 10 secs. Holder of long distance records all over the country, and a famous figure in the Manchester to Blackpool Walk which he has captured several times. In August, 1930, smashed the 50 miles record, which had stood for 25 years, by 1m. 51.4/5th secs. when competing in the Nottingham to Birmingham Walk. Has also successfully competed against the best in Germany, Canada, France, U.S.A. and Holland. items.sum: Sprinter Ernest Obeng, finishing a Ph.D at Loughborough, has published a book of 45 athletics poems, 'One track mind'; his poem 'Just 10' is reprinted.
items.s: One track mind Sprinter Ernest Obeng, finishing a Ph.D at Loughborough, has published a book of 45 athletics poems, 'One track mind'; his poem 'Just 10' is reprinted. One track mind Ernest Obeng never ceases to amaze. You would think that what with nearing the end of his research work for a Ph.D at Loughborough University as well as scorching boards and tracks around Europe he would have little time left for other diversions. Not so. In his quieter moments Ernest is a poet of no mean ability. A collection of his work has recently been published by the Exposition Press of Florida under the appropriate title 'One track mind'. Not unexpectedly the subject matter is athletic endeavour with 45 poems illustrated by guess who? Right! If ever you wondered what it was like to sprint at the highest level Ernest's poem 'Just 10' will give you an idea. To you it's just ten seconds; To me it's been five years. To you it's just a 100 dash; To me it's sweat and tears. To you it's just the gun then run; To me it's skills, technique. To you it's raw aggression, strength; To me it's power and peak. To you it's just dive for tape; To me it's body lean. To you it's over far too soon; To me it's long and mean. To you these men of varied sizes And shapes crouched on one knee Might just as well be saying prayers But who says prayers for me? The success of his book has surprised Ernest and he has even had a request from a blind person to allow it to be reproduced in braille. If you would like to see it for yourself copies at £3.50 (p&p inc) may be obtained from [address withheld]. items.s: "Fastest" Belgravian Injured Junior sprinter Dave Armstrong, brakeman in the British number 2 bobsleigh at the World Championships, had his cheekbone fractured by flying ice and is now back in sprint training. "Fastest" Belgravian Injured About 2 years ago an advert in AW requested the services of top sprinters interested in adventure. The aim was to add some beef to Britain's 4 man Bob teams which were well down the world ranking lists due to lack of "oomph" at the start. Unbeknown to us Belgrave's promising junior Dave Armstrong applied which explains why last year we didn't see much of him. This winter he hit the headlines when the Allied Steel backed British Bobs did so well in the World Champs. He season came to an end however when a cheekbone was badly fractured by flying ice at 90 mph. Dave's story goes like this. Apparently the French team had just gone down and the brakeman failed to do his job at the finish. The result was a bob hurtling 50ft above the ground which disintegrated on landing seriously injuring all four members. The GB number 2 bob was next down and just before the finish for a reason he still can't explain Dave put his head up to check the line to be sure the brakes went on. At that precise moment ice falling off the rim of the run penetrated under his visor and the million to one accident occurred. Fortunately he is now back in full sprint training and should provide a useful back up to our 4 Internationals this summer. He aims to make the No 1 Bob next winter! Dave Armstrong Dave Armstrong junior sprinter; GB number 2 bobsleigh at the World Championships; cheekbone fractured by flying ice Dave Armstrong Dave World Bobsleigh Championships

IN MEMORIUM
E P DONOVAN OBE
items.sum: Obituary of Edmund Donovan OBE, Vice-President, who joined in August 1912, ran cross country and track before the First World War, served in the Royal Flying Corps, and later had an insurance career in New York.
items.s: IN MEMORIUM E P DONOVAN OBE Obituary of Edmund Donovan OBE, Vice-President, who joined in August 1912, ran cross country and track before the First World War, served in the Royal Flying Corps, and later had an insurance career in New York. IN MEMORIUM E P DONOVAN OBE We are sorry to learn of the death of Edmund Donovan in late November. He was one of the our oldest members and a Vice-President. He joined the club on 12th August, 1912 when he was a teenager working at Price's Candle Works - a firm with which we had many associations at the time. He was a C-C runner and in the S of the Thames (Junior) held at Weybridge in November 1912 he finished 171st out of 220, being the third scorer in our "B" team which finished 29th out of 33 teams, the "A" team finishing 11th. Earlier that month the Bels had their annual match against T.V.H and the defunct Ashcombe A.C., the result was T.V.H 36 points, Ashcombe 67 with the Bels 70. His best performance was finishing 8th in a match against St Saviours A.C., he was a little over a minute behind the winner to clinch 3rd place in the sealed handicap. He was probably better on the track. At our annual evening meeting at Stamford Bridge on 14th July 1914 he was ranked 20th out of 36 entries for the 880 yards Steeplechase Handicap and 49th out of 116 in the One Mile Open Handicap. Shortly afterwards the First World War broke out and he joined the Army. The Club minutes for 22nd August 1914 stated "J W Macher was elected Auditor in place of E P Donovan who was unable to attend owing to active service". Within four weeks 33 other members were serving, and many, alas, did not return; for many years their names appeared in a Roll of Honour in the Handbook. We think that he may have been wounded. He became one of the first members of the Royal Flying Corps. Edmund recalls that in those days the Club's HQ was the Spencer Arms in Lower Richmond Road, the course being across Putney Common, Barnes Common up Sheen Lane into Richmond Park. Then, for a short while we were at the Boileau Arms (at the Barnes end of Hammersmith Bridge). Then they moved to St Saviour's Parish Hall, Raynes Park until the outbreak of the First World War. In those days Battersea Borough Council issued special rate tickets from Clapham Junction to Raynes Park for people visiting the Cemetery - a surprising number of members seemed to have relatives buried there! Mid-week training was from the "Rising Sun", Tite Street, Chelsea, running through Belgravia into Hyde Park and along Rotten Row. Many will remember using the "Rising Sun", Ebury Bridge Road, Pimlico in the thirties, using a similar course, with the walkers going over the bridge, up to Clapham Common, doing a lap and then back again. After the war he went to the USA where he had a successful career in Insurance. He took no further part in active athletics. For some time he was President of the St George's Club - a well-known club for New York of English Nationality, he was also involved in the St John's Ambulance Brigade. He was responsible for many of the arrangements when H M The Queen visited New York in 1957 and was subsequently awarded the OBE. On a visit to England in the sixties he got in touch with Alf Harley and has kept in touch ever since and was always pleased to hear of the Club's activities and progress. He was proud of two things, he still held a British Passport and he was a member of Belgrave. Our sympathies are extended to his wife Daye who shared his enthusiasm for Belgrave, she was also English born (Fulham) having gone to the USA at an early age with her parents. It is perhaps fitting that in paying tribute to our departed member we have, in this our Centenary year, been able to recall some of the Club's past history. Gordon Doubleday I have to thank Clive Shippen who kindly provided much of the above material. items.sum: Clive Shippen's review of Belgrave's Centenary Year celebrations so far - the New Year's Eve party, the centenary cross-country match, the 22nd Belgrave 12-stage Relay, centenary mementoes and plans for Club Championships day at Battersea Park.

items.s: CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS Clive Shippen's review of Belgrave's Centenary Year celebrations so far - the New Year's Eve party, the centenary cross-country match, the 22nd Belgrave 12-stage Relay, centenary mementoes and plans for Club Championships day at Battersea Park. CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS Clive Shippen reviews the Centenary Celebrations Already we are halfway through 1987. From seeming ages away Centenary Year suddenly arrived and now we are at the peak of our celebrations. Much work has gone into the planning of the 1987 programme; your Centenary sub-committee first meeting no less than four years ago. Centenary Year was seen in at Belgrave Hall at the sell-out New Year's Eve Party with "champagne" flowing at midnight. Live music and good food produced a lively party spirit and set the tone for the rest of the year's programme. Only seventeen days later we were back at Belgrave Hall for the Centenary Celebration cross-country match against the ECCU, Surrey Co., Middlesex Co., Derby, Essex Beagles and QPH. The weather did its utmost to wreck the fixture but despite heavy snow, which prevented Rotherham attending and decimated the Beagles team, the show went on and was a great success. Once again excellent food was provided. A centenary souvenir programme was produced, with a results supplement on the day, and each competitor took home one of our bone-china Centenary Tankards. The promotion cost over £1,000 and the Club is deeply indebted to Past-President Tom Carter for underwriting the cost of this special occasion. The 22nd Belgrave 12-stage Relay was held on the 4th April. To mark Centenary Year a souvenir programme was produced which included a review of 12-stage relays since the early days of the London-Brighton event sponsored by the News of the World. Further publicity was obtained for the club when Athletics Weekly decided to re-print the article. Once again the weather was appalling and it was a pity that our smart new claret and gold umbrellas had not yet arrived. We have experienced some difficulty in obtaining some of our mementoes just when we need them. Our total order was massive, as you will see on another page, and clearly not everything could be ordered at once for financial reasons. However, by the time you read this all items will be readily available. Response so far has been very good and several items have had to be re-stocked. Members should place their orders very soon as new stock will not be ordered in the final quarter of 1987. Club Championships day on 11th July should see a large display of straw boaters, sporting claret and gold ribbon, besides the popular claret base-ball hats and gold tee-shirts. Remember, this is the big re-union day of the year and we appeal to all our distant and long-lost members to join us at Battersea Park. Many members will be arriving at 12.30 with picnic lunches and perhaps we shall have ice-cream and fruit punch laid on to supplement your meals. Club trophies and photographs will be on display and the children's "interval" programme will be re-introduced. We hope that a carnival atmosphere will prevail; and you may well witness the re-enactment of an 1887 sprint race. Make a note in your diaries now. Only a week later our celebrations will switch back to Wimbledon for our Open '20' road run. This will be the 36th staging of this famous road race which was the brain-child of Arthur Whitehead back in 1952. The Southern Counties AAA have acknowledged our Centenary Year by selecting our promotion for their own 20 mile championship. This will enhance the size and quality of the field and it should be an occasion to remember. The tempo for July will be kept up by the liveliest social occasion of the year, on Saturday the 26th. Belgrave are hiring the 300-passenger S.S. Naticha for a Thames cruise, leaving Putney Pier at 8.30pm. and returning to the same pier at 12.30am. There will be plenty of food, drink and dancing; but tickets are limited so do not delay. August provides some well-earned breathing space with time to dwell on the many team committments of our various sections and, of course, the excitement of the World Athletic Championships in Rome. We cannot claim that the World Championships were slipped into 1987 in recognition of our Centenary but it would be nice to see a couple of Belgravians selected in this special year. With the track and field season complete in September there would seem to be no reason why every able-bodied member should not turn out for our celebration 100 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on the 27th. The race will be incorporated into Blackheath's 50 x 1 mile annual event and Thames Valley Harriers (also 100 years old) will join us in fielding 100 runners. We are so confident of getting a good team together that it is proposed to field a 'B' team too! So whatever your standard, you will get a run on the famous Crystal Palace "tartan" if you turn up on 27th September. This should be an occasion for the claret and gold centenary clothing to dominate the stadium. Wednesday, October 7th, will be the Club birthday and this will be celebrated at Belgrave Hall by the unveiling of an appropriate memento and the cutting of a 100-candle birthday cake. Four days later we hope to see the staging of our most ambitious celebration - the London-Brighton Relay. However, at the time of writing sponsorship has not been forthcoming, despite a year or more of intense lobbying, and if we cannot raise the necessary finance (£8,000 to £15,000) this fine event of National interest will not be staged. The premier social occasion of the year, the Centenary Club Dinner, will be held at the Gloucester Hotel, South Kensington on Saturday 14th November. It will be a very special occasion, with eminent guests joining many of our active athletes on a proud night for Belgrave Harriers. Tickets (£25) are limited to only 250 so orders should be placed before the Club Championships if you are to stand a chance of getting one. Our last special promotion will be held on 18th November when the oldest of our promotions the Open '7' Walk will be staged at Wimbledon. It is hoped to provide a new course which will enable spectators to have a better view of the race. A souvenir programme will feature a history of the event and we have every intention of making it a very special '7'. With memories of last Boxing Day's fancy dress race fresh in mind, it is certain that Boxing Day 1987 will have lots more to say about Centenary Year. Why not think of your fancy dress now? Finally, the year will pass into the annals on New Year's Eve with a disco party at Belgrave Hall. We should have made 1987 a year to remember. Will we have made it so? CENTENARY MEMENTOES I would like to start off with an apology to those of you that have posted order forms but have yet to receive goods. Unfortunately we have encountered problems with the supplies of the clothing and towels who have proved very slow in meeting our orders. We are pressing them to move as quickly as possible. Obviously this is not very satisfactory but I hope you will appreciate that we are dependent on the suppliers for action. If you are awaiting delivery of an order then please ring Sue parrott ([phone number withheld]) or Eric Crutcher ([phone number withheld]) to check on the situation. The items that are in stock at present are selling fairly well with the tee shirts (£3.35) and mugs (£1.50) in particular proving to be very good value. The umbrellas (£13.50), sweat shirts (£7.50) and bags (£8.00) have also proved popular. The china wallplates are very attractive and orders for these (remember it's a limited edition of 100 plates) have passed the half-way mark. Eric Crutcher's Hall and Social column appealing for bar staff, thanking helpers, giving the centenary draw winners and promoting the riverboat trip, club birthday and centenary dinner. Hall and Social. HALL AND SOCIAL - Eric Crutcher MORE BAR STAFF NEEDED! - a plea made last October and which obviously fell on deaf ears. Many thanks to those of you who have served on the bar rota over the past few months but the numbers are slowly dwindling and I would like to see some newcomers volunteer to help share the load. Just 2 or 3 hours once a month is all that is needed. In particular, I must again thank Keith Duckett for not only fitting in several sessions between his shiftwork each month but also cleaning the pipes every fortnight, ordering the beer and helping out at every social. He does a great job for the club. The centenary year kicked off with the New Year's Eve party which proved quite an occasion. Whilst the music may not have been to everyone's taste (I've learnt in this job you can't please all of the people all of the time!) the food certainly was, thanks to Sandra Tiernan and Sue parrott who co-ordinated the efforts of several of our ladies to produce a magnificent spread. The centenary draw was held at about 10.30pm but in view of the number of tickets sold (we raised £1800 profit) it was hardly surprising that none of the winners were present that evening! I hope that everyone who sold tickets received a copy of the results but should I have missed anyone the winners are shown below. My thanks again to those who sold tickets and/or made a donation towards the fund. Moving on to forthcoming events tickets are now available for the centenary riverboat trip on 25 July. The boat has a resident disco and buffet for the very reasonable price of £10 per head. We are hoping to fill the boat to capacity (300 places) and well over 200 tickets have now been sold so if you'd like to come along then contact Harry Porter ([phone number withheld]) or Eric Crutcher ([phone number withheld]) as soon as possible. The boat leaves Putney pier at 8.30pm and returns at 12.30 am. It should be a great evening. The Club's actual birthday will be celebrated on 7 October at Belgrave Hall to which all are welcome. The evening will be fairly informal with a birthday cake to mark the occasion. The centenary dinner at the Gloucester Hotel on 14 November is another event where the tickets are selling very quickly. If you intend going but haven't yet contacted Bill Couzens ([phone number withheld]) then do so quickly to avoid disappointment. Tickets at £25 each for what will be the highlight of the year. items.s: HALL AND SOCIAL Further Hall and Social notes by E.C. (Eric Crutcher) on catering at the invitation cross-country event, helpers, the under/over-35s darts match, a silver wedding surprise party, poorly supported suppers and hall roof repairs. HALL AND SOCIAL The invitation cross-country event saw another catering triumph when Margaret Stroud and Sue Parrott took responsibility for providing runners and officials with a meal after the race. The arctic conditions certainly made the chilli an appropriate meal (in name and nature!) and it actually received a mention in the AW! This is an appropriate point for me to thank Sue for her support behind the bar, mainly in serving refreshments. However, Sue has also helped me out at every social and especiallly put a great deal of effort and energy into planning New Year's Eve. I'm pleased to say that Margaret has also become heavily involved in helping out on the refreshments side (particularly during the week) for which I am grateful. In addition Brian Gorman has continued to look after the Saturday afternoon runners which is much appreciated. Mention must also be made of the efforts behind the bar of Brian Gorman, Keith Duckett and Bert Stroud in helping to make the catering such a success on all fronts. The return darts match between the under 35's and over 35's took place in February and it looked at first as if the over 35's were going to average last year's defeat when they led 5:3 after the singles. However, the 4 doubles matches saw a change in fortune and the score was 6:6 going into the foursomes. Any hopes of a repeat of last year's cliffhanger were dashed when the under 35's won both foursomes to take a winning lead. However, the over-35's salvaged some pride by winning the final leg. An enjoyable evening but despite playing as a member of the winning team I must say that the disruptive tactics used by some of my team mates against the opposition would certainly upset the AAA if they ever reached track and field! However, the most memorable evening was a surprise private party held in March to celebrate the silver wedding anniversary of Dave and Margaret Davies. Their daughters had asked months in advance to book the hall and outlined a plan to hold a "This Is Your Life" style reception. The end result was Dave and Margaret walking into an empty hall (apart from the disco equipment and a bottle of champagne!) whilst 80 friends from their wedding day onwards crammed into the bar area and did their best to keep quiet! Julie did an excellent job as narrator with Tina co-ordinating the guests and by the sound of the delighted exclamations greeting each arrival it was clear that the idea was an enormous success. It was superbly planned and organised and was certainly an evening with a difference. A disappointing aspect has been the lack of support for the suppers which were reintroduced last year. Despite publishing dates in the last Belgravian for suppers in January, February and March there were only a couple of approaches to Sue Parrott or myself to book tickets. Only the March event went ahead as a result of Carl Lawton rustling up support from the walking section. As with previous suppers, everyone had an enjoyable evening whilst Don Anderson and Val Tanner slaved over the ovens to produce a super Italian meal. If all goes according to plan the section of roof covering the ladies changing room and kitchen should be renewed this summer. Following this we shall be redecorating so if anyone is willing to lend a hand could they please let me know. This area is by far the most pressing concern but other areas will need remedial action in the forthcoming years. I owe my thanks to Arthur Penstone who despite having a serious knee injury which was curtailed his running has continued to help maintain the hall, particularly the electrical side. E.C. E.C. items.s: From THE BELGRAVIAN ..... 25 years ago .... & 40 years ago .... Extracts from The Belgravian of 1962 (AGM and Ken O'Kell's honours boards, the youths' fourth in the National cross country, Ray Hall and Ray Middleton's walking) and of 1947 (the first post-war season, the National cross country at Apsley and the AAA Championships). From THE BELGRAVIAN ..... 25 years ago .... The AGM of 1962. "In attendance were the best part of a hundred faces, young and old, the familiar and the almost forgotten. Many of us were introduced for the first time to a member of 40 years service, Ken O'Kell, a man with a genuine and fond affection for the Belgrave Harriers. Ken was present largely for the purpose of handing over to the Club two honours boards, one recording Past-Presidents and the other International athletes. These boards, one of which is already in place, are to grace the walls of our Headquarters." Youths Excel in 1962 National C.C. "Our youngsters gave a most heartening display of running and although Ken Redwood hit a bad patch to slip out of the scoring four, his place was taken by "Noddy" Edwards who made up positions at a rapid rate and flogged himself right through to the funnel. Initially, Belgrave were announced as third but Sale Harriers handed in a late result and the team were bitterly disappointed to find themselves relegated to 4th. This was the first occasion in the season that the team had been out of the medals. We were, however, first Southern club home. Positions : 22. D. Cocks, 30. J. Hampshire, 47. A. Morrison, 50. P. Edwards, 70. K. Redwood, 254. H. Satchell." Walking Review 1962. "Our two Rays of sunshine, Hall and Middleton, have certainly turned on the heat this summer. Their second and third place in the National 50 Kilos at Luton behind Olympic gold medallist Don Thompson was great stuff and earned them well-deserved places in Britain's European Games team for Belgrade. Ray Hall's magnificent win in the Stock Exchange London to Brighton walk earned him a headline of his own in the "News of the World" (back page of course!) "Record Walk for Ray (28)" glared the heading, but the write-up didn't mention that his time of 7 hours 58 minutes and 33 seconds had enabled him to enter that very select band of walkers who have beaten 8 hours for this journey. These are, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson, Tom Misson and now Ray Hall. Three of them have represented Great Britain in Olympic and European Games - two winning titles in the Olympics and the third winning important International walks abroad. We wish number 4 on the list good fortune and the opportunity of proving himself the equal of those other three distinguished men." & 40 years ago .... APRIL 1947 "We are now at the end of what can be termed the first full post-war winter season. From the afternoon of the season's opening meeting at Belgrave Hall the atmosphere was set: time seemed to have slipped back and the years of the war became, in many minds, non-existent. As one who "arrived back" that afternoon not having been near Belgrave Hall since 1940, it was a startling joy to see again so many well-remembered faces and to be greeted with such a warmth of welcome. Many things have changed these past seven years and this club has lost some of its dearest and best members, but we are still a club with enthusiasm and unity about us. At present most things are opposed, or unhelpful, towards the pursuit of Athletics. This country, unlike many others, gives no official or material support to Amateur Sports Clubs of any kind. Whether this is for better or for worse is a debateable question, but it is is our heritage that such clubs as ours should be free to control and run their pursuits without any outside interference or aid, therefore what we achieve can verily be called our own. We have much to achieve, both for the benefit of the Athletic world in general and for the glory of this Club. The task of this Club in the future must be to build a strong, ALL ROUND Club." 1947 National C.C. "Held at Apsley over a course almost knee-deep in snow, this was definitely not a fair test to the runners. Len Herbert finished 6th and so gained yet another international vest, while Albert Frost ran in great style to finish 17th and so gain his club Honours Badge. Sutton Harriers the Northern champions, beat us for the team championship, although we retained the "Finch-Wayte" Cup awarded to the first Southern Club to finish. 6th L.W. Herbert, 17th A.E. Frost, 31st R.W. Tobin, 37th V.S. Blowfield, 51st E.S. Stimpson, 65th S.R.J. Eales, 80th E.H. Herbert, 92nd A.F. Mitchell. Teams: 1. Sutton H. 160, 2. BELGRAVE H 184, 3. Reading AC 187, 4. Blackheath 255." 1947 AAA Championships. "We had quite a good entry for these championships and our men put up a most creditable show. Charlie Smart ran an excellent race in the 6 miles event and although short of training finished a good third behind Chivers (Reading) and Peters (Essex B). Harry Churcher set a thrilling pace in the 2 miles walk, but was pipped by Hindmar of Sweden. Then Willie Nankeville set us roaring by making the pace in the 1 mile final, and he eventually finished 3rd to Garay (Hungary) and Slykhuis (Holland) in the record time of 4 mins. 10.6 secs. Len Marchant had to be content with fifth place in a fast-run 880 yards and George Lucas ran well to gain third place behind Lataster (Holland) and Olney (TVH) in the 3 miles, Len Herbert coming through late to finish sixth." Those that helped in some ways as timekeepers, recorders, judges, catering were all appreciated. Thanks must also go to the pupils and staff of Christ's school of Richmond for their help in distributing leaflets and helping on the day. Generally it turned out to be an excellent day and an extremely accurate course with only a minor traffic problem on one section. Unfortunately as a team we did badly. items.h: Surrey County x/c Championships - Report by Colin Pearson
items.sum: Colin Pearson's report and results from the Surrey County cross country championships at Frimley on 13 December 1986, where John Gladwin won the senior title and Belgrave took team silver in the senior and junior races; boys' and colts' results follow.
items.s: Surrey County x/c Championships - Report by Colin Pearson Colin Pearson's report and results from the Surrey County cross country championships at Frimley on 13 December 1986, where John Gladwin won the senior title and Belgrave took team silver in the senior and junior races; boys' and colts' results follow. Surrey County x/c Championships - Report by Colin Pearson A good result for the Juniors. We packed in well, but it was not quite good enough to beat Aldershot and Farnham with their scoring four in the first six places. They certainly deserved their fine win. Glyn came through well to finish second. He also looked the stronger at the finish. Graham, Martin and Andy showed the sort of backing which could give them a place medal in the Southern and possibly the National Junior races when Matt and Justin Chaston come into the team. Richard, Simon, Matt and Garry could have got a medal most years previously. Adam and John finished well but probably found the course rather tough. Thanks for your support. In the Senior Championship John Gladwin got his revenge over Clive Hensby for a couple of years back when Clive beat him in the Junior race. As they went out on the final big lap Clive was about 50 metres up on John but when they came into the playing fields with about 800 metres to go John changed into overdrive and went by the Woking to win by 8 seconds with Bob Treadwell about a half a minute further back. I am sure that Bob and Clive wish that John would stick to 1500 metres track running. Congratulations to John on winning his first Surrey Senior x/c title. John Wright was our second man home in 8th place and should earn him his first Surrey County Vest. Well done!! It was then a case of its and bits, Andy North, third Bels man home was struggling and we could tell by the look on his face that he was not happy with his own and knowing Andy he will be seeking revenge in the Southern and National. Frank Ward also showed that he intends to remain in the "A" team. We did have some good cheer when we collected our Silver team medals but we were lucky because if Olly or David had dropped out we would not have finished in the frame. They did themselves no good by running with the after effects of flu. Well done Seniors - and thanks again everybody for your support. 13 December 1986 - Surrey x/c Champion Frimley 1.
