items.label: June 1987
items.sum: Report of the Belgrave Centenary cross-country race on Wimbledon Common on 17 January 1987, won by Surrey's Bob Treadwell with John Gladwin first Belgravian in 7th, followed by a two-page photo spread by Mark Shearman.
items.s: CENTENARY CELEBRATION CROSS-COUNTRY Report of the Belgrave Centenary cross-country race on Wimbledon Common on 17 January 1987, won by Surrey's Bob Treadwell with John Gladwin first Belgravian in 7th, followed by a two-page photo spread by Mark Shearman. CENTENARY CELEBRATION CROSS-COUNTRY 17th January 1987 - Wimbledon Weather conditions had been appalling during the preceding week, with heavy snow in Eastern Counties from Kent to Yorkshire. Rotherham Harriers, who had been particularly keen to take part in this fixture, found most of their team were snow-bound and were unable to travel South. Newham & Essex Beagles had similar problems but managed to find three members well to the west of their territory so at least made an appearance. Wimbledon Common was not too badly affected and the old revived course down the cemetery horse ride and up the Queensmere Hill presented no special problems. The ECCU, Surrey and Middlesex County Associations had done us the honour of bringing representative teams to celebrate our Centenary and in addition to the Beagles runners Derby and QPH also fielded teams. The race itself produced a clear-cut win for Surrey's Bob Treadwell who revelled in ideal conditions for him, leading from gun to tape. However, the ECCU strength soon made itself felt in the chase and they finished 4 of the next 5 runners home. John Gladwin ran carefully to avoid unnecessary injury, particulary on the frozen horse-ride section, but came through strongly to finish 7th. Young Justin Chaston ran particularly well to beat two of the ECCU team and finish 15th leaving a trail of good quality runners behind him. The team result was predictable of course, but that was not the most important part of the day's proceedings. Fifty runners had commemorated our 100 years of existence and each was awarded a Belgrave Centenary bone-china tankard as a memento of the occasion. Good quality prizes also went to the first three individuals. Hot chilli-con-carné, french bread, buns and tea were served up after the race, thanks to the stirling efforts of Sue Parrott and Margaret Stroud, whilst Brian Gorman and the bar staff kept the spectators in good fettle with their usual refreshments. It was a pity that of our six surviving England cross-country internationals only four could be present, weather conditions keeping Len Herbert and Gerry North away. Nevertheless, to join the ever-present Carter, Penny and Stimpson we were delighted to receive Verne Blowfield who was visiting Belgrave Hall again for the first time in 37 years! Many other guests were present, including the Mayor of Merton and representatives of the various cross-country organisations. In response to our President's welcoming address, words of appreciation were expressed by Barry Wallman (ECCU) and Alan Domleo (Derby) who felt sure that everyone had enjoyed both the racing and the hospitality. The cost of staging such a fixture, including the commemorative awards and the souvenir programmes, was considerable. The Club was especially fortunate therefore to enjoy the generous sponsorship of TOM CARTER who underwrote the total cost of this memorable occasion. items.sum: Steve Williams' round-up of Belgrave's 1987 indoor season, led by John Regis' European Indoor 200m bronze and UK record, with John Gladwin, Ernie Obeng and Marcus Adam, and a note of ratified UK records.
items.s: Indoor Round Up. Steve Williams' round-up of Belgrave's 1987 indoor season, led by John Regis' European Indoor 200m bronze and UK record, with John Gladwin, Ernie Obeng and Marcus Adam, and a note of ratified UK records. Indoor Round Up. (compiled by Steve Williams) The outstanding performance this season was John Regis' tremendous Bronze Medal run at the European Championships in Lievin, France in February. His third place came in the fastest ever indoor 200m race and his startling time of 20.54 was just 2/100ths away from the World Record as it stood beforehand. It was also the third time John had improved the UK Record. Continuing a remarkable season, John made the 400m men raise their eyebrows as firstly he slipped in an electrifying 45.6 relay leg against the USA and then set a Commonwealth best over 300m two days later, leaving two good American one lap specialists well beaten. Our other main man in the media, John Gladwin, made his indoor debut at the end of the season. John adapted readily to the tight bends, despite his 6' 3" frame, with a sub 4 minute mile win against the USA, showing an impressive burst of speed in the last 50 metres, and he followed that up by collecting a UK Indoor 2000m record behind the World 3000m Champion at the Dairy Crest Invitation. Ernie Obeng continued the fine sequence of 60 metre runs he has set up over the past four years with a 3rd place in the National Indoor Championships and International wins against Hungary and the USA. In Budapest, Ernie shaved one hundredth off his pb to record a fast 6.62 in an invitation run at the International meeting. Life begins at 30 Ernie! Marcus Adam made up a quartet of Belgravians in the same England team for the match against the USA for his Senior International debut, beating the American 'B' string. Marcus later retained his National Under 20 title in a Championship Best Performance and took the Silver medal over 60m in a pb. Timewise over 200m though Marcus's best was a nippy 21.76 in the Senior AAA's Series when still over a month away from his 19th birthday! Records Ratified John Regis's 200metres in 20.54 secs and the England team in the 4 x 400m Relay (John Regis, K Bentham, S Heard, P Harmsworth) time 3mms 7.04 secs at the European Indoor Champs at Lieven (France) have been ratified as UK records. items.sum: H.P.'s Ladies Section report on the 1986 league season (seventh in Division II), farewells to Tracy Denton (injured), Jo Hilliard (returning to New Zealand) and Frances Guy (leaving for the Middle East), a plea for more cross-country support, and a target of Division I in 1988.
items.s: The Ladies. H.P.'s Ladies Section report on the 1986 league season (seventh in Division II), farewells to Tracy Denton (injured), Jo Hilliard (returning to New Zealand) and Frances Guy (leaving for the Middle East), a plea for more cross-country support, and a target of Division I in 1988. The Ladies. After the good summer had by all in 1985 when we were promoted to Division II, I hope that everyone enjoyed the better competition we had in 1986 when Belgrave Ladies finished seventh in their first season in the new League. Well done by all. However, three sad things to report. First, Tracy Denton (javelin) will be sadly missed in 1987 as she has had to have surgery on her back. I am sure that all will wish her well and a speedy return for 1988. Come on Tracy, 46m +? Good Luck, H.P. Secondly, we have had to say Bon Voyage to Jo Hilliard who in December 1986 decided that it was time to return home to New Zealand. I think we have all enjoyed her company in her short stay with us and will miss her presence in the team. She wished me to say thanks to you all in the section for making her feel welcome and that she enjoyed very much competing and being part of the Ladies Section. She wishes the Ladies Section every success in 1987 and the future. I am sure with me you will all wish her well and hope that she enjoys her athletics back home. Good Luck, H.P. Thirdly, another lady we shall miss for four years from the end of September this year will be Frances Guy, who will be going to work in the Middle East. We all wish her good luck in the future and thank her for her support. Also the joy and fun it gave the Ladies Section to see her win the Poly Ladies and Belgrave Marathon Championships. Thanks, Frances - we hope to see you compete for us again on your vacations back in the UK. Again Good Luck, H.P. As you can see, Ladies, the results for the winter season were very disappointing over the country. First I must say well done to those few who turned out, and thank goodness they did. However, just a few is not enough and very disheartening for those who did. After all, running over the country surely is the basic training and stamina work for all middle distance runners and gives one a break from the long and full track season running on hard tracks. (The legs enjoy the break too). So let's see a few more new faces training at Belgrave Hall on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings during the winter. As we are lucky enough to have such a facility for goodness sake let's all use it. Next year, maybe, we won't have so many knee and leg problems. In 1988 I would like to see us go for Division I and I think the time will be ripe for most of you and for the Section. That's what I would like for you and the club to achieve. So Ladies it's all down to you - if you want Division I competition, go out and get it. Good Luck for 1987 - H.P. H.P. H.P. Tracy Denton Tracy Denton javelin; back surgery, out for 1987 Jo Hilliard Jo Hilliard returned home to New Zealand December 1986 Frances Guy Frances Guy won Poly Ladies and Belgrave Marathon Championships; leaving to work in the Middle East Polytechnic Harriers Marathon Belgrave Hall New Zealand Middle East

items.s: Footnote to all Belgravians: Harry Porter regrets the small number of members who help at ladies' track meetings, thanks the officials and parents who do, especially 80-year-old starter Arthur Penny, and appeals for more helpers in the centenary year. Footnote to all Belgravians: I am very disappointed in the support within the club. In the track season there are but a few, and they are a few, who come along to each and every meeting to help. There are some 800 members in the club and the same small group turn out. You do not have to be qualified to assist or help those people who are, who are now very few and some getting on in years. I would like at this point to thank those few officials, and the helpers who are mostly parents of the girls, for coming along and helping. One gentleman I would like to thank is our one and only starter Mr Arthur Penny, who is some 80 years of age and still my "man of the match". Thanks Arthur from all of us. I would like to be able to say the same for many more people next year. So come on all of you that are Bels, we all need your help to keep this the great club that it has always been. Especially as this is our Centenary year. Harry Porter Harry Porter Harry Porter Arthur Penny Mr Arthur Penny the ladies' only starter, aged about 80 Mr Arthur Penny Arthur

items.s: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL ? Boxed appeal for members to become technical officials, describing the categories, the Surrey County A.A.A. introductory lecture each November, and Clive Shippen as contact. WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL ? Our Club is suffering from an acute shortage of Technical Officials. Our Track and Field programme each summer covers young Athletes, Ladies and Men's fixtures in a variety of leagues and other compotitions. In every case we have an obligation to provide Technical Officials. WHY NOT TRY YOUR HAND AT HELPING IN THIS WAY?. No previous experience is necessary and you may choose from the pre-season's fixture list those meetings at which you are prepared to assist. All Judges are only to pleased to help newcomers to learn the ropes. The following Categories are used in Track and Field athletics--- TRACK JUDGE, FIELD JUDGE, STARTER, MARKSMAN and TIMEKEEPER In November each year the Surrey County A.A.A. give an evening's introductory lecture at Wimbledon for newcomers in all these disciplines. If you wish you may take a Grade 4 Test the following week, but it is not necessary. All you need is a copy of the A.A.A. Rule Book, which all officials need to refer to from time to time. Officiating can be a most rewarding and enjoyable part of the Athletics scene WHY NOT GIVE IT A TRY?. For all the advice you need Telephone --- CLIVE SHIPPEN [phone number withheld]. items.s: Boxing Day, Wimbledon 1986. Report and photographs (by Joe Coleman) of the club's Boxing Day fancy dress run at Wimbledon in 1986, where Brian Pritchard's 'Boat Race Four' coxed by Bill Laws won the prize, followed by Biscoe Punch and mince pies at Belgrave Hall. Boxing Day, Wimbledon 1986. This year's Fancy Dress Run was blessed with a nice bright, sunny and mild day and despite the fact that there is no public transport on Boxing Day there was a very good entry and a good following of supporters. There was a wide range of ideas on what is deemed as Fancy Dress and the photographs above and on the following page of those who caught the camera's eye indicates that there was no lack of originality. The prize for the best entry, judged by a panel led by Mrs Sheena Lucas, was awarded to Brian Pritchard's Boat Race Four ably coxed by Bill Laws. The photograph does not do justice to the entry - the four oarsmen with their back to front heads, 'dummy' arms and legs to simulate the correct rowing stance was very unique and bearing in mind that the origins of Belgrave Harriers was with the rowing fraternity, it was also very topical. After the run it was back to Belgrave Hall for what is now the traditional "Biscoe Punch" and lashings of mince pies. Those appearing in the photographs amongst whose disguise can be seen through are:- Johnny Morris, Lionel Mann, Tootsie Gannon, Bob Bridges, Andy Paton, Ron Severn, Jackie Smiter, Geo Flanagan, Ben Cooper, Bill Laws, Olly Foote, Ross Bros, Matt Kinnane and Rin Tin Tin. Our thanks to all those volunteers who always seem to be there behind the scenes preparing the food, doing the washing up etc and often finishing up without a bite because it's all gone. Thank you very much. Boxing Day, Wimbledon 1986. items.sum: Eric Crutcher introduces Sue Morrison, the club's first lady secretary, succeeding Joe Coleman, and outlines her running, walking and administrative background.
items.s: SUE MORRISON - OUR NEW SECRETARY Eric Crutcher introduces Sue Morrison, the club's first lady secretary, succeeding Joe Coleman, and outlines her running, walking and administrative background. For the first time in the club's illustrious history we have a lady secretary. Sue Morrison has taken over the reins from Joe Coleman who, following the tradition of past secretaries, put in some sterling work on behalf of the club. Although Sue is a relatively new member, having joined in early 1986, she has already become an enthusiastic and loyal member of the flourishing ladies walking section in addition to taking on the duties of secretary. Sue's involvement with athletics goes back to 1982 when she took up running and completed a half marathon. Having "got the bug" for running it was only the following year that a marathon was tackled and successfully completed followed by participation in the London Marathon. Her introduction to walking came in 1984 when she competed for the Inland Revenue in the Civil Service Championships. As walking gradually took over from running she joined Belgrave (encouraged somewhat by John Hall and Eric Crutcher!) where the further persuasion of Carl Lawton made the transition complete! Sue's involvement on the administrative side of athletics also started in the early 1980s when she accepted a place on the Inland Revenue Sports Association Committee (Eastern Region). This soon led to the National Committee where she was Publicity Secretary from 1983-87 and Assistant Treasurer from 1985-87. This also included responsibility for compiling their National Sports Bulletin twice a year (could Sue follow Joe and "do the double" - Secretary and Belgravian editor? Although this Committee work covered sport in general Sue still sits on the IR Athletics Committee and in January 1986 accepted a place on the Civil Service Athletics Association Committee where she now has responsibility for the ladies representatives teams. There is no doubt that Sue is a great ambassador for Inland Revenue and Civil Service athletics and equally I am sure that our new Secretary will prove a great Ambassador for Belgrave Harriers. items.label: April 1988
items.sum: President Bill Lucas closes the Centenary year thanking Clive Shippen, and criticises the lack of support from middle-distance runners for winter fixtures after relegation from Division 1 of the Surrey League.
items.s: From the President. President Bill Lucas closes the Centenary year thanking Clive Shippen, and criticises the lack of support from middle-distance runners for winter fixtures after relegation from Division 1 of the Surrey League. Dear Members Our Centenary year has drawn to a close and as your president I would congratulate, on your behalf, all those who have contributed in any way towards its undoubted success. I must however make special mention of Clive Shippen who was chairman of the Centenary Committee and fronted for most of the year's activities. We are deeply indebted to him for all his hard work and the immense amount of time he has devoted to the club not only in 1987 but in the years leading up to our anniversary. Many of you will have contributed to a small memento which, by the time you read this, will have been presented to remind him of BELGRAVE 1987. The year as far as I am concerned ends in disappointment with the inability of our winter teams to uphold the prestige gained by the track and field team during the summer. The great name of this club was built on our successes on the road and over the country but I fear that over the past few years that name has slipped badly through lack of support of the winter fixtures by our leading middle distance runners. We have the names on paper but where are they when they are wanted. Your cross country secretary prepares a programme and works hard to enter teams and appraise the members of each fixture only to find that the numbers taking part are hardly worth his effort. I fail to understand how members can call themselves Belgravians and yet not give of their best to ensure that the name of Belgrave remains prominent in our sport. The number of fixtures at which a major effort is required are very limited viz Country, Area and National Cross Country Championships and Area and National Road Relay races - only five. All other races including club championships are designed to bring an athlete to fitness for these events. Surely it is possible for all middle distance runners to arrange their training programmes around specific dates which are well known in advance - it has been done before with great success both for individuals and club teams - why not again!!! I cannot believe, for it has been disproved on so many occasions that running over country and on the road harms the summmer performances. Such names as Ovett, Moorcroft, Pirie, Cram, Lewis, Hutchings and Bedford to mention only a few bear witness to the benefits of winter competition. It is not too late for runners and their coaches to rectify our poor start of the 1987/8 season. Get together with Colin Pearson and plan a recovery so that the name of Belgrave rides high. What ignominy to be relegated from Division 1 of the Surrey League!!! No-one can participate in British athletics unless he or she is a member of a club. Give back to this club the devotion it deserves and help all its members to share in the glory of which it is undoubtedly capable. Best wishes to you all for 1988. Bill Lucas President Bill Lucas Bill Lucas President Clive Shippen Clive Shippen chairman of the Centenary Committee Colin Pearson Colin Pearson cross country secretary (implied) Ovett Ovett Moorcroft Moorcroft Pirie Pirie Cram Cram Lewis Lewis Hutchings Hutchings Bedford Bedford Surrey League National Cross Country Championships National Road Relay

items.s: Some Notes From A Past President Past President Derek Crookes regrets the seniors' lack of titles in the Centenary year, criticises behaviour towards officials at Battersea Park, and appeals for help as officials at the 1988 home fixtures. (1) Whilst congratulating our Junior Men on winning the Mike Sully race and the Surrey County Cross-Country title it is nevertheless extremely disappointing that in the Club's Centenary year our Seniors have failed to win any Cross-Country or Road Relay titles. This is in spite of the great strength we have "on paper" - probably as great as at any time in the past when we regularly won titles. The main difference, no doubt, is that in the past "team spirit" and "running for the club" were not the dirty phrases they now are. (2) As officials see it was a great disappointment that on two occasions at Battersea park Senior Athletes (Men) came to argue with track officials or timekeepers. We are short of officials as it is without this "professional" attitude creeping into club races. (3) The Club's shortage of officials continues. If anyone (graded or not) can assist at any of our home fixtures, please ring me prior to the dates so that I can use you to the best advantage. items.s: IN MEMORIUM - H. F. KING. Obituary of race walker and Grade I walking judge Harold King, 1922 RWA Junior 10 miles champion, with a 1937 50th Anniversary Dinner photograph identifying him and other Belgrave walkers. IN MEMORIUM H. F. KING. We are sorry to report the death of one of our oldest stalwarts, Harold King. He must have been in his eighties and for many years was a Grade I Walking Judge and was a familiar figure on the roadside and on the track. Harold was a quiet modest man who was liked by all and whose decisions were respected by competitors and officials alike. Like most Walking Judges long years as an official followed an active career - indeed a distinguished one. In 1922 at Regent's Park not only was he the Individual winner of the RWA "Junior" (by qualification based on past performances) 10 miles Championship, but he led the Belgrave team home to victory. The following year he was third in the AAA 7 miles (now 10,000m) Championship held at Stamford Bridge. He also won Kent County Championships, and was a regular Club team man for many years. His work as an engineer took him to East Africa where he contracted an illness which put an end to his career as an active walker. Fortunately his enthusiasm for the sport was channelled into Judging. Harold was a keen and loyal Belgravian, a quiet man who will be remembered with respect and affection. items.s: JOHN BROMLEY Obituary of John Bromley, who died in Perth, Western Australia in December 1987; a runner from 1949 and later race walker, coach and official, with a list of his running titles. John Bromley passed away suddenly and peacefully in December 1987 at Perth, W Australia after competing in a walking race. He was visiting his family at the time. John joined Belgrave Harriers in 1949 whilst serving in the army as a PTI and stationed at Aldershot. John competed for the club on the track, road and cross-country running and in 1970 after a series of Achiles Tendon operations and a replacement big toe joint he transferred his activities to race walking and had competed with distinction in that section up to the time of his passing. He was, up to the time of his retirement, Physical Training Officer at Hendon Police Cadet School and in that capacity he was in charge of all physical training and sport and many fine athletes owe much to him for their earlier instruction. Some of John's wins as a runner were 1944 - Welsh AAA Youth 1 mile, 1946 - Welsh AAA Junior 1 Mile, Kent County Junior 1 mile, 1947 - Singapore AAA 880 yards and 1 mile,1949 - Lancashire County AAA 1 mile, 1953 - Surrey County AAA 2 miles Steeplechase (this record still stands), 1954 BELGRAVE HARRIERS 880 yards and 1 mile, 1955 - Singapore AAA 880 yards, 1957 - Singapore AAA 1 mile and 3 miles (new record). He was a fully qualified AAA Coach in all events and also as Track and Field Judge, Starter, Timekeeper, Meeting Organiser and Administrator and had been Army Senior Athletic Coach and Senior Instructor at the Army School of Physical Training and had acted as Team Manager and Coach to several British Modern Pentathlon "B" teams at home and abroad during the preparations for the Mexico Olympic Games 1968. A quiet spoken man and exceedingly modest. A great all-rounder and it will be hard to find his equal. J.G.C. e: London to Brighton and Back Walk
items.s: Joe Wilson - Centurion No 164 Obituary of road walker Joe Wilson, Centurion No 164, who died on 2 February 1988 aged 79, recalling his London to Brighton races and his work as an RWA Grade I judge. Regrettably Joe passed away on February 2nd 1988 aged 79. He joined the club in September 1939 being introduced by Chas. Churcher our then Road Walking Captain. Joe took up Race Walking at the age of 30 having spent his earlier years as a amateur footballer of some note and also as a prize winning Ballroom Dancer at which he also acted as a demonstrator and judge in dancing competitions. He developed into a good team man and featured in many of our longer distance successes from 20 miles, 50kms to London to Brighton and London to Brighton and back. He competed and finished in 14 London to Brighton races and finished in all of them in under 10hrs. In 1951 he became a member of the podigious Centurions Club when in the Brighton and back race he completed the 100 miles in 21hurs 59mins 30secs. In 1957 "Brighton" he was hit by a car and spent 3 weeks in The Royal Sussex Hospital with a broken jaw and facial injuries. Although primarily a road walker Joe did compete on the track and became a very efficient coach and when his competing days were over he then devoted his time as an RWA Grade I judge in which capacity he officiated at Club, County, Area and National Championship events. The likes of men like Joe Wilson with such club spirit are hard to come by and he will be sorely missed. e: Belgrave Harriers Track and Field Championships
items.s: grapevine Grapevine column of club news: old members Bruce Hayman and Cecil Mains get back in touch in the Centenary year, a table of members with 60 years' continuous membership, tributes to walker Fred Rickards, engagements and weddings, and Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul in the GB bobsleigh at the Calgary Winter Olympics, and thanks to Tom Carter for sponsoring the Centenary Cross-Country match and Belgrave Hall improvements. The fact it was Belgrave Centenary year did remind some elapsed members who had in mind that once "a Belgravian always a Belgravian" to contact the club and make themselves re-known and fortunately there happened to be a couple of us who could go far enough back to recall them. One such man was Bruce Hayman who as one of our top sprinters in the late '20s and early '30s. His athletic career was cut short when he had a severe operation on his head which left him severely incapacitated and in consequence his parents moved back to their original home place in Devon and after some time in convalescence and rehabilitation he regained reasonable good health. Bruce wrote to the Club Secretary asking for details of the Centenary Celebrations. Luckily the Hon Sec (Joe Coleman), and Chas Jones had been members with Bruce in the Belgrave Junior Track teams in 1928/29 era and readily recalled him and so on the Track and Field Championships day Bruce came up to Battersea Park from Devon to meet the Club and to renew his acquaintance with the track that he had not seen since he left London after his operation in the 1930s. You can well imagine his surprise at the difference. When he left it was a three lap to the mile ankle deep dust heap and costing 1 penny to use the dressing room and now the 400 metre lap all-weather track with all mod cons and costing a small fortune to use. Having had a most enjoyable day making himself known to everybody and meeting most of the club officials Bruce returned to Devon, complete with his coveted 60 years old club lapel badge vowing,to keep in touch. Another "contact" came as the result of a lady member of the Cornwall A.C. telephoning the Hon Sec on behalf of a son of an old member. The son (living in Hayle, Cornwall) wanted to buy a club tie as a surprise Xmas present for his 80 year old father who never ceases to talk about his times with the "Bels". Things were sorted out and the 80 year old turned out to be Cecil Mains (not to be confused with Dave) who was a cross-country man and my records show him as finishing 4th to Bert Footer, Arthur Penny and Arthur Allum in the 1933 10 miles Club Cross-Country Championship. Cecil wrote me from home in Dorset to thank me for my services and wished to be remembered to all and in particular Arthur Penny, Bert Footer and Arthur Allum - I have contacted Arthur Penny but unfortunately Bert Footer and Arthur Allum now do their training at extremely high altitude and I do not expect to see them for some time yet. Chris Fairfield now a second claim member and living at Stalybridge, Cheshire, promptly sent in his subs with an accompanying newsletter. He had run a 3 hrs 6 mins in the London Marathon but brought home the bacon when he won a £1,000 worth food voucher in a competition organised by a Bacon Company. Eat your heart out lads. At the time of writing he was leading in his 1st Claim Club,Saddleworth Runners, road running championship (best of 5 out of 8 races) with one race to go. So hang in there Chris. Keep it up. On the question of membership in Centenary Year 1987 it is apposite that we should name those who achieved 60 YEARS OF CONTINUOUS MEMBERSHIP by the close of the Year. They are (with close runners-up) as follows :- (P.P.) = Past President. FRED RICKARDS, who, as you can see from the long serving members' list, was one of the clubs finest longer distance walkers who won the Police Long Distance Championship (Barking to Southend) on 7 occasions from 1924 to 1936 and was in Belgrave's winning teams in the RWA 20 miles and 50 kms Chmpionships up to 1939 also he figured in many "open" races of that period. A real Belgravian, and now approaching his 90th birthday he still shows great interest in the club's activities and to show how diverse his interests are, he asked me to pass on to Ernie Obeng, his congratulations on his (Ernie's) recent 60 mtrs successes and thanks for wearing his claret and gold club vest as shown on TV. Leap-year result just in - Long Jumping, Hurdler, Sprinter and Track Captain, Mark Lindsay-Bayley announced his engagement to Elizabeth!! Absence makes the heart grow fonder! An old proverb but no less true today. No sooner had David Swain returned to the USA after his brief but successful visit to the UK than we heard of his engagement to Jenny. Congratulations and best wishes from your team mates. It must be catching! We hear John Barnes is to marry Jane in June. As the wedding is to be in Bournemouth on 11th June and our second BAL match is to be the following day we understand John might be excused selection - unless things get really desperate. Again our best wishes to you both. Belgrave's army sprinters Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul distinguished themselves by powering their 4 man bobsleigh into the GB 1 slot at the Calgary Winter Olympics. The 4 runs were a lottery with so much depending on the time of day and ice conditions. Their 12th spot overall was only 2 secs off gold in a total elapsed time of just under 4 minutes. Apart from holidays and illness, both rare, can anyone ever remember TOM CARTER being absent from Club activities for more than a Week? This effervescent 79 years old youngster is ever-present. But the Club's appreciation has been especial this year, for not only did Tom sponsor our Centenary Cross-Country match at the beginning of the year but at it's end he had waived payment due to him for a significant part of the Belgrave Hall improvements. His love for the Club is legion. It has been said that if you broke his arm off you would find "Belgrave Harriers" written into the bone like a stick of rock! AGE (Yrs) MEMBERSHIP (Yrs) 1. Our picture shows four of the club's elder statesmen in a relaxed mood during this year's Centenary Club '20' road race. Their ages reach a grand total of 348 years and their combined Belgrave membership a staggering 242 years. They are (left to right) :- Ken O'Kell (86) - 64 years a member Bill Webb (93) - 60 years a member Frank Webb (84) - 59 years a member Norman Dewberry (85) - 59 years a member Ken O'Kell, together with Bill Webb, Bert Footer and Micky Pyer, was a key figure in Belgrave's cross-country revival in the early "twenties"; winning an individual bronze medal in the Surrey County C.C. Championships of 1926 before moving away for several years. Norman Dewberry has been ever-present throughout his 59 years of membership and was made a Life Member many years ago for his unstinting help with Club activities. The Webb brothers, both Past Presidents, hold a unique double record. Bill is the longest serving Belgrave Hon.Treasurer (1934-48) and Frank the longest serving Hon.Treasurer of Vets AC (1949-87). Apart from those posts they have served athletics in a multitude of different ways. How nice to see all four still enjoying our sport so much. items.sum: Clive Shippen's review of the second half of the Centenary year: the Club Track and Field Championships with an 1887 re-enactment sprint, the 36th Club '20' with a tribute to founder Arthur Whitehead, the Thames river trip, the Club Birthday at Belgrave Hall with the new Centenary Bell, the Centenary Dinner Dance and the 68th Open '7' Walk, plus the abandoned London-Brighton Relay plans and remaining mementoes.
items.s: CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS Clive Shippen's review of the second half of the Centenary year: the Club Track and Field Championships with an 1887 re-enactment sprint, the 36th Club '20' with a tribute to founder Arthur Whitehead, the Thames river trip, the Club Birthday at Belgrave Hall with the new Centenary Bell, the Centenary Dinner Dance and the 68th Open '7' Walk, plus the abandoned London-Brighton Relay plans and remaining mementoes. Clive Shippen reviews the Centenary Celebrations The last issue of the Belgravian covered the first half of our year's celebrations and outlined the plans for the remainder of the year. This issue is able to report on the second half of our celebrations, though detailed reports will be found elsewhere in these pages. As we forecast in June, the Club Track and Field Championships proved to be a memorable occasion. The weather was fine, there was a large attendance, and a lively spirit prevailed throughout the afternoon. In addition to the very full programme of athletics events for men and women, boys and girls, there were pole-vault and discus invitation events, children's races and a special re-enactment of an 1887 track sprint - complete with authentic moustachioed runners in their Victorian garb. Great pains were taken to "string" the lanes, and the race was the highlight of the day. A marquee was erected to display club trophies and for the sale of Centenary mementoes; and the announcer and recorders enjoyed the luxury of a tented stall on the special day. Mark Shearman, an athletics photographer of international repute, spent the day with us and took dozens of memorable action shots. His final ones being of the large group which stayed on to the very end and released their helium-filled balloons at his command. Anyone wishing to see contact prints of the day's photographs and desiring to place orders for prints (from en-print size to poster size) should see Carl Lawton at Belgrave Hall. The group photo in poster size (36"x24") is an excellent souvenir. Only seven days elapsed before we were once more busying ourselves with a celebratory occasion. This time the 36th Club '20'. A souvenir programme outlined the history of the event and the part played by its founder, Arthur Whitehead. In recognition of Arthur's service to the event our President presented him with a Belgrave Centenary wall plate. At the presentation, held in the forecourt of Lauriston Cottage, were The Mayor of Merton and the winner of the inaugural event in 1952 - Dave Fotheringham of TVH, who had travelled up from the Isle of Wight. The race sported "Start" and "Finish" banners for the first time in many years and several other extra touches helped to mark the event as a special occasion - not least being the award of centenary mugs to the first 25% of finishers. Surrey County AAA and the Southern Counties AA acknowledged the celebrations by incorporating their own championships into the race. A busy July closed on the 26th with the Thames River Trip from Putney Pier. It was a great pity that this should clash with our British and Southern League matches, but this alone could not account for tickets being undersold. But for those who went it was a night to remember. Lots of spare food, the best disco of the year and a very high-spirited evening saw a happy 111 Belgravians disembark in the early hours of Sunday morning. The introduction of the AAA McVitie's 25x1 mile relay in early October caused the planned 100x1 mile relay involving ourselves, Blackheath and TVH, to be cancelled. It did not seem appropriate to try and use the McVitie's race for our own celebrations, so the Centenary relay slipped from our programme. And so to Wednesday 7th October - the Club Birthday. It was difficult to estimate how many would attend Belgrave Hall for this get-together. There was no music. In the event an estimated 140 came along and it turned out to be a very enjoyable evening with many re-unions. Bill Webb, at 93 our most senior Past Presidsent, unveiled the new Centenary Bell which had been donated by Charlie Manning. The Centenary cake, beautifully made by the President's daughter and sporting a perfect replica of our Centenary logo, was expertly sliced into the appropriate number of pieces within seconds by The Queen's pastry chef, Lionel Mann. "Champagne", provided by The President, enabled all present to toast the Club's health and look forward to the start of our second centenary with keen anticipation. Especial thanks went to Charlie Manning and daughter Linda who donated and served the evening's fine buffet spread. Bill Webb has got an "ology" - Campanology - as he inaugurates the "Centenary Bell" which bears the inscription: "This bell was unveiled by the most Senior past President - W.G.Webb - on the 100th Birthday of the Club 7 October 1987". The Bell was donated by Chas.Manning Past President. The pinnacle of our year, was reached on Saturday, 14th November, when 250 members and guests gathered at The Gloucester, South Kensington, for our Centenary Dinner Dance. It was a magnificent occasion. Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard excelled themselves as organisers and made this the most memorable of our celebrations. Many members, old and not so old, travelled from all parts of the country to be present. But these were out-done by three who flew the Atlantic especially for the occasion; Daye Donovan from New York (how Edmund would have loved to have been present), Chris Steer from Seattle and John Thresher from Toronto. Our Patron, Eddie Kulukundis, and Susan Hampshire delighted us with their presence and amongst the Club's official guests were Rachel and Steve Ovett, the latter rounding off the speeches appropriately with typical Ovett humour. The revelry continued with dancing until 1.00a.m and a disco until 2.00a.m but the farewells were still going on at 2.45a.m! It was an occasion that wanted to go on for ever, and would be very difficult to follow. But our 68th Open '7' Walk promotion was not put off by the previous act. The organisation had been coming together nicely during the preceding weeks and once again we enjoyed the presence of The Mayor of Merton, Councillor H. Turner, who started the race. To mark Centenary year a novices race over 5 miles was introduced and this was successful enough to warrant inclusion next year. Our final souvenir programme featured a history of the event and all previous 67 results. Our Race Walking celebration showed that Belgrave is a vital part of the UK Race Walking scene and it could well be that our introduction of a novices race in our Centenary event will prove to be a milestone in the revival of UK Walking fortunes. It was fitting that Belgrave should win both the men's and women's scratch team events. Bill Lucas presents the Open 7 Miles Walk winning team awards to our Ladies - Gill Brackpool, Jill Borthwick and Sue Morrison. "Centenary" President Bill Lucas and the Mayor of Merton Clr H Turner who graced us with his attendance at the 20mls Run, 7 miles Open Walk and 12 stage Relay. As was expected when the first review was written, the London-Brighton Relay plans had to be abandoned through lack of sponsorship. A study group had followed the course stage by stage on the corresponding Sunday of 1986 and had logged the carefully timed trip complete with supporting photographs. Much other work went into the early planning including the agreement of the three police forces involved. Hopes were raised and dashed on several occasions over the last two years and it was with much disappointment that the Centenary sub-committee had to acknowledge that the required sponsorship would not be forthcoming. Some mementoes are still available for purchase but no further stocks will be ordered. Sue Parrott and Eric Crutcher should be contacted for details of remaining stock. And so, after years of waiting, Centenary year has suddenly slipped behind us. Ahead lies the untrod ground of a second century with another celebratory year at the end of that. The revellers will all be different, but they will be linked to us by a common factor - the club we love and know as Belgrave Harriers. items.s: From Charlie Manning and a Verbatim Report from Committee Meeting 21st December 1987 Charlie Manning's tribute to Clive Shippen, given at the committee meeting of 21 December 1987, for organising the Centenary Year, with the silver picture frame and calligraphic dedication presented to him and the Centenary programmes he produced. Mr President - I hope you will forgive me for reading this but with the Committee's approval I'd like what I have to say to appear in the Belgravian. In our past 100 years Belgrave have produced some quite exceptional men - we have had clever pathfinders who were the original architects of the Club as we know it today - we have had Titans of Track, Gentlemen of the Road, Masters of the Country and more than our share of the Field. Today we still have some of the greatest athletic performers - and - we are very lucky in having a giant among administrators. I say that knowing that many of us do what we can, within our capacity, as amateurs and are consequently always open to critisism. Clive Shippen, on the other hand, has brought a degree of professionalism, at enormous cost to himself, in making our Centenary Year so remarkable and I personally pay tribute to his unique qualities. Consider one point that in his workload is a detail, the Dinner Menu and the brief history of Belgrave Harriers (I do hope that it will be reproduced for members not fortunate enough to have attended the Dinner). That article alone showed such scholarship as would be almost impossible to find in any other quarter. Mr President, as instructed by this Committee and as a result of such a generous response, I would ask you to make this presentation to Clive Shippen. The man who gave us these ... We salute with this Silver Picture Frame and this dedication CLIVE SHIPPEN In recognition of the tireless effort and that unique ability to do everything right for BELGRAVE HARRIERS during their Centenary Year. With many thanks for such outstanding service from the Principle Officers, Committee and Past Presidents. Belgrave Harriers. November 1987 The man who gave us these ... We salute with this Silver Picture Frame and this dedication Charlie Manning Charlie Manning Clive Shippen Clive Shippen organiser of the Centenary Year; presented with a silver picture frame and dedication, November 1987

items.sum: Clive Shippen's letter of thanks, dated 4 February 1988, for the presentation made to him for the Centenary Year, accepted on behalf of his sub-committee and the event organisers.
items.s: THANKS!! Clive Shippen's letter of thanks, dated 4 February 1988, for the presentation made to him for the Centenary Year, accepted on behalf of his sub-committee and the event organisers. When the President announced at the last Committee that a presentation was about to be made to Clive Shippen I was nothing less than astonished. A few minutes later, as nice things were being said, my astonishment turned to emotion; and finally I experienced embarrassment as I realised how many others had also played a large part in the Centenary Celebration. So although I am deeply grateful that the Club Officers, Committee and Past Presidents should consider me worthy of a presentation, I do feel that I am accepting it on behalf of my sub-committee and the various events organisers who contributed to much to this memorable year. The gift in itself is truly beautiful. I shall treasure it always and remember those behind it, always. My thanks to you all. Clive Shippen 4 February 1988 Clive Shippen Clive Shippen Centenary sub-committee

items.s: Postscript to the President's Message The President's postscript lamenting the senior men's relegation from Division 1 to Division 2 of the Surrey League after an injury-hit cross-country season, while praising the Juniors' Southern title and other results and Colin Pearson's team management. Since writing my message to you at about Christmas-time, we have just completed a Cross-Country season which as far as the senior section was concerned was a complete disaster due almost entirely to injuries, illness and non-availability of runners. The biggest disgrace was our relegation from Division 1 to Division 2 of the Surrey League. Three of the four races were badly supported whereas the race in Richmond Park showed that we should have had no trouble in finishing well up in the League. I must however give great credit and congratulations to our Juniors who won the Southern title, finished fourth in the National and contributed largely to the team that finished second place in the South of the Thames race. Not only were they prominent in these races but gave their full support to all other winter fixtures - we can be very proud of them - Colin Pearson has worked hard to enter teams and endeavoured to field teams worthy of the Belgrave name. He must be sorely disappointed with the results of the senior ranks. W.E.L. W.E.L. W.E.L. initials of the President (masthead lists W. E. items.sum: Eric Crutcher's Hall and Social report: a plea for more bar staff, thanks to the catering helpers, disappointing support for socials apart from the 100th birthday night and the first ladies darts championship, the boiler fund, building work on the Hall, and the new physiotherapist Colette Colosimo.
items.s: Hall and Social. Eric Crutcher's Hall and Social report: a plea for more bar staff, thanks to the catering helpers, disappointing support for socials apart from the 100th birthday night and the first ladies darts championship, the boiler fund, building work on the Hall, and the new physiotherapist Colette Colosimo. Bar I must begin by repeating my plea for more BAR STAFF to assist on club training days (Tuesday and Thursday evenings and Sunday lunchtime). My last two requests have passed unheeded and the situation will become critical in September unless further help is forthcoming NOW. All I am asking is 3 hours of your time once a month to ease the burden. Once again, I must thank the same loyal few that have served over the past months. One bright spot is Margaret Stroud's introduction of hot snacks (mainly on a Tuesday between 7 and 8pm) which has been most welcome through the winter. Thank you Margaret. Thanks also go to Brian Gorman for his Saturday catering and Fred Paget for his Sunday morning brew. Socials Moving on to socials I must report a disappointing response to most events held since the last Belgravian. The notable exceptions were the Club's 100th birthday night (reported elsewhere) and the first ladies darts championships held in October which attracted 16 competitors. Considering the relatively small numbers in the ladies section it was an excellent attendance. Pat Mann won the trophy by beating Jenny Christou 2:0 in the final. The Club's disco held in September and the pre-Christmas disco were both sparsely attended and hardly merited the work that goes into staging these events. I hope events in 1988 are better supported FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE CLUB AND ITS MEMBERS. Details of forthcoming socials will be notified with the summer fixture list. Hall I must thank all those who contributed to the boiler fund last September which raised over £1,800. The draw for the wallplate, donated by Stan Vickers, was held on the club's birthday night and was won by Doug Maughan. The new boiler is performing well but has a long way to go to match its predecessor! Following the renewal of the flat roof over the ladies changing room and the kitchen these areas are now undergoing long overdue improvements which will hopefully be completed in April. Harry Porter is carrying out a great deal of renovation work with assistance from Carl Lawton. At this stage I must also thank Arthur Penstone for his electrical work around the Hall. Four months ago we welcomed a physiotherapist by the name of Colette Colosimo to the hall who treats the walking wounded three times a week. Her times of attendance at the hall are 3.30-8.00pm on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. All athletes are treated, with Belgrave members having subsidised treatment (£8) which, by today's prices, is very reasonable. Indeed, several club members have already taken advantage of the reduced rates. Just ring Colette at the hall to make an appointment. items.s: The Centenary Dinner Dance Bill Couzens' account of the Centenary Dinner Dance at The Gloucester, London SW7, on 14 November 1987, with speeches by Clive Shippen (printed 'Skipper'), Bill Lucas, David Denton and Steve Ovett and the Tommy Green Cup and Centenary Cup awards to John Regis and Frances Guy; it gives attendance as 240, where the Centenary review elsewhere in the issue says 250. The Centenary Dinner Dance 14th November 1987 Venue - The Gloucester, Harrington Gardens, London SW7 This occasion was to be the pinnacle of our Centenary year with two hundred and forty Belgrave members and guests attending. The evening commenced at the reception with each member or guest being individually announced by the toastmaster and greeted by our president, Bill Lucas and his charming wife Sheena. The finery of the occasion was evident, with many dinner jackets and bow ties on display and the ladies exotically putting "Dynasty" into the shade. The dinner itself by consensus of opinion was excellent and lived up to the high standard of The Gloucester. Throughout the meal background music was played by the band Tuxedo Class with the occasional drum roll to announce "The President will take wine with all internationals past and present", another drum roll, "The President will take wine with all past presidents" another drum roll "- with the Committee" "with the ladies" etc. I should think for the President the art is not in public speaking but in finding how to remain sober. Then came the speeches, the first by Clive Skipper who gave a most interesting and enlightening portrayal of the club from the first meeting of a group of athletes on Friday 7th October 1887 who formed Belgrave Harriers to Belgrave Harriers 100 years later. Clive also designed the menu card that provided a short written history of the club. All raised their glasses to the toast "Belgrave Harriers". The next speaker was our President, Bill Lucas who talked of the club and its successes together with proposing our guests. The response was by David Denton President of the ECCU. A surprise speaker was Steve Ovett who provided everyone with a most entertaining speech showing his admiration for a club achieving 100 years and also for a certain Belgrave runner who, a number of years ago ran Steve into the ground on a training run across Wimbledon Common. Steve described the runner as "eyeballs out" and in full racing gear, a whisper of "Brian Gorman" was spontaneous. Finally the Tommy Green Cup for the most meritorious performance of the year was presented to John Regis and the equivalent Ladies trophy the "Centenary Cup" was awarded to Frances Guy for her fine marathon run. With the formalities over everyone was ready for the dancing and Tuxedo Class went into full swing, noticeably there was a great convergence onto the dance floor with many letting "their hair down" and getting stuck in, not the place for the faint hearted. At 11.30pm a well earned rest came just in time for some of us "old uns" with the drawing of the raffle, 1st prize was a microwave oven, other prizes a magnum of champagne, a carriage clock and many other excellent prizes. From midnight to 1am dancing continued to the music of Tuxedo Class then with thanks for the band on came the disco "Travelling Gramophone". I was advised previously by this time most people would be gone in fact the majority stayed and the dance floor was packed. At 2am with the music throbbing in our ears and a farewell from the President the Centenary Dinner Dance was over. Truly a night to remember. items.s: From THE BELGRAVIAN ..... 25 years ago .... Reprint from February 1963: Gerry North losing his Inter-Counties title at Reading to T.K. Johnston, and the first season and origins of the North Surrey League. FEBRUARY 1963 Gerry North, the holder, was given little hope by the Press of obtaining a forward position in the Inter-Counties race at Reading. His defeat by Snowdon in a Surrey League match and sixth place in the Lancashire County were the basis of these views. When, seven days before the big race, Gerry only just held off Shelley (N.Staffs) in the Mitcham '15' it was said he was not the force of last year. How wrong they were. Despite suffering from a bad cold he beat all the recognised opposition only to lose his title to Portsmouth's T.K. Johnston who, revelling in the Artic conditions, chose this day to make the biggest break-through of his career. I wonder how many of our senior athletes have noticed that Gerry can race week in and week out yet still produce the big effort for the big occasion. Perhaps, if the lesson is learned, we will soon field our strongest team more than once a season. The first season of North Surrey League fixtures has ended, and was undoubtedly a success. These matches give the bulk of club athletes a chance to experience the big race atmosphere and, with 10 to score, an opportunity of counting for their team. The league was born at the "3 Kings" Mitcham in May of last year. The proposal was put forward by Mitcham AC but, because of traditional fixtures being affected, it was not over-enthusiastically received by the other six clubs present who were, Belgrave, Walton, Surrey, Hercules, Herne Hill and South London. Eventually, however, all except SLH agreed to give it a trial. Gerry North Gerry North Inter-Counties holder; lost the title at Reading in 1963 to T.K. items.s: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL ? Appeal for members to become track and field technical officials, explaining the categories and the Surrey County A.A.A. introductory lecture, with Clive Shippen as contact. Our Club is suffering from an acute shortage of Technical Officials. Our Track and Field programme each summer covers young Athletes, Ladies and Men's fixtures in a variety of leagues and other compotitions. In every case we have an obligation to provide Technical Officials. WHY NOT TRY YOUR HAND AT HELPING IN THIS WAY?. No previous experience is necessary and you may choose from the pre-season's fixture list those meetings at which you are prepared to assist. All Judges are only to pleased to help newcomers to learn the ropes. The following Categories are used in Track and Field athletics--- TRACK JUDGE, FIELD JUDGE, STARTER, MARKSMAN and TIMEKEEPER In November each year the Surrey County A.A.A. give an evening's introductory lecture at Wimbledon for newcomers in all these disciplines. If you wish you may take a Grade 4 Test the following week, but it is not necessary. All you need is a copy of the A.A.A. Rule Book, which all officials need to refer to from time to time. Officiating can be a most rewarding and enjoyable part of the Athletics scene WHY NOT GIVE IT A TRY?. For all the advice you need Telephone --- CLIVE SHIPPEN [phone number withheld]. FEBRUARY 1938 - Our "Open" Walk Reprint from February 1938 reporting Belgrave's success in the club's eighteenth annual Open walk, won by Harry Churcher, with the result. & 50 years ago .... FEBRUARY 1938 - Our "Open" Walk The last Saturday in November, the 27th, was once again the occasion of much activity for walkers. Our Eighteenth Annual promotion attracted 182 entries, and 22 teams were nominated. No less than 33 Belgrave walkers entered, and we started four teams. The afternoon was cold, but fortunately the fog that had threatened during the morning had lifted, and conditions were quite good when our President started the race. Our walkers were soon seen to be prominent, with Harry Churcher and Fred Redman, of the Metropolitan W.C., contesting the lead. Round about three miles, Harry broke away up the hill and proceeded to build up a big lead. The gap between second and third men at half-way was considerable. It was obvious at this point that no other club was near us in the scratch team race. Eventually, our lads finished H.G. Churcher (1st), C.E. Churcher (3rd), P.G. Wright (4th) and J.G. Coleman (6th) - a wonderfully fine team effort and additionally, there was some splendid further support forthcoming. Actually, ridiculous though it seems, in the best supported Open race of the season, Don Brown finished 8th and yet did not score in the team! Bert Clayton, our new member resident at Eastleigh, gave another good display of walking in finishing eleventh. He will undoubtedly prove a great asset when he qualifies for our teams. Len Coleman again showed his promise, and succeeded in taking an individual handicap prize. In fact, the whole race may be considered a testimony to the Club's strength. The result, which is appended, gives ample evidence of the Club's success in the race. The Churcher family, in particular, did well, taking three prizes each! RESULT 1. H.G. items.s: Track and Field. Section Report Track and field section report on the 1987 centenary season: fourth in British League Division 1, GRE Cup semi-final exit, the B team and midweek league, and individual achievements by John Regis, Marcus Adam, John Gladwin and others. Track and Field. Section Report by Leo Coy and Steve Williams. The track and field season has drawn to a close and we can look back with a great deal of pride and satisfaction at the achievements of our teams and individuals in this historic year. In finishing fourth in the 1st Division of the British League we have established ourselves among the very best T&F clubs in the United Kingdom, a marvellous achievement when you think that five years ago we were just an average Southern League outfit. We have had a wonderful run through the British League and our arrival in the top Division for our 100th Birthday couldn't have been better timed. But there's to be no resting on laurels - we must continue to look forward. To break the present grip on this competition held by Birchfield, Haringey and Wolverhampton & Bilston will take some doing but we are already building on the season just gone. We will have new members eligible to compete next season and our strength in depth and in quality will be greater. We shall of course continue to need the utmost support from our Internationals at this level and while nobody expects them to compromise their training towards peak performances in the major championships, we do look to them and their coaches to give every consideration in their programmes to fitting in as many of the four matches as they can, if not necessarily in their primary events. Let's now start to have in mind that league title bringing the chance to represent the UK in the European Club Championships. There is no higher honour for a club in track and field. Returning to the season gone, perhaps the one disappointment was getting knocked out in the semi-finals of the GRE Cup (though the fixture did clash with the AAA's). On the one per event basis of this competition, we should at least make the final even if only some of our top men are available. The 'B' team continued to provide valuable competition for our second tier athletes and a springboard to the 'A' team for those good enough. Promotion wasn't achieved but we'll be having another go next season; a big effort in the first match next season will get everyone in the right frame of mind. In our midweek competition there were encouraging turnouts at most of the matches, with the use of Tooting rather than Croydon playing a part here. Unfortunately we just lost the final by one point. Individually our athletes have never achieved more in one season with John Regis' performances of course uppermost in the mind and Marcus Adam another to have a tremendous year capped by his European Junior win. International honours again fell to John Gladwin and Ernie Obeng while Abi Ekoku becomes a new name for the club honours Board with an England Under 23 appearance, as does Felix Sandy who ran in the World Championships for Sierra Leone. John Gladwin won AAA and UK Championship medals and became Britain's 6th fastest ever miler, while Gary Staines and Dave Swain brought top quality to our 5000m running with Dave winning a World Student Games medal and Gary surely exceeding even his own hopes in his first season at the distance. Stuart Paton, Phil Lovell and Ken Onuaguluchi again won Southern Counties medals as did John Wright for the first time and there were innumerable Area and County representative honours. We provided five County Champions and club records were broken, re-broken or equalled on no less than 28 occasions. 'Centenary' congratulations to all on making it a season to remember. items.s: NEW FACES FOR NEXT SEASON List of track and field athletes joining Belgrave from other clubs for the 1988 season, including Nigel Bevan, Scott Wyld, Chris Ogle and Femi Abejide. NEW FACES FOR NEXT SEASON: Increasing the competition for 'A' team places next season, and relieving a few of our all rounders so they can concentrate on their key events, will be a number of athletes of proven ability who have joined from other clubs. There will be Nigel Bevan who placed 4th in the Javelin at the European Junior Championships and has a best throw of 73.76 - definitely a name for the future. Many will remember the name of Scott Wyld as a young Belgravian with a lot of promise in the jumping events. Scott left when we couldn't provide any appropriate Age Group competition (a lesson for us there) but he returns from Herne Hill as a multi-disciplined jumper with a best Long Jump of 7.23w. Also joined from HHH are Chris Ogle, a middle distance runner who has run 1.50.89 for 800m, Leroy Haughton, a 2.00m+ High Jumper and Ron Corbin, a 15 metre+ Triple Jumper. Strengthening the hurdles are Dennis Baptiste from Luton, who does the highs and lows, and Paul Chong from Bournemouth, a 14 seconds man. Mike Small will have something to think about in the Hammer with 22 year old Jimmy Summers who has thrown 55.74 - a club record will go there in 1988. From Brighton comes Darren Hall, 48.19 400m as a Junior last year, and last but by no means least we'll have the assistance of Femi Abejide, ex Haringey, a talented all rounder who is close to 16 metres in the Triple Jump............Welcome to Belgrave. items.sum: Match-by-match report of Belgrave's first British Athletic League Division 1 season in 1987 (Portsmouth, Birmingham, Warley, Newham), finishing fourth overall.
items.s: GRE/BAL DIVISION 1 Match-by-match report of Belgrave's first British Athletic League Division 1 season in 1987 (Portsmouth, Birmingham, Warley, Newham), finishing fourth overall. GRE/BAL DIVISION 1 Match 1 - Portsmouth - May 9th: On a beautiful sunny day, Belgrave began their first year in Division 1 of the British Athletic League. Our team was not as strong as we had hoped to start our campaign and we were missing some of our star names. Best performance came from John Gladwin when he towed Seb Coe round to break his own league record in the 800m. In the 'B' race John Booth came within a whisker of winning but nevertheless set a pb of 1.52.77. Our first win in the top Division came from Jay Busk in the 'B' 400m. This was to be our only win of the day but we did sufficiently well to finish in 6th place just behind Blackheath and Shaftsbury but ahead of Newham and Southampton. Andy Aitken, John Wright, Paul Cuff, Akin Thomas, John Booth and Peter Farrell made their BAL debuts. Match 2 - Alexandra Stadium, Birmingham - May 30th: Our second league match did not get off to a good start as the Hammer competition was of an incredibly high standard and both our throwers, Mike and Terry, were really up against it. Our long jumpers were also facing mighty opposition but our undaunted duo, Mike Bazire and John Druce did us proud. Ernest was back in our sprint team and with Marcus and Phil, managed 3 wins and 2 seconds to boost our points. There were also wins for Ken (Discus) and, on his BAL debut, for David Swain who had a fine win in the 1500m. Our 'piece de resistance' came in the 4x400m in the shape of John Regis who devastated the field on the third leg (46.7) to help set a new club record. Great stuff! This followed another club record in the 4x100m of 41.07. Other good performances came from Stu' Paton, Paul Cuff, John Wright, Abi Ekoku, Phil Lovell and Peter (I just made it) Farrell. Ian Bland and Derek Capper made their BAL debuts and it was good to see Alistair Johnson, Greggy, Vince and Derek Brown back in the team. At the end of the day we were a clear fourth in the league having finished just 17 points behind Haringey. Match 3 - Warley - July 4th: Back to the Midlands again and we were determined to hang on to our 4th place. Derrick Williams returned following injury, Marcus and Phil covered the sprints and again got maximum points in three out of five races. What a good example these two young men set. Dave Swain and Stuart Paton got good points in the 1500m with Stu' almost catching Rob Harrison in the closing stages! Phil Lovell again got good points in the Vault supported by Peter Farrell who dashed off after a couple of clearances to see ELO at Wembley! Phil Walker and Barney Gardner made their debuts. Although we scored less points than Match 2, our competitors were also weak and we retained our 4th place in the league with our last match in London. Match 4 - Newham - July 25th: We wrapped up our first BAL campaign in East London knowing that a reasonable result would ensure that we finished in 4th place overall; but boy did we cut it fine! With a reasonable team we suffered a series of disasters and we ended up in 7th place on the day but we did retain our 4th place in the final league table, which was an incredible result in our first year. Phil Goedluck had a fine win in the 200m as did Dave Armstrong in the 'B' 100m. Stuart ran a great 1500m but his partner in the 'B' race, Matt Chaston, was unlucky. Matt was looking good with 200m to go but got tripped and was out of it - his chance will come again. Gareth Allison made his debut and set a Junior club record in the 110mH with a fine 15.56. Simon Maynard put the frighteners on Mike Hayes in the 'chase with a marvellous 9.15.19. Next year Division One look out! items.s: GRE CUP Short report on Belgrave's 1987 GRE Cup second-round match at Norbiton and the semi-final in West London, missed out on the final by three points. GRE CUP 2nd Round - Norbiton: A well balanced team had no real opposition in this second round match. Abi made his debut in the Hammer and promptly retired from the event! See results for some very good performances. Semi-Finals - West London: This semi was likely to be tough without the help of the AAA's. They contrived to hold their Championships at Crystal Palace on the same day. We missed our first final by just three points and many post mortems were held in the following days on how we had missed out. Commiserations to Ken, Stuart, Vince, Mike Bazire, John Wright, Phil Walker, Phil Lovell and the others who did so much - but if only! items.s: ROSENHEIM LEAGUE 1987 Report and match-by-match Belgrave results in the 1987 Rosenheim League, in which Belgrave finished second, one point behind HW in the Final. ROSENHEIM LEAGUE 1987 It was the closest we've come to winning this League yet as we were edged out in the Final by local rivals HW by just one point! Never mind there were some very high standards set in this last match for a supposed low key league with, for example, Felix Sandy running 21.6 and finishing 2nd and Phil Walker running a fine pb for 800m - 1.53.7 - and only in 4th! Heavy points scorers for us during the year were the usual mob - Mike Small, Joe Minetti and Mike Bazire (but we could have done with Joe and Mike B in the Final relay!) Some good 3000's from John Wright, Matt Chaston and, in a surprise turnout, John Gladwin having a time trial with Dave Clarke. Of the younger generation, Freddie Ocrah sprinted to some fast times for a 'Boy', equalling the club record over 200m, while Richard Blick showed middle distance promise. Not quite so young Alan Painter set a club Veterans best over 800m in Match 5. Gladwin won't be 40 'til 2003 Alan so you might hold on to that one for a while! items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS - BATTERSEA PARK Reports and results of the 1987 Centenary club track and field championships at Battersea Park: the 5000m (15 June), 10000m (13 July) and main championships (11 July) for seniors, juniors, youths, boys and colts. CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS - BATTERSEA PARK 5000 METRES - 15 JUNE: Marcello Bizio quickly took Nigel Clark clear of John Mather and Don Anderson while Frank Ward dawdled through the opening laps at the rear of the field. Nigel faded from halfway as Frank made smooth progress to join Marcello with a couple of laps left and the writing looked on the wall for the man from Italy. Frank edged ahead in the final home straight but in an eyeballs out last 50 metres Marcello just got back up to win by the smallest of margins. In an equally gutsy battle John held off Don for third. 1 M Bizio 15.35.0; 2 F Ward 15.35.3; 3 J Mather 15.42.9; 4 D Anderson 15.45.6; 5 N Clarke 16.07.0;L O'Hara,A Stone,L Coy nt 10000 METRES - 13 JULY: Frank Ward again started slowly but this time had enough in hand to pull back the men ahead. Pete Sanders, in his first track season, had a promising run in 3rd. 1 F Ward 32.01.0, 2 M Head 32.35.5, 3 P Sanders 32.43.4, 4 T Williams 34.30, 5 A Stone 35.06, 6 D Anderson 35.49.7, 7 L Coy 36.47.1, 8 C Chaston 37.31.7, 9 L Mann 39.55.5. MAIN CHAMPIONSHIPS - 11 JULY: A glorious day for our Centenary Championships was matched by some excellent performances, with heats necessary in many events. Newcomer Lenny Paul did the double in the 100m and 200m. Paul Cuff and Jay Busk had a head to head in the 400m with Paul just getting the verdict. Stuart Paton front ran the 800m and paced the 1500m to enable Matt Chaston to dip well under 4 minutes. In the guest events, Ken was 2nd in the Discus and Phil Lovell won the Pole Vault. Mike Small won another Hammer title and Vince beat a motley crew (!) in the Javelin. In the younger age groups, there were good performances from Richard Blick (800/1500) Joe Minetti (100) and Freddie Ocrah (100/200 Boys). The highlight of the day was the re-enactment of an 100 yards race from the turn of the Century. Six likely lads, in appropriate dress gave a fine exhibition of the art of sprinting!! - props provided by Ron Wyld and Brian Pritchard. There was a disputed finish - if only they had had photo finish equipment in 1887!
