items.s: EVENT ROUND UP OF INDIVIDUAL PERFORMANCES Event-by-event review of Belgrave athletes' individual performances in 1987 (sprints, John Regis's World Championships 200m bronze, middle and long distance, hurdles, jumps and throws). EVENT ROUND UP OF INDIVIDUAL PERFORMANCES 100m Our sprinters were outstanding in 1987. Over 100m we had the sight of two of our men making the final of the AAAs and although it was Ernie Obeng who had collected the fastest semi final time (10.26) John Regis was first Bel across the line, collecting the Silver Medal and a pb of 10.37, ahead of not only our own number one for the past decade but also Wells and McFarlane. Only the American Dwayne Evans could edge out our rising star. In a blanket finish, Ernie was 5th in 10.41. John also finished ahead of Ernie, 10.45 to 10.56, when they took 4th and 5th in the Dairy Crest Games later in the season but timewise it was Ernie who had the fastest clockings. In addition to that 10.26 he had a 10.29 in Budapest and a remarkable 10.14 with marginal wind assistance when 2nd to Christie in the BR Sprint Trophy at Portsmouth in June. That's Ernie's fastest ever discounting a 10.1 manual timing. Earlier that day, Ernie had filled the same position in 10.30 for England v Czechoslovakia and Italy while in July Ernie was 3rd for England v USA in 10.38 and in August, 3rd at the IAC Meet in 10.39 for another couple of quality performances. Our next fastest man was Sierra Leone International Felix Sandy who had signed membership after the Commonwealth Games last season. Felix spent most of the year in the USA where we understand he recorded a best of 10.38. Our leading Junior, Marcus Adam, had a spectacular season. Over this distance he was 3rd in the UK's, 2nd in the BR Junior Sprint Trophy in 10.44w, had a fine win in the AAA's Juniors over Jamie Henderson, took 5th in the European Juniors, after collecting the club record from John Regis in the heats with 10.46, and won for GB Juniors against West Germany and Poland in 10.48. But perhaps Marcus' best 100 was his storming last leg to bring the GB Junior 4x100m team into the Gold medal position to beat FRG by one hundredth in the European Junior Championships. He had to do that of course to complete a Belgrave hat-trick of Junior Championship relay Golds! Phil Goedluck found fewer top quality opportunities in his first Senior year but he was 6th in the UK's and in the BR Sprint Trophy (10.47w) and ran a seasons legal best 10.58 in the AAA's making the semi final amid hot competition. Joe Minetti won the Surrey Junior title and reduced his best to 10.8 while Mike Bazire, Dave Armstrong and Len Paul - a new member who trains with Dave and is a member of the British Bobsleigh Squad - were also under 11 seconds. And to follow in the footsteps of these, a young man showing much promise is Freddie Ocrah who ran a club best (manual timing) for a 'Boy' with 11.7. 200m John Regis commenced the season with a series of moderate runs by his standards while rounding into shape after injury and the first sign of the form to come was shown when he duffed up Derek Redmond over 300m in late July. That preceded John's brilliant run in the AAA's Championship where he just held on to an early dip to outlean the fast finishing Dwayne Evans in the astonishing time for Crystal Palace of 20.25 - a CBP and UK All Comers Record. That assured him of selection for the World Championships and three more 200's - 20.54 2nd to Jefferson at the IAC meet - 20.50 4th in Zurich - 20.78 2nd to Christie at the Dairy Crest - put the finishing touches on his preparations for what turned out to be our individual highlight of the year! In ideal conditions in the 1960 Olympic Stadium, John sailed through the heats and semis getting progressively faster (Hts 1st 20.76, Rd2 3rd 20.60, Sf 1st 20.54) to take his place alongside the World's elite for the final. Let's allow Ron Pickering's TV commentary to pick up the story as the gun goes for a remarkable race. "No problems with the start, Da Silva has gone off well, John Regis has closed down on Floyd Heard, John Regis is running a superb bend, John Regis is coming off the bend and Krylov in the red shirt, Regis and Da Silva, Regis is there and left Floyd Heard, Heard is coming back, John Regis hanging on, its going to be very close and John Regis is going to get there, John Regis gets there!" If only Ron had been right! Reviewing the slow motion replay, the commentator recovered from his excitement... "In the early part of the race, John Regis destroyed Floyd Heard's chances of this race, he runs a magnificent bend, he also does Da Silva of Brazil another of the close favourites. Krylov is fighting Queneherve in the blue and white and Calvin Smith has the terrific finish. John Regis has a magnificent three quarters of the race and look at his chest forward, if he could just duck like Jon Ridgeon then he may have made it but Calvin Smith is the fast finisher on this side. What a superb run from the 20 year old, whatever medal he gets it has been magnificent. His concentration never deserted him. What he's done to World class American, Brazilian and Canadian sprinters here is no man's business and they were into a breeze against of .49 all the way down that long straight so that's an incredible time." It certainly was. When the photo finish had been sorted out John had collected the Bronze medal in a new UK record - the first Senior UK record in track and field to be held by a Belgravian. 1. Smith (USA) 20.16; 2. Queneherve (France) 20.16; 3. John Regis 20.18; 4. Da Silva (Bra) 20.22; 5. Krylov (USSR) 20.35; 6. Heard (USA) 20.25; 7. Pavoni (Ita) 20.49; Mahorn (Can) 20.78. And lets hear from John's TV interview also as he talks almost as well as he runs! "... I dipped again too early but hopefully for next year I'll be able to rectify that. I wanted that line to be there so badly, I saw the dotted line so I thought dip now but again as I said that's about 10 metres before the actual line is so I was dipping way before I should have - that's what basically lost me the race but in saying that I've got to be pleased now, I've got the British record, ranked number one, so it's been a great World Championships for me really... I was drawn in lane 2 which wasn't necessarily a good draw for me; I had Robson Da Silva and Floyd Heard outside me so I just powered round the turn and then coming onto the straight I just concentrated on the finishing line, making sure of my high knee lift and just trying to keep form basically. But I knew the other guys would be coming on me slowly and slowly and as you can see there they're beginning to pick me up and unfortunately I start dipping 'there' which just cost me the gold medal but even so I'm pleased with my performance today ... With guys like Floyd Heard and Robson Da Silva who I've raced three times previously and never beaten and to beat them on an occasion like this has just been a Godsend to me really. I couldn't have predicted that I'd get in the top three but in saying that I've trained hard, worked hard with my coach, come back from injury and now I'm in effect the third best in the World at this moment." You certainly are John and well done from all of us at Belgrave. While John nearly conquered the rest of the World, Marcus Adam absolutely conquered the rest of Europe's Juniors at this distance when he was in blistering form at a damp Alexander Stadium, Birmingham in August. A time of 20.92 in the heats followed by 20.95 in the final was more than the rest could handle and taking a title previously won by Valeriy Borzov was pretty fair compensation for missing a medal over 100m earlier in the week. Marcus was in fact undefeated in all his Junior races over 200m. There were International wins for GB Juniors v West Germany and Poland (21.00) for The England Under 23's in Norway (21.26) and retention of his AAA Under 20 title in 21.30. But that emphatic European title was the one Marcus will savour. Unbeknown to many, Felix Sandy was a second Belgravian selected for the World Championships at 200m. Felix represented Sierra Leone and placed 6th in his heat in 21.67. Making it a great year at 200, we also had Joe Minetti winning the Surrey Junior title, Mike Bazire the Sussex Title also placing 4th in the Inter Counties, and Freddie Ocrah equalling the Boys Club record! 400m New member Paul Cuff from New Zealand was our No. 1 with solid 48's through the season. Jay Busk was also under 49 a couple of times, placing 2nd in the Wilts County Champs and representing his County while Mike Bazire was inside 50 for the first time and took 3rd in the Sussex Champs. Mike Alleyne ran a 49 in May but was injured most of the season. Good progress was made by a number of youngsters at this distance, notably Steven Garcia, Alistair Grant and Adrian Ross. 800m John Gladwin won the UK Championships at this distance before a pelvic problem affected the heart of his season. John did however run a series of 1.46's and came back to run one of his best ever 800's at the IAC Meeting in August where he was a fast finishing 3rd ahead of the eventual World Silver medallist and the reigning Olympic Champion. Stuart Paton was an easy winner of the Surrey 800, took silver in the Southern Championships and was twice under 1.50 while John Booth made a fine early season breakthrough winning the Surrey Juniors (with Graham Adams in 2nd) and running 1.52. Phil Walker and Andy Moore were inside 1.54 and 17 Bels were under 2 minutes. 1500m/Mile It was sad to see John Gladwin unable to produce his best form in time to gain World Championship selection. However, a philosophical John was not displeased to have come through to 3rd in the AAA's in all the circumstances. Fortunately he shook off his injury sufficiently to have a great run in Zurich where he so very nearly pulled back Bile over the mile, recording 3.51.02 (a run that must give food for thought in view of what followed in Rome) and he followed up with Mile wins at the Dairy Crest meet (with Gary Staines in 5th) and in Munich. In the Welsh Championships, Justin Chaston won the Junior title while brother Matt placed 4th in the Senior event, both significantly improving their best times during the season. Dave Swain became our 4th fastest ever 1500m runner with a 3.40.95 at the Rome Grand Prix while Glynn Tiernan was runner up in the Surrey Juniors. 3000m/5000m No sooner had the season started than we learned of Dave Swain's clearance for membership and the first club record of the season had fallen as Dave had chased home Sydney Maree in Philadelphia on 11 April in the fine time of 13.37.8 to remove Eire International Gerry Deegan from the record books. (That will please those members who preferred to recognise Geoff North as our record holder because Deegan never actually ran for the club. He was a paid up member for a year or so though). Back home Dave guested at the Portsmouth International meeting in June with a 3rd place in 13.58.43 and then collected his second club record with a 7.57.60 3000m at the Peugeot Talbot Games on 10 July before setting out for the World Student Games in Zagreb as Britain's only representative in the 5000m. Sadly he was unable to produce his best form there but he did collect the bronze medal. Meanwhile news had filtered through of a 13.45 debut 5000m from Gary Staines down under in Australia where Gary had been spending about 6 months at the Canberra Athletic Institute. A scientific diet under their advice to bring his weight down to around 9 and a half stones and his engagement to Long Jumper Nicole Boegman were two factors obviously doing him no harm. Gary returned home in July and our first view of him in action confirmed the point. Showing his best ever form at any distance Gary had a superb win over a classy 2 miles field at Gateshead, taking the notable scalp of Buckner, for another club best of 8.30.09. That was a week prior to running another blinder in the AAA's 5000m to take the silver medal, beaten only by a resurging European Champion. The club record had fallen again to 13.30.53 but the previous holder didn't go too badly himself as 16 seconds behind Gary came Dave in 12th place. These two then reduced their best 2 mile times; Gary to 8.26.15 at the IAC meeting and Dave to 8.33.92 at the Dairy Crest Games. Dave then called it a day for major competition but Gary was still rounding to a peak and took himself right into the reckoning for an Olympic Games place next year with a brilliant 13.20.00 at Crystal Palace in September with again only Buckner in front. We knew Gary would go well when he moved up from 1500's but that sort of time was remarkable - only a few seconds faster in their whole careers were such household names as Foster and Bedford! Not neglecting a 'workout' at a shorter distance, Gary then took a 4th place over 2000m in Lausanne beating a host of International stars in another fast time (4.53.69) having gone through 4 laps in 3.55! Gary returns to 'Oz' in February for a short period and all we can say is let's have more of the same next Summer Sport! 10000m There were few runs of note over this distance but in the improving John Wright we had the Southern Counties bronze medallist and in Kiwi Daryl Fantham the Surrey County 3rd placer. 3000mSc Illness curtailed Mark Sinclair's season but he had time to retain his County title with our only sub 9. Mike Hayes also had a quiet year but Simon Maynard made good progress. Hurdles Gareth Allison became our fastest ever Junior High Hurdler in the last BAL match while Alistair Grant smashed the Youths 400mH record with 57.7 in the Public Schools Championships in Birmingham. We watch their progress with interest. Of the Seniors, over one lap, Ian Bland ploughed a somewhat lone furrow for us, his fastest being 54.51 in the Southern Championships. Tony Pamah was absent all season and Chris Knight was injured after a promising 3rd place in the Surrey Championships. But was that really John Regis who ran 24.0 for 200mH at Thurrock in September? Watch out Ed Moses! Jumps Chris Cornwell equalled the club High Jump record with 2.00 in the GRE Cup while Phil Lovell's best pole vault result came with another 2nd place in the Southern Counties. Derek Brown was injured much of the season but went over 15 metres for a fine Triple Jump 4th place in the Inter Counties Championships and placed 6th in the 'Southern'. Throws Abi Ekoku made good progress this year. In the Shot he placed 8th in the 'UKs' and 6th at the Pearl Invitation meet at Gateshead before breaking through the 16 metre line for a fine new club record at a Southern Counties match in August. With the Discus Abi was 7th in the 'UKs', 4th in the 'Southern' and 8th in the AAA's. He had a fine best throw of 53.42 and certainly kept Ken Onuaguluchi on his toes all season. Abi also made his International debut for an England Under 23 team against Belgium and Norway, placing 3rd with 52.42. Ken spun the plate out to 53 a few times but was slightly down in distance on previous seasons. Nevertheless he was among the medals with 2nd places in both the Inter Counties and Southern Championships while his best shot came Indoors at the IAC Shot Day at Crystal Palace as early as February - a fine pb of 15.78. A new name at the backend of the year was Nigel Bevan, one of the country's leading Javelin throwers, who became a member on 17 August and five days after that set new club figures for a Senior and Junior with 71.66 representing Southern Counties in Norway. That throw was with the new Javelin and superseded our previous best with the old model by a healthy 4 metres. That's some performance and we look forward to seeing Nigel in Claret and Gold next season. items.s: McVitie's Gold Challenge 25 x 1 Mile Relay. Report (from an APA press release) of Gary Staines running a solo sub-four-minute final mile for Belgrave in the McVitie's Gold Challenge 25 x 1 mile relay at Battersea Park on 4 October 1987, with photos of the A team runners. McVitie's Gold Challenge 25 x 1 Mile Relay. THE WORLD'S FIRST SOLO SUB-FOUR MINUTE MILE IS ACHIEVED IN McVITIE'S CHALLENGE Running the final stage for his club, Belgrave Harriers, in the McVities Gold Challenge 25 x 1 mile Relay on Sunday 4th October, Gary Staines set the fastest individual time of the day, emphatically breaking the four minute barrier in 3mins 59sec. Staines, the AAA 5,000 metres silver medallist earlier this year, thus became the first sub four-minute miler in this kind of race, and since he ran unopposed around the Battersea Park Track, the first recorded sub-four minute mile solo in a properly organised race (Reprint from APA press release). The photographs on the following two pages show all the club's "A" team runners although not all of the take-overs were photographed.- L.to R. They are in takeover order and identifiable by the numbers in Result Sheet. Gary Staines finishing the final stage of the 25 x 1 mile Relay. Gary Staines Gary Staines fastest individual time of the day, 3:59 solo final stage mile; AAA 5000m silver medallist 1987 Gary Staines Staines McVitie's Gold Challenge 25 x 1 Mile Relay AAA Championships Battersea Park

items.s: 4 October 1987 - McVITIES GOLD CHALLENGE 25 x 1 MILE RELAY Result sheet for the McVitie's Gold Challenge 25 x 1 mile relay of 4 October 1987: national result (Belgrave 3rd), fastest individuals, the Belgrave A, B, Young Athletes and Ladies team times, and notes on fund raising for Belgrave Hall's boiler and organising the Battersea Park venue, with a page of photos of the relay organisers and officials. 4 October 1987 - McVITIES GOLD CHALLENGE 25 x 1 MILE RELAY "McVities" took over from "Nike" in sponsoring this year's 25 x 1 mile relay and our usual venue of Crystal Palace was transferred to Battersea Park. Following the demise of the gas boiler at Belgrave Hall this race was seen as a good means of fund raising for the replacement. The "A" team put in a splendid performance - finishing 1st in the Battersea Park race and 3rd in the overall National event and earning £800 for funds. Club patron, Mr Eddie Kulukundis, agreed with a wonderful gesture, to double the amount. Star of the day was Gary Staines who was the only person throughout the country to dip under 4 minutes. John Wright was second fastest Belgravian with 4 min 20 secs. Four teams finished at the Battersea park race and some unfamiliar names were recorded on an excellent day for the club. Leo Coy This 25 x 1 mile relay sponsored by McVities was promoted nationally by Alan Pascoe Associates who delegated local clubs to organise the event at 10 various venue. Belgrave Harriers were allocated Battersea Park and Leo Coy was saddled with the unenviable task of piloting the event through its tortuous channels and with the aid of such die-hards as Harry Porter, Brian Pritchard,Clive Shippen,who on the day of the race had to contend with such things as the non-arrival of a marquee and technical things as a public address system and converting a 400 metre lap track to 440 yards, they produced the goods in an absolutely first class show. items.s: VETS CORNER Veterans' column on the 1987 season: club records by Alan Painter, Dave Mole and Leo Coy, Snowy Brooks' championship medals and world indoor pentathlon best, Laurie O'Hara, Phil Smith and Tony Stone, with road race results. VETS CORNER Alan Painter and Dave Mole were new Vets this track season and both set club records. Alan ran 1.59.9 for 800m on his 40th Birthday, reducing that time to 1.59.1 in a Rosenheim League match. He won the Southern Counties 800m and an Inter Area representative match by wide margins, collected three Vets AC titles and placed 6th in the National Championships. Dave, who was a leading National Junior with the Javelin in 1966 (67.44m) threw 47.68 with the new model implement in a Southern League match which was further than our previous best with the old spear. Another record fell to Leo Coy in the 2000m Steeplechase. Snowy Brooks is now moving to the upper end of the 1A Group but he still likes collecting those Championship medals. Southern Bronze in the Javelin, National Silver in the 110mH and Bronze in the Long Jump were added this year. Snowy also equalled his own Vets Pole Vault mark of 3.20 in the last Southern League match. Indoor results received too late for the last edition showed Snowy to have raised his World Indoor best Pentathlon mark to 2814 (60H 9.2; LJ 6.01; SP 11.52; HJ 1.65; 1000m 3.13.2) to win the British Vets Champs with separate Silvers over 60mH and in the Long Jump. Snowy's just a lad of course alongside Laurie O'Hara who moved into the 2B Group this year. Laurie was 2nd in the Vets AC 10000m Champs (1st 0/50) and ran 16.21 in a Southern League match still twinkling round the last lap like a 20 year old. Laurie also ran a 4.24 1500m and was first 0/50 man home in the Vets AC 1500m. Another new Vet this year, Phil Smith ran 12.5 (100m) and 56.5 (400m) before getting crocked while Tony Stone continues to improve at the age of 46 with a good run in the Club 5000m being his best performance, together with the Vets AC 0/45 title at the same distance. items.s: Editor's note that Alan Jerman, listed in Steve Williams' 5¾ mile road run table, was Belgrave's first fatality of World War II, serving as an RAF air gunner. In Steve Williams' 5¾mile Road Run Table the name of Alan Jerman occurs next to last with a date of Mar. 40. With the maxim of "Lest we forget" in mind I would mention that Alan Jerman was unfortunately Belgrave Harriers' first fatality in World War II. He was serving in the RAF as an Air Gunner. See page 43. J.G.C. items.h: ALL TIME TOP 100 INDIVIDUALS OVER THE 'FIVE AND THREE QUARTERS'
items.sum: Steve Williams' history of the club's 5 3/4 mile road course race since 1929, with the all-time list of its fastest men headed by Geoff North's 27.14 of April 1966 (billed as the top 100; 101 names are printed).
items.s: ALL TIME TOP 100 INDIVIDUALS OVER THE 'FIVE AND THREE QUARTERS' Steve Williams' history of the club's 5 3/4 mile road course race since 1929, with the all-time list of its fastest men headed by Geoff North's 27.14 of April 1966 (billed as the top 100; 101 names are printed). ALL TIME TOP 100 INDIVIDUALS OVER THE 'FIVE AND THREE QUARTERS' As promised in the October 1985 edition of the magazine here are the 100 fastest men round our long established 5 3/4 mile road course; one man for each of our hundred years. Virtually anybody who's been anybody in the way of Belgrave distance running is on the list and no doubt some of the names will evoke many memories for our older members. I believe the compilation to be accurate even though some results over the years were either not fully reported or omitted from the 'Belgravian' but let me know if you have any queries. The first race was held as long ago as 23 March 1929 and the 'Belgravian' of the time tells how it came about. "In view of the London to Brighton Relay, the committee decided to stage a time trial on the road a fortnight before, in order to assist in selecting the team. As the stages of the relay vary from 4 1/2 to 6 1/2 miles approximately, the trial was run over a course at Wimbledon covering a little more than 5 miles representing about the mean distance. The course was the same as is now used by the Walking Section consisting of two 1 mile laps of the Common then down Copse Hill, Coombe Lane and back via Cambridge Road, finishing with another lap of the Common; a very suitable course containing a few hills and mostly good surfaces, similar to those on the Brighton Road." Interestingly, the runners for this first race were despatched singly at 15 second intervals, the order of starting having been drawn for, with the object of simulating as near relay conditions as possible. Twelve men completed the race with T J Flower fastest in 31.27. The following year the 'yacht' start was abandoned for a straight race while a sealed handicap was held in conjunction and the winning time came down to 29.46 which was very respectable for 1930. A year later the winner was one Arthur Penny in 30.16 while the 'Belgravian' reports that "Carter again showed that he is a distinct acquisition and his forward running gained him second prize in the handicap". "Carter", of course, was 'our Tom' then a novice! It's marvellous to be able to record, 56 years later, that these two stalwarts are still very much part of the Belgrave scene. In the next three years Arthur Allum completed a hat-trick while Bert Footer took the record to 29.30 in 1935. The 'Belgravian' report that year captured the finish of the race in the style of prose of the day like this. "Carter leads Footer by a yard at the top of Copse Hill and they stride up the steep incline like horses with no sign of fatigue.... Round the triangle they go.... In this space, Footer managed to get 50 yards away from Carter and win. We looked for the winners usual smile but alas! even the group of charming ladies at the winning post could not inspire the dull dog to cast a little sunshine on the scene!" The 1937 race was run over a shortened course and the times are therefore not relevant but the 'Belgravian' congratulated Ted Stimpson "for his fine stylish run" and W E Lucas, "who won the handicap in splendid fashion." Both men were of course destined for International honours. Arthur Penny reclaimed the race in 1938 in a new record and Tom Carter gained his sole success the following year after having been three times a runner up previously. Later that year saw the outbreak of war but one more race was possible in 1940 before the number of members called to the service of their country caused a necessary curtailment to the full programme of club activity. Len Herbert, another International, won, shaving a second off the record. When the race resumed in 1947, standards were lower because of lack of training in the preceding years but Ted Stimpson brought back respectability the following year, winning in 29.33. In 1949 the first two men home, Vernon Blowfield and Jack Brown went slightly off course and were effectively disqualified but Verne took the record down to 29.09 in 1950, and following the cancellation of the 1952 race through snow bound roads, Ray Tooby opened up the 28 minute era with 28.50 in 1953. But 1954 was to see what might still be regarded as the most remarkable feat of running on the course when Ron Linstead, only just 18 years old, smashed that time with 28.24. Ron was too young to gain selection for the 'Brighton' but a sign of the quality of his run was that the men behind him went on to place 2nd in the National relay. Unfortunately Ron never improved on that time but even now there are few who have beaten it. In October that same year it was decided to hold a second annual race over the course to assist with selection for the newly introduced October London to Brighton Relay which initiated a championship for 'Southern' clubs. Once more a short course was used for this first 'Autumnal' race. Four and a half years then passed before Pat Newell took the record to 28.21 and, in March 1960, 28 minutes was beaten for the first time by our regular correspondent and visitor, Ranjit Bhatia, who showed the form which was to take him to the Rome Olympics, with 27.56. Ranjit's time was astonishing to club members then but only two years later another man at the peak of his powers was to go over 200 yards faster. Gerry North was just two weeks away from winning the National Cross Country title and in superb shape. He smashed the record with 27.15 over two minutes ahead of the next man, Charlie Walker, causing the 'Belgravian' reporter to question "How many of our older runners ever dreamt they'd see the approach of 27 minutes on this course?". Gerry was in fact still (just) a first claim member of Blackpool at the time but it would be pedantic not to count his best time in the list below as he was to become one of the great Belgravians. The Junior record was taken to a fast 28.01 by Tony Fairclough in March 1964 behind one of Bill Kerr's four wins while 1965 saw the first of Laurie O'Hara's record six wins (four in the March race). Then in 1966 the present record was set. Geoff North was known to be going for his elder brother's time and the 'Belgravian' reports he was so on edge that when it was suggested to Geoff that he might like someone to knock in some starting blocks it failed to raise even the merest smile! "No sooner had Bob Taylor's starting arm dropped than Geoff was clear of the field ... Geoff kept his form well on the homeward run and a 'break it or bust' sprint down the finishing straight sent up an ooh! from the watchers that momentarily did not indicate which side of the record his time was. Relief all round (Gerry wasn't there) as it was announced that Geoff had beaten the record by just ONE SECOND!". The following years saw many a pitch battle between the evenly matched runners who formed the backbone of our successful teams of the late 60's and early 70's but only three or four runs, from Geoff and Gerry and Bill Weller approached the record in that time. However two 'age' records fell in the 70's - to Junior Bill Curtin with 28.00 in 1971 and Veteran Laurie O'Hara with 27.40 in 1973. In the mid 70's, John Stow ran up a record four consecutive wins with Oliver Foote taking three on the trot in 82/83; but very few Bels of the 80's have intervened at the sharp end of the list, only John Wright having made the top ten with an impressive solo 27.44 last March. So we await the day when Gladwin, Staines, Swain and company might, in the not too distant future, set seriously about this race and take us below 27 minutes! It would be nice to see! In the meantime, imagine this lot below all gathered at the end of Lauriston Road for the same race. Getting a good team out for the relays would be easy! items.s: ROAD RACE ROUND UP Round-up of Belgrave road running from late 1986 to January 1988, with Martyn Head named Road Section Secretary, Gary Staines' wins on the Continent, team results and full club results from races including the London Marathon, Hogs Back and City 10 Miles. ROAD RACE ROUND UP The odd success is coming the way of the road runners as efforts are being made to consolidate our entries for open races and word is spread of who is doing what! However communications still need improving if we are to do ourselves justice. There are so many races available these days that we should regularly be able to pick up some team prizes. It doesn't even need our very best men to be involved although we still look to them for a lead. A word in the right ear could enable us to get the back up brigade to join in and everyone could benefit. The guys running down the field will make that much more of an effort if they know there's something in it at the end. Martyn Head is your new Section Secretary. Contact him on [phone number withheld]. Two successes missed the boat for the last edition. These were the win in the City of London 10 Miles, where Don Anderson in 5th was a late entry non scorer, and in the Alton 10 Miles where Martin Lake, who was the holder, led the team home in 2nd place this time. In the Fleet Half Marathon, John Wright was representing the Army and didn't score for us but he finished 10th in a fast time with some respectable running behind from our team which placed 8th. Best performance in the London Marathon came from Canadian Peter Anthony who moves into 25th place in the club all time list with his time. Another prominent showing came from Dave North with a 2nd place in the Portsmouth 10 Miles in May in 54.22. Must have been tough, long or both Dave! Some of the best performances of the late Summer came in the breakthrough of 1984 Olympic cyclist Peter Sanders as you can see from the results below. Pete has now completed his first year as a runner and he looks to have plenty of potential. When he lined up alongside John Wright in the Brighton 6, there was a good chance of high placings from the pair and thats how it turned out, with John winning in 30.03 and Pete in 3rd. Unfortunately there was no back up for what would have been an easy team prize. 25.12.86 Lauriston Paarlauf: 1 J Gladwin & A Gayton 6m 909y 2 F Ward & M Peace(Ran) 6m 691y 3 M Riley & A Painter 6m 617y 4 P Sanders & J Bicourt 6m 548y 6 J Booth & S Williams 6m 436y Other good performances in the second half of the year have come from Martin Lake, 3rd in the Wimbledon Half Marathon and Dave North one place behind but running for his firm and not counting for our team which finished 3rd. Richard Pearson collected the Club marathon title in the Poly Marathon where he was first Veteran home. Gary Staines has continued his Summer track form into a Winter road season on the Continent in sensational fashion. On 11 October he was 2nd over 7.6km in Furth (WG) in a time of 20.21 and 16 days later smashed a World class field over 10km in Rennes (Fra) in 28.28. Koskei, Rousseau and Nyambui being just some of the names behind him. Then on 29 November he beat another International line up over a 7.4 mile course in Madrid in 32.55.58. That's an average of 4.27 per mile! On the same weekend that Gary was winning in Madrid, John Wright won the Basingstoke '6' in 29.41 and Stuart Paton won a 5 miler in Epsom nearly 2 minutes clear of the field which included Chris items.s: Young Athletes Report Jim and Dave Mote's report on the 1987 young athletes' league season (Belgrave 8th of 17 in the South Central Division), match by match with Belgrave winners and scores, plus a note on the Belgrave Thameside League for Colts and Boys. Young Athletes Report by Jim and Dave Mote Out came the Wellingtons, Waterproofs and Umbrellas. In went the Sun. Yes it was the summer season again. The 1987 Young Athletes season started with the traditional enthusiasm and expectation. Cross-Country runners chipped the dried mud from their spikes and the sprinters blew the cobwebs off theirs. All prepared for the season's first engagement at Tooting Bec. 3rd MAY 1987 TOOTING BEC Dark clouds greeted us at Tooting Bec and it was not long before the new centenary umbrellas were in use and greatly appreciated by all who huddled under them. It was good to see some new faces mingling with the stalwarts from last year but a head count soon showed that our Boys and Youths teams were far from strong in numbers and the Colts section was almost non-existent. Nevertheless everyone competed with great enthusiasm and after a long wet afternoon the fine efforts of our team were eventually beaten by the superior numbers of the athletes from the recently amalgamated Swale Combined Club. We managed to stay ahead of our South London rivals Herne Hill but sadly missed our Youth sprinters. Winners for Belgrave. Once again we were pipped at the post by a team that could field more athletes on the day. Our faithful nucleus ran, jumped and threw with great gusto but were beaten by the numerical superiority of Kingston and Polytechnic Harriers. Winners for Belgrave. Youths A Grant 400m Hurdles (A) 100m Hurdles (A), M Bowers 1500m (A), R Blick 1500m (B), N Khan 800m (B) 4 x 400m Relay. Boys S Abbeysinger 200m (B) 800m (A) Highjump (A) G Bage 1500m (A), M Loftus 400m (A), D Cooper 400m (B) B Khan 3000m (B), G Dorrell Hammer (A) Shot (A) Discus (B) S Affleck Triple Jump (B), W Chu Discus (A) 4 x 400m Relay Colts M Pettigrew 1500 (B) Final Result Kingston & Poly 154, Belgrave 147, Hastings 83, Tonbridge 37 7th JUNE 1987 DARTFORD On another dull threatening day we set off by coach to Dartford with a team which this time had only five youths and one Colt but our spirits were high and an impromptu game of cricket preceded the athletic match. Unfortunately our lack of numbers again made the match an uphill task from the very beginning but once again enthusiasm countered these problems and once again we finished second. An added bonus was the fact that the rain which threatened us all the afternoon never materialised and there was an air of satisfaction amongst the tired athletes on the journey home. Winners from Belgrave Youths A Grant 400m Hurdles (A) 100m Hurdles (A) Boys S Affleck Triple Jump (B), S Herbert High Jump (A) B Khan Long Jump (B), J Harris 100m Hurdles (A) 4 x 100m Relay Colts M Loden 1500m (A) Final Result Invicta 255, Belgrave 117, Ashford 87 28th JUNE 1987 HORSHAM The sun came out! So shocked were the team that only 10 athletes turned out. Outnumbered by Belgrave parents, coaches, officials and other sundry supporters and not to mention the other teams, our athletes manfully battled against insurmountable odds. Just to add to our problems the three teams we were opposing were Bexley and E Grinstead who were at that time first and second in the league and Horsham who were the host club. Apparently we were hit by the holiday season (not applicable to our opponents) and our results reflected the depleted nature of the team. But we all came home with a lovely sun-tan! Our only individual winner was S Abbeysinger in the Boys High Jump (B). Final Result (1) E Grinstead 268 (2) Bexley 2445 (3) Horsham 90 (4) Belgrave 58 26th JULY 1987 TOOTING BEC Our final match on a fine afternoon gave us our best team in numbers of the whole season but still it was not strong enough. Our close rivals Hercules Wimbledon and Surrey Beagles had even bigger teams and after H.W. had taken a commanding lead early on we engaged in a close battle with Surrey Beagles for second place before losing our grip when our athletes had competed in their maximum number of events and left the Beagles to pick up the spare points. For the first time this season we had competitors in the Youth sprints but still failed to field a sprint relay team. Winners for Belgrave Youths A Grant 400m (A), R Blick 1500m (A) 1500m S/C (A) J Coy 1500m (B), M Egericx 3000m (A), J French 100m (B) Final Result Hercules Wimbledon 217, Surrey Beagles 149 Belgrave 121, Redhill 19 Seventeen teams competed in our South Central Division and Belgrave finished 8th. It has been a hit and definitely miss season in which the consistent nucleus has performed with commendable enthusiasm and enjoyed their individual achievements. Unfortunately some of our talented athletes have been unable to attend on many occasions for various legitimate reasons and this is where our weakness lies Baba and Nadu Khan, Dan Winson, John Coy (Team Captain) and Michael Bowers competed in every match and I would like to thank them for their unswerving loyalty. In reporting the matches above I note that Dan Winson does not appear as a winner at any time but he is a winner in a different because he was always there always finished and always scored valuable points - well done Dan!! Another special mention goes to Michael Bowers our up and coming middle distance runner who injured his foot and could not run in the second part of the season - he came along and "shot-putted" instead!! What more can one say?! Think about it lads. You have a great deal of talent. A little more consistency in your appearances and the league could be yours for the taking. And finally many, many thanks to the parents, coaches, officials and would-be officials who supported us (not forgetting the supporters from the ladies section who graced us with their presence on many occasions). Have a good winter season and come back fit and raring to go! Belgrave Thameside League This league was an interesting innovation five years ago when Belgrave decided to provide additional competition for the younger boys in some local clubs. Its development has been quite remarkable with four very competitive meetings taking place over the short athletic season. Our own teams (Colts and Boys) have not been once sucessful in the competition but have enjoyed the opportunity to compete in a league with surprisingly high standards. On average the turn out of Belgrave athletes was better this year and one encouraging aspect was the increase in the number of Colts taking part. Only two arrived for the first match but by the last one our team had grown to eight. Six teams competed in each of the divisions both of which were won by Croydon. Our Boys finished fourth and the Colts were fifth but we have great hopes of improving on this next year. A number of Belgrave officials work very hard to present this competition and must be applauded on the high standard they have achieved. We trust the Belgrave athletes will show their appreciation of these efforts with an even greater and more consistent turn-out next year. Race Walking. BELGRAVIAN WALKING SECTION REPORT by Carl Lawton The summer is past and in certain cases that may be a good thing. As far as some results go it has been disastrous and well worth forgetting but all is not doom and gloom, we have now a rebuilt ladies team which has got what has been lacking in the means section, a desire to be successful, but even that is only dependant on turning out a team. Suzanne Kew has been 'sidelined' during the summer but hopes to be back on the road having sorted out her problem. The Nation 35kms and 50kms failed to close in a team the latter even a finisher. September began to look a little more hopeful with teams in the Woodford and Southend. items.s: WITH THE LADIES Harry Porter's review of the Belgrave ladies' 1987 season: Angela Abrams' Endeavour Cup, Southern multi and relay medals, Rosenheim League and Melbourne Trophy wins, Frances Guy's Centenary Cup, Frank Simmons' recovery, and thanks to helpers. The Ladies. WITH THE LADIES It has been quite an exciting track season, I hope everybody in the 'SECT' has had an exciting centenary one as I've had myself and are looking forward to the '88 summer season. Of the team I would like to see back in competition in '88 are Tracy Denton and Andrea Coore, both out last year, we all missed you and your points. I hope the back and leg hold out OK good luck to both for '88. I would also like to thank Angela Abrams for her enthusiasm, and sportswomen-like attitude and support for the team, Angela holds all four club records for 80/100/200/400/H. Keep it up Angela (it's electric) for this and all the support to the club, you have been awarded the "Endeavour Cup" good luck for '88 (GB vest??) There are numerous individual performances throughout the year Juniors and Seniors as you will see later. But one of the best days for us was when we went down to Bournemouth for the Southern CW AAA multi and relays championships. We came away with a total of (11 Gold) (1 Silver) (8 Bronze) and 5 Club records. Our Juniors relay team won both the 4 x 100 and 4 x 200. I would like to say well done on behalf of the club on doing the sprint double a first for Belgrave ladies, well done. Keep it up. We also won the Rosenheim League final at Tooting Bec on 19th August. This was the first time the ladies teams have taken part, as before it was a mens league only so Belgrave ladies hold the trophy. The mens team just missing the double by about 2 pts? But it was good fun on the night, well done all. It's good to see the ladies and means team getting together more. Also later at the end of the season on 20th September Belgrave were invited to take part in the Melbourne Trophy meeting at Crystal Palace, where 15 teams took part, there were good performances all round so we found ourselves in 3rd place overall. But we did end up first GB club so that itself was very pleasing. With France 1st, Belgium 2nd, Belgrave 3rd, with 12 more GB clubs behind us, we were awarded the 1987 home club Melbourne Trophy for top GB club on the day. Well done all, keep it up, it's there if you wish to use it? But if it's not then you did even better as a certain Mr Frank Simmons would say. On the 4th of October or before we had a full team for the 25x1 mile relay at Battersea but 3 or 4 ladies failed to show on the day so sadly we did not have a scoring team so some had to run 2 legs to record a time to be bettered next year? With a full team I hope. But for me the run of the day was by one of the sprinters (Dez) well what can one say Dezrine a 6m.mile, behind the sub 4m of Gary Staines, yours for me was second to that. Ask poor old Charles Manning I think he is still running (full team for '88 ladies please). We missed out on the day by £350. On 14 November we held the Centenary Dinner at the Gloucester Hotel. At this prestigious occasion the Tommy Green Cup was awarded for the most or best performance by a male athlete, also for the first time was presented a new cup which is named the Centenary Cup to be awarded to the lady for the best performance of the year. The first name on the cup in centenary year is Frances Guy for her win in the Poly Marathon incorporating also the Belgrave Marathon. Well done Frances from the Sec and myself. Just a few words about one of the older Belgravians of the club, he is just what makes the club one of the great ones that it is, we don't have more than 10 or so of them left and we so very nearly lost this one in September. For ten days 90% of him was with all those Bels who have passed on, but 10% said not yet sir, for three weeks he battled on in the intensive care unit. Many younger men would have lost this race but he kept on striding on and won. His willpower and spirit is something to be admired by all who know him, those of you who don't know him or of him his name is Frank Simmons, and Frank I would like to shake your hand and say on behalf of Belgrave Harriers please accept the merit award for willpower you old so-and-so. P.S. To the doctors and nurses at the East Dulwich Hospital I would like to thank you all for your dedication and care on behalf of Frank and myself. Finally I would like to say thank you to all those people who have given the Ladies Section and myself so much help throughout the year and in particular to Derek Jones for organising all the track meetings and all the back-room work that he does (without question or having to be asked) - "Stick with it Derek", to Cynthia and Ray James, Jenny and Chris Christou, Derek Crookes, the club officials and that small band of officials and that small band of officials that regularly turn out. The club needs many more like you so please if you can help in any capacity, qualified or not do come forward. I would like to thank the Club President Bill Lucas and Sheena his wife, for their support, at several of our home and away fixtures - hope to see you again in 1988 season. Well ladies, the section is numerically stronger but we failed Div 1 and 2 in Centenary year. It must be on for 1988 - you have all to get it together and you can. So let's make it a "super" 1 and 3 this year. Well done all those who competed in 1987 - good luck for 1988. items.label: March 1989
items.sum: News from two former members: Bill Spenser, now cycle racing at 70, and Bernard Eglinton, ex-RAF walker writing from Colwyn Bay.
items.s: Correspondence: News from two former members: Bill Spenser, now cycle racing at 70, and Bernard Eglinton, ex-RAF walker writing from Colwyn Bay. BILL SPENSER - Ex Met. Police now retired and living near Bury St. Edmunds was one of our Road Running stalwarts, but writes to say that he got a bit tired of walking around the country lanes so decided to get on his bike. So after a lapse of 50 years and at the age of 70 he has resumed Road Time-Trials Cycle Racing and intends to keep it up until - as he puts it - to the end of the chapter. Last October he cycled to Newmarket to see Stan Davies and sends regards to all and in particular Frank Webb, Norman Dewberry and Arthur Penstone, BERNARD EGLINTON - Ex R.A.F. regular who joined the club as a runner from Derby AC and eventually excelled as a walker and scored in a number of National 50kms and 20mls R.W.A. Championship teams wins for the Bels, writes from his home in Colwyn Bay, Clwyd, N.Wales with Welsh flavoured fervour and sends greetings to all. Bill Spenser BILL SPENSER former road runner, ex Met. Police; resumed road time-trial cycle racing at 70 Stan Davies Stan Davies Frank Webb Frank Webb Norman Dewberry Norman Dewberry Arthur Penstone Arthur Penstone Bernard Eglinton BERNARD EGLINTON ex R.A.F.; joined from Derby AC as a runner, scored in National 50km and 20 miles R.W.A. championship team wins as a walker R.W.A. items.s: STOP PRESS - WORLD CHAMPION Stop-press note that John Regis won the World Indoor 200m in Budapest in a record 20.54 secs and will be Track and Field Captain. JOHN REGIS bounced back to his best form when he won the World Indoor 200m with a record 20.54 secs. at Budapest on 4th March. His win was Britain's first and so far only victory in these World Indoor Championships and augurs well for the summer. John has agreed to be Track and Field Captain this season! John Regis JOHN REGIS won World Indoor 200m in record 20.54 secs, Budapest, 4 March 1989; Track and Field Captain JOHN REGIS John World Indoor Championships Budapest

items.sum: Profile welcoming junior middle-distance runner Matthew Stickles to Belgrave, with his record and personal bests.
items.s: WELCOME TO MATTHEW STICKLES Profile welcoming junior middle-distance runner Matthew Stickles to Belgrave, with his record and personal bests. With fine performances in the Surrey League and Junior Southern C.C. Championship Matthew Stickles has shown what a fine addition he is to Belgrave's middle distance ranks. Born in February 1969, Matthew is still a junior in the Country in the UK, but is too old now to compeete as an International under the different International age groupings. He started running at the age of 12 and has performed with distinction at all age groups. In 1987 he was 3rd in the Junior AAA's 3000m in a p.b. of 8.18 and gained his first GB Junior vest as a result when he ran 8.20 in a W.Germany & Swiss triangular match. He came third in the '88 Junior later. Counties and his track p.b's include 800 - 1.53.7 and 1500 - 3.51.2. He has never run a 5000m although under Coach Steve Gosling's guidance this will be remedied in 1989. Certainly Matthew has wintered well, including a strengthening programme under the aegis of Mike Winch at the Belgrave Gym. We look forward with anticipation to Matthew's summer performances. items.h: NORFOLK WELCOMES BELGRAVE AND BELGRAVE WELCOMES NORFOLK
items.sum: Bill Laws's profiles of the Norfolk internationals who joined Belgrave in 1988: Paul Evans, Neil Fetherby, Darren Mead and Ian Wells.
items.s: NORFOLK WELCOMES BELGRAVE AND BELGRAVE WELCOMES NORFOLK Bill Laws's profiles of the Norfolk internationals who joined Belgrave in 1988: Paul Evans, Neil Fetherby, Darren Mead and Ian Wells. Five years ago we had a Cup Match in Norwich and past President, Tom Morrell and his family, who had moved to the area many years earlier, backed up our travelling supporters. At that time a few of us could have anticipated that in 1988 several of Norfolk's top runners would chose Belgrave as their club. Bill Laws has talked to our latest batch of Internationals who you will be seeing in action in the near future. PAUL EVANS - Age 27: Paul Evans started running to get fit for football which he played for Lowestoft. His training involved 2 days per week and it was with some reluctance that he entered his first road race - a Carnival 10km in August 1986. To everyones surprise he finished 7th in 33.33. A month later he ran 32.30 and was hooked. Hugh Elder took over as coach and within 6 months Paul had run two ½ marathons, the second one in 65.30. In August '87 he gained his first England vest when he ran in a Home Counties ½ marathon in Scotland. He finished a very creditable 6th reducing his p.b. to 64.31. In 1988 he ran his first 3000m and became the first Brit. to run a sub 8.00 in a debut race. Since then he has represented the ECCU in several overseas races. His track p.b's (as of February 1989) are: 1 mile - 4.02, 3000m - 7.57, 2 miles - 8.32.2, 5000m - 13.57, 10,000m - 29.08. NEIL FETHERBY - Age (stopped counting at 27) Neil Fetherby is a true ultra-distance runner who thrives on the 120+ miles/week training schedules imposed by coach Bud Bolders. His International career started in 1986 when he represented England in the Aberdeen Marathon. He ran the Berlin Marathon twice and on the second occasion set a p.b. of 2.17.35. He gained a full GB vest in the 87 Koscite Marathon following wins in the Wolverhampton and Norfolk Marathons. Since joining Belgrave in 1988 he has been dogged by injury and only now is getting back to past form. His 10KM is 30.20. DARREN MEAD - Age 20 years Darren Mead is a legend in his own young life time. Twice winner of the Youths National C.C. Championship he gained his first England vest in the 1986 Junior World Championships where he finished 12th. He gained a GB vest in 1986 where he ran the World Junior and ran 14.12.3 for 5000m at the age of 17. 1987 saw a period of re-trenchment and it was not until 1988 that Darren started to re-gain form. He finished 2nd in the National Junior C.C. Championships and following a move to Sutton joined Belgrave and immediately made our British League Team running 800, 1500 and 5000m. His current p.b's confirm a surprising turn of speed which could well prove his most valuable weapon in the years ahead. At present he is self-coached and self-employed in the carpet business. P.b's: 200m: 23.7, 400m: 50.5, 800m: 1.52.6, 1500m: 3.45.8, 3000m: 8.08.0, 5000m: 14.12.3, 10,000m: 29.20, 10 Miles 49.03. IAN WELLS - Age 26 Ian Wells has been the Civil Service 400mH champion for the last 4 years. He has joined Belgrave to increase his opportunities for top class competition which is limited in the Great Yarmouth area. His choice of Belgrave was as a result of meeting fellow Civil Service athletes Abi Ekoku, Jay Busk and Derrick Williams. He aims to train at Battersea Park with Bob Bridges squad at least once per month. His p.b's are: 110H: 15.5, 400H: 54.72, 400m: 50.6 and Decathlon 4602 pts. items.label: March 1989
items.sum: Bill Laws's tribute to new club president Leo Coy, tracing his running career and his work rebuilding Belgrave's track and field team.
items.s: Leo Coy, President 1989. Bill Laws's tribute to new club president Leo Coy, tracing his running career and his work rebuilding Belgrave's track and field team. The election in September 1988 of Leo Coy as President gave particular pleasure to those who know how much work he has put into reviving Belgrave's Track and Field fortunes. Like so many of our officials Leo's arrival at Belgrave and involvement in the management side was as a result of a series of coincidences. He started running seriously in 1968 following encouragement from TVH's International 800m man Peter Browne. He so easily could have joined TVH. But no, he 'phoned the AAA's who thought he might consider Belgrave, met Alf Harley at Battersea and in 1969 was in! Belgravian reports of the time spotted this 'new talent' and he was soon making teams which included past greats like Gerry North, Bill Curtin, and Peter Carton. He ran in two 6 stage National road relay teams and five Southern 12 stage road relay teams. Somewhat later he won the Club 3000m s/c Champs. But already other interests were encroaching. In Charlie Manning's Presidential Year - the 'infamous '74' - Leo was cajoled to organise a fund raising fashion show and did so with great success. In '75 he became an official NUT and since then has been responsible for compiling the UK Top 100 performances in the steeplechase 5000 and 10,000m. In '77 he was elected assistant Hon. Gen. Sec. first to Peter Hillier and then Ray Hall. In 1980 when our 'A' team T&F side were struggling at the bottom of Southern League Div.1 Leo decided something had to be done and embarked on a team rebuilding exercise which virtually put paid to his own serious training plans. The success of his efforts could be seen as Belgrave moved from 35th in the National Rankings to its current 3rd place in Div.1 of the British Athletics League. 8 years of solid hard work. Add to that 4 years as Young Athletes Secretary and his current job as Coaching Secretary and you will appreciate just how much Leo has done for Belgrave. During all this he has been ably and loyally supported by his family who on many occasions have been seen together at T&F matches looking after entries, recording, scoring and the myriad of jobs needed to ensure successful organisation. While wife Sue and daughter Nemone are strictly back-room helpers, son Jon has run for Belgrave over many years and is a rapidly improving Junior. So well done Leo, you thoroughly deserve the Honour. items.label: March 1989
items.sum: Charlie Manning's tribute to Bill Lucas, Belgrave's centenary-year president.
items.s: W.E.LUCAS D.F.C. Charlie Manning's tribute to Bill Lucas, Belgrave's centenary-year president. I do not think we should let Memory of our Centenary Year fade too far from our minds without remembering our 'Centenary' President. We were singularly lucky in having a man of that calibre to front our Club. There are many opinions of Bill - not all see him as sweetness and light (I'm one myself) - some think him high handed (yea' I'll go along with that too) most of us have felt the rough edge of his tongue, he doesn't suffer fools gladly and gives short shrift to incompetance idleness and excuses. Hell of a downside isn't there! But the Past Presidents and Committee and Officers put him forward confident that he could serve us. This he has done with distinction. Bill is one of those rare people who are gifted with an abundance of qualities - I won't mention his 1948 Olympic selection - or his war record - or his announcing at International meets - or even his position on the 3 A's Executive Committee. What I will say is "Thank you Bill, you've been a great President during an historic period of our Club - your energy - your dedication - your loyalty to Belgrave Harriers, your personal standing in the broad spectrum of athletics - your impartial enthusiasm for every aspect of our activities - is a tribute to yourself, a benefit to the Club and an inspiration to us all. Thank you. CHARLIE MANNING W.E. (Bill) Lucas W.E.LUCAS D.F.C. Centenary President; 1948 Olympic selection; on the AAA Executive Committee; announcer at international meetings W.E.LUCAS D.F.C. Bill Charlie Manning CHARLIE MANNING Olympic Games 3 A's

items.label: March 1989
items.sum: New president Leo Coy's message on Belgrave Hall, the need for new members, committee volunteers and a Young Athletes organiser.
items.s: From the President. New president Leo Coy's message on Belgrave Hall, the need for new members, committee volunteers and a Young Athletes organiser. Thank you for electing me President of this great Club. I am deeply honoured to undertake this role for this great Club. The position of President in the Club is unique in that you are not given a description of what you should be doing, you are elected and left to get on with it. There are a number of things that I would like your help to achieve, that will be enjoyable for you and very beneficial to the Club. Belgrave Hall One of my aims as President will be to increase the use of Belgrave Hall by Club Members. The Hall is being given a much needed facelift, thanks to the efforts of Tom Carter. Mike Winch is basing all his activities under one roof at Belgrave Hall and this will give us a boost in income and make it a unique Centre of Excellence. A spin-off from this is that the Hall will be open for training on seven days a week. So, get up to the Hall as often as possible, get out for a run, and have a cup of tea or a pint afterwards. New Members For a Club with a membership of over 600 you may be surprised to learn that we desperately need new members, of all ages, particularly young athletes, male and female. All new members should be encouraged to train from Belgrave Hall or from Battersea Park Track and this in turn will develop a foundation for the Club to progress in the future. Belgrave Committee The organisation of Belgrave is placed by you in the hands of the Committee which is elected each year at the AGM. There are about six people who sit on this Committee, that virtually run Belgrave with very little input or ideas from the Club Membership. Should one of these stalwarts decide that they have had enough and cease their activities, then the club would be in real difficulties. We need new administrators, new ideas and more Club Members involved in running Belgrave. If you can spare an hour a week please let me or a Committee Member know. Any help however small would be much appreciated. Young Athletes At one time we had a regular influx of youngsters to fill our teams. This influx has dried up and we now have very few young athletes, girls or boys. We have also got nobody to organise the Young Athletes, which is an unbelievable situation for a Club as distinguished as ours. It is for you to decide whether we continue with running a Young Athletes Section, if nobody comes forward in the very near future then we will have no alternative but to restrict the age of our new members. Please help us to avoid this happening. Thank you for your time and your support so far in my year of office. Remember that no club can survive for long if everybody just turns up for a race or a training run. We need your help now to form a solid foundation for this our second century. We have a great deal going for us at present, the performances of our Junior Cross-Country Teams throughout the eighties is the envy of most other clubs in the country, our Track and Field Team is our best ever. Have you been to support our Juniors or Track and Field side? You don't know what you are missing. Good luck throughout 1989. LEO COY President Leo Coy LEO COY President Tom Carter Tom Carter facelift of Belgrave Hall Mike Winch Mike Winch basing his activities at Belgrave Hall Belgrave Hall Battersea Park Track

items.s: From THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago.... and 40 years ago. Look-back column quoting the Belgravian of April 1967 (headed '25 years ago', as printed) on E.C.C.U. championship results and SCAAA committee elections, and of June 1949 on Percy Wright's Overseas Trophy appeal. From THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago.... "April 1967 - our combined record in Youths, Juniors and Senior E.C.C.U. Championships this year was second only to one other Club - Coventry Godiva H. We were 12th in the Youths race (of 120 Clubs); 9th in the Junior (of 105 Clubs) and 8th in the Senior (of 135 Clubs) - a really splendid combined effort in which we can take great pride. In addition, our congratulations go to Gerry North on his sixth place in the Senior and on International selection; to Tony Fairclough - 5th in the Junior Championship; and to John Bicourt, seventh in the Youths event. All this magnificent running in fields of fantastic size, and its promise for the future. In the recent ballot for the Committee of the Southern Counties Amateur Athletic Association our General Hon. Sec. Alf Harley was placed equal third in the voting, Les Cohen was 5th and Harry Shields equal 14th of the twenty elected members. Bill Lucas, our President, represents the Southern Cross-Country Association and Frank Jarvis the Race Walking Association, Southern Area." and 40 years ago. "June 1949 - THE OVERSEAS TROPHY - Percy Wright says:- 'Remember it? We planned it for after the war with the money that we made on those Airgraphs you chaps sent me. Unfortunately the man that bought the Airgraphs died and this source of income died with him. We had, however, succeeded in getting quite a tidy sum - £6. 19s. 6d., to be exact. I had hoped to plan something else to raise the money to a sufficient sum to purchase a suitable trophy, but my present distance from the Club quarters is not convenient. It has been suggested to me that I make an appeal to all those who served overseas and would like to see the idea of the Overseas Cup materialise to send along a subscription. Well, lads! what about it? Send your cheque, postal order or stamp, either to me or the Hon. Treasurer, not forgetting to mention what it is for. We should also be pleased to have any suggestions on how the trophy shall be awarded.' " (The "Overseas Cup" was designated the Championship Trophy for the Youth cross-country event.) During recent months our starter of very many years - Arthur Penny (and 81 years young) - has been upgraded. Ken Giles (Field), Dave Davies (Track) and Sue Morrison (Time-Keeper) have passed tests and are now graded. Please contact me by 'phone on [phone number withheld] if you are able to help. DEREK CROOKES (Officials Hon. Sec.) items.h: IN MEMORIUM: R.M. 'MEL' THORPE (Born March 1938 - died November 1988)
items.sum: Clive Shippen's obituary of Mel Thorpe, a Belgrave distance runner of the 1960s who came from and returned to Coventry Godiva.
items.s: IN MEMORIUM: R.M. 'MEL' THORPE (Born March 1938 - died November 1988) Clive Shippen's obituary of Mel Thorpe, a Belgrave distance runner of the 1960s who came from and returned to Coventry Godiva. IN MEMORIUM R.M. 'MEL' THORPE (Born March 1938 - died November 1988) It is with sadness that we must report the death of Mel Thorpe. Mel was an integral part of the Belgrave running teams of the 1960's and, with his wife Mary, ever present at the numerous social functions the team enjoyed in those days. When he knew he would be moving South from Coventry Godiva Harriers he joined Belgrave and was elected to membership in August 1963. By the time he had got himself settled in it was March 1964 and his first appearance for us was at the Bexley Relay where he was put in the 'C' team as a 'feeler'. His performance proved to the selectors that he was a serious candidate for our 1st team and he confirmed that view in his first season with us. His enthusiasm for running carried him across a wide spectrum of distances, from one mile on the track to 20 miles on the road, all in that first season with us which culminated in Mel helping the Bels to a fine second place in the News of the World "Southern" London to Brighton Relay. From then on he was ubiquitous, cramming in to four seasons what many would take double that time to achieve. Hardly a team was fielded without his presence. His best performances on the track were 4:19.8 for the mile, 9:04 for two miles and 14:13 for three miles. In the "5 3/4" he ran 28:34 and in the Yacht '3' the second fastest time ever of 14:37, only Gerry North having run faster. But after 4 years of wearing Belgrave colours over track, country and road - and giving us sterling support in all our affairs - his job took him back to Coventry. He retained second-claim membership of Bels for very many years and he and Mary always looked forward to their re-union visits South. The Belgravian of March 1967 wrote:- "We suppose it was inevitable. To hope to hang on to Mel Thorpe indefinitely when he now lives in distant Coventry was too good to be true ..... he will now probably run against us in the National Road Relay wearing the colours of Godiva. Mel writes 'I thank all those at Belgrave for the happiest four years of my life'. It was a pleasure to have you Mel". Our condolences are extended to Mary, Karen and Richard. CLIVE SHIPPEN R.M. items.s: L.A.MITCHELL (LEN) Obituary of race-walking official Len Mitchell, former R.W.A. President, who died on 9 January 1989 aged 82. L.A.MITCHELL (LEN) - passed away January 9th, 1989 aged 82. Len became a member of Belgrave only in the last couple of years, but had been a good friend of the club for many years. He had served the Race-Walking sport at all levels, both as a competitor and official. He had been President of the R.W.A. National and also Southern Area and had also held secretarial positions in the R.W.A. and Surrey County AAA. He moved to Trowbridge on 14 December, 1988 after a lifetime in the Croydon area only to survive a matter of weeks. He was cremated at Bath on January 18th and a number of club members attended. We extend our sincere condolences to Mrs. B. Mitchell and family. L.A. (Len) Mitchell L.A.MITCHELL (LEN) died 9 January 1989 aged 82; race walker and official; President of R.W.A. items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: Eddie Kulukundis's OBE and Athletics Today, news of former members, the Southern Cross-Country team, officials' elections (Cyril Gittens, Doug Fotheringham), engagements, marriages, Dave Davies's police trophy and members' operations. Our congratulations go out to our Patron, EDDIE KULUKUNDIS, on his OBE in the New Year Honours List. The award, for his services as Chairman of the Sports Aid Foundation and to Athletics, was highly deserved. His deep knowledge of athletics and his enthusiasm for helping promising youngsters is well known. Many established internationals have benefitted from his past help and many future teams will spring from his present support. We feel sure that his association with athletics will be long and fruitful. ************ DAYE DONOVAN writes from New York and reciprocates our wishes for a Happy New Year. She recently enjoyed an intoxicating trip around India, but did not see Rangit Bhatia in her travels. She hopes to be in England again in May and looks forward to seeing us again. ************ RANJIT BHATIA, professor of mathematics at Delhi University, sends best wishes to all his former club-mates at Belgrave. Rangit writes and broadcasts on athletics and was in Seoul for the Olympics, where he met Eddie Kulukundis and cheered on John Regis with full Belgrave partiality. His knowledge of athletics won him an Addidas forecast prize and a round-the-world trip. He still carries his Belgrave vest over the roads of India. ************ How good it was to see three Belgrave vests up in the first eight of the Southern Cross-Country Championships at Basingstoke. Matthew Stickles, Darren Mead and Justin Chaston ran superbly and are certain to pull each other through to many successes in the future. Steve Webster carried a heavy burden as 4th scorer in such a team, but he performed with great credit to clinch second place for Belgrave, only 4 points behind the winners. ************ CLIVE SHIPPEN was elected a vice-President of the Southern Counties AA in 1988. Bill Lucas (now 72) continues to shoulder the burden of Chairman during a period of much change and controversy at Area and National level. ************ EDDIE KULUKUNDIS is the new publisher of ATHLETICS TODAY. The magazine is now appearing weekly and is produced by a formidable team of journalists and athletes. It is probably the best magazine on athletics to ever hit the British market. We wish Eddie and his team every success in their enterprise. Race Walking Association - National President 1989. Congratulations to Cyril Gittens on his election to this top post. Cyril has been a second claim member for 36 years and other than a competitor has given yeoman service to the club as an official and in particular as time keeper. 1989 should be an exciting year for Ernest Obeng. He has recently started a Sport Promotions Business which offers, among other things, a low cost electronic timing system for track meets. And in May he marries Sharon whom he met as a post graduate student at Loughborough University. Sharon gained her Doctorate last summer. Marriage next too for fellow sprint star Lenny Paul who we understand is planning 'To tie the knot' before the '89 track season. Not to be left behind middle distance junior star, Darren Mead has recently announced his engagement to Donna. Just to show what a small world it is, Donna who lives in Norfolk, is the niece of former Surrey C.C.Champ. John Roberts. You may have read in the press of John Gladwin's M.E. illness. In a final attempt to free himself of the debilitating after effects, John is to spend 5 months 5 months in Australia at the same Canberra Sports Institute that initiated the remarkable breakthrough of Gary Staines in 1987. In both cases the trips were financed by our patron Eddie Kulukundis. Congratulations to John and Jane Barry who are expecting their first child in May. JOINT SECRETARIES Club Officials are liable to get 'phone calls at all hours and awkward times and our Gen.Hon.Sec., Sue Morrison is no exception. Christmas Day Dinnertime made no difference when she literally received a ring from The Ladies Section Hon. Sec., Harry Porter. Having popped the proposal between courses and they are happy to announce their engagement. Congratulations to Sue and Harry!! Dave Davies Perpetuated (Not a painful operation) On September 6th, 1988 at a function following a Kent Police and City of London Police 10 Miles Road Running Championships Race, the following report appeared in The City Police Magazine "City '88" - New Trophy - The presentation Buffet followed with unveiling of the new trophy, "The Dave Davies Trophy" presented by The City of London Police Athletic and Social Club - Athletics Section, to be competed for annually by Kent and City of London Police athletes in the 10 Miles Road Race. It was pointed out that it had been inaugurated to acknowledge Dave's 23 years as Secretary to the Athletics Section, a post from which he retired last year. Retiring fellow Dave who, when not road running for the club pulls pints behind our Club Bar. Vertebrae (Can be painful) Sheena (Mrs Bill) Lucas and Harry Porter have both recently undergone operations on their troublesome backs and we wish them a complete and speedy recovery. It will be nice to see them moving freely around again. Belgravian is President of Middlesex AAA. Congratulations to Doug Fotheringham on his election to this high office. Doug joined the Bels in September 1953 whilst serving with the Met. Police. He has walked for the club ever since that date and has featured in our championship teams at National level. In recent years he has had considerable success in Veteran events and has competed in several World Championships. items.s: BELGRAVE HARRIERS - BRITISH BOBSLEIGH CHAMPIONS? Report from club coach Eddy Botjler/Bojtler, trainer of the British bobsleigh teams, on Belgrave sprinters Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul winning the British two-man and four-man bobsleigh championships in Austria. EDDY BOTJLER Eddy Botjler is a Belgrave Coach and coaches many of the athletes at the Army School of Physical Training at Altershot. His expertise spans all the Track and Field events and his army athletes have competed with distinction. Belgravians will immediately recognise the names of Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul in the sprints and the distance running star John Wright. Eddy has recently been appointed official trainer of the British Bob-Sleigh teams and has sent in the following report. BELGRAVE HARRIERS - BRITISH BOBSLEIGH CHAMPIONS? Through the 'Belgravian' I would like to record the sporting achievements of certain members of Belgrave Harriers. Normally they are seen exploding out of blocks or being part of our sprint relay team in the British League. I am of course referring to Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul who, in November of this year, were part of the team which, travelling at speeds of around 70 mph, won the British Bobsleigh Championships in Austria. The 'Two-Man" competition saw Dave Armstrong as the brakeman, with Mark Tout as driver, win the British Two-Man Championship. Two weeks before, this highly regarded team, scored another success by breaking the British record for the 'Two-Man Push Start' competition at Winterberg. Both Dave Armstrong and Mark Tout were joined by Audley Richards and Lenny Paul to a very comfortable victory in the 'Four-Man British Championship. (Mark Tout being a decathlete while Audley Richards is a 49 seconds - 400 metre runner, both plan to be members of Belgrave Harriers next season. These results mean that for the remaining competitions this season which includes the World Cup - European Championship and World Championship, we will go into the draw as Great Britain 1 and will, therefore, always be in the top section which is a very important factor. For those who may be unaware, the purpose of the crew is to accelerate a Bobsleigh weight, either 390 kgs Two-Man or 630 kgs Four-Man, over a distance of approximately 50 metres. The greater the speed that can be achieved at the start, the faster the 'bob' should travel on its downward path over 1500 metres. Hence the need for sprinters with strength. Competition between teams to gain the fastest push-start is very competitive with some teams recruiting athletes of the highest standard. The Canadians boast of two athletes that were part of their sprint relay team in Seoul, plus a Canadian decathlon champion. The Swiss two-man bobsleigh team has the Swiss spring champion as their brakeman. If there are any readers who think that they might like to have the opportunity to bobsleigh and believe they possess the necessary physical qualities, bearing in mind the need to become used to warming up in temperatures of minus 10 degrees centigrade and feel they would like the challenge of sitting in a bobsleigh travelling at about 70 mph they should contact the author of this article for further information. Eddy Bojtler Trainer British Bobsleigh Team BELGRAVE HARRIERS - BRITISH BOBSLEIGH CHAMPIONS? items.s: ME ... ME ... ME ... ME! Charles Manning appeals to members to appreciate the club's volunteer officers and the generosity of an anonymous benefactor, and to put the club first. For one minute consider the "doers", "the gogetters", "the action men" (and women) lets forget "the wingers", "the whats in it for me" the selfish who, only, put their own interests first. One particular strata of our club show enormous self sacrifice in the amount of time, energy and skill they put in on your behalf. Most of them are officers of the club. Many of you are unaware of the debt you owe. How many for instance do the daily round of work, school or whatever. The evening spent training or "out" or comfortably in front of the T.V. So for one minute spare a thought and reflect that somewhere one of your club mates is beavering away for you. It may be at a meeting where he or she is representing your interests or they may be physically working on our Hall. They may be using "their time" to sort out the paperwork, in organizing fixtures, getting quotes, transportation, enrolement, the Belgravian, hire agreements, the accounts, the bar, cleaning, socials etc. etc. etc. Consider the shower room - taking out old sinks - rewiring - retiling - extra changing facility, this and a few other things cost £3,000 and you didn't pay a single penny - it was paid for by an old and well loved Belgravian. (He also gave £1,000 for the Centenary Invitation Cross Country Race). Next time you want to criticise, ask yourself what you have done, how you have supported your officers and committee whether its paying your subs without a reminder - turned up to fixtures - marked courses - how many times do you go to a race and expect someone else to send a comprehensive report to the Editor and Sectional Secretary. We cannot all match the generosity of certain people, but we can often put the club, my club, your club, our club before personal considerations. CHARLES MANNING Charles Manning CHARLES MANNING Centenary Invitation Cross Country Race
