items.s: BELGRAVIAN WALKING SECTION REPORT Carl Lawton's walking section resume of a poor year for the men's team, with the ladies more successful, illustrated by a photo of the Ladies Walking Section training in Windsor Great Park. Race Walking. BELGRAVIAN WALKING SECTION REPORT by Carl Lawton WALKING RESUME The last year has not been a success, certainly the worst for many years. We have been unable to start teams let alone finish them in the mens, but the ladies have been more productive and with Sian Spacey finishing 3rd in the National 10kms it has not been absolute disaster. It does seem possible that things will be better this winter but only if we get full turn outs where it matters. If walking in general is to keep its head above water we must try and keep numbers up in all races. Not only are we suffering in numbers of competitors but also numbers of officials without whom we cannot hold races, not just recorders, timekeepers and judges but the simple pointsmen are required, with smaller fields it is that much easier for a walker to go off course if not correctly directed. Other performances of note have been Gill Brackpool's 5th in the National 15kms, Sue Morrison and John Hall winning the Civil Service 3kms. A welcome return to John Llewellin after injury and long lay off and hopefully Paul Warburton making some sort of comeback but regretably no younger faces to the side. items.sum: Bob Bridges' round-up of Belgrave's 1988 Southern League track and field season, in which the team just missed promotion, with the 1989 fixture dates.
items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUND-UP Bob Bridges' round-up of Belgrave's 1988 Southern League track and field season, in which the team just missed promotion, with the 1989 fixture dates. Track and Field. SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUND-UP by Bob Bridges The season got off to a bad start when I had to struggle to get a team out, even though the fixture was in London, but all credit to those who did, especially those who 'doubled' or 'trebled' up who threw or jumped 'out of event' as we managed to finish 3rd. The second match being at Battersea I had no trouble getting a team out and we appeared to romp home winners, but Norfolk O. who were very strong in the distance events and the discus, gave us a late fright. The third match was cancelled due to a waterlogged track at Huntingdon which we were declared the winners due to Belgrave being the highest placed in the league of the clubs involved in that fixture. Our fourth match at Portsmouth was going to be out toughest match as two of the teams were 2nd and 4th in the division and so it proved as we finished equal third. We seemed to be getting stronger on the track and weaker in the throws. This match saw for the first time in Belgrave colours, Phil Sedgrove who sprinted the final 100m to win an exciting 5000m and Trevor Blanchard who won the Long Jump and injured himself on his first Triple Jump but still managed to finish 2nd. For the fifth match we had to travel to Reading. Although we won 12 out of the 20 track races, due to athletes getting stuck in traffic and British Rail being British Rail, we virtually had no throwers (yet again) and very few jumpers and lost the match to South London Harriers by just 3 points. We had to win the last match at Battersea to gain promotion. This was always going to be difficult as Milton Keynes were the division leaders and though there were only two teams in it there was only one winner ... and it weren't us. This match saw the debut of Matthew Stickles in Belgrave colours in which he won a physical and later a verbal 1500m and was also placed 2nd in the 800m. A look through the results will show the high standard of this match and that we did not give up without a fight with many pb's or seasons best being performed, notably Chris Cornwalls 2.03m in the high jump. Although it was a disappointing season in the fact that we just missed out on promotion there were several encouraging performances that looks good for the future, notably Trevor Blanchard in the long and triple jump, Alistair Grant in the 400H, Gareth Allison who amazes with his talent and versatility, the French twins in the sprints and Joe Minetti who was finding his old form and discovering he could also run 400 just before he got injured towards the end of the season. Among others who serve a mention are Andy Paton, he turned out in every match and gave 100% plus every time including the 110H! and the ever youthful Snowy Brooks. We need more throwers and pole vaulters and I am indebted to our ex 400m and 400m runners who filled these events during the season. Southern League dates for the 1989 season are: 6th May: 27th May: 24th June: 8th July and 5th August. * We have now entered a 'C' team in the Southern League Division 7 Sth. for next season. items.sum: Leo Coy's report on Belgrave's 1988 GRE Gold Cup run (second round at Warley, semi-final at Stoke, sixth in the televised final at Haringey), with results from each round.
items.s: THE G.R.E. GOLD CUP Leo Coy's report on Belgrave's 1988 GRE Gold Cup run (second round at Warley, semi-final at Stoke, sixth in the televised final at Haringey), with results from each round. THE G.R.E. GOLD CUP Leo Coy reports ... This year's competition had us travel much further afield than ever before and also saw us reach the final for the first time. The Second Round on May 29 took us to Warley in the Midlands and with a strong looking team we turned out comfortable winners. Individual wins were recorded by Marcus Adam in the sprints, Femi Abejide the Triple Jump, Marcello Bizio the Steeplechase and Jimmy Summers and Abi Ekoku mopping up the Throws. The "French" twins, M & J, made a winning debut in the 4x100m relay and with their progress this year it looks well for the future. The Semi-final had us on the road again, this time to Stoke-on-Trent. Most went up overnight (with thanks to W.R.L.) and savoured the delights of Stoke on a Saturday night and despite the "Cuff" strip tease before the match, everything went very well on the day and we easily qualified for the final by finishing second to Wolverhampton & Bilston 139-137 pts. Individual wins were recorded by Ernie Obeng 100m, Marcus Adam 200m, Stu Paton 1500m, Mike Hayes 3000 S/C, Femi Abejide Triple Jump and Nigel Bevan, Javelin Throw and the 4x400m Relay Team of Cuff, Busk, Maynard and Paton. The Final was held at Haringey on 21st August and was televised on Channel 4. We turned out what was probably our best ever team on paper, but alas, on the day Dame Fortune failed to smile on us and despite the fact that we were facing perhaps our toughest opposition so far, we had two individual winners in Marcus Adam in the 200m and surprise, surprise - John Regis in the 400m, in which he set a new club record of 46.57 secs. Mike Small performed well in the Hammer Throw with 3 throws over 49 mtrs. - NEXT YEAR PERHAPS!! 29 MAY 1988 WARLEY GRE CUP SECOND ROUND 100m: 1.M.Adam 11.4; 200m: 1.M.Adam 22.7; 400m: 4.J.Busk 49.7; 800m: 2.J.Booth 1.57.2; 1500m: 3.J.Barry 4.10.8; 5000m: 3.S.Maynard 15.10.6; 10,000m: 4.D.Anderson 34.46.2; 3000 S/C: 1.M.Bizio 9.46.5; 110H: 2.P.Chong 15.1; 400H: 2.I.Bland 55.0; LJ: 4.F.Abejide 6.54; HJ: 2.B.Gardner 1.85; TJ: 1.F.Abejide 15.06; PV: 4.B.Gardner 2.80; HT: 1.J.Summers 53.22; SP: 1.A.Ekoku 15.32; DT: 1.A.Ekoku 48.68; JT: 5.A.Ekoku 38.20; 4x100: 1.BELS 44.6 (M.French, J.French, F.Abejide, M.Adam); 4x400: 3.BELS 3.22.6 (Cuff, Busk, Adam, Bland). items.s: BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE (DIVISION I) Reports and A/B string results from Belgrave's four 1988 British Athletics League Division 1 matches (Birmingham 7th, Haringey 3rd, Meadowbank 5th, West London Stadium 2nd), finishing third in the final league table. BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE (DIVISION I) 21 MAY 1988 ALEXANDER STADIUM, BIRMINGHAM BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE DIV.I, MATCH 1 Teamwise this was our least successful and we finished in 7th place, just one point ahead of the last team - TVH. Stars of the day were Lenny Paul who beat a good field in the 100m and John Regis who ran a blistering 45.4 sec. leg in the long relay. There were ten new faces in our team on the day and all felt that we were capable of much better. 4x100: 6.BELS (L.Paul, D.Williams, D.Hall, L.Haughton) 41.88; 4x400: 4.BELS (J.Busk 50.3; D.Hall 48.5; J.Regis 45.4; C.Ogle 50.01) 3.14.15. Team Result 1.Haringey 409; 2.Birchfield 342; 3.Shaftesbury 279; 4.W&B 259; 5.ESH 235; 6.Blackheath 221; 7.BELGRAVE 217; 8.TVH 216. 12 JUNE 1988 HARINGEY STADIUM BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE DIVISION 1, MATCH 2 Saw the return of our sprinters. Lenny Paul again won the 100m and Marcus Adam got his beak in front in the 200m, and Chris Ogle in his first race in Bels colours, won the second string 800m. Darren Mead partnered Chris in the 1500m and both gave very good accounts of themselves. Femi Abejide made his debut as a Belgrave man on his former "home track" and made a vast difference to our "jumps" section. His 16.30m TJ was excellent as was Derek Browne's 15.15m. Nigel Bevan was 2nd in the Javelin with a 70.42m throw and Jimmy Summers had a 54.58m Hammer Throw. Jimmy also teamed up with Bob Bridges to get valuable points in the Pole Vault. 4x100: 41.00 (L.Paul, M.Adam, P.Goedluck, D.Armstrong) 4x400: 3.20.06 (J.Busk, P.Cuff, S.Paton, D.Williams) Team Result: 1.Haringey 426; 2.Birchfield 345; 3.BELGRAVE 284. 2 JULY 1988 MEADOWBANK BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE DIVISION 1 - MATCH 3 A long and expensive trip. Fifth team place was a good result but we had hoped for better. Blackheath shaded us by one point. Ernest Obeng was in great tune for the 100m and was leading the field when he had to pull up and that not only ended this race early but also put an end to his Olympic ambition. John Regis broke the Div.1 record in winning the 200m in 20.88, Lenny Paul won the 100m 'B' in 10.64. Star of the day was Ken Onuaguluchi who almost missed his return flight to London, he had a brilliant competition in the Shot Putt, Discus Throw and as a back up to Nigel Bevan in the Javelin. 4x100: 3.BELS 41.26 (L.Paul, D.Armstrong, J.Regis, D.Williams) 4x400: 7.BELS 3.21.29 (C.Knight, P.Cuff, T.Pamah, J.Busk) Team Result: 1.Haringey 367; 2.W&B 360; 3.Birchfield 334; 4.Blackheath 265; 5.BELGRAVE 264. 13 AUGUST 1988 WEST LONDON STADIUM BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE DIVISION 1, MATCH 4 Back to London for the final fixture at the West London Stadium at Wormwood Scrubs. We fielded what was probably our best team ever. It also contained three new faces who were gracing our team for the first time and Andy Moore making a winning return to the team in the 'B' 1500m. Darryl Maynard had a fine debut in the 'A' 800m. Ossie Cham made an impressive entrance with a brilliant 2.10m for 2nd place in the High Jump being ably backed up by Leroy Haughton. Paul Sadgrove had a really outstanding run in the 5000m and was only just out-kicked on the final lap. Ernest Obeng managed to get fit again for this match and got a third place. Individual winners were Lenny Paul 100m 'B', Femi Abejide TJ 'B'. So - with fine backing up performances by Stu Paton, Nigel Bevan, Ken Onuaguluchi, Mike Hayes, Abe Ekoku and Mike Small who all gained 2nd or 3rd places and all the others as shown in the final result, we had a fine old day - finishing up only second team on the day to the Mighty Haringey. So ended the British Athletic League Div.1 for 1988. 13 AUGUST 1988 WEST LONDON STADIUM MATCH 4 (Cont ..) 4x100: 2.BELS 41.39 (Cuff, Armstrong, Adam, Obeng) 4x400: 4.BELS 3.16.9 (Cuff, Maynard, Paton, Busk) Team Result: 1.Haringey 344: 2.BELGRAVE 316½; 3.Birchfield 310½. A very gratifying result, but with some "if only's" we could have made it - Roll on 1989. items.sum: The editor's tribute to team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws for organising the club's best ever track season in the 1988 British Athletics League, and thanks to patron Eddy Kulukundis.
items.s: The editor's tribute to team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws for organising the club's best ever track season in the 1988 British Athletics League, and thanks to patron Eddy Kulukundis. So ended the 1988 British Athletic League - Division 1 and the Club had had its best ever track season. Now let us give due accord to those two men who had engineered this success. In alphabetical order Leo Coy and Bill Laws are the two Team Managers. To organise two teams of track and field men for four matches each of 19 events, the whole gambit of disciplines, is no mean task and considering such things in a club such as ours where members live and work over such a wide area, co-ordinating the travel arrangements for at least 30 per match is only the start of things after the team has been selected and agreed. The venues for the matches meant that in one case flights to Edinburgh had to be arranged, plus accommodation, Birmingham had different arrangements and the two London fixtures likewise. At least 50 different men took part in the Belgrave teams for the events and in some cases a number of our men competed in 3 events and some doubled up in the one day. All this organising was done by Bill and Leo, at great expense in time and energy and no doubt money and also considering that they have their own professions to consider, we owe them a great debt of thanks and gratitude for a marvellous job well done. Thanks Leo and Bill. This tribute to Bill Laws and Leo Coy is in line with the sentiments expressed by the General Committee of Belgrave Harriers. Before bringing these comments to a close it would be ungracious not to bring to the members notice the "behind the scenes" activities of our Patron, Eddy Kulukundis O.B.E. who not only made some financial arrangements for us, but also certain facilities such as accommodation. On December 14th Eddy showed his appreciation to our B.A.L. team by inviting them to a Dining evening out. Thank you Eddy - we truly appreciate your Patronage. J.G.C. (Ed.) Leo Coy Leo Coy BAL team manager 1988 Leo Coy Leo Bill Laws Bill Laws BAL team manager 1988 Bill Laws Bill Eddy Kulukundis Eddy Kulukundis O.B.E. club Patron; hosted BAL team dinner 14 December Eddy Kulukundis O.B.E. items.s: 100M WIN FOR REGIS Belgrave results at the 1988 UK Championships in Derby, where John Regis won the 100m and Gary Staines was third in his first 10,000m. 4/5 JUNE 1988 UK CHAMPIONSHIPS MOORWAY'S STADIUM, DERBY 100M WIN FOR REGIS John Regis tried his hand at some early speed work, and a late charge saw him win the 100 metre title in 10.65 sec. running into a 2m/sec. headwind. Gary Staines made his debut at 10,000 metres and finished 3rd in 28.12.93. In the field new member Femi Abejedi finished 2nd in the triple jump with 15.86, whilst a pb throw of 74.60m in the javelin for Nigel Bevan was only enough for 4th. 100m: 1.J.Regis 10.65 (10.56 sf); 5.L.Paul 10.79 (10.70 sf); sf 5.P.Goedluck 10.84; 200m: ht 2.P.Goedluck 21.71; 400m; ht 7.J.Busk 49.68; 10000m: 3.G.Staines 28.12.93; HJ: 5.O.Cham 2.15; TJ: 2.F.Abejedi 15.86; SP: 10.A.Ekoku 15.70; JT: 4.N.Bevan 74.60. items.sum: Report and results from the 1988 Seoul Olympics: John Regis won 4x100m relay silver in a UK record and Gary Staines reached the 5000m final.
items.s: REGIS RELAY SILVER Report and results from the 1988 Seoul Olympics: John Regis won 4x100m relay silver in a UK record and Gary Staines reached the 5000m final. OLYMPIC GAMES - SEOUL REGIS RELAY SILVER John Regis strikes relay silver! John, Elliott Bunney, Mike McFarlane and Linford Christie set a new UK record of 38.28 secs to finish 1/10 sec. behind the USSR. Things didn't go so well for John in the 100m, a late tackle by an aspiring Portugese rugby player meant he failed to get beyond the 1st round of the 100m. Better progress was made in the 200m where he qualified for the semi-final. Gary meanwhile surprised himself by qualifying for the final of the 5000m, but later said he'd run out of steam by then. He also said later that the Olympic stadium lacked atmosphere! 100m: r1 4.J.Regis 10.76; 200m: r1 1.J.Regis 20.90; r2 2.J.Regis 20.61; sf 7.J.Regis 20.69; 400m: r1 5.F.Sandy 46.82; 5000m: r1 1.G.Staines 13.47.81; sf 4.G.Staines 13.24.51; F 13.G.Staines 13.55.00; 4x100m: r1 2nd GB 39.17; (Bunny, Regis, McFarlane, Callender), sf 2nd GB 38.52 (Bunny, Regis, McFarlane, Christie), F. 2nd GB 38.28; (Bunny, Regis, McFarlane, Christie). items.sum: Team manager Colin Pearson's leg-by-leg account of Belgrave's ninth place in the 23rd Belgrave 12-stage relay on 26 March 1988, regretting the absence of several leading runners.
items.s: 23rd Belgrave Relay - 26th March 1988 Team manager Colin Pearson's leg-by-leg account of Belgrave's ninth place in the 23rd Belgrave 12-stage relay on 26 March 1988, regretting the absence of several leading runners. 23RD BELGRAVE RELAY - 26th MARCH 1988 Stuart Paton started us off in this years relay and what an excellent start he gave us coming in second place and recording our fastest long leg of the day 24.34. Graham Adams took over from Stuart and justified his selection into the team with his run 16.33 coming in six place "cries of come on me ole cocker" could be heard on his run in. Francis Ward ran the third leg not a bad run from Frank proving to me that he can run well when he gets his act together, but also losing places coming in eleventh place with 26.12. Martin Forrester played his part well holding onto eleventh place running 16.33 on the fourth leg a time which most seniors would have been proud of Martin should be a contender for a long leg next year Seniors beware these Juniors mean business. Mike Hayes ran the fifth leg also holding onto eleventh place with 26.07 Mike gave a good chase but just failed to catch the Exeter man. Not the usual scene for John Booth three miles? but showing the strength of character to run 17.02 on the six stage John lost one place finishing twelth always willing to show his loyality to the club. The seventh leg was run by Dave North in 27.18 Dave was well under par for this years race, feeling the effects of little training and moving house, coming in 17th place we all know Dave can run better than this and hope to see him fitter next year. Simon Maynard set off with a vengeance gaining four places giving us the lift we needed at this the Eighth Stage 16.19 faster than I had expected from him, showing the experience of a seasoned relay runner, unlucky not to catch the Luton man in front. John Wright ran our second fastest long stage 24.49. I was impressed with John's run even though he had run a half marathon the week before, he took us up to Sixth place on the Ninth Stage. Matthew Chaston running the Tenth Stage was another runner who excelled my expectations with 16.01 proving a point to me that he is a natural relay runner. Marcello Bizio ran the penultimate stage 26.52 lost one place to Exeter, a good engine room run from Marcello who had to run most of his stage on his own. Steve Zealy ran the last stage although losing three places held on to bring us in Ninth after only being included in the team at the last minute. Aldershot won the race in 4 hours 7 minutes 18 seconds, 2nd: Haringey 4.08.19; 3rd:Blackheath 4.09.40; 4th: Shaftesbury 4.12.42; 5th: Exeter 4.13.24: 6th: Luton 4.15.42; 7th: Highgate 4.15.55; 8th: Newham & Essex 4.16.05; 9th: BELGRAVE 4.16.10; 10th: Invicta 4.16.30. As you can see apart from the first three teams it was a close race, I can only stop to think for a moment what might have been if Justin Chastin, Ollie Foote, John Gladwin, Gary Staines, David Swain had been available we could win this race? Yours, Frustrated Team Manager COLIN PEARSON Stuart Paton Stuart Paton 1st leg 24.34, Belgrave's fastest long leg Stuart Paton Stuart Graham Adams Graham Adams 2nd leg 16.33 Francis Ward Francis Ward 3rd leg 26.12 Francis Ward Frank Martin Forrester Martin Forrester 4th leg 16.33 Martin Forrester Martin Mike Hayes Mike Hayes 5th leg 26.07 Mike Hayes Mike John Booth John Booth 6th leg 17.02 John Booth John Dave North Dave North 7th leg 27.18 Dave North Dave Simon Maynard Simon Maynard 8th leg 16.19 John Wright John Wright 9th leg 24.49 John Wright John Matthew Chaston Matthew Chaston 10th leg 16.01 Marcello Bizio Marcello Bizio 11th leg 26.52 Marcello Bizio Marcello Steve Zealy Steve Zealy 12th leg Justin Chastin Justin Chastin named as unavailable; printed Chastin (Justin Chaston elsewhere in the issue) Ollie Foote Ollie Foote unavailable John Gladwin John Gladwin unavailable Gary Staines Gary Staines unavailable David Swain David Swain unavailable Colin Pearson COLIN PEARSON team manager Belgrave Relay Aldershot Haringey Blackheath Shaftesbury Exeter Luton Highgate Newham & Essex Invicta

I must express my sincere thanks to three smashing club members, for on the day of this race Mike Hayes came all the way from Nottingham, John Wright from Birmingham, and Darrell Maynard, for those who do not know Darrell is 800 metre, 1500 metre man and has represented the club in the British League, also willing to travel from Cambridge to support Belgrave. items.s: 19 NOVEMBER 1988 REEBOK SURREY LEAGUE - DIVISION II Belgrave results, match table and Colin Pearson's report from the second Surrey League Division II race on 19 November 1988, where Belgrave took the first three places and led the division by 146 points. BELS: 1.G.Staines 25.15; 2.S.Paton 26.05; 3.J.Wright; 26.07 7.M.Stickles 26.36; 8.O.Foote 26.42; 14.M.Bizio 27.33; 17.P.Sanders 27.40; 19.P.Gilbey 27.44; 28.J.Mather 28.24; 32.F.Ward 28.31; 37.A.Paton 28.50; 51.M.Head 29.32; 52.S.Webster 29.41; 61.T.Williams 30.09; 85.L.Coy 31.13; 93.T.Mullen 31.47; 104.S.White 32.44; 105.J.Hutchinson 32.45; 136.J.Broad 36.10. Gary again led the club to win this second league race, Stu Paton ran well for second, John Wright again third gave Bels a clean sweep of the first three places. Matthew and Ollie claimed their same positions as the first race, Peter Sanders gained four while Peter (Geronimo) Gilbey took some more scalps on his way back to fitness. John Mather also showing improving form, Andy was scoring after the first lap, alas he had to be contented with first non-scorer. The turnout was not as good as the first match. I hope it won't decline in the last two. (146 points in front). items.label: March 1989
items.sum: Harry Porter's review of the Ladies Section's 1988 season: Southern League, G.R.E. and Rosenheim League, Thameside League, the walkers, club records, the Endeavour and Centenary cup awards and thanks to officials.
items.s: The Ladies. Harry Porter's review of the Ladies Section's 1988 season: Southern League, G.R.E. and Rosenheim League, Thameside League, the walkers, club records, the Endeavour and Centenary cup awards and thanks to officials. The Ladies. Report from Harry Porter Firstly, I would like to congratulate Leo Coy, on behalf of the Ladies Section, on his election as Club President for 1988/89. Once again, there was a disastrous start to the Women's Southern League Division 2, in the first match, when at Kings Park, Bournemouth, we failed to field our best team. Again we struggled in the following matches to maintain our usual mid-league position. Instead, we were fighting against relegation until the last meeting at Battersea Park which took us back to a respectable mid-table position for the end of the season. However, if we had had good results in our first meetings, by starting in mid-table, we may have finished at the top, rather than as we did, start at the bottom and finish in the middle. Also, of course, we have a depleted Junior side, meaning that every Junior is needed to turn out and support the team from the beginning of the season. So - come on Ladies, let us start 1989 with a show of strength from both age groups. Following on from that, our Senior Ladies once again did us proud in the G.R.E. competition. They were the only Non-Division I League Team to reach the semi-final where we duly finished 8th. We were congratulated by three or four of these leading clubs on our reaching the semi-final stage. In the Rosenheim League we won all of the meetings except the final. That was a very close match indeed and we were pipped in the last event by Epsom's win in the Javelin by two points. This means, of course, that we failed to the trophy that we had won for the first time in 1987, the inaugural year for the Ladies Competition also the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Year. In the Thameside League, there is little one can say because of our lack of strength in the girls and minor girls, having only a few members in this. This can also be said for the Boys and Colts sections. So if anyone reading this paragraph knows of any Girl or Boy in these age groups - please bring them along we need them to help ensure the club's continuing success in the future. Therefore, I would like to charge every member, male or female, to introduce one girl or boy in these younger age groups into the club this season. If everyone made an effort on the Club's behalf, we would be the envy of all the club's in the Southern Counties. The Ladies Walking Section has continued to gain in strength and success, winning several team and individual awards for the club during the year. Well done Ladies - keep it up. There have been several good performances this year, most notably by Sian Spacey who finished third in the National 10K Road Walk. She also set new club records in the 2K, 3K, 5K and 10K Walking in the space of 3 months. Andrea Coore, after being out of action, injured, all the winter 1987/88 and half of the summer following with a knee injury, came back with a bang to break the Club Long Jump record 3 times in 3 consecutive jumps bring it up to near the 6 mtr. mark with 5.86m. Congratulations also, to Cindy James for winning the "Endeavour" Cup for amassing the most points throughout the summer season and for supporting every meeting. Well done and thank you Cindy. Runner up in the "Endeavour" Cup was Michelle McIntosh. "Centenary Cup" This prestigious cup is awarded, in the judgement of the committee, for the best performance by any female Belgrave Harrier in the year. The 1988 award went to Sian Spacey for her excellent 3rd place in the R.W.A. Womens 10Kms Road Walk Championship. Runner up, once again was Michelle McIntosh for her fine win in the Southern Counties Girls Long Jump. At this point, I would like to thank, firstly, Derek Jones for all the "backroom" work and for organising the meetings; an endless and thankless task which few people appreciate has to be done. Keep up the good work Derek, and many thanks on behalf of myself and the club. WITH THE LADIES Also those two Ladies - Win Shepherd and Jean Hutcheson who turn out to do the results recording on every occasion when we need them. I would also like to thank Cynthia James, my assistant team manager for her enthusiastic help and support throughout the year. My thanks go, of course, to all those officials who have turned out to support the Ladies Section and especially the Officials Hon. Sec. Derek Crookes for his excellent work. To all the Athletes who have turned out and supported the Ladies Section throughout the season, my special thanks. Keep up the good work for 1989 and good luck. H.P. items.s: PAGE 58. Boxing Day 1988 Family Participation - Enthusiasm Personified Full-page set of four photos of children of the James and Christou families in fancy dress at the club's Boxing Day 1988 event, with a caption printed on page 59 praising the two families' support. PAGE 58. Boxing Day 1988 Family Participation - Enthusiasm Personified Part of the very fine support given to the club's general activities is shown here by two of the families who give all the year round support to the Bels. Cindy James as a St. Trinians Terror and young brother Richard, as an "Imp" and Nina and Charlotte Christou as the Martini Girl and Clown in the Boxing Day event. Parents Cynthia and Ray James are ever present at our meetings, Cynthia is Ladies Section Assistant Team Manager and Jenny and Chris Christou likewise always around. Chris is now a graded coach. Both families also help with a very welcome "Chuck Wagon" at Ladies Track fixtures. items.sum: Photo from the Boxing Day meeting of A.D.Pyer (Mick), 1922 club mile champion and 1923 Surrey AAA champion, with T.C.(Chas) Jones, 1931 Surrey 440 yards hurdles champion.
items.s: Boxing Day Meeting Photo from the Boxing Day meeting of A.D.Pyer (Mick), 1922 club mile champion and 1923 Surrey AAA champion, with T.C.(Chas) Jones, 1931 Surrey 440 yards hurdles champion. Boxing Day Meeting - A.D.Pyer (Mick) Belgrave's Grand Old Man receives some advice from T.C.(Chas) Jones at the corner of Lauriston Road. Mick, now regrettably near sightless, was our 1 mile champion in 1922 and Surrey AAA Champion in 1923 whilst Charlie, a veritable bean-pole at the time, was Surrey 440 yds Hurdles Champion in 1931. items.s: Back Cover Photograph--- "MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN. Back-cover photo of President Leo Coy planting the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Tree on Wimbledon Common, watched by club members, with its caption printed on page 59 (which gives the planting date as 3 November 1989 although the issue is dated March 1989). Back Cover Photograph--- "MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN. Leo Coy puts the final touches to planting of the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Tree watched by Carl and Barbara Lawton, Harry Porter, Chas Manning and Tom Carter. The tree which is on Wimbledon Common opposite No. 30 Parkside, was planted on the 3rd. of November 1989. Also in attendance was Gordon Biscoe who had made all of the arrangements. "THANK YOU" Gordon. Photo by Joe Coleman who was also present. "MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN.
